summary: The publish workflow now supports a manual trigger with an option to publish exclusively to Test PyPI. This change removes the requirement for a specific deployment environment and updates action versions.

This commit improves file upload handling by automatically inferring filenames from file-like objects. The new `guess_filename` utility extracts the name attribute if it is not a placeholder, and `Request.send` now uses this to set the filename in multipart fields.

This commit updates the installation documentation to clarify that the guide specifically covers the Requests library. The change modifies the main heading in the user installation guide to explicitly name the software.
This commit adds a link to the Spanish translation of the documentation in the sidebar. It updates the sidebarintro.html template to include the new language option for users.
This commit adds support for the HTTP PATCH method to the requests library. It updates the `request` function in `requests/api.py` to accept PATCH requests and exports the new `patch` function.

The test `test_mixed_case_scheme_acceptable` in `test_requests.py` now uses the local `HTTPBIN_URL` variable instead of hard-coded external URLs. This change ensures the test for mixed-case URL schemes runs reliably against the local test server.

This commit fixes an issue where mixed-case URL schemes prevented effective connection pooling. The HTTPAdapter class now lowercases URLs before passing them to the underlying pool manager. Tests were added to verify that mixed-case schemes are handled correctly.

This commit fixes a type mismatch error in the `MockRequest` class within `requests/cookies.py`. It ensures that when the host header is patched into a URL, the host is converted to a string if the parsed URL components are strings, preventing crashes from mixing bytes and text types.

This commit updates the project history to record the release of version 0.6.4. It also corrects a typo in the changelog, changing the reference to the advanced response interface from "r.fo" to "r.faw".

This commit updates documentation links to use HTTPS instead of HTTP for improved security. It modifies the README and various documentation files to ensure all references to GitHub, PyPI, and Read the Docs use secure connections.

The `Request.send` method in `requests/models.py` now correctly handles the `prefetch` parameter when explicitly set to `False`. Previously, passing `False` did not override the request's default prefetch setting, causing unexpected behavior. This change ensures the parameter properly controls whether the response is prefetched.

This commit corrects spelling errors in the project documentation and source code comments. It fixes typos in the HTTPProxyAuth class and the RequestEncodingMixin module, improving the accuracy of the user-facing text.
This commit corrects a typo in the advanced user documentation. It fixes a misspelled variable name in an example, ensuring the text accurately reflects the correct spelling.

This commit modifies the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to use weak references when linking a request to its response. This change prevents circular references between the two objects, which helps the garbage collector free memory more efficiently.
This commit adds a new license image file to the extension directory. It introduces the visual asset required for displaying license information within the application.

This commit introduces a new setup.py file to configure the packaging and distribution of the requests library. It defines the package metadata, dependencies, and includes a helper function to publish the project to PyPI.

This commit removes a redundant conditional check for cookies within the `Request.send` method in `requests/models.py`. The change cleans up the code by eliminating a block that performed no action, leaving only a commented-out reference.

This commit fixes a Python 2 compatibility issue in the requests library by ensuring the `str` alias is correctly defined within the `compat` module. It resolves a potential error where the alias was missing or incorrectly placed, ensuring consistent behavior for string handling in older Python versions.

This commit refactors the Session class in requests/sessions.py to improve code readability. It consolidates the request method's parameter list into a more compact format and adjusts comment spacing. No functional behavior changes are introduced.

This commit updates the project's README documentation to clarify that connection pooling is provided by the urllib3 library. It removes the statement that urllib3 is embedded within the Requests module, correcting the description of the dependency relationship.

This commit reorders the arguments in the `HTTPAdapter` initialization method to prevent breaking changes for existing users. By moving the `pool_block` parameter to the end of the argument list, the function maintains backward compatibility with code that relies on the previous positional argument order.

This commit adds documentation for a new `prefetch` parameter in the `request` function within `requests/api.py`. It clarifies that setting this option to true immediately downloads the response content, allowing users to control when data is fetched.

This commit updates the project title in the README file to include decorative emoji characters. It adjusts the underline length to match the new title width, ensuring the documentation header renders correctly.

This commit corrects a typo in the project's dependency list by replacing the invalid package name "pytestt" with the correct "pytest". This ensures the testing framework installs properly during environment setup.

The `Response.json` method in `requests/models.py` now uses `complexjson` instead of the standard `json` module for parsing. This ensures consistent JSON decoding behavior across different Python environments.
Adds a new flake8 target to the Makefile that runs the linter while ignoring line length errors. This allows developers to easily check code style compliance from the command line.

The `unquote_unreserved` function in `requests/utils.py` is rewritten to handle invalid percent-encodings gracefully instead of crashing. This change makes the URL decoding process more robust and simplifies the underlying code logic.

This commit updates the bundled CA certificate bundle in the requests library to version 2017.4.17. It removes the outdated RSA Security 2048 v3 certificate from the cacert.pem file, ensuring the library uses the current trusted root certificates for secure connections.

This commit improves the documentation for the `Session` class in the `requests` library. It adds detailed descriptions for instance attributes like headers, authentication, and timeouts, and includes the class in the API reference.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to clarify that dictionary keys with a value of None are excluded from the URL query string when using the requests library. It addresses a potential confusion for users who expect all provided parameters to appear in the final request URL.

This commit adjusts the visual alignment of the sea turtle logo in the documentation layout. It adds a CSS style rule to the layout template to shift the image slightly to the left, correcting its positioning on the page.

This commit reverts the hooks functionality from a sub-package back to a single module within the requests library. It consolidates hook setup and dispatch logic into requests/hooks.py, removing the previous directory structure.

This commit removes the test suite for the asynchronous API in the requests library. It deletes the file containing tests for the async module, which is no longer supported. Users will no longer see these specific test cases run during the test suite.
This commit updates the project history to document a performance improvement in the CaseInsensitiveDict class. It notes that the dictionary now caches lower-case keys to optimize lookup operations.

This commit updates the packaging configuration in setup.py to explicitly include the requests.packages.urllib3.packages module. This ensures the nested dependency is correctly bundled when the package is installed.
Adds a new image asset named flourish.png to the extension directory. This file is likely used for visual branding or interface elements within the extension.

The `ok` property in the `Response` class now returns a boolean based on whether the status code is less than 400, rather than raising an exception. This change clarifies the method's contract and prevents unexpected errors when checking response status.

This commit updates internal imports in the auth, models, and sessions modules to reference the to_native_string function from the new _internal_utils module instead of the public utils module. This change reorganizes the codebase by moving internal helper functions to a dedicated private module.

This documentation update clarifies that the `params` argument in the Requests library expects a dictionary of strings. It corrects the quickstart guide to specify the required data type for URL query parameters.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar for the certifi project. It adds a link to the official Certifi website, allowing users to easily access the recommended CA bundle information from the project's documentation.
Adds a new default setting called `encode_urls` to the `requests` library's default configuration. This change enables URL encoding by default, affecting how requests handle URL components.

This commit updates the requests adapters module to import the basestring type from the compatibility layer. It ensures the module has access to this type for proper string handling across different Python versions.
The `header_expand` function in `requests/utils.py` now accepts Unicode strings by encoding them to Latin-1 bytes. This prevents errors when users pass Unicode header values directly to the library.

This commit updates the `Response.raise_for_status` method in the `requests` library to attach the response object to the raised `HTTPError` exception. This allows users to access the original response data directly from the exception instance when handling errors.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to explain the request lifecycle. It clarifies that response bodies are downloaded lazily only when the content attribute is accessed, rather than immediately upon making the request.

This commit removes Python 3.3 support from the project's build and packaging configuration. It updates the CI pipelines and setup metadata to no longer test or declare compatibility with that version.

This commit removes the bundled Python 2.7 collections module from the urllib3 package. It eliminates the need for the vendored `__collections.py` file, which contained abstract base classes like Mapping and MutableMapping. This change simplifies the codebase by relying on the standard library's built-in collections.

This release introduces a new command-line utility, `python -m requests.help`, to assist users with debugging and troubleshooting. The version number in the `requests` module is updated to 2.16.4 to reflect this addition.

The Request class in requests/models.py now correctly handles URLs containing unencoded path characters. This ensures that paths are properly percent-encoded when constructing the final request URL, preventing potential parsing errors or malformed requests.

This commit updates the project documentation to replace a Twitter handle link with the plain name "Kenneth Reitz." It improves the readability of the text by removing the external hyperlink reference.

The Makefile now runs the full test suite instead of only the requests tests, adding color output for local runs. It also introduces a new server target to launch the httpbin application via gunicorn.

This commit introduces the chardet module as a replacement for the charade dependency within the requests package. It adds the necessary files and classes, such as the detect function, to handle character encoding detection. This change prepares the library to use chardet for identifying text encodings.

This release fixes a bug where the last line of a response was truncated during iteration. It also enforces safe mode for asynchronous requests and improves how exceptions are handled in that mode. The version number in the requests module was updated to 0.8.7.

This commit updates the documentation to reflect Twitter's increased character limit. It changes the recommended maximum length for support tweets from 140 to 280 characters in the community support guide.
This commit adds a `prefetch` option to the `request` function and `Session.request` method. When enabled, it immediately downloads the response content instead of waiting for the user to access it.

This commit updates the success message displayed by the Makefile after building the documentation. It changes the wording from "Installed!" to "Build successful!" to more accurately describe the action performed.

Adds a new `is_redirect` property to the `Response` class in the `requests` library. This property indicates whether the response status code represents a redirect that the library could process, regardless of whether the redirect was actually followed.
This commit updates the project's author list to include the urllib3 team. It adds Andrey Petrov as a development lead under a new urllib3 section in the AUTHORS file.

This commit updates the project's author list by renaming the "Development Lead" and "Core Contributors" sections to "Keepers of the Three Crystals." It also adds a specific title to Kenneth Reitz's entry.

This commit introduces a `merge_kwargs` function to the `requests/sessions.py` module, allowing the `Session` class to properly combine default and local keyword arguments. It ensures that `None` values in local arguments do not override existing defaults, improving the handling of session configuration parameters.

This commit removes the project's Makefile, which previously provided targets for running tests and managing dependencies. Users will no longer be able to use make commands to install packages or execute test suites.

This commit fixes the rendering of a list in the "Custom Headers" section of the quickstart documentation. It corrects the indentation in the quickstart.rst file to ensure the text displays properly as a list item.

This commit adds regression tests to verify that the requests library correctly handles binary data uploads. It introduces test cases in the RequestsTestSuite class to ensure that sending non-UTF-8 bytes and encoded strings does not cause errors.
This commit restores the ASCII art logo to the module docstring in `requests/__init__.py`. Users will see the familiar graphical banner when viewing the package documentation or help text.
This commit adds a promotional link for Requests stickers to the documentation sidebar. It updates the sidebar templates to display a "Stickers!" heading that directs users to an external store.

This commit updates the project documentation to clarify that HTTP response headers are returned as a case-insensitive dictionary. It also adds a new entry describing the Response.history attribute, which provides a list of responses for tracking redirections.
The lock-issues workflow now runs once daily instead of hourly, reducing unnecessary background activity. It also updates the lock-threads action to version 3.

This commit removes the pytest-mock dependency from the development requirements. It updates the test suite to use Python's built-in unittest.mock module instead, ensuring tests run without the external plugin.
This release fixes a bug in the digest authentication mechanism within the requests library. The version number is updated to 0.7.3 to reflect this specific security-related correction.

This commit adds documentation to the advanced user guide explaining how to use hooks to modify request arguments. It demonstrates a specific example where a hook function injects a custom header into the request before it is sent.

This commit adds the AUTHORS.orig file to the repository, listing the development lead and contributors to the Requests library. The file contains a merge conflict marker, indicating an unresolved conflict between two branches during the addition of contributor names.

This commit fixes a bug where the prefetch setting was not carried over when a request was redirected. It ensures the `prefetch` attribute is correctly propagated in the `Request._build_response` method within the `requests` module.

This commit fixes a bug in the `SessionRedirectMixin` class where redirect URLs with uppercase schemes were not properly normalized. It replaces a simple string split with `urlparse` and `urlunparse` to ensure the scheme is correctly lowercased while preserving the rest of the URL structure.

This commit fixes an issue where byte-string field names in multipart requests were incorrectly encoded, potentially causing errors. The `_encode_files` method in `requests/models.py` now decodes byte strings to Unicode before passing them to urllib3.

This commit adds a new test to the TestRequests class in tests/test_requests.py that verifies HTTP basic authentication works correctly using a tuple for both direct requests and sessions. It also restores the original test method, renaming it to test_set_basicauth to avoid a naming conflict with the new test.
This commit fixes the indentation of the API examples in the README.rst file. It ensures the code snippets are properly aligned within the documentation structure.
This commit removes a promotional sentence from the project's README file. It cleans up the documentation by deleting a line that claimed the software powers everyday tools.
This commit updates the project's README to reflect a higher download count. It changes the stated total from six million to seven million downloads for the Requests package.

This commit corrects a documentation error in the Quickstart guide where the example code incorrectly used StringIO instead of BytesIO for opening image data. It also removes a trailing whitespace character.

This commit simplifies the response handling logic in the `requests` library by replacing separate decompression checks with a unified `stream_untransfer` utility. It updates the `Response` class to use this new function, streamlining how content encoding is processed during data retrieval.

This commit simplifies the certificate verification logic in the `HTTPAdapter` class within `requests/adapters.py`. It consolidates conditional checks for HTTPS URLs and verification settings, making the code more concise while preserving the same behavior for handling default and custom certificate locations.

This commit fixes an issue where proxy bypass logic incorrectly considered port numbers when matching against the no_proxy list. The change updates the Request.send method in requests/models.py to compare only hostnames, ensuring proxies are correctly ignored for specified domains.

The `cookiejar_from_dict` function in `requests/cookies.py` now accepts an `overwrite` parameter to control whether existing cookies are replaced. This allows `Session` to merge new cookies without discarding previously stored ones, preventing data loss during session updates.
This commit adds Alejandro Giacometti to the project's list of contributors. It updates the AUTHORS file to recognize his patches and suggestions.
This commit updates the CI configuration to make Xenial the default distribution for all test jobs. It removes the explicit Xenial setting from the job matrix, simplifying the build process.

This release adds official support for Python 3.10 and introduces a new `JSONDecodeError` exception to unify JSON handling across Python versions. It also improves error messages for schema-related exceptions within the `requests` library.

This commit updates the version number of the requests library from 0.3.2 to 0.3.3. It modifies the version strings in the core module, documentation configuration, and history file to reflect the new release.

This commit reformats the `requests/core.py` module to improve code readability by breaking long lines. It adjusts the parameter lists for the `Request` and `_Request` classes as well as the top-level HTTP method functions. No functional behavior or bug fixes are included in this change.

This commit corrects a spelling error in a comment within the requests/compat.py module. It changes the word "thows" to "throws" to accurately describe the exception raised by simplejson on Python 3.2. No functional code changes were made.

This commit inverts the urllib3 version check in the requests library to use a flag for version 1 instead of version 2. It updates the super_len function in utils.py to correctly handle string length calculations based on the new flag, ensuring compatibility with both urllib3 versions.

This commit fixes a packaging error in `setup.py` that occurred when the `LICENSE` file was missing, which would crash the installation process. It replaces the dynamic file read with a static license string to ensure the package builds successfully across different distribution environments.

This commit removes the "Are you crazy?" section from the development TODO documentation. It eliminates the informal note suggesting SPDY support as a future feature, cleaning up the project's roadmap.

This commit corrects a formatting error in the installation documentation. It adjusts the length of the underline beneath the "Cheeseshop (PyPI) Mirror" heading in the `docs/user/install.rst` file to ensure proper rendering.

The `publish` target in the Makefile now creates a dedicated virtual environment to isolate release dependencies. It replaces the legacy `setup.py` build process with the modern `build` module and adds a flag to skip existing files during upload.

The `proxy_manager_for` method in the `HTTPAdapter` class now accepts additional keyword arguments to configure the proxy manager. This change allows subclasses to pass extra settings without modifying the core method signature, improving reusability for custom adapter implementations.

This commit reverts a previous change that allowed non-HTTP schemes to bypass URL validation. It restores the behavior where `PreparedRequest.prepare_url` and `parse_url` process all URLs uniformly, removing the special handling for oddball schemes.

This commit updates a comment in the Makefile to provide a more specific example of the `-k` flag usage. It clarifies how to filter tests by name, improving documentation for developers running the test suite.

This refactoring moves request data encoding logic from the Request class constructor into a new static helper method named _encode_params. This change clarifies the code structure and prepares the encoding functionality for potential reuse in other parts of the requests module.

This commit removes the `keep_alive` parameter from the `Session` class, making it a configuration-only option. It also updates the default connection pool size to 10 and standardizes how default values for cookies and data are handled in request methods.

This documentation update corrects the HTTP method name in the advanced user guide to use the standard uppercase format. It ensures the example for the `requests` library accurately reflects proper protocol usage.

This commit updates the package manifest to include the Markdown version of the readme file instead of the reStructuredText version. It ensures the correct documentation file is bundled when building the distribution.

This commit updates the version number of the requests library from 0.7.0 to 0.7.1. It modifies the `__version__` and `__build__` variables in the `requests/__init__.py` module to reflect the new release.

This commit adds a test case to the RequestsTestSuite in test_requests.py that verifies the library can successfully post both form data and file uploads to a Postbin instance. It ensures that the POST requests return the expected status codes for these operations.

This commit updates the Flasky documentation theme's stylesheet to improve mobile responsiveness. It adjusts the breakpoint for small screens and adds specific layout rules for the sidebar and body margins to enhance the user experience on narrow devices.

This commit clarifies in the documentation that HTTP connections are only reused after the response body is fully read. It advises users to enable prefetching or explicitly read the content to ensure connection pooling works as expected.

This commit adds a test to the RequestsTestSuite in tests/test_requests.py to verify that the post function correctly handles data arguments containing lists of values alongside file uploads. It ensures that multiple values for a single field are properly serialized when sending multipart form data.

This commit adds documentation to the advanced user guide and the Session class, warning that disabling SSL verification exposes applications to man-in-the-middle attacks. It clarifies that setting verify to False accepts any certificate, ignoring hostname mismatches and expiration, which is only suitable for local development.
This commit adds Ben Toews to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS.rst file. It updates the project's attribution records to include a new name under the patches and suggestions section.

This commit updates the community support documentation to include a new Twitter account for user inquiries. It also adds guidance for non-native English speakers to describe vulnerability issues in their native language for better translation.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar templates to replace a link to Markdown, Please! with a link to the Maya datetime library. The change affects the sidebarintro and sidebarlogo modules, altering the external resources displayed to users.

This commit fixes a bug in the HTTPDigestAuth class where repeated 401 errors occurred when using digest authentication with a session. It resolves the issue by tracking the number of 401 responses directly on the request object instead of relying on response hooks.

This commit adds docstrings to the test methods in the TestTestServer class within tests/test_testserver.py. It improves documentation clarity by describing the specific behavior each test verifies, such as message handling and server lifecycle. No functional code changes were made.

Fixes `get_auth_from_url` in `requests/utils.py` to return an empty tuple instead of `None` when a URL contains an empty authentication section. This prevents errors when parsing URLs with a colon but no credentials.

This commit reverts the project's build and test configuration to use Pipenv instead of standard pip and setup.py. It updates the Makefile to manage dependencies via Pipenv and changes the Travis CI script to run coverage tests.

The `HTTPAdapter` class in the `requests` library now accepts a directory path for the `verify` argument, allowing users to specify a folder of CA certificates instead of only a single bundle file. This change enables more flexible SSL verification configurations for users managing multiple certificate files.
This commit contains no code changes or file modifications. It serves as a placeholder or marker in the repository history without altering any application behavior or functionality.
This commit adds the PySocks library to the test requirements in setup.py. It ensures the necessary dependencies are installed to run the project's test suite successfully.

This release updates the `check_compatibility` function in the `requests` module to allow urllib3 version 1.26. It also adds support for the NETRC environment variable and deprecates the `requests[security]` extra.

The `get_auth_from_url` function in `requests/utils.py` now returns `None` instead of an empty tuple when no authentication credentials are found in a URL. This change allows callers to distinguish between missing credentials and empty credentials.

This commit clarifies that the timeout parameter now applies equally to both streaming and non-streaming requests. It updates the API documentation to specify that the timeout limits individual socket read attempts rather than the total download time.

This commit strengthens a test assertion in the RequestsTestSuite to verify that a cached response contains actual content. It ensures the test correctly validates the data returned by the test_cached_response method.

This commit fixes a PEP 8 style violation in the requests package's initialization module. It corrects the spacing around the assignment operator when unpacking the urllib3 version tuple, ensuring the code adheres to standard formatting guidelines.

This commit removes unused pre-request and pre-send hooks from the requests library, leaving only the response hook. It also adds explicit response hook dispatch logic to the Session.request method to ensure response manipulation hooks are correctly applied.

This commit removes an unused import from the `requests.models` module. It cleans up the codebase by eliminating a reference to `HTTPResponse` that was not being utilized, with no impact on user-facing behavior.

This commit updates the Travis CI configuration to disable the use of sudo privileges during the build process. This change ensures the build runs in a lightweight container environment, which typically results in faster execution times.

This commit adjusts the indentation of arguments passed to the proxy manager within the `proxy_manager_for` method of the `HTTPAdapter` class. The change is purely cosmetic and does not alter the library's behavior or fix any functional bugs.

This commit updates the documentation index to reduce the maximum depth of the table of contents from three levels to two. It also removes the "extensions" page from the community section, leaving only the FAQ.

The commit removes the entire contents of the requirements.txt file, eliminating all pinned dependency versions. This change likely resolves installation conflicts or simplifies the project's dependency management by clearing out the previous list of packages.

This commit updates the project's main documentation page to change the description of the library. It replaces the previous claim that Requests is the only HTTP library for Python with a new statement calling it an excellent and best-in-class option.

This commit updates the project's setup configuration to correctly identify the README file as reStructuredText rather than Markdown. This ensures the package description renders properly on PyPI. The change modifies the long_description_content_type setting in setup.py.

This commit corrects the `test_json_encodes_as_bytes` test in `tests/test_requests.py` to properly validate JSON encoding behavior. It fixes a flaw where the test was passing a string literal instead of the intended variable, ensuring the test accurately reflects the expected functionality.

The `cleanup_url` function in `requests/utils.py` now appends a trailing slash to URLs that lack a path component. This ensures that requests to root domains, such as Twitter, are formatted correctly to avoid potential routing or parsing issues.

This commit updates the project's setup configuration to dynamically load the full license text from the LICENSE file instead of using a static string. This change ensures the package metadata accurately reflects the complete licensing terms.

This commit updates the project's README to ensure the TravisCI status badge links directly to the project's status page. It modifies the documentation file to provide users with accurate build status information.

This commit fixes a minor typographical error in the project's documentation index. It corrects the spacing in a reference to the requests module author, ensuring the text reads correctly for users viewing the project description.

This commit updates the community documentation to list Daikon, a command-line interface for ElasticSearch, as an external module. It adds a reference to the project's GitHub repository in the "Modules" section of the out-there guide.
This commit updates the Ruff linter version in the pre-commit configuration from 0.15.11 to 0.15.12. It ensures the project uses the latest patch release for code quality checks.

This commit refactors the CaseInsensitiveDict class in requests/structures.py to improve performance by caching lowercased keys. It replaces the previous method that recalculated keys on every access with a cached property, ensuring faster lookups for case-insensitive dictionary operations.

This commit pins the GitHub Actions test environment to Ubuntu 18.04 to prevent test failures caused by the upcoming switch to Ubuntu 20.04. It modifies the run-tests.yml workflow file to explicitly specify the older operating system version.
The Makefile's publish target now removes the build directory and requests.egg-info folder in addition to dist and .egg. This ensures a cleaner build environment before packaging.
This commit corrects several spelling errors in the project's history documentation. It fixes the misspelling of the Response class name in multiple entries within HISTORY.rst.

This commit adds a comprehensive test suite to the project and updates the build configuration to run these tests. It also fixes a bug in the RequestEncodingMixin class where passing None for data or files would cause an error.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to explain how to disable SSL certificate verification and specify local client certificates. It clarifies the behavior of the `verify` and `cert` parameters in the `requests` library. Additionally, it adds new contributors to the project's author list.

This commit corrects spelling and grammar errors in the documentation and docstrings for the Requests library. It fixes typos in community guides and clarifies wording in modules such as requests.models and requests.exceptions.

This commit removes an unnecessary print statement from the `get_connection` method in the `HTTPAdapter` class. It eliminates unwanted console output that would appear when establishing a connection, cleaning up the library's behavior.

This commit updates the documentation to fix a broken reference in the installation guide and adds a new "Feature Overview" section to the quickstart. It explicitly lists the capabilities and limitations of the Requests library, such as its support for various HTTP methods and lack of caching.

This commit optimizes the `Session.close` method in `requests/sessions.py` by iterating directly over adapter values instead of unpacking unused keys. This streamlines the cleanup process when closing a session, removing unnecessary variable assignments during the loop.
This commit removes the "Modules" section from the community documentation page. It eliminates a list of third-party Python projects that were previously featured in the out-there guide.

This commit adds a clarifying comment to the `Request.prepare` method in `requests/models.py`. It explains that authentication preparation must occur last to ensure schemes like OAuth function correctly on a fully prepared request.
This commit updates the community support documentation by adding an image to the support page. The change modifies the `docs/community/support.rst` file to include a visual element.
This commit updates the version string in the requests core module to 0.6.2 (dev) to clarify the current development status. It also increments the corresponding build number to reflect this change.
This commit updates the documentation index to correct the URL for financial support. It fixes a broken link in the main documentation page, ensuring users can successfully access the donation page.

This commit prevents the library from silently serializing NaN values into invalid JSON. It introduces a new InvalidJSONError exception and updates the PreparedRequest.prepare_body method to raise this error when NaN is detected during serialization.

This commit updates the documentation for major contributors by adding hyperlinks to the Heroku and Slack sponsor entries. The change modifies the `docs/community/sponsors.rst` file to make these names clickable for users.

This documentation update clarifies that calling `r.json()` on invalid JSON raises different exceptions depending on the Python version. It specifies that Python 2 raises a `ValueError`, while Python 3 raises a `JSONDecodeError`. The change corrects the quickstart guide to reflect these version-specific behaviors.

This commit updates the MANIFEST.in file to reorder the included documentation files. It places the README and LICENSE before the HISTORY file, ensuring a consistent listing order for the package distribution.

This commit fixes a broken link on the advanced documentation page. It updates the reference for connection pooling in the `docs/user/advanced.rst` file to point to the correct urllib3 documentation URL.

This commit adds equality and inequality methods to the HTTPBasicAuth and HTTPDigestAuth classes in the requests.auth module. Users can now compare authentication handler instances directly to check if they hold identical credentials and state.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar to replace a link to monescate.com with a link to the Requests-HTML project. The change affects the sidebarintro.html and sidebarlogo.html templates, ensuring users see the correct related project reference.

This commit adds a future import to the test_requests.py module to enable the with statement syntax. This change ensures the test file remains compatible with Python 2.5, which requires this explicit import to support context managers.

This commit updates the project's NOTICE file to correct the license attribution for the CA Root Certificates bundle. It replaces the previous section header with a more accurate "CA Bundle License" title to properly identify the third-party component.

This commit updates the test suite to verify that HTTP sessions correctly use the new authentication mechanism. It adds an assertion to the `RequestsTestSuite` to ensure that requests made via a session with specific auth credentials return a 401 status code, confirming the auth behavior.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Request.send` method where data encoding occurred before authentication, potentially corrupting data modified by providers like OAuth1. It moves the encoding step to after the authentication logic runs, ensuring the final request payload reflects any changes made by the auth provider.
This commit updates the copyright holder in the project's license file from Kenneth Reitz to Josh Ourisman. It also adds a missing newline at the end of the file to ensure proper formatting.

This commit updates the project's NOTICE file to correctly attribute the Urllib3 library instead of Poster. It also modifies MANIFEST.in to ensure the NOTICE file is included in the distribution package.
This commit updates the fundraising progress displayed in the documentation sidebar. It changes the reported amount raised from $110 to $203 in the sidebarintro and sidebarlogo templates.

This release updates the requests library to version 2.24.0. It ensures redirect resolution only occurs when explicitly allowed and removes unnecessary Content-Length calculations for requests that do not use them.

This commit fixes a typo in the test suite for the requests module by uncommenting an assertion in the test_json_param_post_content_type_works method. This ensures the test correctly verifies that JSON parameters are handled with the proper content type.

This commit updates the test configuration to use the standard PyPy binary instead of the specific PyPy-C variant. It ensures the test environment runs with the correct Python interpreter path. The change is located in the tox.ini file.

This commit refactors the `_parse_content_type_header` function in `requests/utils.py` to simplify how it splits and processes content type parameters. It removes redundant logic for handling empty headers and delimiter appending, resulting in a more direct parsing approach.

This commit updates the test_idna method in the RequestsTestSuite to verify that the response URL contains 'httpbin' instead of 'tinyarrows.com'. This change ensures the test correctly validates the expected domain for the request.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to explain that cookies are returned in a RequestsCookieJar object. It clarifies that this class acts like a dictionary but supports multiple domains and paths, and demonstrates how to pass a custom jar to requests.

This commit removes duplicate entries for Cory Benfield and Ian Cordasco from the project's contributor list. It ensures each author appears only once in the AUTHORS.rst file, cleaning up the credits section.

The documentation for advanced usage now demonstrates streaming requests using the httpbin service instead of the Twitter API. This change removes the need for OAuth credentials in the example, simplifying the code snippet for users.

This commit reverts the version number in the requests package from 2.3.0 to 2.2.1. It updates the version string in the module's initialization file and corrects the release history documentation to reflect the current stable release.

This commit removes the Konami code easter egg, analytics tracking, and the "keep up to date" feature from the documentation site. It deletes the associated JavaScript and image assets, and updates various documentation pages to reflect these changes.

This commit updates the documentation for the Certifi library to fix a broken link. It changes the reference in the recommended community tools list to point to the correct GitHub repository instead of the outdated website.

This commit updates the `requests` library to treat HTTP 308 status codes as permanent redirects, aligning their behavior with 301 and 302 responses. Users will now see the library automatically follow 308 redirects instead of ignoring them.

This commit fixes a potential error in the `RequestException` class where a falsy response object was incorrectly treated as missing. It ensures the code explicitly checks for `None` before accessing response attributes, preventing unexpected behavior when a valid but falsy response is passed.

This commit updates the contribution guidelines to require bug reporters to specify their Requests version and installation method. This helps maintainers distinguish between issues caused by different releases or third-party distribution patches.
This commit updates the release history to document version 2.9.2. It notes a bug fix that prevents the use of the redirect cache when redirects are explicitly disabled.

This commit fixes a missing import in the `requests/sessions.py` module. It ensures that `dispatch_hook` is correctly imported from the hooks module, preventing potential errors when session hooks are processed.

This commit consolidates the separate Linux and Windows CI pipeline templates into a single unified configuration. It removes the dedicated Linux template file and updates the main pipeline to handle both operating systems, simplifying the build process.

This commit fixes a formatting inconsistency in the `Session` class within `requests/sessions.py`. It replaces a tab character with spaces in the docstring of the `request` method, ensuring consistent indentation style.

This commit adds SOCKS proxy support to the HTTPAdapter class in the requests library. It introduces a SOCKSProxyManager to handle connections, allowing users to route requests through SOCKS proxies. If the required dependencies are missing, the system raises an InvalidSchema error.

This commit updates the `PreparedRequest` class in `requests/models.py` to catch `LocationParseError` exceptions during URL parsing and re-raise them as `ConnectionError`. It also adds a test for this behavior and temporarily disables a failing session pickling test.

This commit fixes a compatibility issue in the `SessionRedirectMixin` where redirect handling failed when using standard `cookielib` cookie jars. It replaces the direct dictionary update in `resolve_redirects` with a `merge_cookies` call to properly handle different cookie jar types.
This commit removes the TODO.rst file, which previously listed a task to fix 405 exceptions. It cleans up the repository by deleting this outdated documentation file.

This commit adds a failing test case to the RequestsTestSuite in test_requests.py. It verifies that legal reserved and unreserved characters in a URL path are not percent-encoded, ensuring the library handles these characters correctly.

The quickstart documentation now directs users to the GitHub API events endpoint instead of the deprecated timeline.json URL. This change ensures the example code in the user guide remains functional and up to date.

This commit updates the project's README to clarify the role of the Python Software Foundation. It changes the attribution text to state that the PSF keeps the software safe, rather than simply listing them as a co-designer.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Request.full_url` method where query parameters were incorrectly appended after the URL fragment. It ensures parameters are properly added to the query string before the fragment, resolving issues with malformed URLs.

This commit fixes the width of the fixed footer in the documentation sidebar. It replaces a fixed percentage width with left and right positioning to ensure the element spans the full container width correctly. The change is applied in the custom stylesheet.

This commit updates the project documentation to explicitly state that Requests follows Semantic Versioning. It adds a new section to the philosophy guide explaining the rationale for this standard and removes a stray blank line.

This commit corrects two spelling errors in the HTTP status code names within the requests library. It fixes the misspelled keys for the 301 and 500 status codes in the status_codes module, ensuring the identifiers are accurate.
This commit adds a new contributor to the project's author list. It updates the AUTHORS.rst file to include Marc Schlaich under the patches and suggestions section.
This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to version 1.12. It refactors the HTTPHeaderDict class to inherit from MutableMapping instead of dict, changing how headers are stored and accessed.

This commit moves the documentation for uploading multiple files to the advanced section of the user guide. It removes the example from the quickstart guide and adds it to the advanced documentation, clarifying how to send multiple multipart-encoded files in a single request.

This commit adds a failing test to the UtilsTestCase in test_requests.py. It verifies that the super_len function correctly returns zero for a partially consumed file-like object, addressing a potential issue with length calculation.

This commit reverts the addition of trusted domains to the requests library. It removes the trusted_domains attribute from the Session class and restores the original behavior where authentication headers are always stripped when the hostname changes during a redirect.

This commit updates the CI configuration and build scripts to use system-wide package installation instead of virtual environments. It modifies the Travis CI setup and the Makefile to ensure tests run directly with the system Python interpreter.

Fixes a typo in the Request class within requests/core.py that caused a NameError when sending a request. This change corrects a variable reference in the send method, ensuring the response is built correctly without crashing.

The `get_unicode_from_response` function in `requests/utils.py` previously failed on Python 3 because the `str` type was not imported from the compatibility module. This commit adds the missing import and updates the function to use `str` instead of `unicode`, ensuring correct text decoding across Python versions.

This commit fixes a spelling error in the documentation for the HTTPAdapter class within the requests module. It corrects a typo in the cross-reference link for the get_connection method, ensuring the class name is spelled correctly.

This commit updates the project's author list to acknowledge Justin Barber for their contributions. It adds their name to the credits section of the documentation file, ensuring proper attribution for patches and suggestions.

This commit adds unit tests to the requests library's test suite to verify the behavior of the is_ipv4_address and is_ipv4_network utility functions. It ensures these functions correctly distinguish between valid IPv4 addresses, networks, and invalid inputs.

This commit corrects a spelling error in the docstring of the `_implementation` function within the `requests/help.py` module. It changes the word "verison" to "version" to ensure the documentation accurately describes the returned data.

This commit updates the Pipfile.lock to resolve a security vulnerability in the bleach library. It upgrades the package version from 2019.9.11 to 2019.11.28, ensuring the project uses a secure release.

This commit adds SSL certificate verification support to the `Session` class in `requests/sessions.py`. Users can now configure verification globally during session initialization or override it per request, ensuring secure connections by default.

This commit updates the changelog to prevent the documentation renderer from automatically converting an example proxy URL into a clickable link. By formatting the URL as literal text, it avoids misleading users into clicking a non-functional link. The change is made in the HISTORY.md file.

This commit removes the `Request.copy` method and changes how `PreparedRequest` is created within the `Session` class. Instead of copying the entire `Request` object, the session now merges settings directly when preparing the request, preventing unnecessary duplication of mutable data.

This commit removes a trivial test method from the RequestsTestCase class in test_requests.py. The deleted test contained a simple assertion that served no practical purpose, cleaning up the test suite.

This commit updates the Travis CI configuration to change the dependency installation method. It replaces the standard pip install command with Pipenv, ensuring the project's dependencies are installed using the Pipenv tool.

The `_encode_params` method in `requests/models.py` now correctly handles lists of two-element tuples, preserving their order during encoding. Previously, this input format was not supported, potentially causing errors or incorrect parameter ordering.
This commit updates the project's documentation to reflect a higher download count. It changes the reported PyPI download statistics in the main index file from 23 million to 40 million.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar to display more useful navigation links. It replaces a single link to recommended packages with direct links to the quickstart, advanced usage, API reference, release history, and contributor guide.
This commit updates the package publishing process in setup.py to use modern tools. It replaces the deprecated upload command with a two-step process that builds a wheel and uploads it via twine.

This commit renames the `cookiejar` parameter to `cookies` in the `Request` class and the `request` function. It updates the internal attribute and fixes a commented-out section in `Request.send` to properly handle the cookies argument.

This commit fixes the chardet import logic in the requests compatibility module to work correctly across Python versions. It removes the previous version-specific conditional imports and replaces them with a unified try-except block that attempts to load cchardet before falling back to the bundled package.
This commit updates the project history to document the addition of a prefetch parameter for request methods. It clarifies that users can now control prefetching behavior when making requests.

This commit updates the project history to document version 0.4.1. It highlights improved redirection handling, a new parameter for following non-GET/HEAD redirects, and refactoring of the settings module.

This commit updates the project's README to replace a generic placeholder with a descriptive tagline. It clarifies the library's purpose as an elegant and simple HTTP client for Python, improving the initial user experience.

This commit removes a debug print statement from the `Settings` class in `requests/config.py`. It eliminates an unwanted console output that occurred when exiting the settings context, cleaning up the user experience.

This commit updates the project's README to replace informal, subjective language with a professional description of the library. It clarifies that the tool is an ISC-licensed HTTP library designed for human use, while acknowledging the limitations of Python's built-in urllib2 module.

This commit finalizes the release notes for version 2.34.0 by setting the release date and reorganizing the changelog. It moves the announcement of inline types to a dedicated section and adds acknowledgments for contributors who reviewed the type definitions.

This commit corrects a typo in a comment within the `Request` class in `requests/models.py`. It changes the word "most" to "must" in the documentation for the `prepare` method, clarifying the requirement for the `prepare_auth` step.

The `get_netrc_auth` function in `requests/utils.py` now handles cases where `os.path.expanduser` raises a `KeyError`. This prevents crashes when the home directory is undefined and the system password lookup fails, allowing the library to skip netrc authentication instead of erroring out.

The `get_environ_proxies` function in `requests/utils.py` now recognizes lowercase environment proxy variables in addition to uppercase ones. This ensures that proxy settings defined with lowercase names are correctly detected and returned in a format compatible with the `requests` library.

This commit restores the ability to pass None as the chunk_size argument to the Response.iter_content method. Previously, this value was incorrectly rejected, preventing users from requesting the entire response content in a single chunk.

This commit adds support for HTTP redirects to the requests library. It introduces a new `SessionMixin` class with a `resolve_redirects` method to handle redirect chains, and adds a `close` method to the `Response` class to release connections.

This commit reorganizes the project's test suite by moving test files into a dedicated `tests` directory. It updates the `Makefile` to point to the new location and adds path configuration to the test modules to ensure they can import the main package correctly.

This commit updates the test suite to import the timeout utility directly from the urllib3 library instead of through the requests package. This change removes a deprecated import path, ensuring tests use the standard external dependency location.

This commit refines the test suite for the requests library, updating both integration and unit tests to improve coverage and reliability. It also makes minor adjustments to the PoolManager class in the urllib3 package to support these testing changes.

This commit fixes an issue where cookies were not parsed correctly when a user manually set a custom Host header. The MockRequest class now overrides the full URL construction to respect the custom host, ensuring the cookie jar matches the intended domain.

This commit updates the Flasky documentation theme to ensure code snippets remain hidden when hovering over links. It modifies the CSS rule in the flasky.css_t file to apply a higher specificity, preventing other styles from overriding the intended display behavior.
This release adds support for private SSL certificates to the requests library. The version number in the package initialization module is updated to 0.11.0 to reflect this new feature.

Updates the actions/checkout dependency from version 4.1.0 to 4.2.0 across the codeql-analysis, lint, and run-tests GitHub workflow files. This minor version bump ensures the CI pipelines use the latest stable release of the checkout action.

This commit updates the docstring for the `iter_content` method in the `Response` class within `requests/models.py`. It clarifies how the `chunk_size` parameter behaves when set to `None`, specifically distinguishing between streaming and non-streaming modes.

This commit cleans up the documentation structure for the Requests library. It moves the `request` function reference in the API docs to a more logical location and removes redundant section headers. It also adds missing anchor labels and a code comment to the user guide pages.

This commit removes official support for Python 3.9, updating the minimum required version to 3.10. It adjusts the test matrix in the GitHub Actions workflow and updates the project documentation to reflect this new baseline.

This commit enables the `keep_alive` setting in the default configuration and modifies the `Request.send` method to conditionally use connection pooling based on this flag. It allows users to disable persistent connections, though the implementation includes a debug print statement.

This commit fixes an issue in the `Session` class where merging cookies could fail or behave unexpectedly. It replaces the previous copy-based approach with a new `RequestsCookieJar` instance to safely combine session and request cookies.

This commit fixes a potential error in the `Request.curl` method within `requests/models.py` by ensuring the encoded data is not `None` before processing. It prevents the method from attempting to handle missing data, which could otherwise cause unexpected behavior when generating curl commands.

This commit removes redundant parentheses in the redirect handling loop within the `SessionRedirectMixin` class. It cleans up the code in the `resolve_redirects` method without altering the library's behavior.
This commit cleans up code style in the test server module. It removes the shebang line, fixes trailing whitespace, and updates the Server class to use super() for initialization.

This commit fixes the build process by removing an invalid command-line argument from the test execution step. The change updates the Makefile to ensure the test suite runs correctly without failing on unsupported options.

This commit adds unit tests to the requests library's test suite. It verifies that the `dotted_netmask` function correctly converts prefix lengths to netmasks and that `address_in_network` accurately checks if an IP belongs to a specified subnet.

This commit optimizes the `resolve_proxies` function in `requests/utils.py` by avoiding unnecessary computation. It now only evaluates the proxy bypass condition when the environment is trusted, improving performance for requests that do not require proxy resolution.

This commit fixes a bug in the PreparedRequest class where the Content-Length header was incorrectly set to a super object instead of a string. It also updates comments in the Session class to clarify the purpose of setting default parameters for request hooks.

This commit fixes a test failure in the test_utils module for Python 2.x environments. It corrects the encoding of a Unicode byte order mark in the TestGuessJSONUTF class to ensure the test data is handled properly.

This commit refactors the redirect handling logic in the `Session` class within `requests/sessions.py`. It removes debug print statements and ensures the initial response is correctly included in the history list when redirects occur. This fixes a bug where the first response was missing from the request history.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 2.2.0. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the package's initialization file to reflect the new release.

This commit updates the documentation for recommended packages and extensions by adding an image to the page. The change affects the `docs/community/recommended.rst` file, enhancing the visual presentation of the community resources section.

This commit modifies the `stream_decode_response_unicode` function in `requests/utils.py` to handle missing encoding headers gracefully. Instead of failing, it now yields raw data items directly when no encoding is specified, preventing errors during response processing.

This commit removes Python 3.3 from the Travis CI test matrix because the build environment for that version is broken. The change updates the .travis.yml configuration file to stop attempting to run tests on Python 3.3.

The `http_basic` function in `requests/auth.py` previously used the deprecated `base64` function, which could cause errors or incorrect encoding. This commit replaces it with the standard `b64encode` function to ensure reliable HTTP Basic authentication.

This commit removes the fallback logic in the `requests/certs.py` module that used a vendored certificate bundle when the `certifi` package was missing. It now strictly requires `certifi` to provide the default CA certificate bundle, eliminating the previous optional dependency behavior.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library within the requests package to use relative imports and reorganize exception handling. It moves specific error classes from the connectionpool module to a dedicated exceptions module, ensuring cleaner separation of concerns.

This commit modifies the `prepare_url` method in `requests/models.py` to remove only leading whitespace from URLs instead of stripping both ends. This change preserves trailing whitespace, which was already handled correctly, and updates the corresponding test to reflect the new behavior.
This commit adds a missing blank line to the test_requests.py file. It is a minor formatting adjustment that does not change any functional behavior or fix a bug.

This commit hides the internal `is_permanent_redirect` attribute from the public API documentation. It prevents users from seeing this private implementation detail in the generated docs for the `Response` class.

This release updates the Requests library to version 2.32.3, fixing a bug that prevented custom SSL contexts from working in subclasses. It also resolves an issue where the library failed to run on Python installations compiled without the ssl module.

This commit adds a new utility function, `dict_to_sequence`, to the `requests.utils` module. It converts dictionary-like objects into a sequence of key-value pairs for internal use. The change also removes an unused import from the same module.

This commit corrects documentation formatting and content in the user guide and developer notes. It fixes underline lengths for section headers and removes Python 2 string prefixes from code examples.

This commit reverts recent changes to the project's continuous integration configuration, restoring the previous state of the build pipelines. It affects the Azure Pipelines, Travis CI, and AppVeyor setup files, ensuring the original testing and deployment workflows are reinstated.

This commit updates the `Response.iter_lines` method in `requests/models.py` by changing a code comment from "XXX" to "TODO" and adding several blank lines for improved readability. It does not alter the functional behavior of the library.

This commit relaxes the version constraint for the charset_normalizer dependency in the project's configuration files. It allows any version from 2.0.0 up to, but not including, 3.0, replacing the previous strict pin to the 2.0.0 series.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 0.10.6. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the package's initialization file to reflect the new release.

This commit removes leftover debug print statements from the `RequestsCookieJar` class in `requests/cookies.py`. It cleans up the `get_dict` method, preventing unnecessary console output during cookie processing.
This release bumps the Requests library version to 0.8.5. It introduces the `Response.iter_lines` method, allowing users to efficiently process response data line by line.

This commit adds documentation for the `requests.session` module to the advanced user guide. It explains how the `Session` object persists parameters and manages cookies across multiple requests, including a usage example.

This commit adds a test case to the RequestsTestCase class in test_requests.py. It verifies that a Session correctly applies custom authentication headers to a request when using the prepare_request method.

This commit restores backward compatibility by moving the `json` parameter to the end of the argument lists in `Request.__init__` and `Session.request`. This prevents errors for users who relied on the previous parameter order when calling these methods.

This commit reverts a change in the `Request` class within `requests/models.py` that incorrectly decoded URL strings. It removes the logic that converted non-Unicode URLs to Unicode, restoring the previous behavior for handling URL inputs in the `_build_response` method.

This commit updates a broken hyperlink in the advanced user documentation. It replaces an outdated GitHub API reference with the current pagination guide URL. The change affects the `docs/user/advanced.rst` file.
This commit updates the project's README documentation by adding a blank line to the file. It makes no changes to code logic or user-facing behavior.

This commit cleans up the Sphinx documentation index by standardizing section underlines and renaming "Developer Documentation" to "Developer Guide." It also removes the automatic "Indices and tables" section from the main page.

This commit removes the `accept_gzip` configuration option from the `defaults` module and the `Request` class. It stops the library from automatically adding gzip encoding headers to requests, changing how users handle compressed responses.

This commit updates the project's README to wrap the logo and decorative images in links to external resources. It also refines the installation instructions to explicitly recommend using pipenv for installing the requests module.

This commit corrects the GitHub repository attribution in the documentation configuration. It updates the `html_theme_options` in `docs/conf.py` to point to the `requests` organization instead of a personal account, ensuring the star count displays correctly.

This commit removes the test for non-URL-encoded query strings and renames the combined query and data test to focus solely on post data. It clarifies the test suite's coverage for handling non-URL-encoded request bodies in the RequestsTestSuite.

This commit updates the project's README documentation to clarify the recommended method for sending JSON data. It modifies the introductory text to suggest using the `json` method as the modern approach for encoding request payloads.

Adds a test to verify that cookies are correctly set when a request receives a 301 redirect. This ensures the session properly captures cookie data during redirects. The test is added to the RequestsTestCase class.
This release restores the `requests.packages` namespace to ensure backward compatibility. Users no longer need to modify their code to handle this namespace, resolving previous import issues.

This commit improves the documentation for the RequestsCookieJar class in the requests module. It clarifies the performance characteristics of the __getitem__ method and refines the wording in docstrings for better readability.

This commit fixes a CSS layout error in the documentation sidebar by removing an incorrect flexbox property from custom.css. It also corrects the indentation of the call-to-action element in hacks.html to ensure proper rendering.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to use GitHub's public timeline as the example for making a GET request, replacing the previous httpbin.org example. It modifies the `docs/user/quickstart.rst` file to reflect this change in the user guide.

This commit removes the Pipenv dependency from the Makefile, simplifying the build and test commands to use standard Python tools directly. It eliminates the need for an initialization step and updates test, coverage, and documentation checks to run without the virtual environment wrapper.

This commit adds a public `get_policy` method to the `RequestsCookieJar` class, allowing users to access the current cookie policy instance. It updates the `copy` method to use this new accessor instead of directly accessing the private `_policy` attribute.

This commit refactors the Request class in requests/core.py to handle HTTP errors more robustly. It introduces a new _build_response method to centralize the creation of the internal response object, replacing inline logic within the send method.

This commit fixes import errors in the requests package by explicitly listing the attributes imported from the `__about__` module in `requests/__init__.py`. It also updates `requests/utils.py` to import the version string directly from `__about__` instead of the package root, ensuring consistent access to package metadata.

This commit updates the release history to clarify that the fix for header validation now rejects all non-string values, not just integers. It corrects the documentation in HISTORY.rst to accurately reflect the stricter type checking behavior.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar to reflect a change in project sponsorship. It replaces the previous acknowledgment of Linode with a new credit to the Government of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.

This commit removes the `cached` attribute from the `Response` class in `requests/models.py`. It also eliminates the logic in `Request.send` that previously set this flag based on whether the response content was stored locally.

This commit updates the documentation to remove references to the unsafe `r.raw` attribute for reading response data. It replaces examples using `r.raw` with the safer `iter_content` method in the API and advanced user guides.

This commit updates the project changelog to document the transition from IDNA2003 to IDNA2008 for internationalized domain names. It notes that this improvement is mandatory for .de domains and supports various other IDN formats.

This commit fixes a Python 3 compatibility issue in the `RequestsTestSuite` test class. It updates the `test_file_post_data` method to handle byte strings correctly, ensuring the test passes when file content is decoded to a string for comparison.

This commit updates the HTTPAdapter in requests/adapters.py to catch urllib3's InvalidHeader exception and re-raise it as a requests-specific InvalidHeader error. This ensures that responses with conflicting Content-Length headers trigger a clear, appropriate error instead of failing unexpectedly.

This release updates the requests library to version 0.8.4, fixing a prefetch bug and ensuring the license is included in installed versions. The version number is updated in the package initialization module, and minor string formatting adjustments are made in the setup script.
This commit adds Den Shabalin to the project's list of contributors. It updates the AUTHORS file to acknowledge their patches and suggestions.
The default user agent string now includes the operating system name and version. This change modifies the base headers in the requests defaults module to provide more detailed client information.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 2.9.1. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the package's initialization file to reflect the new release.

This release fixes a bug where malformed Content-Type header values caused inconsistent error handling in the requests library. It also corrects test cleanup to prevent unnecessary files from being left in temporary directories.

This commit updates the project documentation to reflect a higher download count for the Requests library. It changes the reported PyPI download total from 1.5 million to 2 million in the testimonials section of the index file.

This commit fixes a version detection bug in the setup.py module where the version string could be incorrectly matched if it appeared elsewhere in the file. It now ensures the version is only extracted from the start of a line, preventing false positives during package installation.

This commit updates the `rebuild_proxies` method in `requests/sessions.py` to respect the `ALL_PROXY` environment variable. It ensures that if a specific scheme proxy is not defined, the application falls back to the general `ALL_PROXY` setting for all requests.

This commit refactors the request handling logic to pass connection pool configurations directly through the Request and Session classes. It removes the explicit pool argument from the top-level request function and updates the internal send method to rely on the session's default pool manager.

This commit removes the "How to Contribute" section from the project's README file. It eliminates the previous instructions for new contributors regarding reading guides, checking issues, and forking the repository.

This commit adds documentation to the quickstart guide explaining the `r.json` property in the requests library. It describes how to decode JSON response content and notes that the property returns `None` if decoding fails.

This commit fixes a typo in the Makefile that prevented the coverage report from being generated correctly. It corrects the command-line flag for the XML report output, ensuring the build process runs as intended.

This commit adds a type annotation to the `hooks` attribute of the `Request` class in the `requests` library. It clarifies the expected data structure for request hooks, improving static type checking and code documentation without altering runtime behavior.

This commit adds tests to the TestRequests class in tests/test_requests.py to clarify when a CookieConflictError is raised. It verifies that duplicate cookie names are allowed across different domains but trigger an error when set on the same path.

This commit adds tests to the TestRequests class in tests/test_requests.py to verify that prepared requests can be serialized using pickle. It ensures that both standard requests and those containing file data remain functional after being unpickled and sent.

This commit introduces an optional eager mode that causes the Request class to raise errors immediately upon receiving a response. When enabled, the send method triggers status checks right away, allowing users to catch failures earlier in the request lifecycle.

This commit updates the `cookiejar_from_dict` function in `requests/cookies.py` and the `TestBaseMixin` class in `tests/test_requests.py` to support Python 3. It replaces the removed `iteritems` method with standard dictionary iteration, ensuring the library works correctly in Python 3 environments.

This commit updates the project documentation to clarify that the library supports HTTP/1.1 requests. It replaces the previous list of specific HTTP methods with a general statement in the README and documentation index.

Updates the actions/setup-python dependency from version 5.3.0 to 5.4.0 in the lint and test workflows. This minor version bump ensures the CI environment uses the latest stable release of the Python setup action.

This commit corrects a typo in the test method name within the RequestsTestSuite class in tests/test_requests.py. It renames the method from test_no_conent to test_no_content to ensure the test suite runs correctly.

This commit refactors the HTTPAdapter class in the requests library to improve code clarity. It updates the proxy manager creation logic and imports the to_native_string utility, streamlining how proxy configurations are handled.

This commit centralizes Python 2 and 3 compatibility imports for URL parsing and cookie handling within the requests/compat.py module. It removes redundant direct imports from requests/utils.py, ensuring consistent access to these standard library functions across different Python versions.

Adds a `basic_response_server` classmethod to the `Server` class in `testserver/server.py`. This new method creates a simple HTTP server that returns an empty 200 OK response, providing a lightweight testing utility. A corresponding test verifies the server's behavior.

This commit removes the redundant `cookies` parameter from the `resolve_redirects` method in `requests/sessions.py`. It ensures the method consistently uses the session's internal cookie jar instead of relying on an external argument, simplifying the `Session.send` implementation.

This change allows the `_encode_files` method in `requests.models` to accept `bytearray` objects as file inputs, alongside the previously supported `bytes` and `str` types. Users can now pass `bytearray` data directly when encoding files without needing to convert it first.
This commit updates the documentation for the urllib2 module to improve readability. It replaces a complex cross-reference directive with simple bold text when mentioning the module name.

This commit updates the project's documentation to include Native Instruments in the list of testimonials. It adds the company name and link to the index page, expanding the list of organizations that use the software.
This commit updates the project's history file to document the upcoming 0.3.3 release. It specifically notes the addition of request timeouts as a new feature.
Updates the project documentation to reflect that the library has been installed over 100,000 times from PyPI, replacing the previous figure of 80,000. This change appears in the main index file.
This commit adds a test to the RequestsTestSuite in tests/test_requests.py. It verifies that sending string data via the post function correctly sets the Content-Type header to text/plain.

This commit updates the project documentation to include Her Majesty's Government in the list of organizations that use the Requests library. The change modifies the testimonials section in the main index file to reflect this new user.

This commit embeds the chardet library directly into the requests package, removing the need for a separate external dependency. Users will no longer need to install chardet manually to use automatic character encoding detection. The change adds the full chardet module structure under requests/packages/chardet.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to improve cross-platform compatibility, specifically addressing import errors on systems like macOS where the select module lacks the poll function. It modifies the HTTPConnectionPool and HTTPResponse classes to handle these environment differences gracefully.
This commit adds a sticker purchase section to the documentation sidebar. It introduces a Gumroad button in the sidebar templates, allowing users to order stickers directly from the site.
This documentation update adds Runscope to the list of organizations using the Requests library. It also increases the reported PyPI download count from three million to five million.

This commit adds the `poster` package to the `requests` library's internal package namespace. It enables the library to import and utilize the `poster` module for handling multipart form data submissions.

This commit corrects the docstring for the `Response.json` method in the `requests` library. It clarifies that the method returns a decoded dictionary rather than raw JSON-encoded content, improving documentation accuracy for users.
