The test suite in test_requests.py now uses gunicorn to serve the HTTPBin application instead of the previous method. This change updates the server startup command and the target URL for the tests.

This commit adds a trailing newline to the end of the `iter_lines` method in the `Response` class within `requests/models.py`. It is a minor formatting change that does not alter the library's behavior or fix any user-facing bugs.

This release fixes a regression in the requests library where non-string types were incorrectly rejected in basic authentication parameters. The fix restores support for these types while marking the behavior as deprecated for future removal. The version number in the package initialization module is updated to 2.12.4.

This commit fixes an issue where the `requests.packages` module failed to expose attributes for its dependencies. The `requests/packages.py` module now correctly assigns imported packages to local variables, allowing users to access `urllib3`, `idna`, and `chardet` directly.
This commit pins the httpbin dependency to version 0.0.4 in the requirements file. It ensures the project uses a specific, stable version of the library rather than the latest available release.

This commit updates the continuous integration configuration and developer documentation to replace Make commands with the invoke tool. It removes Python 3.2 support and changes the test execution method from make to invoke.

Fixes the `dispatch` function in `requests/auth.py` to correctly handle authentication tuples. It now requires at least two elements and ensures the returned credentials are a tuple, preventing errors when processing auth data.

This commit corrects the installation instructions in the user documentation by adding the "L" flag to the curl commands. This ensures the downloaded archive retains its original filename instead of being saved with a generic name.

This commit fixes an issue in the `http_digest` function within `requests/auth.py` where the query string was omitted from the digest path calculation. By including the query parameters, the authentication process now correctly handles URLs with query strings, preventing potential authentication failures.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar templates to fix a broken link for the Linode sponsor and remove an outdated PayPal donation form. The changes affect the sidebarintro.html and sidebarlogo.html files, ensuring the sidebar displays accurate sponsorship information without the obsolete payment interface.

This commit updates the project's README to display the correct logo image. It replaces a broken or incorrect image link with the proper requests logo file, ensuring the documentation renders accurately for users.

This commit fixes an issue where the `timeout` parameter did not work correctly in safe mode, preventing the `Request` class from properly handling timeouts. It ensures that `Response` objects are generated correctly when exceptions are suppressed, and adds a test to verify that timeouts raise exceptions in normal mode and return blank responses in safe mode.

This commit adds category comments to the status code dictionary in the requests library. It organizes the HTTP status codes into informational, redirection, client error, and server error groups for better readability.

This commit updates the HTTPAdapter class to use the new urllib3 proxy API, replacing the deprecated ProxyManager with proxy_from_url. It ensures that proxy connections are correctly established when making requests through the get_connection method.

This commit simplifies the authentication logic in the `Request.prepare` method within `requests/models.py`. It removes redundant conditional checks by directly passing either the explicit auth or the embedded URL credentials to the preparation step.
This commit adds the omnijson library to the project's dependencies to support Python 2.5 compatibility. It updates the requirements file to include this new package alongside existing dependencies.

This commit cleans up docstrings in the TestRequests class within tests/test_requests.py. It corrects punctuation and adds a missing description for a test verifying that chunked uploads do not set a Content-Length header.

Adds a test case to the RequestsTestSuite in test_requests.py to verify that gzip-compressed HTTP responses are correctly decompressed. This ensures the library properly handles content encoding for users receiving compressed data.

This documentation update removes the recommendation to use the `ok` attribute for checking request success in the quickstart guide. It now advises users to use `raise_for_status()` or verify the `status_code` instead, reflecting changes in the library's API.

This commit adds a new test module to verify that the requests library can successfully establish HTTPS connections. The HTTPSTest class performs basic smoke tests to ensure that both standard and SSL-verified requests to a remote server return the expected success status.
This commit removes the sticker order button and associated script from the documentation sidebar. Users will no longer see the "Stickers!" section in the sidebar templates.
The CI configuration now runs the standard test suite instead of the coverage report. This change updates the build script in the Travis CI configuration file to execute the test target directly.

This commit adds a unit test for the `request` function in the `requests.api` module. It verifies that the function correctly handles various arguments, including timeout and redirect settings, by mocking its internal dependencies.

This commit updates the documentation for the `close` method in the `Response` class within `requests/models.py`. It clarifies that calling this method releases the connection to the pool and prevents further access to the underlying raw object.

This commit adds test cases for the `should_bypass_proxies` function in `requests.utils` to verify correct handling of Windows registry proxy overrides ending with semicolons. It also updates a comment in the source code to clarify the logic for filtering empty strings.

This commit updates the documentation for the Response class in requests/models.py to clarify that the content attribute can be bytes or unicode. It also initializes a new file-like object attribute for advanced usage and adjusts the content initialization to support documentation generation.

The `super_len` function in `requests/utils.py` now correctly calculates the length of in-memory stream objects like `BytesIO` and `cStringIO`. It handles cases where `fileno()` raises an error by falling back to the `getvalue` method to retrieve the data size.

This commit fixes an infinite recursion bug in HTTP Basic authentication where the library would loop forever on 401 errors. It introduces a custom handler in requests/core.py that disables the default retry reset mechanism and instead limits retries to one per request.

This commit updates the sidebar navigation links in the documentation templates to include explicit .html file extensions. This ensures that the links to the Quickstart and Advanced Usage pages resolve correctly in the rendered documentation.

This commit updates the documentation to correct the parameter name for deferring response body downloads from "prefetch" to "stream". It clarifies the behavior of the Response and Session classes in the user guides.

This commit adjusts the vertical spacing of the "Requests" button in the documentation sidebar. It moves the button element within the sidebarintro and sidebarlogo templates to improve layout padding.

This commit adds a threaded test to the RequestsTestCase in test_requests.py to verify that HTTPDigestAuth remains thread-safe. It ensures that concurrent requests using a shared session correctly generate authorization headers without race conditions.

This commit updates the README.md file to adjust the spacing of decorative emoji characters. It replaces a single line of emojis with a version that includes additional non-breaking spaces to improve visual alignment.

This commit updates outdated GitHub links in the documentation to point to the correct repositories under new user accounts. It fixes broken references for the betamax, urllib3, and grequests projects in the community and advanced user guides.

This commit updates the project documentation to reflect current support levels and remove outdated information. It adds the BaseAdapter class to the API reference, updates the FAQ to list Python 3.5 and PyPy, and removes the ScraperWiki integration section.

This commit adds tests for the CaseInsensitiveDict class to verify its behavior when comparing against unrelated objects, copying, and string representation. It ensures the class correctly returns NotImplemented for equality checks with non-dict types and that copy and repr methods work as expected.

This commit updates the copyright year from 2013 to 2014 in the project's license file and documentation configuration. It ensures the legal attribution and documentation metadata reflect the current year.

This commit improves the default values for the `Request` and `Response` classes in `requests/models.py`. It ensures that `params` defaults to an empty dictionary and `cookies` defaults to an empty dictionary instead of `None`, preventing potential errors when accessing these attributes.

This release fixes a security vulnerability where proxy credentials were incorrectly forwarded to destination servers during HTTPS redirects. The update addresses this issue in the Requests library, ensuring sensitive authentication headers are not leaked to unintended endpoints.

This commit adds a unit test to the RequestsAPIUnitTests class to verify that the delete function correctly passes keyword arguments to the underlying request method. It ensures that parameters like headers, cookies, and proxies are handled as expected during HTTP delete operations.

This commit updates the contributing documentation to clarify that model methods are typically, rather than usually, exempt from the docstring requirement. The change refines the wording in the contributing guide to improve precision.

This commit initializes the changelog for version 2.0, documenting upcoming API changes. It notes that header keys will now be native strings and that proxy URLs require an explicit scheme. The entry also introduces new methods for `PreparedRequest` and `Session` objects.

This commit updates the project documentation to correctly format the reference to the urllib3 library. It also refines the description of the library's design goals to emphasize elegance and approachability. The changes are located in the main documentation index file.

This commit applies Prettier formatting to the requests/async.py and requests/core.py modules. It standardizes whitespace and import spacing for the Request, Response, and AuthManager classes without altering their functional behavior.
This commit adds a new image file for the DeepMind Korea office to the project's external assets directory. It introduces the visual resource without modifying any existing code or functionality.

This commit adds a `close` method to the `Session` class in `requests/sessions.py`. It allows users to explicitly close all connection adapters associated with a session, ensuring proper resource cleanup.

The installation documentation now points to the new GitHub organization for the requests library. Users cloning the repository or downloading the tarball will use the updated URLs instead of the old personal account links.

This commit adds support for handling cookies in the requests library. It updates the Request class to parse and store cookies from server responses, while temporarily disabling the previous cookie conversion logic in the API module.

This commit refactors the requests package by moving core classes like Request, Response, and AuthManager from core.py to models.py. It introduces a new api.py module to expose the main HTTP methods, streamlining the public interface for users.

This commit removes the `__about__.py` file and updates the package initialization to stop importing version metadata from it. This change simplifies the versioning structure for the `requests` library by consolidating version information into other modules.

This commit adds a test to the TestRequests class in tests/test_requests.py to verify that chunked uploads do not include a Content-Length header. It ensures that when data is sent as a generator, the request correctly uses Transfer-Encoding instead of specifying a fixed content length.

This commit refactors the `Request.send` method in `requests/models.py` to properly handle authentication. It ensures that if no explicit credentials are provided, the system checks for `.netrc` authentication when the environment is trusted. The change also standardizes how basic HTTP authentication tuples are processed before applying them to the request.

This commit corrects a capitalization error in the docstring for the `send` method within the `Request` class in `requests/models.py`. It changes the return value description from "false" to "False" to ensure proper documentation formatting.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to replace an example using httpbin.org with one using github.com. It corrects the SSL verification demonstration to use a domain with valid certificates, ensuring the example accurately reflects successful HTTPS requests.

This commit updates the development philosophy documentation to accurately reflect the current project structure. It clarifies Kenneth Reitz's responsibilities within the Requests project, specifically noting his role in the library's presentation alongside its technical direction.

This commit adds a warning to the requests library when an older version of the cryptography package is detected. The new `_check_cryptography` function alerts users that versions prior to 1.3.4 may cause performance slowdowns.

This commit moves the conversion of the HTTP method to a built-in string from the top-level request function to the Session class. This ensures the method is properly handled within the session context. A new test case verifies that unicode method names work correctly.

This commit updates the development documentation to reflect the new testing workflow. It replaces instructions for installing gunicorn and httpbin with a single command to install py.test dependencies. The guide now directs users to run the test suite using py.test instead of the previous Makefile targets.

This commit corrects a typo in the project's changelog, changing "UnicodeDecodeErrors" to the proper singular form "UnicodeDecodeError." It ensures the release history accurately describes the reduction in decoding errors on Python 2.

This commit repositions a comment within the HTTPAdapter class in the requests/adapters.py module to improve code clarity. It clarifies why the proxy_manager attribute is not included in the pickling attributes due to lambda function limitations. No functional behavior or bug fixes are introduced.

This commit updates the project's README to list new features, including redirection history, recursion fixes, and Unicode URL support. It also simplifies the roadmap section by removing outdated items.

This commit removes the NoseXUnit plugin from the test suite and dependencies, replacing it with standard nose xunit output. It also adds a new Makefile target to generate a pyflakes violation report.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar to replace the outdated Gratipay donation link with a new "Buy Requests Pro" button. It modifies the sidebar templates to direct users to the Gumroad store for supporting the project.

This change allows users to pass custom authentication handler objects to the `AuthObject` class in `requests/core.py`. Previously, only the four built-in string-based handlers were supported, but now any valid handler instance can be used directly.

This commit updates the test suite to handle the removal of SNIMissingWarning in urllib3 2.0. It prevents import errors in tests/__init__.py by catching the exception when the warning class is unavailable. This ensures the test suite remains compatible with newer urllib3 versions.

This commit fixes a typo in the docstring of the `resolve_proxies` function within the `requests` utility module. It corrects the phrase "such a NO_PROXY" to "such as NO_PROXY" for clarity. No functional behavior is changed.

This commit removes the optional gevent dependency from the package's setup configuration. It eliminates the "async" extra, which previously allowed users to install gevent for the requests.async API. The change simplifies the installation process by removing this non-required dependency.

This commit removes the bundled poster package from the requests library. It deletes the module's files, including the multipart encoding logic and streaming HTTP handlers. Users will no longer have access to these specific upload utilities within the requests distribution.
This commit ensures the license file is included in the generated wheel package. It adds a metadata section to the setup.cfg file to specify the license file, improving package compliance.
This documentation update clarifies that setting session proxies may be overridden by environment variables. It adds a warning to the advanced user guide to prevent unexpected proxy behavior.

This commit standardizes the module docstrings and coding comments across the Requests library and its test suite. It ensures consistent formatting and naming conventions for documentation headers in files like requests/api.py and requests/compat.py.
This commit updates the API documentation to include the missing `patch` function. It ensures the `patch` method is properly listed alongside other HTTP request methods in the `docs/api.rst` file.

This commit pins the httpbin dependency to version 0.4.0 in the requirements file. This ensures the project uses a specific, stable version of the HTTP testing server, preventing unexpected behavior from automatic updates.

This commit removes the custom PyTest command class from setup.py, which previously allowed running tests via the setuptools test command. Users will no longer be able to invoke tests using that specific legacy interface.

This commit fixes a bug in the `proxy_bypass_registry` function within the `requests` module where empty strings in the proxy override list caused the function to incorrectly return true for all URLs. By filtering out these empty values, the function now correctly evaluates proxy bypass rules on Windows systems.

This commit removes the "danger mode" feature from the `Request` class in `requests/models.py`. Previously, enabling this mode would automatically raise an exception for failed HTTP responses during the `send` method. Users will no longer see automatic error handling triggered by this specific configuration flag.
This commit removes Readability from the list of organizations using the project in the documentation. It updates the index page to reflect that Readability is no longer a listed user.
This commit adds Michael Newman to the project's list of contributors. It updates the AUTHORS.rst file to include his name and email address under the "Patches and Suggestions" section.

The `get_unicode_from_response` function in `requests/utils.py` now correctly returns a Unicode string instead of a byte string. This ensures that response content is properly decoded for Python 2 compatibility.

This commit updates all references to the legacy PyPI domain to the new pypi.org address across the project. It ensures that links in the README, documentation, and configuration files point to the current package index, preventing broken links for users.

This commit expands the unicode multipart post test in the RequestsTestCase class. It adds new test cases to verify that the library correctly handles both string and byte-encoded data fields when sending multipart form requests.

This commit refactors the `Request.send` method in `requests/models.py` to handle network timeouts as standard errors. It consolidates exception handling to ensure `socket.timeout` instances are properly converted to `Timeout` objects, improving consistency in error reporting.

This commit adds a test to verify how the requests library handles redirects when the response incorrectly includes a gzip content-encoding header. The new test case, located in the RequestsTestCase class, ensures the session correctly processes such malformed responses.

This commit updates the `requests` library's `adapters` module to import specific exception classes and utilities from `urllib3`. It ensures that the adapter correctly references these dependencies, likely resolving import errors or missing attribute issues when handling HTTP requests.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library from 0.9.3 to 0.10.0. It modifies the `__version__` variable in the `requests/__init__.py` module to reflect the new release.
This release updates the version number to 2.16.5 and improves the output of the `requests.help` module. Users will notice better diagnostic information when running the help command.

This commit updates the project's documentation to add Twilio as a sponsor. It acknowledges their financial contribution to the 2018 Requests 3.0 fundraiser, noting that they matched a previous donation from Slack.

This commit updates the README.rst file by adding a decorative line of emojis to the installation instructions. It does not change any functional behavior or fix bugs, serving only as a cosmetic addition to the project documentation.

This commit fixes a gevent compatibility issue in the `Request` class within `requests/core.py`. It restructures the `_get_opener` method to correctly handle authentication and cookie processing, ensuring the request opener is built properly when these features are enabled.

This commit refactors the `iter_content` method in the `Response` class of the `requests` module. It replaces a manual loop that yields chunks with a `yield from` expression to delegate iteration directly to the underlying stream. This simplifies the code without changing the observable behavior for users.

This commit updates the development requirements to allow the latest 9.x series of the pytest testing framework. It removes the previous version cap that blocked 9.x releases, ensuring the project can utilize newer features and fixes.

This commit updates the `setup.py` file to remove the upper version bound from the `python_requires` specification. It aligns the package configuration with Python Packaging Authority guidelines, which discourage restricting future major versions. This change ensures the package remains compatible with upcoming Python releases without requiring manual updates.

This commit merges the upstream develop branch into the local develop branch. It synchronizes the local codebase with the latest changes from the remote repository. No specific functional changes or bug fixes are described in this merge.

This commit fixes a bug where unpickling an HTTPAdapter instance failed due to a missing proxy_manager attribute. The HTTPAdapter class now initializes this attribute as an empty dictionary during the unpickling process to ensure successful restoration.

This commit updates the documentation for the `request` function in `requests/api.py` to clarify that the `data` parameter accepts a list of tuples. This change informs users that they can pass duplicate field names in form-encoded requests, a feature previously undocumented.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to correct a typo in the session attributes list and clarify that Requests supports concurrent rather than non-blocking requests. It also adds a note explaining the throttling parameter for the map function.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar and the recommended packages page to include extensions in the title. It removes a separate link to the Certifi CA bundle, consolidating the reference into the main "Recommended Packages and Extensions" entry.

This commit fixes a bug in the HTTPAdapter.send method where retry logic was incorrectly configured. It now properly instantiates a Retry object with read retries disabled, ensuring that connection issues are handled as intended without unexpected read retries.

In the `requests/cookies.py` module, the `MockRequest` class now uses a property decorator for the `unverifiable` attribute instead of a custom `__getattr__` method. This change simplifies attribute access by directly exposing the result of the `is_unverifiable` method.

This commit modifies the `get_netrc_auth` function in `requests/utils.py` to improve how it locates and parses netrc files. It refactors the logic for finding the netrc path and handling authentication data, likely to fix issues with file detection or parsing errors.

Updates the actions/setup-python dependency from version 5.1.0 to 5.2.0 in the lint and test workflows. This minor version bump ensures the CI environment uses the latest stable release of the Python setup action.

This commit corrects formatting errors in the project's release history documentation. It fixes broken line continuations and a factual inaccuracy regarding the chardet library in the HISTORY.rst file.
This commit removes an embedded image from the project's main documentation page. The change updates the index.rst file to clean up the layout by deleting the reference to an external photo.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar for certifi to include a link to the Requests-Toolbelt project. It adds a new list item and a horizontal rule to the sidebar template, improving navigation for users exploring related tools.

This commit updates the test suite in test_requests.py to replace unstable external URLs with more reliable endpoints like httpbin.org and github.com. It ensures that tests for HTTP requests and user agent verification continue to function correctly by targeting consistent services.

This commit removes outdated, commented-out code from the Session class in requests/sessions.py. It cleans up the initialization process by deleting obsolete lines related to cookie handling and argument mapping. The change improves code clarity without altering the library's functional behavior.

This commit removes the direct git dependency on the oauthlib library from the project's requirements file. This change likely addresses installation issues or simplifies dependency management by relying on a standard package index instead of a specific repository branch.

This commit introduces a new utility function, `to_key_val_list`, to standardize how key-value pairs are processed from various input types. It refactors the `Request` and `Session` classes to use this helper, eliminating repetitive logic for handling proxies, headers, and parameters.

This commit updates the project's README to include a contributor badge. The badge links to the GitHub contributors graph, providing a visual indicator of the number of people who have contributed to the codebase.

This commit updates the README.md file to correct a typo in the documentation link. It changes the display text from "2.python-requests.org" to "//2.python-requests.org" to better reflect the URL structure.

This commit updates the documentation for the requests library to remove outdated references to Python 2 support. It clarifies that the chardet library is no longer a mandatory dependency, as the library now relies on charset-normalizer for encoding detection.

This commit removes a redundant sentence from the quickstart introduction in the documentation. It clarifies the text by eliminating the assumption that the user has already installed the library, which is covered in a separate section.

This commit fixes failing doctests in the requests package by correcting expected output types and clarifying documentation examples in modules like requests.api and requests.models. It also enables doctest execution in the test suite by adding the --doctest-modules flag to pytest.ini.

This commit fixes an issue in the HTTPAdapter.send method where the original exception was not properly re-raised during error handling. Users may have previously seen a generic error instead of the specific underlying exception when a request failed.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation for the requests library to clarify how sessions handle default data. It corrects the example for setting authentication and headers by showing that these should be assigned to session object properties rather than passed as constructor arguments.

This commit removes temporary testing scripts and data files from the repository. It cleans up the codebase by deleting ad-hoc files used for manual debugging, such as t.py and test, which are not part of the main application logic.
This commit adds blank lines to the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to improve code readability. It does not change any functional behavior or fix a bug.

This commit adds a test to the RequestsTestSuite in test_requests.py that verifies the availability of standard HTTP methods and session objects. It ensures that users can access core request functions like get, post, and head without errors.

This commit removes outdated commented-out code from the `Request.send` method in `requests/models.py`. It adds placeholder logic to handle file, data, and cookie attributes, though the specific actions are currently empty.

This commit updates the README and FAQ documentation to replace outdated GitHub API examples with httpbin.org endpoints for basic authentication. It also removes specific download statistics and dependency counts from the project description.

This commit refactors URL and parameter encoding logic by moving it from the Request class to standalone utility functions. It removes the HTTPError import from the models module and updates the Request initialization to use the new encode_params utility.

This commit adds Sphinx as a setup requirement to enable documentation building and updates the API documentation to demonstrate proper logging configuration. It also modifies the .gitignore file to exclude build directories and egg files from version control.

This commit corrects a spelling error in the documentation for the `_encode_files` method within the `RequestEncodingMixin` class. It changes the word "abritrary" to "arbitrary" in the docstring, ensuring accurate documentation for the `requests` library.

This commit updates the `should_bypass_proxies` function in `requests/utils.py` to correctly handle plain IP addresses in the `no_proxy` setting. Previously, only CIDR notation was recognized, causing valid plain IP entries to be ignored. Now, the function bypasses the proxy when the target IP matches a plain IP entry in the configuration.

This commit cleans up the documentation build configuration by removing obsolete CSS styles and template files. It also adds internationalization wrappers to the Sphinx configuration to support translated documentation.

This commit adds optional Server Name Indication support for Python 2 users. It automatically enables SNI in the requests library if the ndg-httpsclient and pyopenssl packages are installed, improving TLS compatibility.

This commit updates the project's tagline in the README to describe the library as "simple, yet elegant" instead of "elegant & simple." It refines the marketing copy to better reflect the library's design philosophy.

This commit ensures that request data is preserved when following redirects, preventing data loss during HTTP redirect chains. It modifies the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to pass the original data payload through the `_build_response` method.

This commit adds a test to verify that the requests library correctly handles standard Python cookie jars, not just its own custom implementation. It ensures that a generic cookie jar can be assigned to a session and that cookies are properly sent with requests.

This commit updates the test for sending bytes and bytearray objects with files to use string input instead of a float. The change ensures the test correctly validates the behavior of the `test_can_send_bytes_bytearray_objects_with_files` method within the `RequestsTestCase` class.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Session` class where loading `.netrc` credentials would override explicit authentication settings. It ensures that environment-based authentication is only applied if no other auth is explicitly provided, preserving user-defined credentials.

This release updates the certificate bundle and fixes several regressions introduced in version 2.8.0. It ensures the `json` parameter is respected in the PreparedRequest flow and corrects Unicode method name handling on Python 2. Additionally, it restores proper error handling for connection timeouts.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the README documentation where a code example was missing an opening apostrophe. The correction ensures the example Python code is valid and copy-pasteable for users.
This commit updates the test target in the Makefile to remove the color output flag from the nosetests command. It simplifies the test execution process for the requests module.

This commit restructures the test suite by moving tests into a dedicated `tests` package and updating the Makefile to run them. It introduces shared fixtures and compatibility helpers to support the new test organization.

This commit adds the HTTP 208 status code to the requests library's status code definitions. It maps the code to the label "already_reported" in the status_codes module, ensuring the library correctly identifies this specific response status.

This commit adds a unit test to verify that the `max_retries` parameter is correctly passed to the underlying HTTP connection pool. It ensures that when a user specifies a retry limit in a request, that value is properly forwarded to the `urlopen` method.

This commit fixes a crash in the requests module that occurred when urllib3 reported a version with only two components. It ensures the version string is padded with a zero before parsing, preventing errors during the library's initialization.

The `unquote_unreserved` function in `requests/utils.py` no longer suppresses `ValueError` exceptions during URI decoding. This change ensures that invalid percent-encoding sequences raise errors instead of being silently ignored, allowing developers to detect malformed input.

This commit updates the `requests` package to use a relative import for the `core` module instead of an absolute one. This change ensures the package functions correctly when installed in different environments or when the parent directory is not on the Python path.

Adds a decorative image to the "How to Help" section of the developer documentation. This update modifies the `docs/dev/todo.rst` file to include a visual element for the project's contribution guidelines.

This commit updates the installation documentation to use an HTTPS URL instead of the deprecated git protocol for cloning the repository. This change ensures users can successfully clone the project without encountering connection errors due to blocked git ports.

This commit replaces the chardet dependency with the charade library within the requests package. It updates the internal character encoding detection module to use the new implementation, ensuring continued functionality for identifying text encodings.

The Request class now accepts HTTP Basic Auth credentials as a two-element tuple, providing a convenient shorthand for authentication. This change allows users to pass username and password directly without explicitly instantiating an auth object.

The `patch` function in `requests/api.py` now explicitly passes an empty string as the default data argument to the underlying request handler. This ensures consistent behavior when no data is provided, preventing potential issues with default parameter handling.

This release updates the redirect handling behavior so that POST requests follow up with a GET request, matching standard browser behavior. It also introduces a new strict_mode configuration option to disable this updated redirect logic.

This commit updates the project's philosophy documentation to rename the "Benevolent Dictator for Life" role to "Benevolent Dictator." It also corrects a missing newline at the end of the file in the `docs/dev/philosophy.rst` module.

This commit fixes a crash in the `Request` class when sending POST data that is not a dictionary. Previously, the code assumed the data was a dict and failed on other types. It now correctly handles non-dict data before attempting to process dictionary items.
This commit updates the project's test dependencies to require version 2.7 or higher of the pytest framework. It ensures that the testing environment uses a compatible version of the tool.

This commit improves the documentation for the `requests.status_codes` module by adding a descriptive docstring that lists all available status code names. It also prevents internal initialization variables from leaking into the module scope, which previously cluttered the interactive help output.

This commit removes unused imports from the requests library's adapters, auth, models, and utils modules. It cleans up the codebase by eliminating unnecessary dependencies, such as removing the unused `to_native_string` import from the adapters module.

This commit fixes a typo in the default port configuration for HTTPS connections within the urllib3 pool manager. Users relying on the default port for secure requests will now correctly connect to port 443 instead of the erroneous 433.

This commit refactors the `requests.utils` module by extracting the header parsing logic from `get_encoding_from_headers` into a new module-level function named `_parse_content_type_header`. This change improves code organization and allows for more robust handling of content type headers. The commit also adds specific unit tests to verify the behavior of the new parsing function.

This commit adds initial PyCharm project configuration files to the repository. It sets up the project structure and specifies Python 3.5 as the interpreter. These changes support local development environments and do not alter application behavior.

This commit fixes an issue where the Response.text property failed to strip UTF-8 byte order marks from response content. By forcing the use of the utf-8-sig codec when the encoding is set to UTF-8, the library now correctly removes the BOM, preventing it from appearing in the returned text.

This commit adds a MANIFEST.in file to ensure the project's history, readme, and license files are included in source distributions. It addresses a packaging issue where these essential files were previously missing from the built package.
This commit updates the copyright year in the project's license file from 2016 to 2017. It ensures the legal documentation reflects the current year of maintenance.

Adds a `send` method to the `Session` class in `requests/sessions.py`. This method accepts a prepared request and delegates the actual transmission to the request object itself, providing a direct interface for sending requests within a session.
This commit updates the README to use specific code block directives for Python console and Bash commands. This change enables proper syntax highlighting for these sections in rendered documentation.

This commit updates the User-Agent header generation in the requests defaults module to use percent-style string formatting instead of the format method. This change ensures compatibility with Python 2.5, which does not support the newer formatting syntax.

This commit refactors URL authentication handling in the `requests` library by moving the extraction of credentials from the URL into the `PreparedRequest.prepare_auth` method. It ensures that `Request.prepare` correctly passes the URL to the preparation step, allowing the library to automatically apply embedded authentication when no explicit auth is provided.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar by replacing PNG images with JPG files for the logo and sidebar graphics. It also adjusts the sidebar template to reference the new image formats, ensuring the documentation site displays the correct assets.

This commit updates the bundled CA root certificates in the requests library to the latest Mozilla set. It replaces the outdated certificate data in the cacert.pem file to ensure secure connections use current trust anchors.

This commit updates the documentation index by adding an image to the project description. It modifies the `docs/index.rst` file to include a visual element for users viewing the main documentation page.

This commit corrects the documentation for the `Session.request` method in the `requests` library. It replaces inaccurate parameter descriptions with the correct `stream` parameter, which controls whether response content is downloaded immediately.

This commit updates the documentation for custom header precedence in the quickstart guide. It clarifies that Authorization headers are overridden when credentials are provided via the auth parameter or a .netrc file.
Adds a Konami code easter egg to the documentation site. The new Konami class detects the classic button sequence on both keyboard and touch inputs to trigger a hidden feature.

The `merge_cookies` function in `requests/cookies.py` now returns a new cookie jar instead of modifying the original one, preventing unintended side effects. The `Session` class in `requests/sessions.py` was updated to use this new method when preparing requests.

This commit fixes an import error in the `requests` package by changing the vendored `pyopenssl` import to a relative path. Users will no longer encounter import failures when the library is installed in specific environments.

This commit fixes a test failure in new environments where the import machinery broke when running `python setup.py test`. It modifies `setup.py` to parse the version number directly from `requests/__init__.py` using a regular expression instead of importing the `requests` package. This prevents the `VendorAlias` logic from interfering with the test execution.
This commit updates the documentation to correct the phrasing of a testimonial. It changes the description from "a Federal US Institution" to "a U.S. Federal Institution" in the main index file.

This commit updates the project's README documentation to reflect modern Python syntax by removing the print statement from an example. It also adds a new section describing the HTTP Authentication Registry feature.
This commit removes an outdated image from the header of the advanced usage documentation. It cleans up the presentation of the `docs/user/advanced.rst` file by deleting the external image reference.

This commit updates the default HTTP headers in the requests library to remove the "identity" encoding option. It modifies the base headers configuration in the defaults module to prioritize gzip, deflate, and compress encodings by default.

This patch fixes a TypeError raised by the HTTPConnectionPool class when handling read timeouts on Python 2.7. The _raise_timeout method now safely handles the exception to prevent the request from failing unexpectedly.

This documentation update clarifies that users may need to manually set the Connection header to keep-alive to prevent servers from closing connections. It notes that while major browsers set this header by default, Python's urllib does not, which can affect connection persistence.

This commit fixes import failures for built-in modules on Python 2 by ensuring the VendorAlias import hook takes precedence over other third-party hooks. It modifies the requests packages module to insert the alias at the start of the system meta path, preventing incorrect module resolution attempts.

This documentation update clarifies that method-level parameters, such as cookies, are not persisted across requests when using a session. It explains that users must manually manage session cookies to ensure they are sent with subsequent requests. The changes are located in the API and advanced user guides.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to use the `r.text` attribute instead of the deprecated `r.content` attribute. It ensures that the examples correctly demonstrate how to access the decoded response body in the Requests library.
This commit updates the project's README documentation. It increases the font size of a specific text element to make it more prominent.

This commit updates the project history to note that exception handling was removed from the dispatch_hook function. This change ensures that errors are no longer silently ignored during the dispatch process, allowing them to propagate as expected.

This commit fixes a naming conflict in the test suite by importing the urllib3 Timeout class with an alias. It prevents the test module from accidentally shadowing the requests library's own Timeout class, ensuring that timeout tests correctly reference the underlying urllib3 implementation.

This commit fixes a documentation error in the quickstart guide where a POST request was incorrectly shown for demonstrating redirection. It corrects the example to use a HEAD request, ensuring the documentation accurately reflects the intended behavior.

This commit adds a deprecation notice to the `session` function in the `requests` module. It informs users that the lowercase `session()` method is deprecated since version 1.0.0 and that they should use the `Session` class instead for new code.

This commit cleans up the `unquote_unreserved` function in `requests/utils.py` by removing a redundant docstring and replacing a broad exception handler with a specific `ValueError` catch. This change improves code clarity and ensures only expected decoding errors are handled.
This commit removes the deprecated OAuth1 authentication class from the requests.auth module. Users relying on this specific legacy authentication method will no longer be able to use it.

This commit prevents the HTTPAdapter from attempting to parse a proxy URL when none is provided. It fixes a potential error in the request_url method by adding a check to ensure the proxy value exists before processing.

This commit updates the documentation in the advanced user guide to clarify the usage of the keep-alive connection header. It corrects the grammar and refines the explanation to note that manually setting this header is rarely necessary and does not guarantee the server will keep the connection open.

The `guess_json_utf` function in `requests/utils.py` previously failed to correctly identify UTF-32 big-endian data by its byte order mark. This fix corrects the detection logic so that UTF-32 big-endian content is properly recognized, ensuring accurate encoding handling for JSON responses.

This commit updates the CodeQL security analysis workflow to use version 3.30.0 of the github/codeql-action. It ensures the automated code scanning process runs with the latest minor release, incorporating recent improvements and fixes from the upstream project.

This commit updates the proxy bypass logic in `requests/utils.py` to support Windows registry settings without requiring DNS lookups. It ensures the `proxy_bypass` function correctly handles Windows-specific configurations, improving how the library determines when to bypass proxies on that platform.
This commit adds Nick Chadwick to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS.rst file. It updates the project's credit list to acknowledge his patches and suggestions.

This commit adds support for multipart file uploads to the Request class in requests/models.py. It allows users to send files alongside form data by encoding the request body using the encode_multipart_formdata function.

This commit fixes a test in the TestRequests class that was previously skipped, ensuring the hook correctly receives request arguments. It updates the test to use a Session object to properly prepare and send the request, resolving the execution issue.
This commit corrects a grammatical typo in the community support documentation. It changes the phrasing from "a questions" to "questions" in the introductory sentence of the support guide.

This commit updates documentation and code comments to use the standard spelling "Google App Engine" instead of "AppEngine." It clarifies the naming convention in the project's development notes and the `get_netrc_auth` function within the `requests` utility module.

This commit removes a debug print statement from the `iter_content` method in the `Response` class within `requests/models.py`. It eliminates unwanted console output that previously displayed each item yielded by the content generator.
This commit bumps the library version to 0.5.1 in the requests/core.py module. It also updates the .gitignore file to include itself and ensures the file ends with a newline.

This commit updates the API and quickstart documentation to clarify that header values must be strings. It notes that stricter enforcement of this rule began in version 2.11.0 and advises users to avoid passing unicode header values when possible.

This commit corrects a grammatical typo in the docstring of the `address_in_network` function within `requests/utils.py`. It changes "on IP" to "an IP" to improve the clarity of the documentation for users checking if an IP address belongs to a specific network subnet.

This commit updates the copyright year in the documentation configuration to use Roman numerals instead of standard digits. The change modifies the copyright string in the `docs/conf.py` file, altering the displayed year from 2017 to MMXVII.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` now uses a context manager to ensure the session is closed even if an exception occurs. This prevents open sockets from triggering resource warnings or appearing as memory leaks during error handling.
This commit adds Rob Madole to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS file. It updates the project's credit list to acknowledge his patches and suggestions.
This commit fixes a bug where response hooks were executed multiple times during a request. It modifies the Session class in requests/sessions.py to ensure hooks are dispatched only once.

This commit updates the contributing documentation to clarify that all functions, methods, and classes must include docstrings. It notes that object data model methods, such as `__repr__`, are typically exempt from this requirement.

This commit introduces a new ConnectionError exception to the requests library for handling connection failures. It replaces the previously defined AuthenticationError class within the exceptions module.

This commit removes unnecessary blank lines and fixes indentation in the `unicode_from_html` function within `requests/utils.py`. It cleans up the code structure without altering the module's behavior or functionality.

This commit adds a unit test to the RequestsAPIUnitTests class to verify that the requests.patch function correctly passes keyword arguments to the underlying request method. It ensures that parameters like data, headers, and timeout are handled as expected during a patch operation.

This commit adds a migration guide to the API documentation, detailing key changes between version 0.x and 1.x. It explains that the Response.json attribute is now a method and that the Session class no longer accepts initialization parameters.

This commit fixes a bug in the `PreparedRequest` class where copying a request object incorrectly shared the same header dictionary instance. By creating a copy of the headers, the `copy` method now ensures that modifications to the new object do not unintentionally affect the original request.
This commit updates the project's README documentation. It adds an empty paragraph tag to adjust the layout and spacing of the text.

The `is_ipv4_network` function in `requests/utils.py` is renamed to `is_valid_cidr` and now performs stricter validation of CIDR notation. This ensures that proxy configurations in the `no_proxy` environment variable correctly reject invalid network masks.

This commit fixes an import error in the requests exceptions module by updating the source of the BaseHTTPError class. It changes the import to use the standard urllib3 package directly instead of a deprecated internal path, ensuring the library loads correctly.

The `set_environ` function in `requests/utils.py` previously swallowed exceptions when restoring environment variables, preventing users from seeing underlying errors. This fix ensures that exceptions raised during the restoration process are properly propagated to the caller.

This commit streamlines the project's test setup by removing Pipenv dependencies and switching to standard requirements files. It updates the Makefile to run tests and coverage checks directly, eliminating the need for virtual environment wrappers.

This commit updates the AUTHORS.rst file to reflect Kenneth Reitz's new role as the "reluctant Keeper of the Master Crystal." It removes his previous title and adjusts the introductory text to state that Requests was lovingly created by him.

This commit fixes a bug in the `PreparedRequest` class where requests with generator bodies incorrectly sent a `Content-Length` header of "None". It ensures the header is only set when a valid length can be determined, preventing malformed HTTP requests.

Adds tests to the low-level test suite verifying that the digest authentication 401 counter resets correctly after a successful authentication followed by a redirect. These tests ensure the 401 challenge is not resent unnecessarily during subsequent requests.

This commit adds a GitHub Actions workflow to automatically run linting checks on every push and pull request. It ensures code style consistency by executing pre-commit hooks in a continuous integration environment.

The HTTPDigestAuth class in requests/auth.py now supports SHA-256 and SHA-512 hash algorithms for digest authentication. This allows users to authenticate against servers that require these stronger hashing methods, which were previously unsupported.

This commit fixes a test configuration issue in the `tests/test_requests.py` module. It ensures the `HTTPBIN_URL` environment variable is only set on Windows systems if it is not already defined, preventing unintended overrides on other platforms.

This commit updates the oreos package to explicitly import the dict_from_string function from the core module. It replaces a broad wildcard import with a specific one, ensuring only the intended utility is exposed to users.

This commit updates the Makefile to fix the Travis CI build process. It replaces the previous dependency installation steps with `pipenv lock` and `pipenv install --dev`, and ensures tests run within the virtual environment using `pipenv run`.

The ProxyManager class in the urllib3 module now automatically sets the Host header for proxied requests if it is not explicitly provided by the user. This change ensures that proxy servers receive the correct host information, preventing potential connection issues or misrouting.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Response` class where closing a session response with unconsumed content failed to close the underlying connection. It ensures that `Response.close` properly releases the raw stream if the content has not been read, preventing resource leaks.

This commit fixes a crash in the `MockRequest` class within `requests/cookies.py` by correcting the usage of the `urlparse` compatibility function. The error previously occurred when processing secure cookies, as the code incorrectly called `urlparse.urlparse` instead of `urlparse`.
The CI configuration now runs a new `ci` target instead of the standard test suite. This change updates the Makefile to define the `ci` target, which executes the Python setup test command.

This documentation update clarifies that users can explicitly set the content type and custom headers when uploading files. It modifies the quickstart guide to show how to pass these additional parameters in the file tuple.
This commit removes a trailing blank line from the HTTPAdapter class in the requests library. It is a minor cleanup that does not change any functional behavior or fix a user-facing bug.

This commit updates the project documentation to clarify the officially supported Python versions. It corrects the version range in the README to explicitly list Python 2.6 through 2.7 and 3.3 through 3.5.

The lock-issues workflow now runs hourly instead of daily to better manage GitHub API rate limits. This change aims to ensure the lock-threads action processes all eligible issues and pull requests more reliably.

This commit moves the logic for checking the CURL_CA_BUNDLE environment variable from the HTTPAdapter to the Session class. It ensures that the CA bundle path is correctly resolved during the request process, improving compatibility with curl-based configurations.

This commit fixes an issue in the `Request` class where redirect history was incorrectly recorded. It ensures that the `redirect` flag is only set if the response status indicates a redirect and the flag was not already true, preventing duplicate entries in the history.

This commit extends the test suite for the requests library to verify HTTP Digest authentication using SHA-256 and SHA-512 algorithms, in addition to the existing MD5 support. It updates the TestRequests class to iterate through these different authentication types, ensuring the library correctly handles various digest methods.

This commit fixes a bug in the `get_encoding_from_headers` function within the `requests` library. It prevents errors when the content-type header is empty by returning early instead of attempting to parse a missing value.

This commit updates the project documentation by adding a statement about Python standards and listing Twitter and the Library of Congress as users of the library. It also removes a redundant section header from the index page.

This commit adds a new section to the community documentation recommending the Betamax library. It describes Betamax as a tool for recording HTTP interactions specifically for Python-Requests, helping users manage test data.

This commit removes outdated documentation from the Response class in requests/models.py. It clarifies the behavior regarding automatic decompression of gzip-encoded response data by deleting a misleading comment.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar templates to change the image title attribute from a character description to a URL. The change affects the `sidebarintro.html` and `sidebarlogo.html` files, altering the tooltip displayed when users hover over the logo.

This commit simplifies the data preparation logic in the `Request` class within `requests/models.py`. It removes an unnecessary conversion of the data dictionary to a list of key-value pairs, relying instead on the dictionary's native iteration. This change streamlines the `_encode_files` method without altering the final request behavior.

This commit improves the clarity of test failures in the test_requests module. It adds descriptive error messages to the TooManyRedirects tests so that if a redirect does not raise the expected exception, the failure output explains the specific expectation.

This commit updates the package installation process to explicitly declare external dependencies for chardet, idna, and urllib3. It replaces the previous method of bundling these libraries as internal subpackages, ensuring users receive the correct versions when installing the requests library.
This commit removes an unused import from the requests/certs.py module. It cleans up the codebase by eliminating unnecessary dependencies without altering any user-facing behavior or functionality.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar templates to replace the outdated Gittip donation section with a "Get Support" heading. It removes the embedded donation widget and related text from the sidebar intro and logo templates.
This commit removes a financial support request from the project's README. It updates the documentation to eliminate the call to action for donations, streamlining the introductory text for users.

This commit adds a tox configuration file to define test environments for multiple Python versions and sets up the test command. It also removes the tox configuration file from the gitignore list to ensure it is tracked by version control.

This commit updates the contributing guidelines to soften the tone of the code of conduct section. It changes the heading from a direct command to a simple "Be Cordial" and moves the strict warning into a bolded sentence below.

This commit updates the project documentation in docs/index.rst by replacing the "Say Thanks" badge with a PyPI download badge. It also removes the maintenance-mode notice and the "Non-GMO" tagline, leaving only the project name.

This commit updates a test case in the test_requests.py module to remove an unnecessary UTF-8 encoding step. It ensures the test correctly validates that JSON parameters do not override data parameters by using a standard string key instead of a byte string.

This commit updates the Ruff linter version in the pre-commit configuration from 0.15.22 to 0.16.0. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the Ruff pre-commit hook for code quality checks.

This commit removes trailing whitespace from the test_requests.py file. It cleans up the RequestsTestSuite class and its test methods, such as test_unicode_get, to improve code consistency. No functional behavior is changed.

The HTTPAdapter.close method now clears pooled connections from all active ProxyManager objects, not just the direct connection pool. This ensures that closing a session properly releases all proxy-related resources.

This commit reverts a previous documentation update regarding connection keep-alive settings. It removes the note in the advanced user guide that advised manually setting the keep-alive header for older servers.
This commit updates the build configuration to support the cchch dependency. It adds a development install target to the Makefile and removes the six module from the setup.py package list.

The `requote_path` function in `requests/utils.py` is simplified by removing the unnecessary step of splitting the path on forward slashes. This change relies on the fact that forward slashes are not encoded, allowing the function to process the entire path string directly.

The `iter_content` method in `requests.models` now uses urllib3's stream generator for more efficient data handling. This change improves performance when reading response bodies in chunks, while maintaining backward compatibility with standard file-like objects.

This commit updates the documentation index to rephrase the testimonials section. It removes the informal "cool kids" phrasing from the opening and moves the download statistics to the end of the paragraph for better flow.

This commit updates the test CA certificate configuration to include a key usage extension, ensuring the certificate explicitly permits signing certificates and CRLs. It regenerates the test CA certificate to reflect these changes, improving the accuracy of the test environment for certificate validation scenarios.
This commit adds Jérémy Bethmont to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS file. It updates the project's credit list to acknowledge his contributions.

This commit removes the unused AuthObject class from the requests module. It simplifies the Request class by replacing manual authentication tuple handling with a direct call to the auth_dispatch function.

This commit refactors the `raise_for_status` method in the `Response` class within `requests/models.py`. It simplifies the conditional logic and removes duplicate code used to raise HTTP errors for different status code ranges.
This commit releases version 0.5.0 of the requests library. It updates the version number in the core module and records the release date in the project history.

The `_encode_files` method in `requests/models.py` now accepts an optional third element in file dictionary values to specify an explicit content type. This allows users to override the default MIME type detection when uploading files.

In `requests/utils.py`, the module now checks if the certifi certificate file exists before assigning its path. This allows users to delete that specific file to force the library to fall back to the operating system's default CA certificates.

This commit updates the project's README to replace the previous description with a new, humorous tagline. It redefines the library as a "Non-GMO" HTTP tool for Python, emphasizing safety and ease of use over the old technical explanation.

This commit fixes errors caused by merging an outdated pull request, ensuring the request function handles cookies and hooks correctly. It updates the request function in requests/api.py and adjusts hook dispatching logic in requests/hooks.py to prevent runtime failures.

This commit updates the project's author documentation to recognize additional team members. It adds a new "Core Contributors" section to the AUTHORS file, listing Cory Benfield and Ian Cordasco alongside the existing development lead.

This commit removes a placeholder comment in the `Request` class within `requests/models.py`. It does not change any user-facing behavior or fix a bug, as it only deletes a line of code that was not active.

This commit updates the urllib3 connection pool module to use the select.poll method instead of select.select for checking socket readiness. It also adjusts imports for socket errors and HTTP ports to improve compatibility across Python versions.

The `proxy_bypass_registry` function in `requests/utils.py` now handles `ValueError` exceptions alongside `OSError` when reading Windows proxy settings. This prevents crashes caused by invalid registry entries, allowing the library to gracefully ignore bad data instead of failing.

This commit updates the documentation for the `Response.text` property in `requests/models.py` to reflect the switch from the `chardet` library to `charade` for encoding detection. It clarifies that `charade` is now used to guess the encoding when it is not explicitly set.

This commit updates a test in the requests test suite to verify that the Content-Type header is an empty string rather than "text/plain" when sending string data. It corrects the expected behavior for the test_str_data_content_type method.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the `requests/auth.py` module that would have prevented the library from loading. It corrects the closing brackets for the `__eq__` methods in both the `HTTPBasicAuth` and `HTTPDigestAuth` classes.

This commit tightens the type annotation for the `reason` attribute in the `Response` class to strictly require a string, removing the previous allowance for `None`. It ensures that the attribute is always treated as a string in type checking, even though it is initialized to `None` during construction.
This commit cleans up the project's setup configuration. It modifies the setup.py file to refine how the package is installed and distributed.
This commit removes an unused import from the requests.auth module. It cleans up the code by eliminating a redundant reference to the bytes type, which does not affect user-facing behavior.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to correctly format the SOCKS proxy scheme names. It ensures that `socks5` and `socks5h` are displayed as inline code, improving readability in the guide.

This commit removes a redundant import statement from the test module. It cleans up the codebase by eliminating a duplicate reference to the operating system module, which does not alter any functional behavior.

This commit finalizes the release of version 0.11.2 for the requests library. It updates the version number and build identifier in the package initialization module and records the specific release date in the project history.

This commit adds a static method to the RequestMixin class that constructs the body for multipart form data requests. It handles encoding file uploads and form fields, ensuring that the order of parameters is preserved when provided as a list of tuples.

This commit updates the project's tagline in the README from "The Simple (i.e. usable) HTTP Module" to "HTTP for Humans." It removes the parenthetical remark to present a more neutral and welcoming description of the library.

This commit updates the test suite in tests/test_requests.py to replace a deprecated buffer-based stream implementation with a modern byte-string approach. It renames the internal helper class to TestStream and adjusts the read logic to use standard slicing, ensuring the test for POST requests with seeked objects remains compatible with current Python versions.
This commit removes a trailing newline from the NOTICE file. It ensures the license text ends cleanly without an extra blank line.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to explain how to pass a list of tuples to the data argument for form submissions with duplicate keys. It also adds a new contributor to the project's author list.
This commit updates the project history to document version 2.12.5. It records a bugfix that corrects JSON encoding detection for big-endian UTF-32 files with a byte order mark.
This commit adds Vikram Oberoi to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS.rst file. It updates the project's attribution records to include a new name under the patches and suggestions section.

This commit upgrades the bundled urllib3 library to version 1.3. It reorganizes imports in the package initialization and updates the connection pool, request, and response modules to reflect the new library structure.

This commit adds a test to the RequestsTestSuite in test_requests.py that verifies the behavior of the requests.settings context manager. It ensures that setting a timeout of zero causes a request to fail, while a valid timeout allows the request to succeed.

This commit adds support for configuring HTTP and HTTPS proxies via the `HTTP_PROXY` and `HTTPS_PROXY` environment variables. The `Request` class in `requests/models.py` now automatically detects these variables, allowing users to set proxy settings globally without passing arguments to each request.

This commit fixes a bug in the `requests.utils` module where the `is_ipv4_address` and `is_ipv4_network` functions could raise unexpected errors. By narrowing the caught exceptions to `socket.error`, the functions now handle invalid IP strings more gracefully without triggering broad exception handling.

This commit updates the .gitignore file to exclude the toy.py file from version control. This prevents the file from being tracked by git, likely because it is a temporary or development artifact not intended for the repository.
This commit adds imports for the poster library to the requests core module. It enables multipart encoding and streaming HTTP functionality by registering the necessary openers.

The Request class in requests/core.py now supports cookie management by adding a cookiejar attribute. The _get_opener method builds a unified opener that includes a cookie processor when a jar is provided, allowing requests to handle cookies automatically.

This commit refactors the user agent string generation logic from the defaults module into a dedicated utility function named default_user_agent. It consolidates the code that determines the Python implementation and version, making the process more modular and reusable.

This commit corrects spelling errors in the documentation and code comments. It updates the changelog and the docstring for the extract_zipped_paths function in requests/utils.py to use the correct terms "nonexistent" and "necessary."

This commit refactors the proxy lookup logic in the HTTPAdapter class to improve code clarity. It replaces a complex nested dictionary access with explicit conditional checks, making the per-host proxy resolution process easier to understand without changing the underlying behavior.

This commit updates documentation and code comments in the requests library to reference modern HTTP standards, replacing outdated RFC 2616 citations with RFC 7230 and 7231. It clarifies that HTTP header names are case-insensitive and that relative location headers are permitted, improving accuracy in the SessionRedirectMixin class.

This commit adds a test to the requests test suite that demonstrates a failure when posting binary data from a seekable object that lacks an iterator. The test defines a custom stream class to reproduce the issue, highlighting a bug in how the library handles such data sources.

This commit replaces the abbreviated license text with the full Apache-2.0 license to ensure correct detection by scanning tools. It also adds a NOTICE file, which triggers specific attribution requirements under the license.

This commit updates the project history file to document the v0.3.0 release. It highlights the introduction of a new authentication manager system, an automatic authentication API change, and improved URL parameter handling.

The `should_bypass_proxies` function in `requests/utils.py` now uses the hostname instead of the full network location to check proxy bypass rules. This change removes username and password credentials from the lookup, fixing DNS resolution failures on macOS.

This commit updates the project's README documentation. It replaces non-breaking space entities with standard non-breaking space entities in the HTML markup. This change ensures consistent spacing in the rendered text.

This commit ensures that the README and HISTORY files are explicitly read using UTF-8 encoding in the setup.py script. This prevents potential decoding errors when the package metadata is processed on systems with non-UTF-8 default locales.

This commit replaces the previous Carbon ad integration with a direct Native CPC unit from BuySellAds. It updates the `native.js` module to handle the new ad placement and adjusts `custom.css` to style the sidebar ad container.

The `iter_lines` method in the `Response` class no longer strips trailing whitespace, preserving meaningful spaces in the output. It also handles line breaks more robustly by relying on standard string splitting rather than assuming specific terminators.
Fixes a minor grammatical error in the docstring for the `options` function in `requests/api.py`. The description now correctly uses the article "an" before "OPTIONS request."

This commit updates the certificate bundle in the requests module to match the certifi 2015.9.6.2 release. It ensures the library uses the current trusted root certificates for secure HTTPS connections.

This commit adds a new "Response Headers" section to the quickstart documentation. It explains how users can access server response headers using a dictionary-like interface. The update clarifies that this dictionary is specifically designed for HTTP headers.

This commit corrects a typo in the documentation for the `request` function in `requests/api.py`. It fixes the variable name in the description of the 4-tuple format for file uploads, ensuring it correctly references `content_type` instead of `content-type`.

This commit renames the `get_clean_url` function to `cleanup_url` within the `requests` library. The change updates the function definition in `requests/utils.py` and its usage in `requests/models.py` to reflect the new name.

This documentation update corrects the example output for the `raise_for_status` method in the quickstart guide. It clarifies that the library raises a `requests.exceptions.HTTPError` rather than a standard `urllib2.HTTPError`, ensuring the displayed error message matches actual behavior.

In the `requests/cookies.py` module, the `MockRequest` class now uses a property decorator for the `unverifiable` attribute instead of a custom `__getattr__` method. This change simplifies attribute access and ensures the value is retrieved directly from the `is_unverifiable` method.

This commit fixes a bug in the HTTPDigestAuth class where authentication failed if the server returned multiple quality-of-protection options. It updates the build_digest_header method to correctly parse and handle comma-separated qop values, ensuring the client can proceed with the 'auth' mechanism.
This commit updates the AUTHORS file to add Bruno Renié to the list of contributors. It also fixes a missing newline at the end of the file.
This commit updates the project's README documentation file. It repositions the "Say Thanks" badge image within the text layout. No functional code or user-facing behavior is changed.

The `read` method in the `Request` class now accepts additional arguments, allowing users to pass extra parameters without causing errors. This change improves flexibility when interacting with the request object in `requests/core.py`.

This commit updates the README documentation to correct a typo in a URL example and adds a method field to a sample request dictionary. These changes clarify the usage examples for users reading the project guide.

This commit updates the documentation examples for the `requests` library to include additional parameters like `timeout`, `allow_redirects`, and `proxies` in the `post` and `delete` method signatures. It ensures the README accurately reflects the full range of available options for these HTTP requests.

This commit updates the Ruff linter version in the pre-commit configuration from 0.15.17 to 0.15.18. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the Ruff pre-commit hook for code quality checks.

This commit reverts the addition of a `max_retries` argument to the `requests` library. It restores the previous behavior where retry limits were configured solely through the `HTTPAdapter` instance rather than passed directly to request methods. The change affects the `HTTPAdapter`, `Session`, and top-level `request` functions.

This commit corrects several spelling errors in documentation and code comments across the requests library. It fixes typos in the changelog, the PreparedRequest and Response classes, and the Session module. No functional behavior is changed.

The Request class in requests/core.py now encodes both keys and values of incoming unicode data as UTF-8. This change fixes a bug where UTF-8 encoded byte strings were incorrectly encoded twice, which previously caused an UnicodeDecodeError.
