This commit fixes a compatibility error in the chardet2 test module that prevented it from running under Python 2.7. It adds a future import to ensure the print function behaves correctly across Python versions.

This commit updates the documentation in the advanced user guide to improve the readability of the request preparation example. It refactors the code snippet to use a separate variable for the request object before calling the prepare method.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation for the Requests library. It clarifies the guidance on setting proxy environment variables, advising users to configure only the specific variables relevant to their needs rather than implying a single export is sufficient.

This commit updates the developer documentation to clarify that additional dependencies are required to run the test suite. It replaces the simple pip install instruction with steps to create a virtual environment and use the Makefile, ensuring new contributors can successfully set up the project.
This commit adds Matt Spitz to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS.rst file. It updates the project's attribution records to include his name under the patches and suggestions section.

This commit adds a test to the RequestsTestCase class in test_requests.py. It verifies that attempting to connect to an invalid domain correctly raises a ConnectionError, ensuring the library handles network failures as expected.

This commit adds documentation to the advanced user guide explaining how to assign hooks to a Session instance. It clarifies that these hooks execute on every request made through that specific session, providing a practical example of using a response hook.

The `raise_for_status` method in the `Response` class now accepts an `allow_redirects` parameter. This allows users to explicitly permit 3XX status codes without raising an exception, overriding the default behavior.

This commit adds a new documentation page to the community section that lists curated third-party extensions for the Requests library. It organizes these tools into categories such as exceptional extensions and worthy mentions, providing users with a directory of available add-ons.

This commit configures the project to build universal Python wheels by default, removing the need for a specific command-line flag. It updates the Makefile to simplify the build process and adds a new setup.cfg file to declare the wheel as universal.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library within the requests package. It introduces a new `ssl_wrap_socket` utility and refactors `VerifiedHTTPSConnection` to use it, improving SSL handling. The change also adds new exception types and updates connection pool logic.

This commit updates the test suite to align with the latest upstream master branch. It modifies the RequestsTestCase class in test_requests.py by adding blank lines to adjust formatting. No functional behavior or bug fixes are introduced.
This commit fixes a typo in the contributing documentation by correcting the spelling of "philosophical." The change is located in the docs/dev/contributing.rst file.
The README documentation now displays the Python Software Foundation logo instead of the license badge. This change updates the project's visual branding in the main documentation file.
This commit adds a new Makefile target to verify the project's readme file. It also includes the readme_renderer dependency in the Pipfile to support this validation process.

This commit corrects a grammatical typo in the quickstart documentation. It fixes the phrasing in the Timeouts section to accurately describe when an exception is raised if the server has not issued a response.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Response` class where the `text` property incorrectly attempted to decode empty content. It prevents a potential error by only performing the decoding step when the content is not empty.

The `get_environ_proxies` function in `requests/utils.py` now supports IP ranges in the `no_proxy` environment variable. This allows users to exclude specific subnets from proxy usage, which previously only supported simple host suffixes.

This commit updates the project's README to document new features, including support for various HTTP methods, header and data attachment, and basic authentication. It also refines the introductory text for the usage section to emphasize simplicity.

This commit updates the documentation for the `Session` class in the `requests` library to clarify how proxy configurations are specified. It explains that the `proxies` dictionary can now map both simple protocols and specific protocol-host combinations to proxy URLs, providing a more accurate description of the supported behavior.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to reference the correct module path. It changes the module directive from the top-level package to the specific models submodule, ensuring accurate documentation links.
This commit fixes a broken hyperlink in the documentation index. It corrects the URL for the Requests III project page, ensuring users can successfully navigate to the external resource.

This commit marks the `test_request_recovery` test in the `TestTestServer` class as skipped. It addresses a non-deterministic failure that occurs when running the test suite with the pytest-xdist plugin.

This commit adds documentation examples to the advanced user guide, demonstrating how to configure SSL verification and client certificates for persistent sessions. It clarifies how to set the verify and cert attributes on a requests.Session object.

This commit adds a new documentation section titled "CA Certificates" to the advanced user guide. It explains how Requests uses the certifi package to manage trusted root certificates, recommending frequent updates for security.

The `super_len` function in `requests/utils.py` now catches `AttributeError` in addition to `io.UnsupportedOperation`. This fixes a crash when calculating the length of files obtained via `Tarfile.extractfile()`, allowing such objects to be processed correctly.

This commit updates the test suite to match the new error message generated by urllib3 when an invalid timeout value is provided. It ensures that the TestTimeout class correctly validates that timeout arguments must be an int, float, or None.

This commit updates the documentation for the `data` parameter in `requests.api`, `requests.models`, and `requests.sessions` to consistently state that it accepts a list of tuples. It clarifies that all convenience functions support this format, matching the underlying behavior of `RequestEncodingMixin`.
This commit updates the release date for version 2.0.0 in the project's history file. It replaces a placeholder date with the specific release date of September 24, 2013.

This commit adds tests to the TestRequests class in tests/test_requests.py. It verifies that PreparedRequest correctly sets either Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding headers, but not both, when sending byte streams with authentication.

This commit removes the `AuthenticationError` class from the `requests.exceptions` module. Users will no longer be able to catch this specific exception type, as it has been completely deleted from the library.

This commit adds a missing colon to the "Support Requests Development" heading in the documentation sidebar templates. It ensures the text in `sidebarintro.html` and `sidebarlogo.html` is grammatically consistent.

This commit updates the project's README to remove the phrase "for the open source community" from the library's description. It clarifies the project's tagline without altering any functional code or behavior.

This commit applies PEP 8 style fixes across the requests library, including modules like auth, cookies, and models. It adjusts formatting in classes such as HTTPBasicAuth and Session to ensure code consistency. No functional behavior changes are introduced.

This documentation update clarifies that the `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` environment variable is supported as a fallback for trusted CA certificates. It specifies that this variable is used when `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` is not set, helping users understand the configuration hierarchy in the advanced user guide.

This commit adds a test to the low-level test suite that verifies a ChunkedEncodingError is raised when a server returns an invalid chunked response. The new test function, test_chunked_encoding_error, simulates a server that sends a chunked header but fails to provide valid data chunks.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 2.17.1. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the `__version__.py` file to reflect the new release.

This commit adds a new contributor to the project's author list. It updates the AUTHORS.rst file to include Stephen Zhuang in the patches and suggestions section, ensuring proper credit is given as per the contribution guidelines.

This commit fixes the verbose logging example in the advanced documentation, which previously failed to enable logging. It updates the instructions to use a configuration dictionary passed to the request instead of setting a global attribute.

This commit ensures that the Response.json method consistently raises a RequestsJSONDecodeError instead of a generic ValueError when parsing fails. This fixes an inconsistency where the specific exception type depended on whether the response encoding was explicitly set.

The HTTPAdapter.send method in requests/adapters.py now uses urllib to handle chunked requests. This change simplifies the request sending logic by removing the previous conditional branching that treated chunked and non-chunked requests differently.

This commit ensures that every response object retains a reference to the original request that generated it. It modifies the `Request` and `Response` classes in `requests/models.py` to automatically link these objects, allowing users to access the request details directly from the response.

This commit updates the test workflow to run Python 3.8 and 3.9 on macOS 13 instead of the latest version. It resolves a failure where these older Python versions could not execute on the new arm64 hardware. The change modifies the run-tests.yml file.

The `merge_kwargs` function in `requests/sessions.py` now accepts key-value lists for the `params` argument, not just dictionaries. This change allows users to pass list-based parameters directly to session requests. A new test verifies that this list format is handled correctly.
Updates the Python setup action in the lint and test workflows to version 5.1.0. This minor version bump ensures the CI environment uses the latest stable release of the setup tool.

This commit updates the `curl_from_request` function in `requests/utils.py` to use percent-style string formatting instead of concatenation. It improves the readability of the code when generating curl command strings from request data.

This commit updates the project's changelog to document recent changes. It lists new support for PATCH requests, fixes for redirects, verbose stream writing settings, and querystring handling for all methods.

This commit restores version control metadata for the requests_open_source project by re-adding IDE configuration files and the Travis CI build script. It ensures the project's build and development environment settings are properly tracked in the repository.

This commit fixes a bug where empty proxy strings caused request failures. The Request class now removes any proxy entries with empty values during initialization. New tests verify that requests succeed when empty proxies are provided.

This commit moves the conversion of the HTTP method to a native string from the Session.request method to the PreparedRequest.prepare_method function. This ensures the method is consistently normalized during request preparation rather than at the session level.

This commit removes the reference to the CA certificate file from the package manifest. It ensures the distribution archive no longer includes the certificate, which may have been unnecessary or caused packaging issues. The change affects the MANIFEST.in configuration file.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` now supports multiple hooks for each event type instead of just one. This change allows users to register several callback functions that will all be executed in sequence during the request lifecycle. The underlying logic is handled by the new `dispatch_hooks` function in `requests/hooks.py`.
This commit removes Python 3.4 from the test environment list in the tox configuration file. Users will no longer see Python 3.4 included in the automated test runs.
This commit updates the project's changelog to document version 0.5.2. It lists new features including relative redirect support and improved HTTPS testing, alongside general bug fixes.

The HTTPAdapter class in requests/adapters.py now supports sending custom headers to HTTP and HTTPS proxies. This aligns the library with urllib3's capabilities for proxy authentication and configuration.

The CI workflow now includes Python 3.13 beta in the test matrix. This ensures the project is verified against the upcoming Python release. The change is made in the GitHub Actions test configuration.

This commit fixes a bug in the HTTPAdapter.send method where chunked upload connections were incorrectly released twice. This prevents potential connection pool corruption or errors when handling large data uploads.

This commit adds a clarifying comment to the `raise_for_status` method in the `Response` class within `requests/models.py`. It explains the logic for decoding HTTP reason strings, noting that UTF-8 is attempted first before falling back to ISO-8859-1 for localized server responses.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` now accepts a `_return_request` flag to construct and return the request object without automatically sending it. This change also ensures that user-provided hooks are correctly passed to the underlying request preparation logic.

This commit improves cookie handling in the Requests library by allowing the RequestsCookieJar to accept cookie objects directly when accessing or setting items. It also refines the SessionRedirectMixin to simplify redirect resolution and cookie management, ensuring that updating a jar with another jar works correctly.

This commit updates the project's README to replace outdated download statistics with current metrics. It highlights the library's popularity by citing weekly download counts and the number of dependent repositories.

The HTTPAdapter class in requests/adapters.py now accepts a pool_block argument to control connection pool behavior. This prevents the pool from exceeding its maximum size when using threading, avoiding warnings about discarding connections.

This commit updates the documentation for the `request` function in `requests/api.py`. It removes a sentence from the `data` parameter description that explained how to duplicate fields using a list of tuples.

This commit updates the HTTPAdapter to raise a new RetryError exception when a request fails due to a urllib3 ResponseError. It also changes the default retry count from a sentinel object to zero and adds a test to verify this retry behavior.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to a newer version, improving how HTTPS connections handle hostname verification. It modifies the VerifiedHTTPSConnection class to allow disabling hostname checks when explicitly configured, and updates related connection pool and response handling modules.

This commit updates documentation references in the requests.cookies module to use the correct Python standard library module name, http.cookiejar, instead of the deprecated cookielib. It clarifies the compatibility code for MockRequest, MockResponse, and RequestsCookieJar without changing any functional behavior.

This commit replaces the LGPL-licensed chardet dependency with the MIT-licensed charset_normalizer to resolve licensing ambiguity for downstream projects. The Response class now uses charset_normalizer for encoding detection, while still falling back to chardet if it is installed.

This commit fixes character encoding detection errors in the chardet library by correcting byte string handling in the CharSetProber class. It also resolves a compatibility issue in the charade module by fixing a typo in the version check and updating string type comparisons for Python 3.
This commit updates the project to support Python 3.14 while removing support for Python 3.8. It modifies the CI workflow, setup configuration, and documentation to reflect these version changes.
This commit updates the advanced user documentation to correct the capitalization of the Response class name. It ensures the term is consistently formatted as a proper noun within the text.

This commit fixes a minor code style inconsistency in the `merge_kwargs` function within `requests/sessions.py`. It adds a space after the comma in a tuple unpacking loop to align with standard formatting conventions. No functional behavior is changed.

This commit removes several test dependencies, including pytest and its plugins, from the project's requirements file. It leaves only the main package installation with the socks extra, likely to simplify the environment or resolve conflicts.

This commit updates the test suite to verify that the URL shortener correctly resolves to the expected domain. It also replaces the conditional simplejson import with the standard json module. The changes are located in the test_requests.py file.

This commit fixes a Jenkins build failure caused by the missing Pyflakes tool in Python 3 and PyPy environments. It modifies the Makefile to conditionally use a no-op command when Pyflakes is unavailable, ensuring the CI pipeline completes successfully.

This commit updates the cookie parsing logic in the `oreos` module to allow the equals sign in cookie keys. Previously, the presence of an equals sign would trigger an error, but it is now treated as a valid character.
This commit updates the documentation to use the correct URL for the monthly download badge. It fixes a broken image link on the project's main page by pointing to the updated static badge service.

This commit updates the docstring for the `__iter__` method in the `Response` class within `requests/models.py`. It clarifies that the method allows a response object to be used as an iterator, replacing the previous vague description.

This commit removes the unused `inspect` module import from the `requests` package initialization file. It cleans up the codebase by eliminating an unnecessary dependency without altering any user-facing behavior.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library within the requests package. It introduces a new Timeout class to handle connection and read timeouts more robustly, affecting how HTTPConnectionPool manages request durations.

This commit removes the import of the settings module from the main requests package initialization. It deprecates the previously exposed settings configuration, meaning users can no longer access it directly through the top-level namespace.

This commit updates the Session class in requests/sessions.py to check for the "keep_alive" configuration key instead of "keepalive," ensuring connection persistence settings are correctly recognized. It also prevents errors when updating cookies by safely handling cases where the response contains no cookies.

This commit removes a test script that demonstrated a URL encoding issue in the requests library. The deleted code showed how disabling URL encoding allowed special characters to pass through unmodified in a GET request.

This commit fixes a bug where using the Response object with lxml caused a TypeError instead of a proper AttributeError. The issue occurred because the Response class's attribute lookup method failed to raise an exception for missing attributes, leading to incorrect behavior. The fix ensures that missing attributes correctly trigger an AttributeError.

This commit updates the release log for version 2.9.0, documenting new warnings for text-mode file uploads and the addition of the 511 status code. It also lists bugfixes in the request handling module, including improved content-length calculation for partial file uploads and correct chunked transfer encoding for empty files.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` now automatically expands header values using the `header_expand` utility. This ensures that header data is properly formatted before being sent, preventing potential issues with malformed headers.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to explain how to configure proxy settings for an entire requests.Session object. It adds examples showing both manual dictionary updates and the use of the set_http_proxy helper method.

The Makefile now builds a universal wheel during the publish step, ensuring the package is compatible with both Python 2 and Python 3. This change modifies the build command to include the universal flag.

This commit simplifies the OAuth1 authentication logic in the requests library by moving validation responsibilities to the oauthlib dependency. It reduces the complexity of the OAuth1 class's callable method, streamlining how requests are signed and processed.

The `get_auth_from_url` function in `requests/utils.py` no longer checks if the input URL is empty before parsing. This removes unnecessary defensive checks, allowing the function to handle null or empty values directly through standard parsing and exception handling.

This commit ensures that the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` automatically adds a content-type header if one was not explicitly provided by the user. This prevents requests from being sent without a proper content-type, which could cause issues with servers expecting specific data formats.

This commit updates the test for request history tracking to verify that each redirect response contains the complete history of all previous requests, rather than just a count. It also corrects a comment in the SessionRedirectMixin class to accurately describe the history update process.

This commit initializes the changelog for the upcoming release by adding a new development section to the history file. It establishes empty categories for improvements and bug fixes to track changes leading to the next version.

Updates the continuous integration configuration to test against the final Python 3.8 release instead of the development version. This ensures the project is validated against the stable Python 3.8 environment.

This commit adds documentation to the quickstart guide explaining how the library handles HTTP redirections and request history. It describes the `Response.history` attribute and how to disable automatic redirects for specific methods.
The CI workflow now runs tests on PyPy 3.8 and 3.9 for Windows and macOS. This expands test coverage to include these Python implementations on non-Linux platforms.

This commit refactors the Request class in requests/models.py to consistently use self.cookies instead of a local variable. It removes a redundant dictionary update call within the _build_response method, simplifying the code without changing user-facing behavior.

This commit fixes a bug where URL prefix checks failed for mixed-case URLs by converting the URL to lowercase before comparison. The change affects the `HTTPAdapter` and `Session` classes in the `requests` library.

The `merge_cookies` function in `requests/cookies.py` now correctly returns the updated cookie jar instead of modifying it in place. This ensures that the function behaves as expected when callers rely on the return value to access the merged cookies.

This commit updates the OAuth1 authentication class in requests/auth.py to correctly handle form-encoded request bodies. It ensures that the body is properly decoded and signed when the content type is explicitly set to application/x-www-form-urlencoded, fixing potential signature mismatches.

The `Request.send` method in `requests/models.py` no longer treats GET, HEAD, and DELETE requests as safe methods that bypass file handling logic. This change ensures that file uploads are processed consistently for all HTTP methods, preventing potential issues where data might be ignored for these specific request types.

This commit updates the project's README to include a PyPI license badge. The change adds a visual indicator linking to the package's PyPI page, improving the documentation's appearance and accessibility.

This commit removes the dependency on Pipenv for running the code coverage upload in the AppVCI build configuration. It updates the success step to invoke the codecov tool directly instead of through the Pipenv environment.

This commit introduces a new `requests.async` module that provides asynchronous HTTP request capabilities using gevent. It allows users to create request objects and send multiple requests concurrently via a `map` function, rather than executing them sequentially.

This commit updates the project's README to replace text-based documentation links with centered image banners. It adds a license image and a screenshot linking to the documentation site, removing the previous plain text descriptions.

This commit removes trailing whitespace from the error message in the `check_header_validity` function within `requests/utils.py`. It is a minor cleanup that does not change the library's behavior or fix any user-facing bugs.

This commit updates the documentation in `docs/community/vulnerabilities.rst` to fix broken links to CVE records. It removes the invalid `www` subdomain from the URLs, ensuring users can successfully access the referenced vulnerability details.

This commit updates the README documentation to improve the formatting of the feature list. It replaces a standard HTML div element with a preformatted text block to better align the listed capabilities.

Adds a basic Travis CI configuration file to automate testing. It sets up the environment to run the test suite across multiple Python versions, from 2.6 to 3.6, using the project's requirements and make commands.
This commit removes the unused `InvalidMethod` exception class from the `requests` library. It also cleans up the corresponding import in `requests/models.py` and removes an unused `codecs` import.

This commit updates the project's README to fix a minor formatting issue. It replaces empty paragraph tags with non-breaking space characters to ensure consistent vertical spacing in the rendered documentation.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` now explicitly closes the session after making a request. This prevents open sockets from lingering, which could trigger resource warnings or appear as memory leaks to users.

This commit updates the development documentation to replace pipenv instructions with standard virtual environment setup and make commands. It also adds a note on using tox to run tests across multiple Python versions.

This commit updates the project's history log to clarify that GET and HEAD requests now respect the `allow_redirects=False` setting. It corrects the previous description regarding safe verbs to accurately reflect the implemented behavior.

This commit updates the package metadata in setup.py to correctly identify the bundled library as urllib3 instead of poster. It ensures the project is properly recognized as containing the urllib3 dependency.

This commit introduces a new HTTPForcedBasicAuthHandler class in the requests/monkeys.py module. It ensures that Basic authentication is automatically applied to resources that return a 404 status code, preventing users from encountering unauthenticated errors on missing pages.

This commit updates the development and test dependencies to use the final release of pytest-httpbin 2.1.0, replacing the previous release candidate. It modifies the version pin in both the requirements-dev.txt and setup.py files to ensure the project uses the stable version of the testing library.
This commit removes the easy_install installation instructions from the README. It ensures users are directed unambiguously toward pip, as easy_install is no longer recommended.
This commit updates the documentation index for the Requests library. It reformats the introductory text describing the limitations of Python's built-in urllib2 module to improve readability.

This commit renames the `content` attribute in the `Response` class to `_content` to indicate it is a private internal variable. It also corrects a syntax error in the docstring for the `content` property.

This commit improves error reporting in the `Request.send` method of the `requests` module. It distinguishes between socket timeouts and connection pool exhaustion by propagating specific urllib3 timeout messages to the user.

This commit updates the `test_urllib3_pool_connection_closed` test in `test_requests.py` to correctly verify the error message when a connection pool is closed. It fixes a test failure caused by checking the deprecated `e.message` attribute instead of the exception object itself.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` now defaults the timeout parameter to `None` instead of a hardcoded setting. This allows the function to fall back to the configured timeout value only when no explicit timeout is provided, improving flexibility for callers.

The `Response` class now stores the request duration in an `elapsed` attribute as a `timedelta` object instead of a float in `time_taken`. This change, implemented in `HTTPAdapter.send`, allows users to access the response time using standard datetime arithmetic.

This commit updates the project's README to refine the library's description and feature support text. It replaces the previous tagline with a new one emphasizing the open source community and expands the statement about the library's readiness for modern web applications.

This release fixes a parsing bug in the requests library where the authentication component was incorrectly dropped from proxy URLs. The version number is updated to 2.27.1 in the version module and changelog.
This commit contains no code changes or file modifications. It serves as a placeholder or marker in the repository history without altering any application behavior or functionality.

This commit updates the project documentation to include NPR in the list of organizations that use the Requests library. It replaces the previous list in the testimonials section of the index file with the updated version.

This commit updates the certifi package's setup configuration to explicitly declare a dependency on the certifi library itself. It ensures that the required version is installed when the package is set up, preventing potential missing dependency errors during installation.

This commit simplifies the `prepare_content_length` method in the `PreparedRequest` class by removing redundant logic for calculating request body sizes. It ensures that the Content-Length header is set correctly for various body types, including file-like objects and standard data, without unnecessary conditional checks.

This commit refactors the `PreparedRequest` class in `requests/models.py` to properly initialize and prepare request components like URL, headers, authentication, and body. It updates the `Request.prepare` method to pass all necessary parameters to these preparation steps, ensuring the request is fully constructed before sending.

This commit improves how the HTTPAdapter handles chunked uploads by refining the connection setup and data transmission process. It ensures that headers are sent correctly and that the chunked body is formatted properly before the response is read, leading to more reliable upload behavior.

The OAuth1 class in requests/auth.py now signs requests with non-standard body types instead of skipping the signature. Previously, requests with body data that was not urlencoded or multipart were not signed, which could cause authentication failures. This change ensures the message is signed without including the body in the signature calculation.

This commit removes the `requests.async` module, which provided asynchronous HTTP request capabilities using gevent. Users relying on the `map` or `imap` functions for concurrent requests will no longer have access to this feature.
This commit pins the pipenv version to 0.2.0 in the Makefile to resolve CI failures. It replaces the flexible version constraint with an exact match to ensure a consistent build environment.

This commit removes the Pipfile and Pipfile.lock files, switching the project's dependency management to standard requirements files. It updates the MANIFEST.in to include requirements-dev.txt instead of the Pipfile artifacts. The change also adjusts test files to align with the new dependency setup.

This commit updates the CA bundle in the requests library to remove the expired Wells Fargo Root Certificate Authority. This ensures that HTTPS connections relying on this specific certificate will no longer fail due to an outdated trust store.

The `Request` class in `requests/core.py` now supports multipart file uploads for PUT requests. Previously, sending files with a PUT method was not handled, but this change allows the `send` method to encode and transmit multipart data when specified.

This commit renames the `multipart_files` parameter to `files` in the `requests` module to simplify the API. Users will now pass file data using the `files` argument in `post` and `put` requests instead of the previous name.

This commit changes the error raised by `PreparedRequest.prepare_url` when a URL cannot be parsed, switching from a generic `ConnectionError` to a more specific `InvalidURL` exception. This allows users to distinguish between network connection failures and malformed URL inputs.

This commit changes the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to encode data, parameters, and files only when sending the request, rather than during initialization. This prevents hooks and authentication callbacks from accidentally overwriting encoded values with unencoded originals, ensuring that modifications made to the request body are correctly reflected in the final output.
This commit updates the fundraising progress displayed in the documentation sidebar. It increases the reported amount raised from $10 to $110 in the sidebarintro and sidebarlogo templates.

This commit adds a test case to the RequestsTestCase class in test_requests.py. It verifies that the Request class correctly handles bytes and bytearray objects passed to the files argument, ensuring the resulting request uses multipart form data encoding.

This commit fixes a broken test command in setup.py that previously failed to locate the test file. It updates the path to correctly point to tests/test_requests.py, ensuring the test suite runs successfully when invoked via the setup script.
This commit updates the project version to 0.13.0 in the history file. It documents the removal of the Requests.async feature, which is now replaced by the grequests library.

The `Session.send` method in `requests/sessions.py` now uses the session's configured defaults for stream, verify, cert, and proxies instead of hardcoded values. This ensures that custom settings applied to a session object are correctly respected during request execution.

This commit refactors the redirect handling logic in the `SessionRedirectMixin` class within `requests/sessions.py`. It simplifies the process of removing the Authorization header when a request is redirected to a different hostname, improving code readability without changing the underlying behavior.

This commit implements the actual HTTP request logic within the `Request` class in `requests/core.py`. It enables the `send` method to construct and execute GET and POST requests, including handling headers, form data encoding, and basic authentication.

This commit removes a broad exception handler in the Response class that was silently catching AttributeError errors. This change ensures that unexpected attribute errors are no longer suppressed, allowing them to surface as visible bugs rather than being ignored during content processing.
This commit adds Ian Cordasco to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS.rst file. It corrects an oversight where the author was previously missing from the project's credits.
This commit updates the community documentation page for integrations. It adds a new image to the "Integrations" section of the out-there.rst file.
The CI configuration now runs the `simpleci` make target instead of `lazy` during the test phase. It also removes the explicit pip installation step from the install phase.

This commit fixes a Python 2.5 compatibility issue in the `HTTPBasicAuthHandler` class within the `requests/monkeys.py` module. It initializes the `retried` attribute to zero in the constructor, preventing potential errors when the handler is instantiated.

The `_basic_auth_str` function in `requests/auth.py` now correctly handles string inputs by encoding them to bytes before base64 encoding. This fixes a potential error when passing standard strings instead of byte objects for authentication credentials.

This commit adds a test case to the RequestsTestSuite in test_requests.py to verify that URLs containing percent-escaped characters are not double-escaped. It specifically checks for illegal, reserved, and non-ASCII characters to ensure the request URL remains unchanged. The test currently passes in Python 2 but fails in Python 3.

This commit allows the Request class to accept Unicode strings as file data in addition to byte strings. Previously, passing a string to the files parameter would fail, but now it is handled correctly. A new test verifies that POST requests with Unicode file content succeed.

This commit updates the `SessionRedirectMixin` in `requests/sessions.py` to reuse the existing `PreparedRequest` object during redirects instead of creating a new one. This change ensures that the request URL is correctly updated and prevents potential issues with request state management during the redirect process.
This commit updates the project's README to make the TravisCI status badge clickable. It adds a target link so users can navigate directly to the build status page.
This commit adds UTF-8 checkmark and cross symbols to the status code aliases in the `requests` library. Users can now reference HTTP 200 and 500 responses using these new Unicode characters.

This commit removes the static fundraising progress text from the documentation sidebar templates. It updates the `sidebarintro.html` and `sidebarlogo.html` files to stop displaying the specific goal and amount raised figures.

This commit fixes a crash in the PreparedRequest.copy method when headers or cookies are not initialized. It ensures that copying a request with missing attributes works correctly instead of raising an error.

This commit refactors the URL construction logic in the `requests` module by introducing a new `_build_url` static method to the `Request` class. It also updates the data validation check to use `hasattr` instead of `isinstance` for broader compatibility.

This commit fixes a memory leak in the requests library by ensuring the underlying socket is properly released when a response is closed. The change modifies the Response class to explicitly nullify the socket's receive method before closing the file object.

The CI test matrix now includes Python 3.15 alpha builds, marked as optional so failures do not block the pipeline. This change updates the GitHub Actions workflow to set a specific environment variable for 3.15 builds to ensure compatibility with PyO3.

This commit fixes the Request class in requests/core.py to properly initialize the response attribute and correct the method validation logic in the __setattr__ method. It also updates the module imports and renames the global AUTHOAUTHS list to AUTOAUTHS.

This commit updates the documentation index to reflect a higher monthly download count for the Requests library. It changes the stated figure from six million to seven million downloads in the introductory text.

This commit updates documentation and comments within the requests library. It adds a module docstring to the internal utilities file and clarifies a backward-compatibility import in the main utilities module.

This commit adds test cases to the RequestsTestSuite in test_requests.py to verify URI cleaning behavior within the query part of URLs. It ensures that escaped characters and reserved symbols are handled correctly when making requests, confirming that the final response URL matches the expected format.

This commit fixes a hang that occurred during streaming uploads when using HTTP Digest Authentication. The issue arose because the request body was already consumed when the client attempted to resend the request after a 401 response. The HTTPDigestAuth class now tracks the file position and rewinds the body before resending to allow the upload to complete.
This commit removes the Debian packaging files for the python-requests library. It deletes the changelog, control, and rules files, effectively stopping the project from providing a Debian package.

The `map` function in `requests/async.py` now accepts a `prefetch` parameter. When set to false, it prevents the immediate download of response content, allowing users to defer data retrieval until explicitly requested.

This commit strengthens the test for the `copy` method in the `CaseInsensitiveDict` class. It verifies that modifying the original dictionary after copying does not affect the copy, ensuring the copy is truly independent.

The Server class in testserver/server.py now includes a new text_response_server classmethod that sends arbitrary text as a response. The existing basic_response_server method was refactored to use this new helper, simplifying the code structure.

This commit introduces a backup module containing a legacy `OldRequest` class to preserve previous request handling behavior. It also updates the `PreparedRequest` class in the models module to support this new structure.

The Server class in the test server module now raises a RuntimeError if the server fails to become ready within the expected timeout. This change ensures that low-level tests report a clear error message instead of hanging or producing ambiguous output when a timeout occurs.

This commit fixes a bug in the HTTPDigestAuth class where the digest header value was incorrectly modified. It ensures that only the first occurrence of the "Digest" string is removed, preventing accidental changes to other parts of the header.

This commit fixes a crash in the requests library's compatibility module when running on Python 3.1 or 3.2. It prevents a SyntaxError from halting execution when the simplejson package is imported, allowing the library to fall back to the standard json module instead.
This commit updates the documentation sidebar template to include a "Say Thanks" link. It adds a visible call-to-action for users to express gratitude to the project maintainer.

The test suite in test_requests.py now targets httpbin.org instead of external Google URLs. This change ensures tests verify the local application's behavior, such as echoing user-agent headers, rather than relying on third-party services.

This commit bumps the Requests library version to 1.2.3 to address a simple packaging issue. It updates the version number in the `requests/__init__.py` module and adds a corresponding entry to the project's history file.

Replaces the invoke-based task runner with a standard Makefile to manage project dependencies and tests. This change removes the tasks.py module and introduces Makefile targets for initialization, testing, and fetching certificates.

This commit cleans up the `header_expand` function in `requests/utils.py` by removing outdated comments and adding a note about removing trailing separators. It does not change the function's behavior or fix any user-facing bugs.

The `RequestException` class in the `requests` library now inherits from `IOError` instead of `RuntimeError`. This change allows users to catch network-related errors using standard `IOError` handlers, improving compatibility with existing exception handling patterns.

The test for basic HTTP authentication in the TestRequests class was updated to remove complex byte-string handling and specific auth assertions. It now simply verifies that a standard GET request to the httpbin endpoint returns a successful status code.

This commit introduces a new async module to explicitly signal to users that they are utilizing asynchronous network calls. It ensures the underlying urllib2 library is patched with eventlet or gevent to support these operations. The changes primarily affect the requests/async.py file.
This commit adds a new FAQ page to the user documentation and updates the main index to link to it. It also adjusts line wrapping in the existing documentation text for better readability.

This commit fixes a broken hyperlink in the quickstart documentation by adding a missing underscore to the URL reference. The change ensures the link to the Toolbelt documentation renders correctly for users.

This commit updates the documentation comments for the `Session` class in `requests/sessions.py`. It corrects a grammatical error and clarifies that the default cookie jar is a `cookielib.CookieJar` compatible object.

This commit updates the test suite in test_requests.py to consistently use the httpbin fixture for all tests. It ensures that tests for the requests library rely on a standardized local server environment, improving test reliability and consistency.

This commit updates the Ruff linter version in the pre-commit configuration from 0.15.12 to 0.15.14. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the Ruff pre-commit hook for code quality checks.

This commit fixes an issue where cookies were incorrectly associated with the target domain during redirects. It updates the `resolve_redirects` method in the `SessionRedirectMixin` class to use the original request object instead of the prepared request when extracting cookies.

The `full_url` method in `requests/models.py` now requotes the entire URL instead of only the path component. This ensures that special characters in the scheme, network location, query, and fragment are properly encoded, preventing malformed URLs.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` now uses a new hooks API that expects a dictionary structure instead of a list. This change ensures that hook arguments are accessed directly via keys, simplifying the internal dispatch logic for pre- and post-request events.
This commit removes the PyPI version and license badge images from the project's README. It cleans up the documentation by eliminating these external links, which may have been broken or redundant.

This commit upgrades the bundled urllib3 library to version 1.13, updating its internal modules and version metadata. It introduces a new `__all__` list in the package initialization to explicitly define the public API surface for users.

This commit updates the vendored idna library to version 2.1 within the requests package. It refreshes the core, codec, and compatibility modules to ensure proper internationalized domain name handling.

This commit removes an unused import of the Server class from the test utilities module. It also cleans up a trailing blank line in the test file. These changes do not alter any functional behavior or fix a user-facing bug.

This commit fixes a connection leak where sockets were not returned to the urllib3 pool after requests. It enables prefetching by default and adds a close method to the Session class to properly release resources. The module-level request function now explicitly closes temporary sessions when finished.

The `Response.ok` property in `requests/models.py` now catches all `RequestException` types instead of only `HTTPError`. This ensures the property correctly returns `False` for any request failure, preventing unexpected errors when checking response status.

This commit updates a test in the CookieTests class to ensure compatibility with Python 2.6's unittest module. It replaces an assertion method that was unavailable in older versions with a standard equality check, preventing test failures in legacy environments.

The `Request.send` method in `requests/core.py` now correctly handles DELETE requests by appending query parameters to the URL instead of ignoring them. This ensures that DELETE requests with parameters are sent as intended, fixing a bug where such parameters were previously lost.

The installation documentation for the Requests library now recommends using Pipenv instead of pip for installing the package. This change updates the user guide to reflect the new preferred installation method.

This commit updates the development documentation to reflect the correct command for running the test suite. It replaces the outdated py.test instruction with the standard setup.py test command in the todo.rst file.

Updates the actions/setup-python dependency from version 5.6.0 to 6.0.0 in the lint, publish, and run-tests GitHub workflow files. This ensures the CI environment uses the latest major version of the Python setup action.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` now correctly passes the `allow_redirects` parameter to the underlying session. This restores the ability for users to control whether HTTP redirects are followed, which was previously ignored.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar to replace a link to edmsynths.com with a link to monescate.com. The change affects the sidebarintro.html and sidebarlogo.html templates, ensuring users see the new external resource in the navigation menu.

This documentation update restructures the advanced user guide by adding a dedicated sub-header for client-side certificates. The change clarifies the section organization within the advanced.rst file, making it easier for users to locate specific configuration details.

This commit prevents HTTP errors from being recorded when a request is part of a redirect loop. It modifies the `Request.send` method in `requests/models.py` to skip setting the error attribute if the request is currently redirecting.

This commit adds documentation for a specific SSL version use case in the advanced user guide. It clarifies how to handle SSL version selection when the default library behavior is insufficient. The changes are located in the `docs/user/advanced.rst` file.
This commit adds an `init` target to the Makefile. It allows users to install the project in editable mode with the socks extra by running a single command.
This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library within the requests package to version 1.10.3. It modifies the version string in the urllib3 module's initialization file to reflect the new release.

This commit removes a commented-out line in the Session class initialization that previously referenced mapping and wrapping API methods. It cleans up the codebase by deleting this obsolete comment, which had no functional impact on user behavior.

This commit removes redundant cookie handling logic from the `request` function in `requests/api.py` and updates the `Request` class documentation in `requests/models.py` to reflect the use of a CookieDict. It also adds a placeholder note for future multi-value header support.

This commit updates the documentation for the `post` and `put` functions in `requests/api.py` to clarify that the `data` parameter accepts both dictionaries and bytes. It also corrects the `put` documentation to reference the `data` parameter instead of the hidden `params` argument.

The `Request` class in `requests/models.py` is updated to use a new connection pooling system, replacing the legacy `urllib2` opener mechanism. This change removes the old `_get_opener` method and introduces a `_poolmanager` parameter to handle HTTP connections more efficiently.

This commit updates the documentation for the `request`, `post`, and `put` functions in `requests/api.py`. It clarifies that when a dictionary is passed to the `data` parameter, it will be form-encoded. This change improves clarity for users regarding how dictionary data is handled in request bodies.

This commit corrects the documentation for the requests library to accurately reflect that automatic redirection is disabled by default only for HEAD requests. It updates the quickstart guide to clarify which HTTP methods support the `allow_redirects` parameter for enabling or disabling this behavior.

This commit removes the dependency on the unittest2 package, which is no longer needed. It updates the test suite to use the standard library's unittest module instead, ensuring compatibility with modern Python versions.

The `curl_from_request` function in `requests/utils.py` now includes cookie data in the generated curl command. This change ensures that requests containing cookies are accurately represented when converted to a curl string.

This commit clarifies the documentation for the `request` function in the `requests` module. It explicitly states that the `timeout` parameter is measured in seconds, removing ambiguity for users configuring request timeouts.

This release updates the included CA bundle to ensure secure connections use the latest trusted certificates. The version number in the requests module is bumped to 2.0.1 to reflect this maintenance update.

This commit simplifies the redirect handling logic within the HTTPDigestAuth class in the requests library. It replaces a manual check for specific status codes with a more concise property check, ensuring consistent behavior when processing HTTP responses.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to improve line wrapping for better readability. It adjusts the formatting of paragraphs in the user guide without changing the technical content or behavior of the Requests library.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar templates to change the newsletter section heading from "Newsletter" to "Get Updates." The change affects the sidebarintro and sidebarlogo HTML files, providing a clearer call to action for users seeking updates.

This commit updates the `RequestsTestSuite` in `tests/test_requests.py` to use a local `httpbin` helper instead of hardcoded external URLs for redirect tests. It ensures the `test_max_redirects` test reliably verifies the `max_redirects` configuration variable under both normal and safe mode conditions.
This commit corrects a broken link in the project documentation. It updates the target URL for the download statistics badge in the main index file to point to the correct package name.
This commit removes the Travis CI configuration file, ending automated test runs for the project on that platform. Users will no longer see build status updates from Travis for this repository.

This commit updates the README documentation to fix a formatting error in the import example. It replaces an incorrect line break character with a standard newline, ensuring the code snippet displays correctly for users.
This commit updates the community sponsors documentation by adding a decorative line of emojis and slashes. It modifies the `docs/community/sponsors.rst` file to include this new visual element.

The `curl_from_request` function in `requests/utils.py` now supports basic authentication. This change allows users to generate curl commands that include basic auth credentials, resolving a previous limitation where only OAuth was noted as a future task.
This commit updates the project changelog to document version 0.6.2. It notes that safe HTTP verbs now default to not following redirects, preventing unexpected behavior for users making requests.

This commit removes the NOTICE file, which previously documented the license for the vendorized Poster library. This change eliminates the explicit attribution notice for that specific third-party component from the project.

This commit reorganizes the API documentation by moving the Request and Response class references into a new "Lower-Level Classes" section. It also updates the Sessions section heading and adds a usage example to the Request class in requests/models.py.
This commit adds a new introduction document to the user documentation. It outlines the project's design philosophy and explains the rationale for choosing the ISC license over the GPL.
This commit removes the VendorAlias class from the requests packages module. It eliminates a custom meta_path hook that previously managed module imports, simplifying the package structure.
This commit adds the "kr" and "kr_small" Sphinx themes to the documentation directory. It includes layout templates, static styles, and the FlaskyStyle class to support these new visual designs.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar templates to wrap the "Requests Pro" button in a paragraph element. This change ensures the promotional link displays with proper spacing and formatting in the rendered documentation.

This commit corrects the spelling of "Stack Overflow" in the project's documentation and issue templates. It ensures the proper name is used in the support guide and custom issue template for consistency.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar to replace the "Get Support" section with a "Donate" section. It changes the call to action from purchasing Requests Pro to supporting the author via Gittip, updating the relevant HTML templates.

This commit refactors the requests library to centralize version metadata in a new `__version__.py` module. It removes hardcoded version details from `requests/__init__.py` and replaces them with an import from the new file. This change simplifies version management and ensures consistency across the package.

This commit fixes a bug in the Request class where parameter encoding failed for unicode strings in Python 2. The issue occurred because the str type alias caused incorrect type checks during data preparation. The fix updates the _encode_params method to use the correct string type for validation.
This commit corrects a typo in the README.md file. It fixes the documentation link text by removing an extra colon from the displayed URL.

This commit updates the project documentation by replacing a brief testimonial from Rich Leland with a longer, humorous quote from Matt DeBoard. The change modifies the content displayed on the main index page.

This commit adds support for pre-request and post-request hooks to the `Request` class in the `requests` module. Users can now register callbacks that execute before a request is sent, allowing for custom logic or modifications to the request object.

This commit adds proxy support to the requests library, allowing users to route HTTP requests through specified proxy servers. It updates the `request` function in `requests/api.py` and the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to accept and process a proxies dictionary.

The TestServer now allows request handlers to store data for later retrieval by the main thread. This change enables the server to recover and process requests even after a connection is closed, improving the robustness of the test environment.

This commit updates the development dependencies to resolve a Jinja compatibility issue. It pins the markupsafe version below 2.1 and adjusts the Flask version constraint to ensure the application runs correctly with the updated library stack.

This commit removes the entire oreos package from the requests library, eliminating the internal cookie parsing and data structure modules. Users will no longer have access to the dict_from_string function or the custom cookie classes previously provided by this package.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to a newer version, improving how HTTP connection pools handle proxy headers and refining SSL hostname matching logic. It also adjusts the PyOpenSSL integration to import from the correct connection module.

This commit updates the visual assets for the project by modifying the existing flourish image and adding a new requests logo. These changes affect the graphical elements displayed in the documentation or interface.

This commit fixes an issue where authentication credentials were not properly preserved during redirects. It updates the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to store the initial auth configuration in a private attribute, ensuring it is correctly passed to subsequent requests.

This commit corrects a typo in the documentation for the `HTTPAdapter` class in the `requests` library. It fixes the parameter name from `ca_certs_dir` to `ca_cert_dir` in the description of `build_connection_pool_key_attributes`.

This commit fixes an issue where session cookies could incorrectly overwrite explicit cookies provided in a request. It updates the Session.request method to properly merge cookie jars and implements the previously missing RequestsCookieJar.copy method.

This commit updates the project documentation to include a call for financial support. It adds a message encouraging users to contribute to the sustainability of the open-source work. The change is located in the main documentation index file.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` no longer passes the `hooks` parameter to the `Request` object. This change ensures that request hooks are applied only at the API layer, preventing them from being duplicated or misapplied during the underlying request construction.

The Settings class in requests/config.py now initializes its attributes to None instead of an empty list. This ensures that default values for verbose and timeout are explicitly set to None, providing cleaner and more predictable default behavior for users.

This commit fixes a bug in the `RequestsCookieJar` class where the cookie policy was lost when creating a copy of the jar. Previously, this could cause unexpected behavior during requests if a non-default policy was configured. The `copy` method now explicitly transfers the policy to the new instance.

This commit removes trailing whitespace from the `curl_from_request` function in `requests/utils.py`. It cleans up the source code formatting without altering the library's behavior or fixing any user-facing bugs.

This commit adds docstrings and a string representation method to the AuthManager class in requests/core.py. It also includes minor whitespace adjustments to the Request class. These changes improve code readability without altering functionality.

This commit adds clarifying comments to the `Session.request` method in `requests/sessions.py`. It documents the process of merging local and session keyword arguments and the step of adding context to the response.

This commit updates the flake8 linting configuration in the Makefile to suppress warnings for lambda expressions. It adds the E731 error code to the ignore list, preventing the linter from flagging lambda assignments as style violations.

The `super_len` function in `requests.utils` now correctly calculates the length of string objects by first encoding them to UTF-8 bytes. This ensures that the reported size accurately reflects the actual number of bytes transmitted, rather than just the character count.

Fixes a bug where `requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError` instances could not be pickled, causing process pools to crash when handling invalid JSON. The fix adds a `__reduce__` method to the `JSONDecodeError` class to ensure all necessary arguments are preserved during serialization.

This commit updates the project description in the README to highlight that the library is handcrafted for the Python community. It replaces the previous tagline with a new one emphasizing the project's dedication and simplicity.

This commit fixes a bug in the `PreparedRequest.prepare_body` method where string data was not correctly identified in Python 2 environments. By checking for `basestring` instead of just `str`, the function now properly handles both byte strings and Unicode strings, ensuring consistent request body preparation across Python versions.
This commit updates the Requests library to version 0.2.0. It removes unused imports for httplib, urllib2, and urlparse from the core module.

This commit fixes an import error in the test suite by removing a direct import of the standard library cookielib module. It updates test_requests.py to import cookielib from requests.compat instead, ensuring compatibility across Python versions.

This commit removes the logic in setup.py that temporarily disabled Python bytecode generation during the package publishing process. The change simplifies the build script by eliminating these environment variable manipulations, which are no longer required.

This commit reverts a previous change that restricted URL preparation to only HTTP and HTTPS schemes. It restores support for other protocols, such as `http+unix`, in the `PreparedRequest.prepare_url` method within the `requests` module.

This commit adds tests to verify that expected security warnings are emitted during HTTPS requests. It ensures that SubjectAltNameWarning and SNIMissingWarning are consistently triggered by the test environment's secure server. The changes primarily affect the test suite initialization and the TestRequests class.

This commit fixes a bug in the `PreparedRequest.prepare_body` method where passing an empty JSON object incorrectly triggered form encoding. It corrects the logic to properly distinguish between a missing JSON payload and an explicitly provided empty one, ensuring the correct content type is set.

This commit updates the HTTP Basic Auth documentation examples to use a more reliable test endpoint. It replaces the previous GitHub API URL with a dedicated httpbin.org service for demonstrating authentication. The changes affect the user-facing documentation in the authentication module.

This commit updates the project history file to document version 0.8.0. It highlights the addition of keep-alive support and the complete removal of Urllib2, Poster, and CookieJars. It also notes new error handling features, including a specific ConnectionError and a safe mode for catching errors.
This commit clarifies the documentation for the `extract_cookies_to_jar` function in the `requests/cookies.py` module. It also corrects the author name in the project credits file.

This commit updates the project's contributor list by adding Torsten Landschoff to the "Patches and Suggestions" section. It modifies the AUTHORS.rst file to acknowledge this individual's contributions.

This commit corrects a spelling error in the project documentation. It fixes the typo "extrmely" to "extremely" in the main index file, ensuring the description of the library's ease of use is accurate.

This commit updates the README.md file to reflect the current download statistics for the requests library. It increases the reported download count from 11 million to 50 million to provide users with more accurate usage metrics.

This commit adds the ability to rewind request bodies, allowing the library to re-send POST data when following redirects. It introduces a new UnrewindableBodyError exception and updates the PreparedRequest class to track the body's starting position for this purpose.

This commit adds a configuration file to help developers ignore specific commits when using git blame. It specifically excludes a large automatic code formatting change from the history, ensuring that blame output points to the original author of the code rather than the formatter.

This commit applies PEP 8 style fixes across the requests library, including removing trailing whitespace and correcting indentation in modules like auth, models, and sessions. It does not change any functional behavior or fix bugs, but improves code consistency and readability.

This commit cleans up the project's README by removing outdated text that criticized Python's built-in urllib2 module. It also corrects a documentation example to use the correct GitHub API endpoint and updates a link to a code comparison.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar templates to use the new GitHub button service domain. It replaces the outdated URL in the sidebar intro and logo files, ensuring the watch button loads correctly for users viewing the site.

This commit updates the project documentation to clarify that connection pooling is provided by the external urllib3 library. It removes the inaccurate statement that urllib3 is embedded within the Requests module.

This release adds SSL certificate verification to requests, introducing a new 'verify' argument for SSL requests. It also includes the release of Cerifi, Mozilla's certificate list, and updates the underlying Urllib3 library.

This commit updates the project documentation to clarify Armin Ronacher's role as the creator of Flask. It also adds a new section encouraging organizations to financially support the development of the upcoming 3.0 release.

This documentation update clarifies that a Session instance can support multiple hooks, which execute in the order they are added. It corrects previous wording that implied only a single hook could be assigned to a session.
This commit updates the release history to document version 2.17.1. It notes an improvement to the `packages` namespace identity support, which enhances compatibility with monkeypatching libraries.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to simplify the file upload example by removing the unnecessary `data=None` argument from the `requests.post` call. It also adds a sample JSON response to illustrate the expected output of a multipart file upload.

This commit fixes invalid reStructuredText syntax in the HISTORY.rst file that was causing the project's long description to fail rendering on PyPI. The change corrects the formatting of a file extension reference to ensure the documentation displays properly.
Removes the `invokefile.py` module, which contained a `build` task that simply printed a message. This deletion eliminates the unused build automation script from the project.
Updates the GitHub Actions workflows to use newer versions of the setup-python and zizmor-action dependencies. This ensures the CI pipeline runs with the latest stable releases of these tools.

This commit updates the project's README to clarify a warning about HTTP library usage. It specifies that using the Python standard library for HTTP, rather than other libraries, may cause dangerous side-effects.

This commit fixes a documentation error in the quickstart guide where the text incorrectly stated that Tablib was required. It updates the description to correctly identify Requests as the necessary dependency for users.

This commit releases version 1.1.0 of the requests library, introducing support for chunked requests and streaming uploads. It also updates the user documentation to explain how to send large files without loading them entirely into memory.

This documentation update clarifies the error behavior of the `r.json()` method in the quickstart guide. It specifies that `simplejson.JSONDecodeError` is raised if the simplejson library is installed, regardless of the Python version.

This commit removes redundant session setup in the `test_mixed_case_scheme_acceptable` test within `test_requests.py`. It simplifies the test code by eliminating unnecessary variable assignments and duplicate session creation, improving code clarity without changing the test's behavior.

This commit adds support for streaming response content to the Response class in requests/models.py. It introduces an iter_content method that allows users to read large responses in chunks, preventing excessive memory usage. The implementation also updates utility functions in requests/utils.py to handle streaming decompression and decoding.
This commit updates the copyright year in the project's license file from 2017 to 2018. It ensures the legal documentation reflects the current year of maintenance.

This commit updates the changelog to clarify that sessions are now closed in all cases, including exceptional ones, when using the functional API. This prevents sessions from leaking and waiting for garbage collection.

This commit updates the Makefile to automatically rewrite import statements within the idna package. It ensures that internal module references are adjusted to use the correct namespace when the package is built.

This commit adds a test to verify that the `max_redirects` configuration correctly limits HTTP redirects. It checks that exceeding the limit raises a `TooManyRedirects` exception in normal mode and returns a response with an error attribute in safe mode.

This commit updates the documentation index to use clearer and more consistent section headings. It renames several sections, such as changing "Testimonials" to "User Testimonials" and "Feature Support" to "Supported Features," to improve readability for users navigating the site.

Updates the CodeQL security analysis workflow to use version 3.22.11 of the github/codeql-action. This major version bump replaces the previous 2.22.1 release in the codeql-analysis.yml file, ensuring the repository uses the latest supported security scanning tools.

This commit updates documentation in the requests library to clarify that the verify parameter accepts either a boolean or a file path. It replaces references to SSL with the more accurate TLS acronym in docstrings for BaseAdapter and HTTPAdapter. This commit corrects the terminology in error messages and docstrings within the requests library, changing "schema" to the correct term "scheme." It updates the `InvalidSchema` and `MissingSchema` exceptions in `requests/exceptions.py` and the `PreparedRequest` class in `requests/models.py` to ensure users see accurate descriptions when URL errors occur.
This commit updates the AUTHORS.rst file to add Lucian Ursu to the list of contributors. It acknowledges the individual's patches and suggestions within the project's documentation.
This commit adds Alberto Paro to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS file. It updates the project's credit list to acknowledge his patches and suggestions.

This commit improves the documentation for the `Request` and `PreparedRequest` classes in `requests/models.py`. It corrects the `PreparedRequest` docstring, which previously incorrectly described the `Request` class, and updates both to use proper cross-references.

This commit refactors the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to simplify data type checking by combining string and byte checks into a single condition. It also adjusts the class docstring formatting for improved readability.

This commit updates the CodeQL security analysis workflow to use version 2.22.1 of the github/codeql-action. It ensures the automated code scanning process runs with the latest minor release, incorporating recent updates and improvements to the analysis tool.

This commit removes the `__attrs__` attribute from the `Session` class in `requests/sessions.py`. This change likely fixes an issue where the session object failed to serialize correctly or caused unexpected behavior during copying or pickling.

This commit corrects a broken test in the TestRequests class that verifies the fallback to latin-1 encoding for HTTP response reasons. It ensures the test properly handles byte strings and decodes them before asserting the error message, fixing a failure discovered during a branch merge.

The setup script now derives the package version directly from the installed requests library instead of using a hardcoded string. This ensures the version number automatically matches the underlying dependency.

This commit removes a commented-out staticmethod decorator from the HTTPAdapter class in the requests library. It cleans up the codebase by deleting an unused annotation, with no change to the library's runtime behavior.

This commit updates the project documentation to clarify that Python 3.7 is not yet officially supported. It corrects the supported version range in the README to end at Python 3.6, preventing users from assuming full compatibility with the newer release.

This commit corrects a documentation error in the README where the example for PATCH requests incorrectly displayed the `post` method. It updates the example to properly reference the `patch` function, ensuring users see the correct syntax for sending PATCH requests.

This commit adds a new requirements file to define dependencies for continuous integration and development environments. It lists testing and linting tools such as nose, mock, and pyflakes, along with gevent, to standardize the project's tooling setup.

This commit updates the README documentation to reflect support for multipart file uploads. It adds a feature bullet point and updates the function signatures for `request.put` and `request.post` to include a `files` parameter, clarifying how to pass file objects for upload.
This commit corrects a typo in the advanced user documentation. It fixes a missing space in the phrase "sent off to a server" within the `docs/user/advanced.rst` file.

This commit updates the documentation structure by renaming the history section to "Release History" and the updates page to "Community Updates." It also adds a new "Software Updates" section that includes the release history file.

This commit updates the documentation to restore Twitter as a support channel for the Requests library. It adds a section to the support page encouraging users to tweet specific maintainers, while removing the outdated Twitter update section from the releases page.

This commit updates the project's author list in AUTHORS.rst. It changes the maintainer group title from "Keepers of the Three Crystals" to "Keepers of the Four Crystals" and adds Nate Prewitt to the list of contributors.

This commit updates the test suite to stop relying on an external server for connection error tests. It modifies the `test_connection_error_invalid_port` method in `test_requests.py` to target a local address instead, ensuring tests run reliably without external network dependencies.

This commit introduces the new `oreos` package, which provides utilities for parsing and managing HTTP cookies. It includes a `MultiDict` structure for handling multiple values per key and a `SimpleCookie` class for decoding cookie strings. The `dict_from_string` function in `core.py` converts raw cookie data into a structured dictionary.

This commit refactors the test suite by moving the TestTestServer class from the general utilities test file into a dedicated test_testserver.py module. This change organizes the codebase by separating server-specific tests from other utility tests, improving maintainability without altering any functional behavior.

This change modifies the HTTPAdapter class in the requests module to always default the proxy scheme to HTTP. Previously, the system attempted to infer the scheme from the target URL, which could lead to unexpected behavior. Now, proxy connections consistently use the HTTP protocol regardless of the destination URL's scheme.

The commit removes the test suite script, which previously ran tox, generated coverage reports, and executed pylint checks. This eliminates the automated testing and linting workflow from the repository.
This commit fixes a minor formatting error in the README.rst documentation. It removes an unnecessary space before the double colon in the usage section, ensuring the text renders correctly.
