This commit updates the contribution guide in the README to help new users understand the pull request process. It adds a direct link to GitHub's documentation for creating pull requests from a fork, making the instructions clearer for contributors unfamiliar with the workflow.

This commit updates the `get` method in the `RequestsCookieJar` class to allow users to retrieve cookies using a dictionary-like syntax with a default value. It changes the argument order so the default value is the second parameter, matching standard Python dictionary behavior.

This commit corrects a syntax error in the project's dependency configuration by removing an unintended extra parenthesis. It also adds the `httpbin` and `trustme` packages to the test dependency group in `pyproject.toml`.

This commit fixes a documentation build error in the `requests` library where unescaped asterisks in docstrings caused Sphinx to fail. It updates the `Session` class methods to properly escape the `**kwargs` parameter notation, ensuring the API documentation generates correctly.

This commit updates the Quickstart documentation for the `Response.json()` method. It clarifies that the method raises an error for empty or invalid JSON responses and warns that successful decoding does not guarantee a successful HTTP status code.

This commit removes unused comments and commented-out code from the Request class in requests/core.py. It cleans up the _get_opener method by deleting obsolete lines related to password managers and URL fetching. No functional behavior is changed.
This commit removes the Travis CI build status badge from the project's README. It updates the documentation to reflect the removal of the continuous integration service link.
This commit updates the project documentation to remove the claim that the library runs well on PyPy. The change clarifies the official Python version support in the README.
This commit updates the copyright year in the documentation configuration from 2017 to 2018. It modifies the copyright string in the `docs/conf.py` file to reflect the current year.

This commit updates the test suite for the requests library to fix a test failure in safe mode. It modifies the test_safe_mode method within the RequestsTestSuite class to correctly assert that a timeout exception is raised when a request exceeds the specified limit.

This commit documents that the `Response.iter_lines` method in the `requests` library is not reentrant safe. It warns users that calling the method multiple times can cause data loss and advises saving the iterator for reuse instead.

This commit removes the default Content-Length header from GET requests in the PreparedRequest class. Previously, GET requests incorrectly included a Content-Length of zero, which could cause issues with certain servers. Now, the header is only added for POST and PUT requests.

This commit updates the project roadmap in the README to include support for cookies. It signals that the application will soon handle cookie data, a feature previously absent from the planned development list.

The Request class in requests/core.py now supports basic POST requests by initializing data as a dictionary and encoding form data. This change replaces a previous hardcoded test URL with dynamic request handling using urllib2.
This commit updates the project's README documentation. It adds a period to the end of the main description sentence for the Requests library.

This commit improves the readability of the user documentation by wrapping long lines in the advanced and quickstart guides. It adjusts the text formatting in the advanced.rst and quickstart.rst files to ensure consistent line lengths.
The test runner is switched from pytest to detox to improve test isolation. The Makefile updates the test command to invoke detox, and the requirements file adds the necessary dependencies.
This commit updates the vulnerability reporting documentation to list Jeremy Cline as the new contact person, replacing the previous contact. It also fixes a missing newline at the end of the file.

This commit updates the project changelog to document a breaking change in the Session module. It clarifies that cookies set on individual requests are no longer persisted to the Session object, preventing unexpected state retention.

This commit ensures that HTTP connections are properly returned to the connection pool after a request is redirected. It modifies the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to release the underlying connection, preventing resource leaks during redirect handling.

This commit rewrites the quickstart documentation to improve clarity and correct grammatical errors. It updates the introductory text and simplifies the first example to focus on importing the module and making a basic request.

This commit modifies the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to ensure only the URL path is sent to servers. It replaces the internal `_build_url` method with a `full_url` property and updates the response construction logic to use this new attribute.

This commit updates the MANIFEST.in file to remove a reference to the non-existent pytest.ini file. This ensures the package build process does not attempt to include a missing file, preventing potential packaging errors.

This commit adds Sphinx and its dependencies to the project's requirements files to support documentation generation. It updates the dependency list to include specific versions of Sphinx, Alabaster, and other related packages.

This commit renames the `eager_mode` configuration option to `danger_mode` across the `requests` library. It updates the `Request` class and default settings to use the new name, ensuring that immediate error raising behavior is controlled by the updated key.

This commit fixes a parsing error in the `parse_header_links` function within `requests/utils.py`. It corrects how the function splits header values, ensuring that links separated by commas followed by spaces and angle brackets are parsed correctly.

This commit removes outdated test configuration files, including coverage settings and tox definitions, to clean up the repository after a merge. It updates the Makefile to use pytest directly instead of the deprecated setup.py test command.

This commit updates the `requests` library's `Session` and `SessionRedirectMixin` classes to use modern string formatting methods instead of legacy percent-style formatting. It improves the clarity of error messages for redirect limits and missing connection adapters by using more precise formatting options.

This commit updates the project's README to replace placeholder text with a more engaging overview and concrete usage examples. It introduces the `requests` module and demonstrates how to perform HTTP requests using methods like `get`, `put`, `post`, and `delete`.

This commit modifies the `rebuild_proxies` method in `requests/sessions.py` to prevent proxy repopulation when the environment is not trusted. It ensures that proxy settings are only inherited from the environment if the `trust_env` flag is enabled, avoiding unexpected proxy behavior for users who have disabled environment trust.

The test suite in test_requests.py now uses the httpbin.org service for all HTTP and HTTPS request tests. This change replaces hardcoded URLs with helper functions to ensure consistent and reliable test endpoints.

This commit fixes a minor typo in the `Response` class within the `requests` module. It removes two unnecessary blank lines from the source code, which does not change any user-facing behavior or functionality.

This commit updates the copyright link in the documentation configuration to point to a specific open projects page. It ensures the project attribution in the generated docs directs users to the correct URL for Kenneth Reitz's work.

This documentation update clarifies that `Response.raw.read()` returns bytes rather than a string, correcting the example output in the quickstart guide. It also standardizes the quote style for URLs in the request examples.

This commit fixes the quick start documentation by adding the missing `allow_redirects` parameter to the `requests.post` example. This ensures users see the correct syntax for explicitly enabling redirects when using POST requests.

This commit updates the setup.py script to recognize the "publish" and "test" commands when they appear anywhere in the command-line arguments, rather than only as the final argument. This ensures the corresponding build and test scripts execute correctly regardless of argument order.

This commit updates the contributing documentation to correct a reference label for the PEP 8 style guide. It ensures the link target is properly formatted with a space, improving the accuracy of the internal documentation links.

This commit enables colored output for the test suite by adding the `--with-color` flag to the `nosetests` command in the Makefile. It also updates the dependency list in `reqs.txt` to use the `rudolf2` package instead of `rudolf`.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library from 0.7.2 to 0.8.0. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the package's initialization file to reflect the new release.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to replace outdated references to the deprecated timeline.json endpoint with the current GitHub API events URL. It ensures the examples in the user guide reflect the correct, functional API endpoint for fetching data.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to use Python 3-compatible syntax for printing a URL. It changes the example command to include parentheses around the variable, ensuring the code snippet runs correctly in modern Python environments.

This commit updates the README documentation to accurately reflect the return value of the request functions. It replaces the generic placeholder with the specific response object users actually receive, ensuring the examples match the library's behavior.

This commit updates the project history file to document changes in version 1.2.0. It highlights fixes for cookie handling, OAuth 1 data transmission, and DigestAuth errors, alongside improvements to hook dispatching and proxy support.

This commit updates the GitHub issue template to improve clarity for users reporting problems. It changes the instruction for pasting diagnostic output from "insert here" to "paste here" within the requests module documentation.

This commit updates the Session class in requests/sessions.py to improve cookie handling. It ensures that when a dictionary of cookies is passed to a request, those values are merged into the session's existing cookie jar rather than replacing it. This prevents the loss of previously stored cookies during subsequent requests.

This commit modifies the `Request.send` method in `requests/models.py` to only validate private certificates when the `verify` option is enabled. It also updates the certificate type check to use length comparison instead of a strict type check.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 2.4.3. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the package's initialization file to reflect the new release.
This commit updates the project's release history to document the upgrade of the bundled urllib3 library to version 1.13.1. It also records the initial update to version 1.13 in the changelog.

This commit introduces a new Makefile to standardize project workflows. It defines targets for installing dependencies, running tests, and building documentation, simplifying common development tasks.

This commit updates the GitHub issue template to replace the previous diagnostic instructions with a structured format. It introduces sections for expected results, actual results, and reproduction steps to help users provide clearer bug reports.

This commit corrects a misleading comment in the OAuth1 class and removes the logic that overwrites the Content-Type header for multipart requests. Users relying on custom multipart headers will now see them preserved instead of being replaced.

This commit fixes Python 3 compatibility errors in the `Request` class within `requests/models.py` by ensuring file fields are converted to lists before processing. It also removes the verbose flag from the test command in the Makefile.

This commit updates the project's metadata in setup.py to declare compatibility with Python 3.2 and 3.3. It adds the corresponding classifiers so that package indexes correctly display support for these newer Python versions.

The publish workflow now uses the artifact ID to download build outputs instead of relying on a generic name, ensuring the correct files are retrieved. This update also upgrades the download action to version 5.0.0 and adds credential persistence restrictions to the checkout step for improved security.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the project's author list. It updates the name of a contributor in the AUTHORS file from "Jeremy Selie" to "Jeremy Selier."

This commit adds documentation to the quickstart guide explaining how to send multiple files in a single request. It demonstrates using a list of tuples for the files parameter to upload multiple images to an HTML form.

This commit updates the `resolve_redirects` method in `requests/sessions.py` to correctly handle HTTP 301 responses. It ensures that a POST request receiving a 301 status code is converted to a GET request, aligning with standard browser behavior.

This commit fixes a bug in the requests library where the status code alias for 200 was incorrectly set to a literal backslash character. It updates the status_codes module to skip aliases starting with a backslash, preventing invalid attribute names from being created.

This commit updates the test suite to verify that httpbin correctly returns multiple values for a single form field. It modifies the test_urlencoded_post_query_multivalued_and_data method within the RequestsTestSuite class to expect a list of values instead of a single string.

This commit removes incorrect `__all__` definitions from the `requests.api` and `requests.async` modules. It fixes a bug where the library incorrectly exposed internal symbols, ensuring that only the intended public API functions are available to users.

This commit adds documentation to the advanced user guide explaining how to use `contextlib.closing` with streamed requests. It clarifies that this pattern ensures the connection is properly released back to the pool, preventing inefficiency when response bodies are only partially read.

Removes the setup.cfg file, which previously configured the build system to mark the package as universal for both Python 2 and 3. This change stops the project from declaring compatibility with Python 2 during the wheel build process.

This documentation update clarifies Python 3 support status in the community FAQ. It replaces a vague statement with a direct link to the list of supported interpreters, helping users quickly find compatibility details.

This commit removes the unused `is_error` parameter from the `Request._build_response` method in the `requests` module. It also eliminates the logic that previously set an `error` attribute on the response object when that flag was true.

This commit updates the equality test for the CaseInsensitiveDict class to verify that comparing the dictionary to an unrelated object returns False, rather than checking for a NotImplemented return value. This ensures the test correctly validates the user-visible behavior of the inequality operator.

This commit fixes two spelling errors in the documentation of the `requests.async` module. It corrects the module name and the word "asynchronous" in the description, ensuring the text is accurate for users reading the documentation.

This commit updates the `Session.send` method in the `requests` library to apply correct default values for stream, verify, and proxies parameters. It also removes an obsolete internal argument and updates the test suite to verify that hooks receive the expected request arguments.

This commit refactors the `SessionRedirectMixin` class in `requests/sessions.py` to simplify how the `Cookie` header is removed during redirects. It replaces a try-except block with a direct dictionary pop operation and removes an unnecessary return statement from the `rebuild_auth` method.

This commit updates the Response class in requests/models.py to handle changes in the urllib3 API by replacing IncompleteRead exceptions with ProtocolError. It removes the IncompleteRead import from requests/compat.py and adds a test to verify that socket errors are handled correctly during content iteration.

The `get_netrc_auth` function in `requests.utils` now ignores empty default entries in the netrc file. Previously, a blank default line could cause the function to return an empty credential tuple instead of `None`. This fix ensures that only valid, non-empty credentials are returned.
This commit adds Richard Boulton to the project's list of contributors. It updates the AUTHORS file to include his name under the "Patches and Suggestions" section.
This commit adds chardet as a required dependency for the chardet package. It ensures the library is available for character encoding detection.

This commit renames the dummyserver module to testserver to better reflect its purpose as a basic socket server for unit testing. It updates the corresponding test class in test_requests.py and adjusts the Server class documentation to clarify its role.

This commit updates the project's dependency specifications to include newer versions of testing and web framework libraries. It introduces a new file for freezing requirements and refreshes the main requirements list to ensure consistent environment setup.

Fixes a bug in the `Request` class where HTTP handlers were incorrectly concatenated instead of extended, potentially causing duplicate handler entries. This change ensures the `_get_opener` method properly appends new handlers to the existing list.

This commit removes the bundled chardet package from the requests library, eliminating the internal character encoding detection module. Users will no longer have access to the detect function or related prober classes within the requests namespace.

This commit corrects inconsistent whitespace in several documentation files, including the theme README and support guide. It standardizes indentation in code examples and text lists to improve visual consistency. No functional behavior is changed.

This commit updates the `requests` package to import `urllib3` directly from the global namespace instead of from the bundled `packages` directory. It also adjusts the test suite to import `urllib3` without the package alias, ensuring consistent dependency resolution.

The documentation sidebar now displays "Donate" instead of "Support Requests" for the donation section. This change updates the user-facing label in the sidebarintro.html template to better reflect the action.

This commit fixes a grammatical error in the advanced user documentation for the Requests library. It removes a redundant word from the description of custom authentication mechanisms, improving the clarity of the text.
This commit updates documentation links and text in the README and docs. It changes the download badge to show monthly counts and corrects the recommended Python version to 3.6 in the FAQ.

This commit updates the project's README to list PATCH requests and proxy support as available features. It also replaces outdated example URLs and credentials with new ones for the basic authentication demonstration.

This change makes `ContentDecodingError` a subclass of `BaseHTTPError` in the `requests` module. Users will no longer need to catch the new exception separately, as it is now compatible with existing `HTTPError` handling.

The `Response` class in `requests.models` now supports the context manager protocol, allowing users to use it directly in a `with` statement. This change removes the need to manually wrap response objects with `contextlib.closing()` to ensure proper resource cleanup.

This commit adds support for HTTP digest authentication and introduces response hooks to the requests library. It modifies the HTTPAdapter to attach request context and dispatch hooks, while updating the PreparedRequest and HTTPDigestAuth classes to handle the new authentication flow.

The lock-issues workflow now only runs on the main psf repository, preventing it from executing on forks. This change stops the automated issue-locking behavior from triggering in forked copies of the project.
This commit adds Bob Carroll to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS.rst file. It updates the project's attribution records to include his name and contact information.

This update to the HTTPAdapter class in the requests module enables per-host proxy configuration. It allows users to specify proxies for specific hostnames, which take precedence over general scheme-based proxies when making requests.

This commit removes unused logging imports and logger instances from the `requests` library. It cleans up the `auth` and `models` modules by deleting the `logging` import and the `log` variable, which had no active usage.

This commit changes the base class of the `BaseSSLError` exception in the `connectionpool` module from `Exception` to `BaseException`. This ensures that SSL errors are not caught by generic exception handlers, allowing them to propagate as intended.

This commit introduces a new dispatch function in the requests.auth module to standardize how authentication credentials are processed. It allows users to specify authentication types using simple strings like "basic" or "digest," which are automatically mapped to the appropriate handler functions.

This commit reverts the automatic detection of system CA certificate paths in the setup.py file. It restores the behavior where the certifi package is always required as a dependency, preventing potential SSL verification issues on platforms where the system bundle is not automatically detected.

This commit updates the package metadata in setup.py to represent the project classifiers as a list rather than a tuple. This change ensures the data structure aligns with standard Python conventions for this type of configuration.

This commit updates the changelog for version 2.2.0, documenting new API changes and bug fixes. It highlights the introduction of a new ContentDecodingError exception and resolves issues related to proxy handling, netrc authentication, and cookie persistence.
This commit adds Aram Dulyan to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS file. It updates the project's credit list to acknowledge a new author.
This commit adds Rick Mak to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS file. It updates the project's credit list to acknowledge his contributions.

This commit updates the copyright year from 2011 to 2012 across the project. It modifies the license file, documentation configuration, and the main package initialization module to reflect the new year.
This commit updates the project's history log by adding blank lines to the file. It adjusts the formatting of the changelog without altering any functional code or user-facing behavior.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar templates to wrap the "Requests Pro" button in a paragraph element. This change ensures the promotional link displays with proper spacing and formatting in the rendered documentation.

This commit refactors gzip decompression logic by moving it from the Response class into a new utility function named decode_gzip. It replaces direct zlib calls with this helper to improve code organization and reusability within the requests library.

This commit updates the default headers in the requests.defaults module to comply with PEP 8 style guidelines. It changes the list of accepted encodings to a tuple, removing unnecessary whitespace and brackets. No functional behavior is altered.

This commit moves hook execution into the internal event loop for the Request class in requests/models.py. It ensures pre-request, response, and post-request hooks are dispatched via a dedicated function, allowing hooks to modify the request or response objects directly during the request lifecycle.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` now converts the method argument to a string before passing it to the session. This ensures the HTTP method is handled consistently, preventing potential errors when non-string types are provided.

The `merge_setting` function in `requests/sessions.py` previously raised a `RuntimeError` on Python 3 when removing keys with `None` values during dictionary iteration. This commit fixes the crash by collecting the keys to delete before modifying the dictionary.

This commit updates the authentication documentation to clarify that the library supports OAuth 2, not just OAuth 1. It adds a new section with direct links to specific OAuth 2 workflow guides to improve user discoverability.

This commit adds a test to the CookieTests class in tests/test_cookies.py to verify that cookies set by a 302 redirect response are correctly processed and retained. It ensures that subsequent requests using these cookies include both the original and new values.

This commit fixes a Python 2 compatibility issue in the `Request` class where string data was incorrectly identified due to `str` being rebound to `unicode`. It ensures the `send` method correctly detects byte strings by checking against the original built-in `str` type.

This commit fixes a bug in the requests/async.py module where the system could exhaust available sockets before processing responses. It ensures the send function always passes the prefetch flag to the underlying pool, preventing resource exhaustion during asynchronous request handling.

The Request class in requests/models.py now automatically converts legacy list or tuple authentication inputs into the new function-based format. This change ensures that authentication is correctly applied during the send process, fixing issues where credentials were ignored.

This commit updates the HTTPAdapter and SessionRedirectMixin to use the geturl method for URL reconstruction. This ensures the URL scheme is consistently lowercased, preventing potential issues with case-sensitive URL handling during requests and redirects.

This commit removes unused imports and debug print statements from the Request class in requests/models.py. It cleans up the codebase by eliminating unnecessary dependencies and leftover logging code that did not affect user-facing behavior.

This commit adds the idna library to the requests package's vendored dependencies. It updates the setup configuration to include the new module and ensures the package correctly imports idna, falling back to the system version if the vendored copy is unavailable.

This commit updates the project history to document a new feature in the Response class. It notes that the text property will now automatically guess the encoding using chardet if no explicit encoding is set.

This commit updates the repository's funding configuration to include the Python Software Foundation as a GitHub sponsor. It modifies the FUNDING.yml file to display the PSF's GitHub profile in the funding section.

This commit fixes an issue where all session cookies were incorrectly attached to every response object. It removes the line in the `resolve_redirects` method of the `SessionRedirectMixin` class that copied the entire session cookie jar to the response.

This commit applies minor PEP-8 formatting adjustments to the `Request` class in `requests/models.py`. It restructures the conditional logic within the `_build_response` method to improve code readability without altering the underlying behavior.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to correct the example output for GitHub pagination link headers. It removes outdated rate limit details and adds a proper code block marker to ensure the text renders correctly in the final documentation.

This commit clarifies the distinction between raw byte data and decoded text in the `requests` library. The `Response.content` property now strictly returns bytes, while a new `Response.text` property provides the decoded unicode string. This change removes the previous automatic decoding behavior from `iter_content` and `content`.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to a newer version, incorporating two unspecified fixes. The changes primarily affect the connection pool and exception handling modules, including updates to HTTPConnectionPool and PoolManager.

This commit updates the community documentation to include a new entry for the Requests-Threads library. It describes how this tool enables asynchronous programming with the Requests library by returning Twisted Deferreds instead of standard response objects.

This commit introduces a backup of the legacy request handling logic, including the `old_request` method and `OldRequest` class. It preserves the previous behavior for constructing and sending requests, ensuring compatibility with older code patterns.

This commit fixes a documentation error in the quickstart guide where the prerequisite library was incorrectly listed as Requests instead of Tablib. It updates the installation and update instructions in the user documentation to reference the correct package.

This commit updates the API documentation to include a new section for authentication classes. It adds references to the base class and specific authentication types within the requests.auth module, making these components visible in the generated API reference.

This commit updates the test file to import the requests library and execute a basic HTTP request to verify header retrieval. It also instantiates a new Request object, likely to support upcoming test cases for the requests module.

The Settings class in requests/config.py is re-implemented as a singleton to manage global configuration state. This change replaces the previous settings module, ensuring that configuration values like timeout are shared consistently across the application.

This commit updates the project history to document version 0.9.2, which includes an asynchronous send method and SSL verification fixes. It also notes improvements to chunk stream handling, session arguments, and various bug fixes in HTTP authentication and response iteration.

In the CookieTests class, the test for disabled cookie persistence now uses a direct identity check instead of the assertIsNone method. This change resolves a build failure by ensuring the assertion correctly verifies that the cookie value is None.

This commit disables the test for HTTP 302 redirect handling in the RequestsTestCase class within test_requests.py. The test is commented out rather than removed, likely to temporarily exclude it from the test suite.

This commit adds several testing dependencies, including pytest and its plugins, to the project's requirements file. It ensures the necessary tools for running and measuring test coverage are installed alongside the main package.

This commit fixes a broken hyperlink in the community recommendations documentation. It updates the reference to the Requests-Threads project in the `docs/community/recommended.rst` file to ensure the link resolves correctly.

This commit replaces a simple script in test_requests.py with a formal test suite. It introduces the RequestsTestSuite class to verify basic HTTP and HTTPS requests, as well as error handling for invalid URLs.

This commit updates the project dependencies to include the rudolf2 package and removes the color output option from the test command in the Makefile. These changes affect the build and testing environment for the application.

This commit updates the project's README documentation to organize API methods under specific HTTP request type headings. It adds sections for GET, HEAD, PUT, and DELETE requests, while also correcting a typo in the POST request label.

This commit adds a test to verify that the text response server correctly handles HTTP responses with specific headers and body content. It ensures that the server returns the expected status code, text, and Content-Length header when a request is made.

This commit corrects several spelling and grammar errors in the project's history log. It updates the changelog to accurately describe features like the new exception hierarchy and asynchronous send method.

This commit updates the project's README to center the main description text. It wraps the introductory sentence in a span element with center alignment to improve the visual layout of the documentation.

This commit updates the project documentation to reflect the addition of a seventh main interface method. It corrects the API reference to list seven methods instead of six and updates the class references for the Response object.

This commit adds a default null logging handler to the requests package to prevent "No handler found" warnings. It also removes the `store_cookies` default setting and updates the `Request` class to use a module-level logger.

This commit adds documentation to the quickstart guide explaining how to use the timeout parameter in the requests library. It clarifies that this setting limits the connection wait time but does not affect the duration of the response body download.

This commit fixes a bug in the HTTPAdapter where the Host header was incorrectly skipped during chunked uploads. It ensures the header is only omitted if explicitly provided by the user, preventing missing headers in requests. New tests verify this behavior for both default and specified host headers.

The `iter_lines` method in the `Response` class now accepts a `chunk_size` parameter, allowing users to control the size of data chunks processed during iteration. This change simplifies the internal logic by passing the user-defined value directly to `iter_content` instead of using a hardcoded default.

This commit updates the documentation for the `Response` class in the `requests` library to better explain the utility of the `encoding` attribute. It clarifies that users should manually set `r.encoding` after inspecting `r.content` when the response body specifies its own encoding, ensuring `r.text` decodes correctly.
This commit adds a testimonial from Armin Ronacher to the project documentation. It highlights the quality of the API design in the main index file.
The Makefile's lazy target no longer passes the color flag to the test runner. This removes colored output from the test results when running the lazy target.

This commit adds blank lines to the RequestsTestSuite class in test_requests.py. It improves the visual spacing between test methods for better readability. No functional behavior or logic is changed.

This commit fixes a grammatical error in the project's README documentation. It corrects the phrasing of a warning about using the Python standard library for HTTP, changing "use the" to "use of" for clarity.

This commit updates the pre-commit hook versions and adds a new dependabot configuration to automatically manage pre-commit updates. It also introduces additional linting checks for case conflicts, merge conflicts, TOML files, and mixed line endings.

This commit adds a new `docs` target to the Makefile, allowing users to build the project's HTML documentation. It also introduces a `docs/requirements.txt` file to manage the necessary Sphinx dependencies for the build process.

This commit fixes a bug in the CaseInsensitiveDict class where deleting a key failed if the case did not match the stored key. It updates the __delitem__ method to resolve the correct key using the internal lower_keys mapping before deletion.

Adds a new `set_http_proxy` method to the `Session` class in `requests/sessions.py`. This provides a user-friendly way to configure HTTP and HTTPS proxies with simplified parameters, replacing the need to manually construct proxy dictionaries.
This commit adds a community photo to the documentation page for community updates. It modifies the `docs/community/updates.rst` file to include an image reference.

This commit updates the project history to document a fix for URL quoting issues in Python versions prior to 2.7. It also notes the addition of a new `r.iter_content` method for handling response data.

This commit updates the project's README file to fix the placement of HTML formatting tags. It moves the closing pre tag and alignment paragraph to the end of the document, ensuring the footer text displays correctly.

This commit updates the bundled chardet library to version 3.0.2 within the requests package. It refreshes the character encoding detection logic, including the detect function and various prober classes, to ensure accurate identification of text encodings.

This commit updates the requests library to support chardet version 7. It modifies the dependency specification in pyproject.toml and the version validation logic in the check_compatibility function to allow the newer release.

This commit updates the actions/checkout dependency from version 2.7.0 to 3.5.3 in the project's GitHub Actions workflows. It ensures the CI pipeline uses the latest major version of the checkout action for the codeql-analysis and run-tests workflows.

The `select_proxy` function in `requests/utils.py` now supports an 'all' key to define a default proxy for any scheme or host. This ensures consistent proxy selection when reading environment variables or applying user-defined proxy settings.

This commit simplifies the `MockRequest` class in `requests/cookies.py` by removing logic that checked response history for origin hosts and unverifiable status. It also updates `Session` in `requests/sessions.py` to persist cookies after redirects and removes an outdated parameter description from `requests/api.py`.

This commit updates the project's build and test workflows to use Pipenv instead of standard pip. It modifies the Makefile to run installation, testing, and linting commands within the Pipenv environment, ensuring consistent dependency management.

This commit fixes a typo in the documentation for the `Response` class in `requests/models.py`. It corrects the spelling of "solely" in the description of the `text` property, ensuring the documentation is accurate.

This change updates the internal storage of the CaseInsensitiveDict class to use an ordered dictionary instead of a standard dictionary. This ensures that the insertion order of keys is preserved when iterating over the dictionary, providing predictable ordering for users.

This commit restricts the pytest dependency to versions below 4.1 in the Pipfile to prevent compatibility issues. It also updates the corresponding lock file and corrects the Python version string formatting in the Travis CI configuration.

This commit updates the `requests` package to use absolute imports instead of relative ones. It modifies the `__init__.py` files in the main module and its subpackages to ensure consistent module resolution.

This commit modifies the `send` method in `requests/adapters.py` to simplify timeout handling. It removes conditional logic that previously prevented passing a `None` timeout, ensuring the timeout value is always forwarded directly to the underlying connection.

This commit adds a test to the TestRequests class in tests/test_requests.py to verify that the PoolManager class remains importable from the requests.packages.urllib3.poolmanager module. It ensures this legacy import path continues to function for users who rely on it.

This commit updates the test suite for the requests module to ensure compatibility with Python 3. It corrects the `test_DIGEST_STREAM` method in `RequestsTestCase` by comparing raw byte data directly instead of converting it to strings, which prevents type errors during test execution.
This commit updates the internal build identifier for the requests package. It changes the version constant in the main module to reflect a new build number.

This commit re-enables the previously disabled test_session_pickling method within the RequestsTestCase class in test_requests.py. It verifies that a requests.Session object can be successfully pickled and unpickled while retaining its functionality for sending HTTP requests.

This commit updates the test suite for the requests module to fix a failure in the response iterability test. It introduces a mock read function that correctly handles the decode_content parameter, ensuring the test passes when using StringIO objects.

This commit updates the actions/setup-python dependency from version 6.2.0 to 6.3.0 across all GitHub Actions workflows. It ensures the CI/CD pipelines use the latest minor release of the Python setup action.

This commit prevents URLs from being lowercased before parsing, as the parsing function already handles lowercasing the scheme and hostname. This change fixes potential issues with case-sensitive URL components in the HTTPAdapter and select_proxy functions.

The Session class now stores transport adapters in an ordered dictionary to preserve the sequence in which they are mounted. This ensures that the most recently mounted adapter takes precedence when resolving requests, fixing potential routing conflicts.

This commit renames the `prefetch` parameter to `stream` across the `requests` library, including `HTTPAdapter`, `Session`, and `Response` classes. It inverts the logic so that setting `stream` to `False` triggers immediate content download, aligning the API with standard streaming conventions.

This commit fixes an issue in the `PreparedRequest` class where a zero-length body incorrectly triggered chunked transfer encoding. It updates the `prepare_body` method to only set the `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` header when the content length is explicitly null, preventing unnecessary headers for empty requests.
This commit removes unused redirect status code definitions from the requests models module. It also adds numeric value comments to the remaining redirect codes in the sessions module for clarity.

This commit updates the `Request` class in `requests/core.py` to use Python 3-compatible exception syntax. It fixes a syntax error that would prevent the module from running on Python 3 by replacing the old comma-based exception handling with the `as` keyword.
This commit updates the project's README documentation. It replaces the license badge with a link to the maintainer's website and adjusts the surrounding layout spacing.
This commit adds Johnny Goodnow to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS.rst file. It updates the project's attribution records to include a new name under the "Patches and Suggestions" section.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar templates to use secure HTTPS links for all translated versions of the project. Users will now access the French, German, Japanese, and other language pages over an encrypted connection instead of plain HTTP.

This commit renames the "keepalive" configuration key to "keep_alive" in the requests library's default settings. Users accessing this specific option in the configuration dictionary will now need to use the new underscore-separated name.

This commit corrects a typo in a comment within the `super_len` function in `requests/utils.py`. It updates the example reference from `cStringIO.StringI` to `cStringIO.StringIO` for accuracy. No functional behavior is changed.

This commit removes a debug script tag from the documentation layout template. It eliminates a dependency on a local WeInRe server, preventing potential connection errors or console noise for users viewing the docs. The change affects the `layout.html` file within the `kr` theme.

The lint workflow now runs on Ubuntu 24.04 instead of the unsupported Ubuntu 20.04. This update ensures the continuous integration environment remains compatible with current GitHub Actions standards.
This commit adds a link to a blog post about sending JSON data with the Requests library. The update is made to the community documentation page, specifically the "Articles & Talks" section.

This commit updates the project history file to document the upcoming 1.0.0 release. It highlights major changes including a massive refactor, the introduction of connection adapters, and the adoption of standard library logging.

This commit fixes typos in the project's documentation by correcting the domain name in example URLs. It ensures the README accurately references the correct endpoint for basic authentication examples.

This commit removes the bundled oauthlib package and the associated OAuth helper module from the requests library. Users will no longer have access to the built-in OAuth 1.0 and 2.0 client and server utilities.

This commit updates the cookie parameter test in the RequestsTestCase class to ensure compatibility with Python 2.6. It replaces the assertIn method with a standard assertTrue check, as the former was not available in that older Python version.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to clarify that a new callback is used to hijack request arguments. It also adds a prompt to test the implementation. The changes are limited to the advanced documentation file.

The publishing process for the Requests library now uses the twine tool instead of the deprecated setup.py upload commands. This change updates the Makefile to build source and wheel distributions before uploading them, ensuring compatibility with modern PyPI requirements.
This commit updates the project's README to change the alignment of the logo image from the right side to the center. The change affects the visual presentation of the documentation's front page.

This commit removes the custom Sphinx themes previously used for documentation styling. It deletes the theme configuration files and assets from the docs directory, simplifying the project's documentation setup.

The test_cookie_jar method in test_requests.py now uses httpbin.org endpoints instead of an external cookie testing site. This change updates the test to verify cookie setting and retrieval against a more reliable, standard testing service.

This release updates the requests library to version 2.28.1, improving the speed of the `iter_content` function by optimizing its internal iteration logic. It also adds compatibility with newer versions of the chardet and charset-normalizer dependencies.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Response.iter_content` method of the `requests` library where chunked HTTP responses were not parsed correctly. It ensures that carriage return and line feed characters are properly discarded after reading each chunk, preventing data corruption or parsing errors.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar template to reflect the rebranding from Gittip to Gratipay. It also increases the width of the donation button from 48 to 60 pixels to improve its appearance.

This commit removes the unused `httpbin` parameter from several test methods in the `TestRequests` class within `tests/test_requests.py`. It cleans up the test signatures for proxy authentication and session adapter prefix matching tests, which did not require the mocked HTTP endpoint.

This commit updates the test for transfer encoding removal on redirects to manually construct a Response object instead of sending a request. This change ensures the test correctly validates the behavior of the requests module's redirect handling logic.

This commit removes the global logging configuration from the requests core module. It stops the library from automatically setting up basic logging for urllib3, preventing unexpected log output for users.

This commit adds a `rebuild_proxies` method to the `SessionRedirectMixin` class in `requests/sessions.py`. It ensures that proxy settings and authentication credentials are correctly re-evaluated and applied when a request is redirected.

This commit updates the project's README to change the documentation description to "fantastic" and add a "limited time only" note. It also renames the contribution section header to "How to Contribute."

This commit removes the internal configuration module and its Settings class, which previously managed global request defaults. The functionality is consolidated into the defaults module, simplifying how users access and modify standard request settings.
The test suite no longer displays colored output when running the requests tests. This change removes the color flag from the Makefile to disable rudolf until it behaves correctly.

This commit updates the test suite for the requests extension to ensure compatibility with Python 2.6. It replaces the assertIn and assertNotIn methods, which were introduced in Python 2.7, with standard assertTrue checks in the RequestsTestSuite class.

The `register_hook` method in the `Request` class now accepts a list, tuple, or set of hooks, allowing multiple hooks to be registered at once. This change prevents errors when users pass a collection of hooks instead of a single callable. A regression test was added to verify this behavior.

This commit refactors the cookie handling system to use the standard library's CookieJar, replacing the previous custom implementation. It introduces a new RequestsCookieJar class in requests/cookies.py to manage cookie storage and retrieval, ensuring better compatibility and standardization.

This commit corrects inconsistent indentation in the `Request` class within `requests/models.py`. It replaces mixed tabs and spaces with standard spaces in the `send` method to ensure consistent code formatting.

This commit updates the GitHub issue template to simplify the instructions for users. It changes the wording to "Run this command" and adds indentation to the example command in the requests module documentation.

This commit corrects a spelling error in the documentation index, changing the section header from "Testimonals" to "Testimonials." It also updates the testimonial list to include an unnamed federal US institution alongside Twitter, Inc.

This commit improves JSON parsing in the `Response` class by detecting the correct UTF encoding when none is explicitly specified. It introduces a new utility function, `guess_json_utf`, to identify the encoding based on the initial bytes of the content, ensuring compliance with JSON standards.

This commit updates the project's metadata in setup.py to reflect supported Python versions. It removes the classifier for Python 2.6 and adds support for Python 3.5, ensuring the package correctly advertises its compatibility on distribution platforms.

This commit moves the response hook dispatch in the `Session.send` method to occur before the session follows any redirects. This ensures that user-defined hooks can inspect or modify the initial response before the client automatically handles the redirect chain.

This commit updates the Makefile to ignore the E128 flake8 error, which flags incorrect indentation on continuation lines. This change prevents the linter from reporting false positives for valid multi-line code structures in the requests module.

The `stream_untransfer` function in `requests/utils.py` now correctly handles Content-Encoding headers with mixed casing, such as "GZip" or "DEFLATE". This ensures that compressed response bodies are properly decompressed regardless of the header's capitalization, adhering to RFC 2616 standards.

This commit adds the project's README file, providing a high-level overview of the Requests library. It includes badges for version, license, and coverage, along with a brief description of the tool's purpose.

This commit removes the exclusion of the .idea/ directory from the .gitignore file. This change allows IDE configuration files to be tracked by version control, which may be necessary for team consistency or specific project requirements.

The OAuth1 class in requests/auth.py now correctly signs GET querystring parameters by passing the full URL to oauthlib. This fixes an issue where APIs relying on GET parameters would fail due to missing signatures.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to clarify how session parameters merge with request-level parameters. It explains that method-level values override session defaults and describes how to remove specific session keys by setting them to None.

This commit removes the deprecated `config` parameter from the `request` function in `requests/api.py` and the `Session` class in `requests/sessions.py`. Users will no longer be able to pass a configuration dictionary to these methods, simplifying the API surface.

The `select_proxy` function in `requests/utils.py` no longer raises an exception when processing URLs without a hostname, such as file paths. It now returns `None` for these cases instead of failing, allowing requests to proceed without proxy configuration.

The `register_hook` method in `requests.models` now validates that items in a list are callable before adding them to the hook registry. This prevents non-callable objects from being registered, which previously could cause errors during request execution. A regression test was added to ensure this validation remains in place.

This commit updates the `super_len` function in `requests.utils` to calculate string lengths as UTF-8 bytes when using urllib3 2.x, aligning with its new encoding behavior. It adds a version check in `requests.compat` to detect the urllib3 major version and ensures accurate content-length headers for string data.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar templates to correct the Requests-HTML project URL from a .com domain to a .org domain. It ensures users clicking the link in the sidebar are directed to the correct website.

This commit updates the actions/checkout dependency from version 6.0.2 to 7.0.0 across all GitHub Actions workflow files. It ensures the repository uses the latest major version of the checkout action for its CI/CD pipelines.

This commit updates the test suite for the test server to explicitly compare response bodies using Unicode strings. It ensures that assertions in the TestTestServer class correctly handle text data, preventing potential type mismatches during testing.

Adds tests for the `should_bypass_proxies` function to verify it correctly reads proxy bypass settings from the Windows registry. This ensures the utility properly identifies which URLs should bypass the proxy based on system configuration.

This commit updates the test suite for the `_basic_auth_str` function to verify that it correctly handles non-ASCII usernames and passwords. It ensures the generated authorization header matches the expected base64-encoded string for unicode inputs.

The Requests library now defines its own HTTPError class instead of relying on the standard library's urllib2 module. This change in requests/core.py allows the library to handle HTTP errors independently, providing a more consistent interface for users.

This commit modifies the `patched` function in `requests/async.py` to enforce safe mode for all asynchronous requests. It ensures the `safe_mode` configuration is always enabled, preventing potential unsafe operations during async execution.
Bumps the package version number in the requests module from 0.10.2 to 0.10.3. This update reflects a minor release change without altering any functional behavior or fixing specific bugs.

Adds tests to the RequestsTestCase class in test_requests.py to verify that the get_auth_from_url function correctly handles URL-encoded spaces and percent characters within credentials. These tests ensure that authentication data is parsed accurately from various URL formats.

This commit removes extraneous comments from the `rebuild_proxies` method within the `SessionRedirectMixin` class in `requests/sessions.py`. It does not alter any functional behavior or fix bugs, serving only to clean up the codebase.

This commit adds a test to the TestRequests class in tests/test_requests.py to verify that header order is preserved when using OrderedDict. It ensures that the prepare_request method maintains the specific sequence of headers, including updates to existing keys, during request preparation.

This change modifies the `Response.content` method in the `requests` library to return `None` when the status code is `None`, not just when it is zero. This prevents potential errors when handling responses that lack a status code.

This commit fixes an issue where SSL errors from urllib3 were not properly converted into Requests' SSLError exception. It updates the HTTPAdapter.send method to correctly raise the appropriate error type based on the urllib3 version.

This commit removes unused imports and redundant variable assignments in the PreparedRequest class and fixes an indentation error in the CaseInsensitiveDict copy method. These changes address static analysis warnings without altering the library's runtime behavior.

The `header_expand` function in `requests/utils.py` now explicitly handles cases where the input is `None`. This prevents potential errors when processing headers that have not been set, ensuring the function returns `None` instead of failing.

This commit updates the `catch_exceptions_if_in_safe_mode` decorator in `requests/safe_mode.py` to handle `socket.gaierror` exceptions. It prevents safe mode from failing to catch DNS resolution errors, ensuring that network issues are properly managed during request execution.
This commit fixes a minor documentation formatting error in the quickstart guide. It removes an unnecessary double dot from an admonition directive in the `docs/user/quickstart.rst` file.

The `dict_from_cookiejar` function in `requests/utils.py` now iterates directly over the cookie jar instead of using inefficient nested loops. This change improves performance when converting cookies to a dictionary.

This commit enables query parameters to be correctly applied to GET requests in the requests library. It introduces a helper method to manage authentication handlers and refactors the request sending logic within the Request class.

This commit updates the Flask documentation theme to improve the layout on small screens. It hides the sidebar and adjusts margins and widths in the small_flask.css file to ensure content fills the available space.

This commit adds support for three new HTTP status codes to the requests library's status_codes module. It enables users to recognize responses with codes 428, 429, and 431, which were previously undefined in the library.

This commit updates the security vulnerability reporting documentation in the requests project. It replaces the previous contact information for sigmavirus24 with new details for Seth, and updates the associated PGP key fingerprints.

This commit fixes an issue where the `max_redirects` setting was not preserved when serializing a `Session` object. By adding this attribute to the `Session` class's `__attrs__` list, the setting now correctly persists during serialization and deserialization processes.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to clarify how to use the `iter_content` method for streaming downloads. It specifies that the `chunk_size` parameter can be freely adjusted to better fit specific use cases, replacing the previous note that it was optional.
This commit removes the default timeout setting from the requests library's defaults module. Users will no longer have a predefined timeout value in the default configuration dictionary.
Updates the project documentation to reflect that the library has been installed over 80,000 times from PyPI, replacing the previous figure of 60,000. This change appears in the main index file.
This commit updates the project documentation to include Sony in the list of organizations that use the Requests library. The change modifies the index page to reflect this new user.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Request` class where the library would incorrectly follow redirects for non-30X status codes. It ensures that the `location` header is only processed when the response status code is a valid redirect status.

The HTTPDigestAuth class now stores authentication credentials and challenge details internally. This allows the object to automatically replay valid credentials on subsequent requests, preventing unnecessary 401 errors when the same instance is reused.

This refactoring extracts proxy selection logic from the HTTPAdapter class into a new utility function called select_proxy. It simplifies the request handling process by centralizing how the appropriate proxy is determined for a given URL.

This commit updates the package initialization to use absolute imports instead of relative ones, ensuring compatibility with Python 2.5. It modifies the `requests` module to explicitly import the `packages` and `core` components.

This commit fixes broken API documentation sections for Cookies, Encodings, and Exceptions in the requests library. It corrects incorrect function references and anchor links, and removes the obsolete decode_gzip function from the docs/api.rst file.
Adds a .nojekyll file to the docs directory to prevent GitHub Pages from processing the site with Jekyll. This ensures static files are served directly without build steps.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 2.14.0. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the package's initialization file to reflect the new release.
This release updates the requests library to version 2.17.3. It improves namespace identity support for the packages module, which helps libraries that rely on monkeypatching.

This commit updates the .gitignore file to exclude the .eggs directory from version control. This prevents build artifacts generated by Python packaging tools from being accidentally committed to the repository.

The Session class now initializes a connection pool manager with configurable limits for connections and pool size. This allows the request method to reuse these settings, improving connection management efficiency.
This commit updates the project's README documentation. It adds a blank line to the text, likely to improve visual spacing or formatting within the file.

This commit updates the test CA configuration to include the basicConstraints extension, marking it as a valid certificate authority. This prevents recent OpenSSL versions from rejecting the test certificate as invalid during regeneration. The change modifies the expired CA configuration file.
This commit fixes a broken link in the advanced user documentation. It updates the reference to the Twitter Streaming API in the `docs/user/advanced.rst` file to point to the correct current URL.
This commit updates the README to correct the weekly download count and add a documentation badge. It also removes several unused image files from the repository.
The commit removes a blank line from the `request` function in `requests/api.py`. This is a minor formatting change that does not alter the library's behavior or fix any user-facing bugs.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library from 0.3.4 to 0.4.0. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the core module to reflect the new release.

The Response class in requests/models.py now supports pickling, allowing users to serialize and deserialize response objects. This change adds state management methods to ensure content is fully consumed before saving, preventing data loss during the process.

Updates the step-security/harden-runner dependency in the publish workflow from version 2.13.0 to 2.14.2. This minor version bump ensures the CI environment uses the latest security hardening features for the runner.

This documentation update clarifies the specific error message raised by the `r.json` method when it encounters an empty response. It informs users that a `ValueError` with the message "No JSON object could be decoded" will be thrown instead of a generic exception.

This commit updates the project history to document a fix where request fragments are now correctly preserved during redirects. This change ensures compliance with RFC 7231 section 7.1.2, improving how the application handles URL fragments.

This commit fixes a bug in the `HTTPAdapter` class where creating a proxy connection would fail due to an incorrect attribute reference. It updates the `get_connection` method to instantiate the `ProxyManager` directly from the imported module instead of accessing it through the pool manager instance.
This commit updates the contributing documentation for the Requests library to improve clarity and tone. It removes unnecessary formatting and adjusts the wording to be more direct and professional.
Adds SSL support to the `Request` class in `requests/models.py`. Users can now enable certificate verification or specify a custom certificate path via a new `verify` parameter.

This commit updates the requirements file to install the project in editable mode. This ensures that local code changes are immediately reflected without requiring a reinstall, mimicking the behavior of running the development setup script.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Response.iter_lines` method where newlines at the end of data chunks were incorrectly dropped. It ensures that line endings are preserved during processing and properly stripped from the final output, preventing data loss when reading streamed responses.

This commit updates the `requests` library to support chardet version 4.x. It modifies the `check_compatibility` function and the `setup.py` dependency specification to allow chardet versions up to, but not including, 5.0.0.

This commit enables the warnings plugin in the project's pytest configuration by removing the flag that previously suppressed it. Users will now see warning messages during test runs instead of having them hidden. The change is made in the pyproject.toml file.

This commit updates the Session class in requests/sessions.py to use relative imports for the api module, resolving potential import path issues. It also adds context manager support via __enter__ and __exit__ methods, allowing Session objects to be used with the with statement.

Introduces a new CaseInsensitiveDict class in the requests.structures module to provide case-insensitive key access for HTTP headers. This replaces the previous implementation derived from Werkzeug, ensuring consistent behavior for dictionary operations like lookup and deletion.

This commit cleans up formatting in the requests exceptions module by removing trailing whitespace and adding a missing newline at the end of the file. It affects the InvalidURL class definition but does not change any functional behavior.

This commit adds a new HISTORY.md file to document the project's release history. It records bug fixes, such as making Content-Type header parsing case-insensitive, and lists improvements for recent versions.
This commit updates the project's README documentation. It changes the marketing tagline for the Requests library to a new phrase, altering the descriptive text visible to users.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Request.send` method where SSL errors were incorrectly masked as timeouts. Users will now see the specific SSL error instead of a generic timeout message when a connection fails due to certificate issues.

This release fixes a packaging error in the Python Requests library where the wheel file contained incorrect data, regressing a previous fix. The version number in the `__version__.py` module is updated to 2.18.1 to reflect this correction.

This commit updates the HTTP 307 redirect tests in the TestRequests class to verify that the request body content is preserved after the redirect. It ensures that both standard and seekable data payloads are correctly transmitted to the final destination.

This commit restores the default Accept-Encoding header in the requests library's defaults module. It fixes an issue where the library failed to advertise support for common compression formats like gzip and deflate, potentially preventing efficient data transfer.

This commit adds tests to verify that the `info` function in the `requests.help` module correctly handles SSL version detection. It ensures the function returns an empty version string on Python 2.6, where the OpenSSL version number is unavailable, and a valid version on Python 2.7 and later.
This commit adds a "Support Requests 3.0" banner to the documentation sidebar. It updates the sidebarintro.html and sidebarlogo.html templates to include a link to the sponsorship page.
This commit removes the "Configurations" and "Utilities" sections from the API documentation. It cleans up the docs by deleting references to the `requests.defaults` and `requests.utils` modules.
This documentation update clarifies that the Requests library officially supports Python 3.7. It corrects the supported version range in the project's index file to reflect this new compatibility.

This commit restores the assignment of the HTTP response reason phrase in the `HTTPAdapter.build_response` method. It ensures that the `reason` attribute is correctly populated from the raw response object, fixing a potential issue where the reason might be missing or incorrect.

This commit fixes an infinite loop in the HTTPDigestAuth class when handling incorrect Digest Authentication responses. It prevents the handle_401 method from re-registering itself indefinitely by limiting the number of times it processes a 401 status code.

This commit fixes an issue in the `Request` class where cookies and headers were incorrectly handled during redirects. It ensures that the original cookie state is preserved and that stale cookie headers are removed before sending the redirected request.

This commit disables automatic authentication handling in the `Request` class by commenting out the logic that resolves credentials from the `AuthManager`. It also modifies the `send` method to assign the raw response object directly to the response's `raw` attribute, altering how response data is processed.

This commit prevents the README rendering test from running on Python 2.6, where the tool is unsupported. This stops test failures in the Python 2.6 environment. The change modifies the test script in the Travis CI configuration.
This commit adds a new contributor to the project's author list. It updates the AUTHORS.rst file to include André Graf under the "Patches and Suggestions" section.

This commit removes the small_flask.css stylesheet and its reference in the documentation layout. It eliminates a specific mobile device style override that was previously applied to the Flask documentation theme.

This commit consolidates the test execution commands in the Makefile by merging the separate CI and coverage targets into a single coverage target. It updates the test runner to use a dedicated coverage configuration file, streamlining the build process for the requests module.

The `post` and `put` functions in `requests/api.py` now default the `data` argument to an empty byte string instead of `None`. This ensures that requests are sent with an explicit empty body, preventing potential issues where a missing body might be interpreted differently by servers.

This commit adds a documentation note to the advanced user guide regarding SSL certificate verification. It clarifies that if the verify option points to a directory, that directory must be processed with the OpenSSL c_rehash utility to function correctly.

This commit fixes a typo in the project's documentation where "PST" was incorrectly used instead of "POST" when describing request types. The change updates the README to accurately reflect the standard HTTP method name.

This commit updates a comment in the `PreparedRequest.prepare_body` method within `requests/models.py`. It clarifies that `urllib3` requires a bytes-like body, noting that Python 3's `json.dumps` returns a Unicode string instead of the bytes-like object needed for proper upload resumption.

This commit adds the CP949Prober class to the charade module, enabling the detection of the Korean EUC-KR character encoding. It introduces the necessary initialization and charset identification logic to support this specific encoding scheme.

This commit adds Michael Van Veen to the AUTHORS file and fixes a missing newline at the end of the file. It also standardizes keyword argument formatting in the request function within the requests module.
This commit updates the installation documentation for the Requests library. It adds a decorative image to the user guide, enhancing the visual presentation of the installation instructions.

This commit updates the project's dependencies to include the certifi package. It ensures that the requests library has the necessary certificate data for secure connections, resolving potential SSL verification issues.

This commit updates the project's README to use standard Markdown syntax instead of embedded HTML. It removes complex layout elements like centered images and styled code blocks to ensure the documentation renders correctly across different platforms.

This commit finalizes the release of version 2.11.1 for the requests library. It updates the version number and build identifier in the package initialization module and sets the official release date in the history file.

This commit updates the project's history log to record the vendoring of the urllib3 library. It ensures the changelog accurately reflects this dependency change for users reviewing the project's development timeline.

This commit adds the `imap` function to the `requests/async.py` module, enabling concurrent processing of generator objects. It allows users to iterate over a stream of requests and receive responses as a generator, rather than waiting for a complete list.

This commit updates the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to replace the standard `SimpleCookie` parser with a new `oreos` module for handling cookie headers. It changes how cookie data is extracted and stored during response building, potentially altering how specific cookie formats are processed.
This commit adds a download count badge to the project's README. The badge links to the package's crate.io page, providing users with a quick visual indicator of the library's popularity.
This commit updates the project's README to improve the visual presentation of the introductory text. It centers the tagline and changes the closing phrase to "built just for you."
This commit updates the project's README documentation. It renames the "Installation" section header to "Python Module Installation" to clarify the specific installation method for users.
This commit updates the documentation file for contributing to the project. It standardizes the capitalization of the project name from "requests" to "Requests" in the introductory text.

This commit fixes a regression in the RequestsCookieJar class where the iteritems method was missing or broken. It restores compatibility for iterating over cookie items, ensuring users can access cookie data as expected.

This commit adds automatic Brotli decoding support to the requests library. If the brotli or brotlicffi package is installed, the default_headers function in requests/utils.py now includes Brotli in the Accept-Encoding header and decodes compressed responses.

This commit modifies the Response class in requests/models.py to handle missing encoding detection. If no encoding is specified and the chardet library is unavailable, accessing the response text now raises a ValueError instead of silently failing.

Adds tests to verify that the text response server correctly handles request timeouts. It confirms that data sent after a timeout is ignored and that the server recovers to process new requests when a longer timeout is configured.
This commit updates the project history to document improvements in cookie management for 401 authentication responses, streaming downloads, and redirect behavior.

This commit removes the "Roadmap" section from the project's README file. It eliminates the planned item for Sphinx documentation, updating the project's public documentation to reflect current priorities.

This commit removes the "Thread-safety" claim from the project's README documentation. It clarifies the library's capabilities by eliminating a potentially misleading statement about its concurrency features.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the project's release history documentation. It changes the word "viewd" to "viewed" in the description of how dictionaries are displayed in the interpreter.

This commit improves the API documentation by adding detailed sections for the Response class, session function, and various exception types. It also introduces a new section for configuration defaults, making the library's interface more accessible to users.

The `super_len` function in `requests/utils.py` now correctly calculates the length of partially read files by tracking the current position. This fixes an issue where the function returned the total file size instead of the remaining bytes available for reading.

The license identifier in the requests version module is updated to use the standard SPDX format. This change corrects the license string from "Apache 2.0" to "Apache-2.0" for better compliance and machine readability.

This commit adds a new test case to the RequestsTestSuite in test_requests.py to verify that HTTP Digest authentication works correctly. It checks that requests with valid digest credentials return a 200 status, while unauthenticated requests and session-based requests behave as expected.
This commit updates the project documentation to reflect a higher download count. It changes the reported PyPI download statistics from 16 million to 21 million in the main index file.

This commit updates the documentation link for connection pooling in the advanced user guide. It corrects the URL to point directly to the specific urllib3 connection pool reference page instead of the general index.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` now correctly removes the `session` argument from the keyword arguments before passing them to the `Session` class. This prevents an error that occurred when the `Session` method received an unexpected `session` parameter.

This commit adds return type documentation to various methods across the requests library, including HTTPAdapter, Session, and utility functions. It clarifies the expected data types for developers using the library's internal APIs.

This documentation update explains how to pass a list of items as a query parameter value. It instructs users to append square brackets to the key name to indicate a list, ensuring the request library formats the URL correctly.

This commit updates the core module of the requests library by adding the httplib import and refining the Request class. It corrects the send method's docstring and adds return value comments to the get, head, post, put, and delete helper functions.

This commit fixes a bug in the HTTPDigestAuth class where the connection was not properly released after handling a 401 response. By consuming the response content and releasing the connection in the handle_401 method, the library can now reuse the same connection for subsequent requests.

This commit reverts a previous change that expanded the CI test suite to run all non-external tests. It restores the original behavior where the continuous integration pipeline only executes the core test file, avoiding the execution of external dependency tests. The changes affect the Makefile and Travis CI configuration.
