This commit adds a new `ci` target to the Makefile that initializes the environment and runs the test suite with JUnit XML output. It also fixes a missing newline at the end of the file.

Updates the GitHub Actions workflow for locking issues to use the latest version of the lock-threads action. This ensures the repository uses the most recent dependencies for its automated issue management tasks.

The `Request` class in `requests/models.py` now automatically includes configured base headers when a new request is initialized. This ensures that default headers are consistently applied to outgoing requests without requiring manual setup by the user.

This commit corrects spelling errors in the documentation for the Response.iter_content method and in a test string within the TestTestServer class. It fixes typos in the requests library without altering any functional behavior.
This commit updates the project's README to improve the formatting of the main tagline. It replaces a single line with a font size attribute by splitting the text into two separate paragraphs.

This change prevents the `PreparedRequest` class from overwriting an existing `Content-Length` header. The `prepare_content_length` method now returns early if the header is already present, ensuring user-defined values are preserved.

This commit fixes a typo in the test suite for the requests module, renaming a test method to correctly refer to an invalid scheme rather than a schema. It also updates a related comment to use the correct terminology.

This commit clarifies the definition of the `elapsed` attribute in the `Response` class within `requests/models.py`. It specifies that this value measures the time from sending the first request byte to finishing header parsing, ensuring it remains consistent regardless of how the response content is consumed.

This commit reverts a previous change to the `Session` class in `requests/sessions.py`. It removes the `return_response` parameter from the `request` method, restoring the original behavior where the method always returns a response object.

This commit reorganizes the initialization of the `config` attribute within the `Request` class in `requests/models.py`. It also adds a new test case to `tests/test_requests_ext.py` to verify handling of unicode errors in URLs.

This commit fixes a typo in the quickstart documentation that broke a hyperlink. The anchor text for the GitHub organization link was corrected from "organisation" to "organization" to ensure the reference works properly.

This commit updates the project's README to refine the tagline, replacing the phrase "Carefully handcrafted, with love" with "Thoughtfully handcrafted, with ♥". The change improves the visual presentation of the text by using a heart symbol instead of the word "love".

The `init_poolmanager` method in the `HTTPAdapter` class now accepts additional keyword arguments to configure the underlying connection pool. This allows users to pass custom settings, such as timeout values, directly when initializing the adapter.

The test_cookie_jar method in test_requests.py now verifies that cookies are correctly stored and returned by a server. It replaces a previous placeholder test with a functional check that posts data to a cookie tester and asserts the expected cookie value is present in the jar.

This commit updates the `PreparedRequest.prepare_body` method in `requests/models.py` to accept any `Mapping` object for the data parameter, rather than strictly requiring a `dict`. This allows users to pass custom mapping types when making POST requests without encountering type errors.

This commit updates the project documentation to better describe the library's automatic handling of connection pooling and data encoding. It clarifies that users do not need to manually manage query strings or form-encoding, as these features are handled automatically by the embedded urllib3 module.
This commit updates the project's author list to include Brian Bamsch. It ensures proper credit is given for contributions to the codebase.
This commit removes an embedded Gratipay donation widget from the documentation sidebar template. It cleans up the HTML file by deleting the iframe element that displayed the donation button.

This commit updates the project documentation to recommend using Pip for installation and removes outdated support channels like Twitter, email, and IRC. It also deletes the philosophy and todo pages to streamline the documentation structure.

This commit restructures the Travis CI configuration to separate testing and coverage stages. It removes the previous post-success coverage upload and instead runs the coverage tool as a dedicated job for Python 3.6.

The `Response.json` method in `requests/models.py` now uses `complexjson` instead of the standard `json` module for parsing. This ensures consistent JSON decoding behavior across different Python environments.
This commit corrects spelling errors in the module docstring of requests/_oauth.py. It fixes typos in the words "contains" and "necessary" and adjusts the line break for better readability.

The `map` function in `requests/async.py` no longer accepts a `keep_alive` parameter or manages connection pools. This removes the unused `PoolManager` import and simplifies the asynchronous request dispatch logic.

This commit removes the `decode_content` argument from the `read` call within the `Response.iter_content` method. It ensures that the general request code no longer passes urllib3-specific keyword arguments, improving compatibility with different underlying HTTP adapters.
This commit adds a HelloBar promotional banner to the documentation layout. It modifies the `layout.html` file within the `kr` theme to include the necessary JavaScript for displaying the banner.
This commit updates the project's README documentation. It replaces a decorative symbol with a larger text element to improve visual presentation.

This documentation update clarifies that the `chunk_size` parameter is optional when streaming content to a file. It helps users understand they do not need to specify this value in the quickstart guide.
This commit corrects a typo in the project's tagline within the README. It changes the abbreviation "e.g." to "i.e." to accurately convey that the library is simple and usable.

This commit fixes an issue where numeric values other than floats were not correctly encoded when sending POST requests. It updates the Request class to recognize all numeric types, including integers, by using a new compatibility constant.

This change moves the trustme import from the global scope into the nosan_server fixture within tests/conftest.py. This allows users to deselect the test via the command line when the trustme package is not installed, preventing import errors.

This commit makes character detection libraries optional in the requests library, preventing import errors when they are missing. It updates the compatibility check and response encoding logic to handle their absence gracefully. A new test job verifies that the library functions correctly without these dependencies.

This update adds a `release_conn` parameter to the `HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen` method, allowing users to control when a connection is returned to the pool. It also updates the `HTTPResponse` class to support this new behavior, preventing premature connection release when response content is not immediately preloaded.

This commit fixes test failures in the TestRequests class by correcting the instantiation of the Request object and updating how the Authorization header is accessed. It also removes an unused parameter from the basic auth test method.

This commit adds a new Makefile to standardize project build and test workflows. It defines targets for installing dependencies, running unit tests, executing continuous integration checks, and generating documentation.

This commit adds documentation to the advanced user guide explaining how to configure host-specific proxies. It clarifies that the library checks for a specific host entry in the proxies dictionary before falling back to the general scheme-based proxy.

This commit adds inline type annotations to the Requests library, improving static type checking for users. It introduces a new `_types` module and updates core classes like `Session` and `HTTPAdapter` to support these annotations.

This commit fixes a formatting error in the test utilities that caused failures on Python 2.6. It updates string formatting in the TestContentEncodingDetection and TestTestServer classes to use indexed placeholders, ensuring compatibility with older Python versions.

This commit adds a new debugging module to the requests library to help users generate diagnostic information for bug reports. The `print_information` function in `requests/_bug.py` collects and displays details about the Python environment, SSL configuration, and library versions.

This commit updates the response hook functions in the requests library to comply with the standard hook interface. It ensures that `decode_response` and `unicode_response` correctly modify the internal content buffer and return the response object, rather than returning raw data.

This commit updates the `JsonType` definition in `requests/_types.py` to use read-only `Sequence` and `Mapping` types instead of mutable `list` and `dict`. This change clarifies that JSON data structures are immutable collections, improving type safety for users working with JSON payloads.

This release updates the requests library to version 1.2.1, adding compatibility with Python 3.3.2. It fixes connection adapter matching to prioritize the most specific match and prevents a KeyError when link headers are missing.

This commit corrects a syntax error in the usage example within the requests package's main module. It removes an unnecessary space before the parenthesis in the print statement, ensuring the documentation displays valid Python code.
This update allows the equals sign to be used within cookie values, fixing a parsing limitation. The change is documented in the project's history file for version 0.10.6.

This commit fixes a broken hyperlink in the installation documentation. It updates the URL for the Cheeseshop mirror in the `docs/user/install.rst` file to include the proper protocol, ensuring users can successfully access the link.

This commit updates the TestRequests class in test_requests.py to use the httpbin relative-redirect endpoint for testing excessive redirects. It ensures that the final URL in the TooManyRedirects exception matches the expected endpoint exactly, rather than just checking for a substring.

This documentation update corrects the quickstart guide to reference the `allow_redirects` parameter instead of the removed `disable_redirects` option. It ensures users are directed to the correct method for controlling redirect behavior in the `requests` library.

This commit updates the `test_uppercase_scheme_redirect` test in `test_requests.py` to use a local HTTP server instead of an external domain. It ensures the test validates uppercase scheme redirects against the local `HTTPBIN_URL` endpoint, removing reliance on hard-coded external resources.

This commit refactors error handling in the `Request` class within `requests/models.py`. It introduces an `is_error` flag to the `_build_response` method, allowing the response object to directly store the error state. This simplifies the logic in the `send` method by removing redundant manual assignments.

This commit removes the Python 2 compatibility check from the `prepare_headers` method in `requests/models.py`. It now consistently encodes header names to ASCII for all Python versions, simplifying the logic for handling Unicode header names.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the Travis CI configuration that prevented the readme check from being correctly skipped on Python 2.6. The change updates the conditional logic in the build script to ensure the test runs only on supported Python versions.

This commit updates the project's README to fix the centering of the main description text. It replaces an invalid HTML span tag with a proper paragraph tag to ensure the text displays correctly in the documentation.

This commit adds a test to verify that cookies are correctly saved to the session when a request is made with `return_response=False`. It ensures that the `requests` module properly handles cookie persistence in this specific scenario, preventing potential data loss.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Request` class where relative URLs were incorrectly processed during response building. It ensures that URL joining only occurs when the provided URL lacks a network location, preventing malformed requests.

This commit fixes import errors in the requests core module that occurred when running under Python 2.5. It changes the import statements to use absolute paths instead of relative ones, ensuring the library loads correctly in older Python environments.

The `get_netrc_auth` function in `requests/utils.py` now handles file permission errors when reading the `.netrc` file. This prevents crashes in shared hosting environments where the file is not readable by the current user, allowing the request to proceed without netrc authentication.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the `requests` library's `status_codes` module that caused a duplicate `if not` condition. The correction ensures the code parses correctly when processing HTTP status code titles.
This commit removes a duplicate entry for the Sphinx package from the Pipfile. It resolves a configuration error caused by the repeated dependency declaration.

This commit adds a persistent banner to the documentation sidebar that displays a countdown to the end of Python 2 support. It introduces a new template file to render this warning, ensuring users are reminded of the upcoming deprecation.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar to link to a new "Recommended Packages" page instead of a specific tool. It also adds a section to the community guide describing the Certifi package for SSL certificate validation.

This commit fixes an issue where proxy credentials containing URL-encoded characters were not properly decoded before use. The `HTTPAdapter` class now unquotes the username and password in the `add_headers` method to ensure correct authentication.

The `_basic_auth_str` function in `requests/auth.py` now explicitly converts non-string username and password values to strings before encoding. This ensures that basic authentication works correctly when users pass integers or other non-byte types, preventing potential errors during the base64 encoding process.

This commit updates the docstrings for the HTTP request functions in the requests.api module to explicitly document their return types. It replaces informal return descriptions with structured Sphinx directives, improving the generated API documentation for users.

This commit renames the `fo` attribute to `raw` within the `Response` class in `requests/models.py`. It updates the `Request` and `Response` classes to use the new name when storing, closing, and reading the underlying response stream.

This commit updates the Makefile to ensure the project's dependencies are installed strictly according to the lockfile. It removes the flag that previously allowed pipenv to skip the lockfile during the development environment setup.

This commit fixes a grammatical error in the FAQ documentation by removing an unnecessary word from the explanation of hostname mismatch errors. The change is located in the docs/community/faq.rst file.

This commit removes unnecessary unicode literals from the `default_user_agent` function in `requests/utils.py`. It updates the function to use standard string types instead of explicit unicode prefixes, simplifying the code without changing the generated user agent behavior.

The `dispatch_hook` function in `requests/hooks.py` no longer silently swallows exceptions raised by user-defined hooks. Previously, errors were caught and printed to the console, but now they propagate to the caller, allowing for proper error handling.

This commit updates the test suite for the requests library to replace unittest assertion methods with standard Python assert statements. It modifies the RequestsTestSuite class to check response types and error classes using simpler syntax.

This commit updates the FAQ documentation to confirm that Python 3 support is now available, replacing previous statements that it was still pending. The change clarifies the current status for users checking the project's compatibility.

The CI test matrix now includes PyPy 3.11 for Linux and macOS while removing PyPy 3.9. This change updates the GitHub Actions workflow to reflect the new supported Python versions. PyPy 3.11 tests are excluded on Windows due to build limitations.

The CI configuration now runs the full test suite, excluding external and async tests that are unsupported under Python 3. This change updates the Makefile to define a new target that filters out specific test files, replacing the previous limited test execution.

This commit adds a test to verify that the TestServer correctly handles a specific number of requests before stopping. It ensures that the server accepts the expected number of connections and then properly rejects subsequent attempts. The change is located in the TestTestServer class within test_requests.py.
This commit adds docutils to the project's dependency list. It ensures the documentation generation tool is explicitly installed alongside other required packages.

This update clarifies that the library no longer accepts integers as valid header values, correcting a behavior from previous releases. The change is documented in the HISTORY.rst file to inform users of this stricter validation.

This commit updates the project history file to document version 0.9.0. It notes that SSL verification is now enabled by default, changing the security behavior for users connecting to secure servers.

This commit adds a promotional message to the documentation sidebar, encouraging companies to purchase a copy of the Requests library. The change updates the sidebar template files to include a link to a Gumroad store.

This commit fixes a failing test in the test_requests module by updating the test_prepare_unicode_url function. It resolves an error caused by a missing required argument by explicitly passing an empty list for the hooks parameter.

This commit adds a unit test to the RequestsTestCase in test_requests.py to verify the behavior of the RequestsCookieJar. It ensures that cookies are correctly stored with specific attributes like secure, domain, and HttpOnly flags.

This commit adds a script to the documentation layout that loads an external tracking code from a third-party service. The change modifies the `layout.html` file within the `kr` theme to inject this analytics snippet into the page.

The `get_encoding_from_headers` function in `requests/utils.py` now explicitly returns UTF-8 when the content type is application/json. This ensures JSON responses are decoded correctly according to RFC 4627, preventing potential character encoding errors when the charset is not specified in the headers.
The quickstart documentation now includes a section on OAuth authentication. It directs users to the requests-oauth project for a simple interface to establish OAuth connections.

This commit adds a warning to the advanced user documentation stating that requests does not support encrypted private keys for local certificates. It clarifies that users must provide an unencrypted key to avoid connection errors.

This commit fixes an issue where redirect requests failed to pass all original arguments to the underlying adapter. The `resolve_redirects` method in the `SessionRedirectMixin` class now forwards additional keyword arguments, ensuring consistent behavior during redirects.

This commit adds a "Release History" link to the documentation sidebar. It allows users to easily navigate to the software updates page from the main navigation menu. The change modifies the sidebar template file.

This commit adds documentation explaining how to use custom authentication handlers in the Requests library. It clarifies that users can pass a callable object to the `Session.request` method to define custom authentication logic, such as setting specific headers.

This commit fixes a crash in the `get_netrc_auth` function when processing byte-string URLs. It ensures the network location is split correctly based on whether the input is a Unicode string or bytes, preventing type errors during authentication retrieval.

This commit corrects minor grammatical errors and capitalization inconsistencies within the project's documentation. It updates several files, including the README and user guides, to ensure "GitHub" is properly capitalized and other text is polished.

This commit fixes an issue in the requests packages module where unbundled dependencies like urllib3, idna, and chardet lost their module identity. It ensures that submodules of these packages are correctly mapped to their original identities, preventing unexpected behavior when accessing nested modules.
This commit updates the quickstart documentation to improve clarity and conciseness. It removes redundant blank lines and corrects minor grammatical errors in the authentication section.

This commit updates the Sphinx documentation for the `curl_from_request` function in `requests/utils.py`. It adds a new section to the API reference and expands the function's docstring to include parameter details and a usage example.

The `RequestException` class in `requests/exceptions.py` now inherits from `RuntimeError` instead of the base `Exception` class. This change allows the exception to be caught by code that specifically handles `RuntimeError` instances.

This commit replaces the Python file `api.py` with a reStructuredText file named `api.rst` in the documentation directory. It establishes a new structure for the API documentation, including sections for the main interface, exceptions, and internals.

This commit adds a new exception class named StreamConsumedError to the requests exceptions module. It allows the library to explicitly signal when a user attempts to read response content that has already been consumed.

This commit updates the documentation to explain how to explicitly set a filename when uploading files using the `files` argument. It clarifies the syntax for the `request` function in the `requests` library, ensuring users understand how to specify custom filenames for multipart uploads.

The Requests library no longer supports CPython 3.7, raising the minimum required version to 3.8. This change updates the project's documentation, development requirements, and continuous integration workflows to reflect the new baseline.

This commit fixes a formatting error in the timeout error message within the HTTPConnectionPool class. It corrects the string format specifier to properly display the timeout duration, ensuring users see the correct number of seconds instead of a formatting artifact.
This commit adds a new "pyc" target to the Makefile. It allows users to clean up the project by removing all compiled Python bytecode files from the directory tree.

The Session class in requests/sessions.py now supports pickling by implementing serialization methods and adding the verify attribute to the state. This change allows users to save and restore session objects without losing configuration or encountering errors.

This commit updates the API documentation to reflect the addition of a seventh request method. It corrects the count of available methods and adjusts class references in the `requests` module documentation.

The CaseInsensitiveDict class in requests/structures.py now inherits directly from dict instead of DictMixin. This change simplifies the implementation by removing the need for a separate internal data attribute and redundant initialization logic.

Adds a Gumroad script to the documentation layout to enable overlay functionality. This change affects the `kr` theme's `layout.html` file, integrating external payment or purchase options into the site interface.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to a newer version, modifying core modules like connectionpool and response. It changes the HTTPHeaderDict class to inherit directly from dict instead of MutableMapping, altering how HTTP headers are stored and accessed.

This commit updates the bug report issue template to hide instructional text from the final GitHub issue while keeping it visible to the user. It also improves the code snippet formatting for the environment dump.

This commit fixes a bug in the `requests` library where the status code title for 400 was incorrectly converted to uppercase. It prevents the title starting with a forward slash from being modified, ensuring the correct text is displayed to users.

This commit updates the docstring and comments for the `merge_environment_settings` method in the `Session` class. It clarifies that the method checks for cURL-compatible environment variables to determine the SSL verification setting.

This commit updates the `Request.send` method in `requests/models.py` to handle raw socket errors. It converts these errors into `Timeout` exceptions, ensuring users receive a consistent timeout message instead of a generic socket error.

This commit removes unused import statements from the requests/api.py module. It cleans up the codebase by deleting references to config, models, status_codes, hooks, and utils that were not being used. No user-facing behavior changes.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the `PreparedRequest.prepare_url` method within the `requests` module. The change corrects the formatting of an error message, ensuring the library functions correctly when handling invalid URLs.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar to replace a link to edmsynths.com with a link to howtopython.org. The change affects the sidebarintro.html and sidebarlogo.html templates, ensuring users see the correct external resource reference.

This commit updates the test environment configuration to include Python 3.13 in the list of supported versions. It ensures that the project's test suite runs against the new Python release, allowing developers to verify compatibility with the latest interpreter.

This commit fixes a typo in the variable name within the `_get_autoauth` function in `requests/core.py`. The change ensures the automatic authentication feature works correctly by resolving a naming inconsistency in the loop.

This commit corrects a minor inaccuracy in the docstring for the `dotted_netmask` function in `requests/utils.py`. It clarifies that the input mask is an integer rather than a CIDR notation string, ensuring the documentation accurately reflects the function's expected arguments.

This commit updates the project's README documentation by relocating a decorative emoji line. It moves the text from the installation section to the documentation section, improving the visual layout of the guide.

This commit updates the project history to document support for Unicode URL-encoded data. It clarifies that the system now handles non-ASCII characters within URLs, improving compatibility for internationalized web addresses.

This commit updates the authentication and quickstart documentation to explain how Requests locates the netrc file. It details the search paths, including the NETRC environment variable, and shows how to disable this feature using the trust_env setting.

This commit corrects typos in the docstrings of the `request` function in `requests/api.py` and the module docstring in `requests/models.py`. It removes a duplicated word in the API documentation and fixes an incorrect module reference in the models documentation.

This commit updates the Response class in requests/models.py to use urllib3's built-in streaming decompression feature. It removes the custom stream_decompress and stream_untransfer utilities from requests/utils.py, simplifying the content iteration process.

This commit adds a missing trailing comma to the `default_headers` function in `requests/utils.py`. It corrects a syntax error in the dictionary definition, ensuring the module loads correctly without raising a parsing exception.

This commit fixes a crash in the `Response.close` method when the underlying raw object lacks a `release_conn` attribute. It now safely checks for the method's existence before calling it, allowing non-urllib3-like responses to close correctly.

This commit moves the logic for reading response content from the HTTPAdapter to the Session class. It ensures that non-streaming requests automatically load the response body, maintaining consistent behavior for users. The change affects the send methods in both the HTTPAdapter and Session modules.
This release updates the Requests library to version 2.21.0. It adds support for the idna v2.8 dependency, ensuring compatibility with the latest version of the international domain name library.

This commit removes Python 3.2 from the continuous integration test matrix in the .travis.yml file. It clarifies that the project does not support this older Python version, preventing unnecessary test runs.

Adds a test to verify that the `iter_lines` method correctly yields the expected number of lines when streaming responses of varying sizes. This ensures the `requests` library handles line iteration accurately for different data volumes.

This commit removes a redundant import statement from the requests package initialization module. It cleans up the codebase by eliminating a duplicate warning import that was not necessary for the library's functionality.

This commit adds the pytest cache directory to the project's .gitignore file. It prevents local test failure metadata from being accidentally committed to the repository, keeping the version control history clean.

This commit updates the test suite for the TooManyRedirects exception to ensure compatibility with Python 3.x syntax. It corrects the exception handling in the TestRequests class, allowing the redirect limit tests to run without syntax errors.

The CI test target in the Makefile now runs tests using pytest with parallel execution and JUnit XML reporting, replacing the previous setup.py test command. This change updates the test runner configuration for the project's continuous integration pipeline.

The `unquote_unreserved` function in `requests/utils.py` now raises a descriptive `InvalidURL` exception when it encounters malformed percent-escape sequences. Previously, this scenario would trigger a generic `ValueError`, making it harder for users to identify the specific cause of the failure.

This commit adds a link to the new development philosophy documentation in the main project index. It ensures users can easily access the project's guiding principles from the primary documentation page.

This commit updates the project's author list to include a new contributor. It modifies the AUTHORS.rst file to add the name and GitHub handle of Jonathan Wong to the "Patches and Suggestions" section.

This commit renames the thread-local storage attribute in the HTTPDigestAuth class to a private, more descriptive name. It improves code readability and follows Python naming conventions without changing the authentication behavior.

This commit removes the `requests.monkeys` module, which contained monkey patches for `urllib2` to support custom HTTP methods and redirect handling. Users relying on these internal patches will no longer have access to the `Request` and `HTTPRedirectHandler` classes.

This commit updates the documentation for the Request class in the requests module. It clarifies that dictionary values for query parameters can be lists to represent multivalued parameters. This helps users understand how to correctly format requests with multiple values for a single key.

Fixes a bug in the `Request` class where relative URLs were incorrectly resolved against the initial request URL instead of the most recent one. This ensures that `Request._build_response` correctly handles chained redirects by using the latest URL for joining.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to clarify how to send JSON data using the `json` parameter in `requests.post`. It adds a note explaining that this feature, available since version 2.4.2, simplifies data encoding for users.

This commit updates the documentation link in the AppEngineManager class to point to the correct urllib3 reference page. Users will now be directed to the accurate documentation when encountering the App Engine integration.

This commit updates the project documentation to reflect that the Requests library now exceeds 11 million monthly downloads. It modifies the README and documentation index files to replace the previous 7 million figure with the new milestone.

This commit updates the documentation configuration to include Python's official documentation in the intersphinx mapping. It enables automatic cross-references to Python standard library objects within the project's user guides. The changes primarily affect the docs/conf.py file and related documentation pages.

This commit cleans up the requests/async.py module by adding an explicit public API list and improving docstring clarity for the _patched and _send functions. It also removes an unused session import and refines the documentation for the map function.

This commit adds a test to the RequestsTestCase in test_requests.py verifying that cookies passed directly to a request do not persist in the session. It ensures that using the cookies parameter on a single request does not inadvertently modify the session's cookie jar.

This commit reformats a conditional statement in the `get_dict` method of the `RequestsCookieJar` class to satisfy flake8 line length rules. It splits a long line into multiple lines using parentheses, improving code readability without altering the underlying logic.

This commit fixes a bug where the documentation sidebar triggered duplicate image requests for custom ad designs. It updates the native ad integration in the docs static files to use the official framework, ensuring the ad ribbon displays correctly without redundant network calls.

This commit removes a redundant type check for `builtin_str` within the `PreparedRequest.prepare_body` method in `requests/models.py`. It simplifies the logic for handling request body data by relying solely on the `basestring` check and the presence of a `read` attribute.

This commit removes an unnecessary workaround in the `get_netrc_auth` function within `requests.utils` that handled missing home directories, as this is no longer required in Python 3.8 and later. It also adds new tests to the `TestGetNetrcAuth` class to ensure the function correctly parses URLs and prevents regression of a specific security vulnerability.
This commit contains no code changes or file modifications. It serves as a placeholder or marker in the repository history without altering any behavior or functionality.

This commit removes a commented-out line from the `get_connection` method in the `HTTPAdapter` class within `requests/adapters.py`. It cleans up the codebase by deleting unused, obsolete code that had no effect on the library's behavior.

This commit removes redundant URL decoding for proxy credentials in the `HTTPAdapter.proxy_headers` method. It prevents usernames and passwords from being unquoted twice, ensuring they are handled correctly when setting proxy authentication headers.

This commit updates the Session class in requests/sessions.py to ensure that cookies passed during initialization are correctly added to the session. It addresses a potential issue where initial cookies might not be properly registered, ensuring they are available for subsequent requests.

This commit fixes a documentation build failure by removing unsupported Sphinx extensions from the configuration. It updates the `extensions` list in `docs/conf.py` to include only `sphinx.ext.autodoc`, resolving errors caused by missing or incompatible modules.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the test suite by removing unnecessary unicode prefixes from string literals, as Python 3 treats all strings as unicode by default. The change updates the `test_POSTBIN_GET_POST_FILES_STRINGS` method within the `RequestsTestSuite` class to ensure compatibility with modern Python versions.

This commit removes outdated certificate details for the GTE CyberTrust Global Root from the NOTICE file. It cleans up the cacert notice section by deleting unnecessary issuer, subject, and fingerprint information.
This commit updates the project history to note that cookie errors are now suppressed. This change prevents users from seeing error messages related to cookie handling.

This commit removes an unnecessary horizontal rule from the documentation sidebar template. It cleans up the visual layout of the project's documentation site without altering any functional behavior.

This release notes update documents version 1.0.1, which fixes a bug related to certificate verification exceptions. The change clarifies the specific issue resolved in this patch for users reviewing the project's history.
This commit updates the documentation to improve the formatting of user testimonials. It adjusts the punctuation and applies italic styling to the quotes in the index file.

This commit introduces the version metadata file for the requests library, establishing the package's identity and release information. It defines the version as 2.14.2 and includes standard attributes like the title, author, and license.

The Server class in testserver/server.py now accepts parameters to limit the number of requests handled and to wait for an external event before closing. This allows the main thread to block the test server's shutdown, preventing premature termination during tests.

This commit updates the `prepare_url` method in `requests/models.py` to raise an `InvalidURL` error when a hostname begins with a period. Previously, such malformed URLs were not rejected, allowing invalid hostnames to pass validation.

This commit enables the GitHub banner in the documentation by updating the theme options in `docs/conf.py`. Users viewing the generated documentation will now see a link to the project's GitHub repository.

This commit updates the project's README by removing inline CSS styles and HTML table markup. It simplifies the documentation structure for the "International Domains and URLs" and "Keep-Alive & Connection Pooling" sections.

This commit changes the default behavior of the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` so that URI encoding is enabled by default. Users will now see special characters in request paths automatically percent-encoded without needing to explicitly configure the `encode_uri` option.

This commit updates the project's author list to reflect a change in maintainership. It moves Ian Cordasco to the previous keepers section and adds Seth M. Larson as a new keeper in the AUTHORS.rst file.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar to include links for English and Portuguese language versions of the Requests library. It modifies the `sidebarintro.html` template to allow users to easily switch between these language options.

This commit updates the security dependency in setup.py to require pyOpenSSL version 0.13 or higher. It ensures the library has access to the set_tlsext_host_name function, preventing installation failures on systems with older pyOpenSSL versions.

This commit introduces a new helper function, `merge_kwargs`, within the `requests/sessions.py` module to handle the combination of local and default keyword arguments. It ensures that local arguments override defaults and that any keys explicitly set to `None` are removed from the final configuration.

This commit refines cookie key validation in the `requests` library by separating non-RFC compliant characters from the standard set. It ensures that characters like brackets and braces are tracked distinctly within the `monkeys` module to improve compliance handling.

This commit updates the AUTHORS.rst file to add Robert Gieseke to the list of contributors. It ensures the project's credit list accurately reflects all individuals who have provided patches or suggestions.
This commit updates the documentation to list Twitter, Spotify, and Microsoft as users of the library. It also removes a mention of thread-safety from the feature list.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Request` class where deleting empty proxies caused an error during iteration. It ensures the proxy dictionary is safely copied before modification, preventing runtime issues when cleaning up proxy settings.

This commit disables several Pyright linting rules in the project configuration to reduce noise from checks unrelated to type safety. It removes corresponding inline type ignore comments from various modules, including `requests/__init__.py` and `requests/adapters.py`.

This commit updates the project's dependency lists to include missing packages required for the build process. It adds pytest-mock, funcsigs, mock, and pbr to the requirements files, resolving build failures caused by these missing dependencies.

This commit restricts the import of the oauthlib library to Python 2 environments within the requests/auth.py module. It prevents import errors on Python 3 by conditionally loading the OAuth 1.0 client components only when running on Python 2.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Request` class where parameter encoding failed due to an incorrect type check. It restores the use of the `str` type for validation, ensuring that string parameters are properly encoded to UTF-8 in the `_encode_params` method.

This commit adds the missing `requests/hooks` sub-package, which previously caused import errors for users trying to access hook utilities. It introduces modules for pre-request, post-request, and response hooks, including the `decode_response` and `unicode_response` functions.

This commit updates the documentation for advanced usage to remove references to the deprecated Twitter API. It clarifies how to handle streaming requests by setting the stream parameter to false and using the iter_lines method.

This commit corrects a spelling error in a comment within the MockRequest class in the requests/cookies.py module. It changes the word "doain" to "domain" in the get_full_url method. No functional behavior is altered.

This commit improves the visual layout of the sponsors documentation page by adding a horizontal separator line. It modifies the `docs/community/sponsors.rst` file to enhance readability. No functional code changes are included.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` now automatically converts dictionary-based cookie inputs into a cookie jar object. This ensures consistent cookie handling for users passing simple key-value pairs instead of explicit jar instances.

This commit corrects the quickstart documentation to clarify that appending empty brackets to a key is not required to send multiple values in a query string. It updates the example in the user guide to show that a standard list value works without special notation.

This commit fixes test failures on Python 2.6 by updating the test suite to use the OrderedDict class from the requests compatibility module. It replaces direct references to the standard library's collections module within the RequestsTestCase to ensure consistent behavior across Python versions.

This commit fixes a layout issue in the documentation sidebar where the fundraising goal and amount raised were displayed on the same line. It adds a line break to separate these two pieces of information for better readability. The changes affect the sidebarintro.html and sidebarlogo.html templates.

This commit fixes a bug in the `dispatch_hook` function within `requests/hooks.py` where hooks returning error responses were incorrectly ignored. Previously, the initial response would replace the error, preventing users from seeing the actual failure. The logic now checks for `None` instead of relying on boolean evaluation, allowing hooks to properly return error responses.

This commit adds official support for Python 3.7 to the requests library. It updates the project's configuration files to include Python 3.7 in the test matrix and removes the previous development version designation.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 0.4.1. It modifies the version constants in the core module and adds a release date to the project history file.

This commit adds blank lines to the test server module to ensure two lines of separation between top-level definitions. It improves code readability and formatting consistency in the test server file.

This commit updates the contributing and advanced documentation to replace the informal "Be Cordial" section with a formal reference to the Python Software Foundation Code of Conduct. It clarifies community interaction guidelines for contributors and users.

This commit corrects the documentation for the `requests` library's quickstart guide. It clarifies that the `Response.history` attribute contains `Response` objects rather than `Request` objects, fixing a misleading description of how redirections are tracked.

This commit adds support for openSUSE systems by including a new certificate bundle path in the list of possible CA bundle locations. It ensures the requests library can locate the system's trusted certificates on openSUSE, preventing SSL verification errors for users on that distribution.

This commit adds documentation to the `get_redirect_target` method within the `SessionRedirectMixin` class in `requests/sessions.py`. It clarifies that the method is invoked multiple times during the redirect processing cycle. The notes suggest caching the redirect location on the response object to optimize custom implementations.

This commit updates the `extract_zipped_paths` function in `src/requests/utils.py` to use `tempfile.mkstemp` for creating temporary files. It resolves a potential race condition and ensures the extracted file retains its original extension, improving the reliability of temporary file handling.
Adds a third-party analytics script to the documentation layout. This enables tracking of user interactions on the requests documentation site.

This commit removes the Pipfile and Pipfile.lock files, consolidating dependency management into requirements.txt. This change simplifies the project's build process by eliminating the Pipenv configuration.
This commit upgrades the httpbin dependency from version 0.7.0 to 0.10.0 in the development requirements. It also adds pip caching to the GitHub Actions test workflow to speed up test execution.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` now passes arguments to the underlying session using explicit keyword names instead of positional order. This change ensures that parameters are correctly mapped to their intended destinations, preventing potential errors if the internal function signature changes.

This commit updates the installation documentation to display the package installation command as a code block instead of a plain text heading. This change improves readability and clarity for users following the setup instructions in the user guide.

This commit introduces the `requests/compat.py` module to handle Python version compatibility. It defines boolean flags that identify the specific Python version and minor release currently in use. This allows the library to adjust its behavior based on whether it is running on Python 2 or 3.

This commit updates the project's release history to document version 2.3.0. It details changes to proxy scheme defaults, header dictionary behavior, and various bug fixes related to redirects and encoding.

In the `HTTPDigestAuth` class within `requests/auth.py`, the `noncebit` variable is now constructed directly inside the `build_digest_header` method. This change hardcodes the quality-of-protection value to "auth," removing the previous variable reference since only that specific value is supported.

This commit removes tests for the deprecated safe_mode feature from the RequestsTestSuite in tests/test_requests.py. It eliminates test cases that verified connection error handling and redirect limits when safe_mode was enabled.

This commit updates the PyTest class in setup.py to modify how tests are executed. It changes the default pytest arguments to enable parallel execution with eight workers and use boxed output, improving test performance and readability.

The RequestsCookieJar class in requests/cookies.py now supports dict-like iteration by adding keys, values, and items methods. It also raises exceptions when accessing or setting items directly if the jar contains cookies from multiple domains, preventing ambiguous operations.

This commit prevents redundant resource freeing during HTTP redirects by removing a previously required double flush. It modifies the `_build_response` method in the `Request` class within `requests/models.py` to ensure the socket is consumed and released efficiently.

This commit updates the doctest in the requests package to use `print(r.text)` instead of `r.json()`. It addresses the instability of the previous test by using ellipsis and whitespace normalization to handle variable response data.

This commit updates the project's README to display the Requests logo as a standalone image on the right side of the page. It removes the previous image link that pointed to the documentation site, simplifying the visual layout.

This commit fixes a bug in the HTTPDigestAuth class where reusing the authentication object with a non-file body incorrectly treated it as a file. It ensures the internal position variable is reset to None, allowing the library to correctly detect the body type and avoid errors.

This commit updates the documentation for the advanced user guide to fix a broken link reference for the gevent library. It replaces an undefined internal reference with a direct URL to the gentry package on PyPI, ensuring users can correctly access the installation instructions.

This commit restores the argument injection hook in the `Session.request` method of the `requests` library. It allows users to modify request arguments before they are sent, a feature that was previously removed.

This commit introduces a new HACKING file to establish project coding standards. It outlines requirements for PEP8 compliance, documentation formatting for Sphinx, and the necessity of maintaining pure Python implementations alongside optional Cython optimizations.

This commit updates the contributing documentation by removing the "All Contributions" section and standardizing heading styles. It also adds a new guideline requiring contributors to use single-quoted strings when presenting Python code examples.

This commit removes official support for Python 3.4 in the Requests library. It updates the installation requirements to exclude version 3.4 and removes the corresponding test job from the continuous integration configuration.

This commit cleans up the codebase by removing unused imports and fixing a missing newline in the requests library. It affects the HTTPAdapter, HTTPDigestAuth, and Response classes, improving code hygiene without changing user-facing behavior.

This commit fixes a minor documentation error in the HTTPAdapter class within the requests library. It removes a duplicate word from a comment explaining why the poolmanager attribute is not pickleable. No functional behavior is changed.

This commit reorders the test dependencies in setup.py to place the pytest version constraint at the end of the list. This change likely resolves a dependency resolution conflict or installation error that occurred when the base pytest package was listed first.

The `merge_kwargs` function in `requests/sessions.py` now performs case-insensitive key lookups when merging request parameters. This ensures that local arguments correctly override default settings regardless of capitalization differences, preventing unexpected behavior when keys are mixed case.
This commit adds Matt Giuca to the project's list of contributors. It updates the AUTHORS.rst file to credit him for patches and suggestions.

This commit updates the advanced and quickstart user documentation to use the Python 3 print function syntax instead of the legacy print command. This ensures the code examples in the docs are compatible with modern Python versions.

This commit adds support for the MD5-sess algorithm to the HTTPDigestAuth class in the requests library. It enables proper handling of session-specific authentication challenges by calculating the required client nonce and updating the nonce count.

This commit updates the project documentation to announce that Requests 2.x is now in maintenance mode, focusing only on critical security fixes. It directs users to the new Requests 3.0 release for active development and general support.

The test target in the Makefile now explicitly runs only files matching the test_* pattern. This ensures the test suite executes the intended test files rather than potentially including unrelated modules.

This commit adds a test to verify that streaming requests work correctly when using HTTP Digest authentication. It ensures that the response body is readable when the stream option is enabled, addressing a previous limitation where authentication hooks did not properly pass keyword arguments.

This commit adds a test to verify that multivalued form-encoded data is correctly serialized as a list of key-value pairs. It ensures that sending a dictionary with a list value produces the expected repeated parameter format in the request body. The test is located in the TestRequests class within the test suite.

This commit updates the documentation for the `iter_content` and `iter_lines` methods in the `requests` library's `Response` class. It clarifies that these methods prevent loading large responses into memory only when the `stream` parameter is enabled in the request.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to version 1.0.2 within the requests package. It introduces thread safety to the RecentlyUsedContainer class and adjusts the package initialization to import urllib3 instead of poster.
This commit updates the project documentation to list HTTP and HTTPS proxy support as a new feature. It clarifies the available capabilities for users reviewing the README.

This commit fixes a serialization error in the `Session` class that occurred when the `__attrs__` attribute was missing. It ensures the `__getstate__` method safely returns an empty dictionary instead of failing, preventing crashes during session pickling.

Updates the CodeQL analysis workflow to use version 4.37.0 of the init, autobuild, and analyze actions. This routine maintenance ensures the security scanning pipeline runs with the latest available features and fixes.

The Makefile now installs pipenv using a version range that excludes known bad releases instead of pinning to a specific version. This change prevents the installation of problematic pipenv versions while allowing newer, stable releases.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to recommend using `Response.iter_content` for saving streamed downloads to a file. It explains that this method simplifies handling compared to using `Response.raw` directly, providing a preferred pattern for retrieving content.

This commit associates a Session object with each Request instance, allowing the request to access session-level parameters. It fixes an issue where session parameters were not applied to requests involving redirects. The changes modify the Request class and Session.request method.

Adds a new `max_retries` configuration option to the `requests` library, defaulting to zero. This allows users to specify how many times the `Request` class should attempt to reconnect if a connection fails, improving resilience against transient network issues.
This commit adds Michael Becker to the project's contributor list in the AUTHORS.rst file. It ensures he receives credit for his patches and suggestions.

The `session` function in `requests/sessions.py` no longer accepts keyword arguments. This change prevents users from passing configuration options directly to the factory function, requiring them to configure the returned `Session` object explicitly instead.

This commit fixes a Unicode handling issue in the OAuth1 class within requests/auth.py for Python 3 compatibility. It ensures the Authorization header is correctly identified and removed from response headers, preventing potential encoding errors during authentication.

The test target in the Makefile now runs the test suite via the Python setup script instead of calling the pytest command directly. This change ensures tests are executed using the project's standard installation and testing workflow.

The TooManyRedirects exception raised by SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects no longer includes the prepared request object, only the response. This simplifies the exception data structure and updates the corresponding tests to reflect the removal of the request attribute.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Session.request` method where the hooks argument was incorrectly passed to the hook dispatcher. It ensures the `args` dictionary is properly updated when dispatching the 'args' hook, preventing potential errors during request preparation.

This commit fixes a resource leak in the test suite by ensuring the socket is closed before the test completes. It moves the socket closure call to the correct location within the `test_server_closes` method of the `TestTestServer` class.

The `Response` class in `requests/models.py` now exposes `content` as a property instead of relying on `__getattr__`. This makes the attribute discoverable via `dir()` and prevents errors from missing `AttributeError` raises. It also removes the need for a temporary attribute hack used to satisfy Sphinx documentation generation.
This commit updates the email address for Hugo Osvaldo Barrera in the project's author list. It ensures the contributor's contact information in the AUTHORS.rst file is current.

This commit removes several unused dependencies, including appdirs, packaging, pyparsing, and six, from the project's requirements file. This streamlines the installation process by reducing unnecessary package downloads.

This commit removes a temporary TODO comment and trailing whitespace from the Request class in requests/models.py. It cleans up the codebase without altering the behavior of the Request.send or _get_opener methods.
This commit updates the Ruff linter version in the pre-commit configuration from 0.16.2 to 0.16.3. It ensures the project uses the latest patch release for code quality checks during development.

This commit fixes an issue where file uploads were incorrectly retained during HTTP redirects. It modifies the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to clear the `files` attribute when constructing a new request for a redirect response.

This commit cleans up the advanced user documentation by removing trailing whitespace and deleting a section of text. It updates the docs/user/advanced.rst file to improve formatting consistency. No functional code changes are included.

This commit adds two new user testimonials to the project documentation. It includes quotes from Rich Leland and Steve Pike praising the simplicity of the Requests library. The changes are located in the main documentation index file.

This commit fixes a formatting error in the timeout error message within the HTTPConnectionPool class. It corrects the string formatting specifier to ensure the timeout duration is displayed as a string rather than a float, preventing potential display issues in the error output.
This commit fixes a typo in the documentation for the Requests library. It corrects the spelling of "introducing" in a link description within the community articles section.

This commit adds a test to verify that the `sent` attribute of a request object is correctly set to true after a request is made. It also reduces the sleep duration in the test setup to speed up the test suite execution.

This commit adds a centered attribution notice to the project's README, crediting Kenneth Reitz and the Python Software Foundation. It updates the documentation to acknowledge the contributors without altering any functional code.
This commit updates the project's README to reflect a higher download count for the Requests library. It changes the stated figure from 50 million to 60 million downloads.
This commit updates the HISTORY.md file to finalize the release date for version 2.32.3. It replaces the placeholder date with May 24, 2024, and adjusts the formatting of the HTTPAdapter entry.

This commit fixes a grammatical error in the advanced user documentation by correcting the possessive form of "it" to "its." The change clarifies the explanation for customizing request behavior within the docs/user/advanced.rst file.

The documentation homepage for the requests library was updated to include status badges for license, wheel availability, Python versions, and build status. This change adds visual indicators to the main index page to provide users with quick project health information.

This commit updates the requests library to support Python 2.5 by replacing Python 3-style exception syntax with Python 2-compatible syntax in the Request class. It also adjusts the package imports in the main module to use absolute paths instead of relative ones.
This commit updates the project history to document the introduction of a new configuration system. It notes that global settings have been removed in favor of this new approach.

The `default_user_agent` function in `requests/utils.py` now accepts an optional name parameter, allowing users to customize the user agent string without modifying the entire generation logic. This change also ensures the returned string supports Unicode characters.

This commit updates the project's dependency configuration to use the standard "requests" package name instead of a specific commit hash. It refreshes the corresponding lock file to ensure the correct package version and checksums are installed.

Updates the GitHub Actions workflow in the publish.yml file to use version 5.0.0 of the actions/upload-artifact action. This major version upgrade ensures the CI pipeline uses the latest artifact upload functionality.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to version 1.8 within the requests package. It introduces a new HTTPHeaderDict class for managing HTTP headers and updates connection handling logic in the connection and connectionpool modules.

This commit updates the philosophy section of the Requests documentation to clarify the project's management structure. It renames the "Benevolent Dictator" heading to "Management Style" and expands the description to detail the specific responsibilities of the project leaders.

This commit updates the import statements in the requests models module to reference urllib3 directly instead of through the internal packages namespace. This change ensures the library correctly resolves dependencies, preventing potential import errors or version conflicts for users.

This commit establishes the initial project structure for the requests library, adding configuration files like setup.py and tox.ini. It introduces a comprehensive test suite in test_requests.py covering core functionality such as case-insensitive dictionaries, content encoding detection, and timeout handling.

This commit adds a GitHub Actions workflow to automatically close and lock issues created from specific templates. It configures the Custom and Feature request templates to apply labels that trigger this automated closure process.
This release fixes a crash in the `requests.help` module on Python 2.6 caused by a missing SSL version attribute. It also adds support for urllib3 version 1.22.

This commit updates the documentation to list Amazon as a user of the Requests library. It also reorders the existing list of organizations to place Amazon first. The change affects the project's public-facing index page.

The HTTPAdapter.send method now raises a ProxyError when a connection failure is caused by proxy issues, such as address resolution errors. This change ensures users receive a specific exception type for proxy-related problems instead of a generic connection error.

This release updates the requests library to version 0.8.6, addressing socket timeout issues and adding support for Proxy Authorization. The version number in the package initialization module is updated to reflect these changes.

This commit updates the user documentation to consistently capitalize the library name "Requests" in several sections. It corrects capitalization in the advanced guide, specifically within the SSL verification, encrypted keys, and proxy configuration descriptions.

This commit adds a promotional sidebar section to the documentation templates, featuring a link to the physical book version of the guide. It updates the sidebarintro.html and sidebarlogo.html files to display the book cover and purchase information for users.

The `super_len` function in `requests/utils.py` now returns zero for files that raise errors when determining their length, rather than assuming a default position. This change allows the library to handle such streams by chunking the data instead of failing or misreporting the size.

This commit introduces the LookupDict class to the requests.structures module. It provides a dictionary-like interface that allows users to access attributes directly as keys, returning None for missing values instead of raising an error.

This commit removes the `decode_unicode` configuration option from the `requests` library's default settings. Users will no longer see this key in the default configuration dictionary, simplifying the library's internal state.

This release fixes a bug where the Authorization header was incorrectly removed during redirects to default ports. The update bumps the library version to 2.20.1 in the version module and documents the fix in the history file.

The `requests.help` module now includes version information for the `urllib3` and `chardet` dependencies in its diagnostic output. This change also renames the `print_information` function to `main` and adds a standard entry point for direct execution.

This commit updates the `get_encoding_from_headers` function in `requests/utils.py` to explicitly return `None` when no content type is found, ensuring consistent behavior. It also adds Josselin Jacquard to the project's author list.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to clarify that the timeout parameter limits the wait for the server's initial response, not the total time to download the entire body. It corrects a previous description that incorrectly stated the timeout only affected the connection process.

This commit extends the digest authentication test in the requests test suite to verify that a second request using the same credentials bypasses the authentication challenge. It confirms that the second request succeeds directly without a redirect, ensuring the session correctly reuses the established authentication state.

This commit moves the doctest options NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE and ELLIPSIS from the requests/__init__.py module to the pytest.ini configuration file. This change ensures these flags are applied globally to all doctests in the project, rather than requiring manual specification in individual docstrings.
This commit updates the project history log to clarify a previous change. It corrects the description regarding the removal of exception handling from the dispatch_hook function.
This commit updates the advanced user documentation to remove unnecessary parentheses from an example if statement. It clarifies the syntax for checking HTTP status codes in the requests library.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Request._encode_files` method within the `requests` module. It corrects a variable reference error that previously caused incorrect field names to be used when encoding multipart form data.

This commit updates the project history to document new HTTP handling methods added to the Response class. It introduces properties and functions that allow users to check HTTP status codes and raise stored errors, improving error management.

This commit simplifies the IDNA import logic in the `PreparedRequest` class within `requests/models.py`. It removes the fallback mechanism for downstream repackagers that unvendor dependencies, ensuring the library consistently uses the standard `idna` package.

This commit fixes a UnicodeDecodeError that occurred when using Unicode header names in Python 2. The fix is implemented in the `PreparedRequest.prepare_headers` method within `requests/models.py` to ensure header names are converted to ASCII strings.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to improve response decoding and multipart form data handling. It introduces a new DeflateDecoder class to handle decompression in the response module and ensures the content type in filepost is returned as a string.

This commit refactors the proxy handling logic in the requests/utils.py module by splitting the get_environ_proxies function. It introduces a new should_bypass_proxies function to specifically determine if a URL should bypass proxies based on no_proxy settings. This change allows developers to access the bypass logic independently from the general proxy retrieval process.

This commit corrects the documentation title for the sessions module in the requests library. It updates the header in `requests/sessions.py` to accurately reflect the module name as `requests.sessions` instead of the singular form.

This commit restructures the `requests` package by moving core imports from `core.py` into `__init__.py`. This change resolves a limitation where relative splat imports were not permitted, ensuring the package initializes correctly.

This commit corrects a spelling error in the documentation for community sponsors, changing "effictive" to "effective." It also adds a missing newline at the end of the file to ensure proper formatting.

This commit updates the version number of the requests library from 0.3.1 to 0.3.2. It modifies the version constants in the core module and the documentation configuration file to reflect the new release.

This commit adds Python 3.8 beta to the project's continuous integration test matrix. It updates the Travis CI configuration and the tox environment list to include the new Python version, ensuring the codebase is tested against the upcoming release.

This commit introduces the core API for the requests library, defining the main request functions and the Response class. It establishes the foundational data structures, including the Request model and CaseInsensitiveDict, to handle HTTP interactions and response data.

This commit refactors the `get_netrc_auth` function in `requests/utils.py` to simplify how port numbers are stripped from network locations. It replaces separate logic for handling byte and string types with a unified approach that dynamically decodes the split delimiter, improving code clarity and compatibility.

This commit fixes an issue where authentication credentials in URLs were incorrectly included in HTTP request headers. It updates the HTTPAdapter to use a new utility function, urldefragauth, which strips both fragments and authentication details from URLs before processing.
This commit adds a documentation example to the advanced user guide. It demonstrates the execution of the response hook within the advanced.rst file.

This commit cleans up the formatting in the test_requests.py module. It adjusts line breaks and indentation for import statements and decorators to improve readability without changing any test behavior.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to improve readability by simplifying the example request. It replaces a complex POST request with a basic GET request using a user-agent header in the `docs/user/quickstart.rst` file.

This commit updates the CodeQL security analysis workflow to use version 4.30.8 of the github/codeql-action. The change upgrades the init, autobuild, and analyze steps in the codeql-analysis.yml file to the latest major version.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to include SSL bug fixes, improving the reliability of HTTPS connections. It modifies the VerifiedHTTPSConnection class to handle certificate requirements more robustly and updates utility functions for SSL version resolution.

This commit corrects a typo in the NOTICE file by changing the modification copyright year from 2022 to 2012. It ensures the legal attribution for Kenneth Reitz's contributions reflects the accurate timeframe.

The `Response.iter_content` method in `requests/models.py` now raises a specific `StreamConsumedError` instead of a generic `RuntimeError` when attempting to read content that has already been consumed. This change allows users to catch and handle this specific state more precisely.

This commit resolves linting violations in the requests library by standardizing string quotes and adjusting line lengths. It updates the SessionRedirectMixin class in sessions.py and the TestRequests class in tests/test_requests.py to comply with style guidelines.
Adds Nike to the list of user testimonials in the documentation index. This update highlights the company as a notable user of the project.

This commit switches the documentation theme from the custom kr sphinx theme to alabaster. It preserves the previous ad tracking functionality by adding the necessary JavaScript tags to the new layout template.
This commit removes the unused `timeout` parameter from the `Request` class in `requests/models.py`. It cleans up the constructor signature and documentation, as this argument was not functional.

This commit fixes a bug in `PreparedRequest.prepare_url` where IDNA encoding was incorrectly applied to the entire network location, limiting user info and port segments to 63 characters. It now restricts IDNA encoding to only the hostname portion, allowing for longer authentication credentials and port numbers.

The `get` function in `requests/api.py` now explicitly accepts a `params` argument, making its signature clearer for users. This change ensures query string parameters are passed directly to the underlying request handler, improving documentation and API consistency.

The test target in the Makefile now runs the test suite using the standard Python interpreter instead of the nose testing framework. This change removes the dependency on the nose package and its parallel processing capabilities for executing the test file.

This release reverts the `headers` input type to `Mapping` to resolve type invariance issues with `MutableMapping` and inferred dictionaries. Users calling `Request.headers.update()` may need to adjust their type annotations. The version number in `src/requests/__version__.py` is updated to 2.34.2.

This commit fixes a bug in the requests library where importing unrelated modules from the vendored packages namespace was incorrectly allowed. It modifies the VendorAlias class to restrict imports to specific vendored dependencies, such as urllib3 and chardet. This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 0.11.1. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the package's initialization file to reflect the new release.

This commit updates the project's README to swap the license and flourish images, correcting their placement and source URLs. It ensures the documentation displays the correct branding assets for the requests library.

This commit clarifies the documentation for the `Response.ok` property in the `requests` library. It explicitly states that the property returns a boolean value, ensuring users understand it yields `True` or `False` based on the status code.

This documentation update clarifies that OAuth 2 is the underlying protocol for OpenID Connect. It helps users searching for OpenID Connect support in the requests library find the relevant authentication section. The changes are made in the user authentication documentation file.

This commit reverts a previous change to the `PreparedRequest` class in `requests/models.py`. It restores the original behavior of the `prepare_hooks` method, which previously included a check to ensure the hooks argument was not None before processing.

The `register_hook` method in `requests.models` now validates that items in a list are callable before adding them to the hook registry. This prevents non-callable objects from being registered, which previously could cause errors during request execution. A regression test was added to ensure this validation remains in place.
This commit updates the requests library to version 2.4.2. It corrects the example URLs in the module's documentation to use secure HTTPS links and consistent quoting.

This commit updates the documentation to correct the library name from "request" to "Requests" in a user testimonial. The change ensures the proper branding is displayed on the project's main index page.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library from 0.12.1 to 0.13.0. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the package's initialization file to reflect the new release.

This commit expands the advanced user documentation for the Requests library. It details the available event hooks, such as pre_request and post_request, and explains how to attach custom callback functions to specific request stages.

The `select_proxy` function in `requests/utils.py` now correctly prioritizes specific scheme proxies over the generic "all" proxy. This fixes a bug where the wrong proxy was selected when both types were defined.

This commit updates the tox configuration to include Python 3.7 in the test environment list. It ensures the project's test suite runs against the new Python version, expanding coverage for developers using that interpreter.

This commit modifies the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to respect the `trust_env` configuration setting. It ensures that environment variables for proxies, authentication, and certificates are only applied when this setting is enabled, preventing unintended behavior for users who disable environment trust.

This commit modifies the Response class in requests/models.py to allow iter_content and iter_lines to operate on already-fetched response data. Previously, calling these methods after consuming the content would raise an error, but now they return an iterator over the stored content using a new helper function.
Adds the mock library to the project's requirements file to support test execution. This change ensures the necessary dependency is available for running the test suite.
This commit adds two blank lines to the `AuthManager` class in `requests/models.py`. It does not change any functional behavior or fix a bug, serving only as a minor formatting adjustment.

This commit updates the project description in the README to remove the phrase "Handcrafted, with ♥, for the Python community." The change simplifies the library's tagline to focus solely on it being a simple and elegant HTTP library.
