Adds a test case to the RequestsTestSuite in tests/test_requests_ext.py to verify correct cookie handling during HTTP redirects. This ensures that cookies set for a specific domain are not incorrectly applied to subsequent requests on different domains.

This commit removes the unused IteratorProxy class from the requests/structures.py module. It also deletes the now-unnecessary imports for os and itertools.islice. No user-facing behavior changes as the removed code was not utilized.

Adds a post-request hook to the Request class in requests/models.py. This allows users to modify the request object's attributes after it has been sent, providing a new extension point for custom behavior.

Adds a `settings` context manager to the `requests` module, allowing users to temporarily override global configuration values like `timeout` within a specific block of code. This change ensures that the original settings are automatically restored when the context exits, preventing unintended side effects on subsequent requests.

This commit reverts a previous change that required proxy URLs to have explicit schemes, restoring the previous behavior where missing schemes were automatically prepended. It modifies the `HTTPAdapter` class in `requests/adapters.py` and updates utility functions in `requests/utils.py` to use `prepend_scheme_if_needed` instead of raising an exception.
This commit adds the requests-logo.ai file to the project. It introduces the official logo asset for the Requests library, making it available for use in documentation or branding materials.
This commit adds David Pursehouse to the project's list of contributors. It updates the AUTHORS.rst file to include his name and contact information under the "Patches and Suggestions" section.
This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to version 1.1, ensuring compatibility with Python 3. It modifies core modules like connectionpool and response to support the new Python version.

This commit adds documentation for the `keep_alive` parameter in the `map` function within the `requests/async.py` module. It also cleans up the module's public interface list by formatting the exported names.

This commit updates the test target in the Makefile to remove an outdated reference to Python 2. It clarifies that the test suite now runs on all supported Python versions, reflecting the project's current compatibility scope.

This commit updates the project history to announce the addition of International Domain Name support in version 0.5.1. It documents this new feature for users, indicating that the software can now handle non-ASCII domain names.

This commit removes the Sphinx dependency from the package's build requirements in setup.py. This change prevents the build system from automatically installing Sphinx when setting up the project, streamlining the installation process.

This commit updates the documentation to clarify that prepared requests do not automatically apply environment variables. It warns users that settings like custom SSL certificates may be ignored, causing verification errors. The change is located in the advanced user guide.

This commit adds the OAuthlib license text to the NOTICE file. It ensures the project properly attributes the third-party OAuthlib library, which is a compliance requirement for open-source distribution.

This commit updates the release history for version 2.4.3, documenting bug fixes for Unicode URL handling in Python 2 and JSON parameter ordering. It also notes the automatic defragmentation of authentication schemes from host/pass URIs.

This commit updates the project's contribution guidelines to reflect the current development workflow. It changes the recommended branch for new contributions from "develop" to "master" in the README documentation.

This commit updates the documentation in the advanced user guide to reflect a change in function signatures. It clarifies that the `print_url` function now accepts additional positional and keyword arguments, ensuring the example code matches the current implementation.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Session` class where iterating over keyword arguments failed because it treated the dictionary as a list of tuples. It also cleans up the `merge_kwargs` function by removing debug print statements and clarifying its docstring.

This commit corrects the docstrings in the `requests.models` module, specifically for the `Request` class and its `send` method. It replaces a placeholder description with accurate documentation explaining that the method sends the HTTP request and populates the response attribute.

This commit updates the installation documentation to replace a broken Cheeseshop mirror URL with a working alternative. It changes the recommended source for installing the Requests library from a personal mirror to crate.io.

This commit updates the `_basic_auth_str` function in `requests/auth.py` to ensure compatibility with Python 2.6. It replaces modern string formatting syntax with older-style formatting in error messages, preventing syntax errors when the library runs on that legacy version.

This commit updates the API documentation to clarify that the main interface consists of five methods. It notes that these methods provide access to all Request functionality and return a Response object.
This commit adds the JSONDecodeError exception to the API documentation. It ensures users can find reference information for this specific error in the official docs.

This commit updates the project's test dependencies to newer versions. It bumps the versions of the py, pytest, and pytest-cov packages in the requirements file to ensure compatibility with the latest testing tools.

This commit updates the project's changelog to document a fix for HTTP Basic authentication. It notes that usernames and passwords extracted from URLs are now properly decoded, resolving potential issues with special characters in credentials.

This commit updates the project's contribution guidelines by removing the requirement for contributors to read the development philosophy. The change simplifies the pre-submission checklist in the CONTRIBUTING.md file, leaving only the Contributor's Guide as a mandatory resource.

This commit fixes the Codecov upload step in the Travis CI configuration. It ensures the coverage tool runs within the project's virtual environment by invoking it through Pipenv, resolving potential environment conflicts.

This commit updates the project's release history to document a change in import paths. It clarifies that code previously importing from the `requests.packages` namespace must now use direct module-level imports, providing a specific example for `urllib3`.

This commit adds a `max_retries` argument to the `request` function, `Session` class, and `HTTPAdapter` in the requests library. It allows users to specify the number of retry attempts for a request, overriding the previous default behavior where retries were fixed.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to clarify how to specify local certificates. It explicitly mentions "client side certificate" to improve searchability and explains that the certificate can be provided as a single file or a tuple of paths.

This commit fixes a platform-dependent path construction issue in the `requests/_oauth.py` module. It replaces manual string splitting with standard `os` functions to ensure the OAuth package directory is located correctly on all operating systems.

This commit introduces the OAuth1 class to the requests.auth module, enabling users to sign HTTP requests using the OAuth 1 protocol. It integrates the OAuthLib library to handle various signature methods and types, providing a new authentication option for API interactions.

This commit removes tests for the `danger_mode` configuration from the `RequestsTestSuite` in `tests/test_requests.py`. It deletes checks that verified HTTP errors were raised for non-200 responses and that redirects were handled correctly when this mode was enabled.

Adds support for automatic authentication using netrc files in the requests library. The new get_netrc_auth function in requests/utils.py reads credentials from standard netrc locations to provide username and password pairs for HTTP requests.

This commit adds a failing test to the RequestsTestCase in test_requests.py. It verifies that the URL attributes in a response's history are not incorrectly overridden by the request URLs, ensuring the original redirect chain is preserved.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to advise users on handling large file uploads. It notes that the standard requests library does not support streaming multipart requests by default and recommends using the requests-toolbelt package for this purpose.

This commit updates the project documentation to correct a cross-reference link and improve the clarity of the introductory text. It modifies the main index file to better describe the library's purpose and address the limitations of Python's built-in HTTP modules.

The `full_url` method in the `Request` class now raises an `InvalidURL` exception instead of a `UnicodeError` when a URL contains an invalid label. This change provides a clearer, more specific error message to users attempting to process malformed URLs.

This commit corrects the documentation for the `get_unicode_from_response` function in the `requests` module. It removes an inaccurate step regarding meta charset detection, ensuring the docstring accurately reflects the function's actual fallback behavior.

This commit fixes a bug in the HTTPDigestAuth class where authentication failed if the request URI included a query string. The handle_401 method now correctly constructs the path for the digest calculation by explicitly appending the query string with a question mark.

Updates the PyPI publishing GitHub Action in the publish workflow from version 1.13.0 to 1.14.0. This minor version bump ensures the CI pipeline uses the latest stable release of the pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish tool.

This commit introduces a new `ChunkedEncodingError` exception to handle cases where a server sends invalid chunked data. It updates `Response.iter_content` in `requests/models.py` to catch `IncompleteRead` errors and raise this specific exception instead of failing silently or with a generic error.

This commit fixes the `Session.merge_environment_settings` method in `requests/sessions.py` to correctly preserve the existing `verify` setting when no environment variables are defined. Previously, the method would incorrectly override the user's verification configuration if `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` or `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` were not set.

This commit fixes a minor grammatical error in the docstring of the stream_decode_response_unicode function within the requests/utils.py module. It corrects the article used to describe the input parameter, changing "a iterator" to "an iterator" for proper English usage.

In the `PreparedRequest` class, the logic for handling the `data` parameter was updated to explicitly check for an empty dictionary instead of a falsy value. This ensures that passing an empty dictionary does not incorrectly trigger the JSON encoding path. A redundant encoding step was also removed from the corresponding test case.

The `Request` class in `requests/core.py` now automatically decompresses gzip-encoded response bodies when the content-encoding header is present. This ensures users receive readable data instead of compressed bytes for supported responses.

This commit adds documentation to the advanced user guide explaining how to control HTTP header ordering. It clarifies that passing an OrderedDict to the headers argument preserves custom order, though default headers from the requests library take precedence.

The `where` function in `requests/certs.py` now prioritizes the `certifi` package for locating the CA certificate bundle. If `certifi` is unavailable, it falls back to the previously bundled certificate file.
This commit removes debug print statements from the Request class in requests/models.py. It also adds tests to verify that cookies set by a server persist correctly across requests within a session.

This commit makes the test server port configurable by reading the HTTPBIN_PORT environment variable instead of using a hardcoded value. It updates the RequestsTestSuite setup to use this dynamic port for both the base URL and the gunicorn server connection.

This commit updates the bundled chardet and urllib3 libraries within the requests package to their latest versions. It refreshes the internal code for character encoding detection and HTTP connection handling, including updates to the UniversalDetector and HTTPConnectionPool classes.

This commit adds documentation to the user guide explaining how Requests handles character encodings and adheres to RFC standards. It clarifies that the library prioritizes HTTP headers for encoding detection before falling back to automatic detection, helping users understand potential response behavior.

This commit corrects the documentation for the `Response.ok` property in the `requests` library. It clarifies that the property returns true for any status code below 400, rather than specifically checking for a 200 OK response. This prevents user confusion regarding the actual behavior of the attribute.
This commit updates the documentation for the Reddit module. It corrects a typo in a warning message and adds Reddit to the list of user testimonials.

Adds a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow to automatically lock inactive issues and pull requests. This prevents stale threads from remaining open indefinitely. The new configuration is defined in the lock-issues.yml file.

This commit updates the development documentation to reflect that the master branch is now the primary target for contributions. It also corrects the link to the AUTHORS file to point to the master branch instead of the develop branch.

This commit updates the project's README documentation to include example output for request objects. It clarifies how the library displays response data to users by adding placeholder text to the examples.

This commit updates the Pipfile to align dependency versions with setup.py, specifically pinning pytest and pytest-httpbin to stricter constraints. It also adds Sphinx and Alabaster to the development dependencies to support documentation generation.

This commit updates the `setup.py` module to dynamically load package metadata from a central `about` dictionary instead of using hardcoded strings. This change ensures that the project name, description, author, and license information remain consistent with the source code.

This commit adds unit tests to verify that the `iter_content` method in the `requests` library correctly returns Unicode strings when the `decode_unicode` option is enabled. It ensures this behavior works for both standard and streaming responses, preventing potential encoding errors for users.

Adds tests to the RequestsTestSuite in test_requests.py to verify HTTP status handling. It checks that response objects evaluate to False for errors, that the ok attribute reflects success, and that raise_for_status correctly raises exceptions or passes for valid responses.
This commit adds section labels to the advanced user documentation in the requests library. These labels enable other projects to create direct links to specific topics using Intersphinx.
This commit removes the standalone unicode test suite from the project. It deletes the test file that previously verified HTTP response handling for various character encodings.

This commit fixes URL resolution in the `Request` class by replacing manual string concatenation with the standard `urljoin` function. This ensures relative URLs are correctly resolved against the parent request URL, preventing malformed links.

This commit fixes a documentation build error in the requests library where unescaped asterisks in docstrings caused Sphinx to fail. It updates the parameter descriptions for the get, post, put, and other HTTP method functions in requests/api.py to properly escape the double asterisks.

This commit replaces the direct nosetests invocation in the test script with a tox-based workflow. It introduces a new configuration file that defines test environments for Python versions 2.4 through 2.7, standardizing how the test suite is executed across different interpreters.

This commit adds a test to the TestRequests class in tests/test_requests.py that verifies a security fix for netrc credential leakage. It ensures that requests to malicious URLs with specific prefixes do not incorrectly apply credentials intended for a different domain.

This commit updates the redirect handling in the `SessionRedirectMixin` class to improve authentication management. When a request is redirected to a different host, it now strips existing authorization headers and repopulates them using credentials from the user's `.netrc` file if available.

This commit fixes the OAuth1 authentication class in requests/auth.py to correctly handle requests without a Content-Type header, preventing unnecessary signature generation. It also resolves a bug where the body parameter was incorrectly checked against the string type instead of the body variable itself.
This commit adds Rhys Elsmore to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS.rst file. It updates the project's credit list to acknowledge the individual's patches and suggestions.

This commit fixes a linting error in the requests version module by removing a trailing blank line at the end of the file. It ensures the codebase complies with flake8 style guidelines regarding file endings.

The `Request.send` method in `requests/models.py` now passes the request timeout to the underlying urllib3 connection. This ensures that network requests respect the configured timeout, raising a `Timeout` exception if the connection exceeds the limit.

This commit integrates the urllib3 library into the requests package by adding its core modules for connection pooling and HTTP handling. It introduces classes like HTTPConnectionPool and PoolManager to manage thread-safe connections and request execution.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to version 1.16, bringing in various bug fixes and improvements to the HTTP connection handling. It modifies core modules like connectionpool and response to ensure compatibility and stability for users making HTTP requests.

This commit corrects the HTTP status code for the "im_used" informational response in the requests library. It updates the mapping in `status_codes.py` to use the correct IANA-assigned code 226 instead of the incorrect 208.

This release fixes an error when accessing the text or JSON content of responses that lack a body. It also enables passing file-like objects as data and allows hooks to return error responses. The changes are reflected in the requests package version 0.13.1.

This commit reorganizes import statements in the requests package's main module to satisfy flake8 linting rules. It moves version-related imports to the end of the file and updates the Makefile to ignore the E402 error code, ensuring the codebase passes static analysis checks.
This commit updates the contributing documentation to correct the formatting of the PEP 8 reference. It ensures the style guide name is consistently written with a space in the contributing guide.
This commit releases version 2.18.3 of the requests library. It updates the version number in the `__version__.py` module and finalizes the release notes in the history file.

This commit updates the .gitignore file to exclude Python bytecode and Vim swap files from version control. It also removes the previous exclusion of the .gitignore file itself and cleans up the file's line endings.

This commit adds documentation warnings to the Requests library's user guides, specifically in the advanced and quickstart sections. It advises users to open files in binary mode to prevent errors when the library calculates the Content-Length header.

This commit updates the project's README to display a more realistic API example using the GitHub repository URL. It also corrects a malformed HTML closing tag and adjusts the layout of the introductory text.

This commit updates the project's metadata in setup.py to declare compatibility with Python 3.2 and 3.3. It adds the corresponding classifiers so that package indexes correctly display support for these newer Python versions.

This commit fixes an issue where 301 redirect requests failed to use the configured proxy settings. The change updates the `Request._build_response` method in `requests/models.py` to pass the proxy configuration when constructing the new response object.

This commit updates the basic authentication test in the TestRequests class to accommodate httpbin's lack of support for byte strings. It modifies the test parameters to include pre-computed authentication strings and changes the request logic to use a standard GET endpoint instead of the specific basic-auth route.

This commit removes the `test_DIGESTAUTH_THREADED` test from the `TestRequests` class in `test_requests.py`. The test previously verified that HTTP digest authentication worked correctly when making concurrent requests using a thread pool.

This commit updates the build status badge in the project's README to reference the master branch instead of the develop branch. This ensures the displayed CI status accurately reflects the current default branch for the Requests library.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to version 1.2.2. It introduces new exception classes for host changes and location parsing errors, and modifies the connection pool logic to use a LifoQueue for managing connections.

This commit updates the documentation for the `verify` parameter in the `requests` library. It clarifies that users can pass a string path to a CA bundle file, adding a code example to illustrate this usage.

This commit updates the project's README to replace the "Say Thanks" badge with a download count badge from PePy. It also refreshes the library's tagline and expands the list of officially supported Python versions to include 3.8.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to clarify the difference between `Response.iter_content` and `Response.raw`. It explains that `iter_content` automatically decodes compressed data, while `raw` provides the untransformed byte stream. This helps users choose the correct method for accessing response data.

This commit fixes a bug where the generic "all" proxy setting incorrectly overrode specific scheme-based proxies. The `select_proxy` function and `SessionRedirectMixin.rebuild_proxies` now prioritize specific scheme proxies over the generic fallback.

This commit corrects the package names in the Pipfile to match their official PyPI identifiers, ensuring dependencies like Sphinx and pytest plugins are recognized properly. It also updates the Pipfile.lock to reflect these changes and adjust the dependency tree accordingly.
This commit updates the project history to document a bug fix in the `parse_header_links()` function. It clarifies that parsing empty Link headers no longer incorrectly returns a single bogus entry.

This commit adds Rohan Jain to the project's list of contributors. It updates the AUTHORS.rst file to include his name under the "Patches and Suggestions" section, acknowledging his contributions to the codebase.

This commit adds a link to a French blog post about the Requests library to the community documentation. It updates the "Articles & Talks" section in the out-there.rst file to include this new resource.

This commit refactors the settings module to define a default timeout value directly within the module scope. It updates the core module to import the Settings class explicitly, ensuring the configuration object is properly initialized.

This commit fixes an issue where POST requests were not correctly redirected after a 303 response. It ensures the HTTP method is upper-cased in the Session.request method to match the redirect logic. A new test verifies that POST redirects work as expected.

The `Request.prepare` method in `requests/models.py` now automatically extracts authentication credentials from the URL if no explicit auth is provided. This allows users to include basic authentication directly in the request URL without manually parsing it.

This commit updates the Codecov badge in the project's README to point to the correct repository location. It fixes a broken link that previously referenced the old organization name, ensuring the coverage status displays properly for users.

This commit updates the package configuration to declare supported Python versions, preventing pip from installing the library on incompatible interpreters. The change modifies the setup.py file to include the python_requires argument, ensuring users receive a clear error if their Python version is unsupported.
This commit adds Flavio Curella to the project's list of contributors. It updates the AUTHORS.rst file to credit the new author for patches and suggestions.

This commit adds project URLs to the package metadata in setup.py. It provides direct links to the documentation and source code repository, making these resources easily accessible from the package's public information.

The HTTPAdapter class now raises an IOError instead of a generic exception when a user provides an invalid path for a CA bundle or certificate file. This change ensures that missing or non-existent file paths are explicitly reported as input errors during SSL verification setup.

This commit fixes import errors in the requests library by updating the poster package to use relative imports. It ensures that the streaminghttp and encode modules are correctly loaded within the packages namespace.

This commit updates the documentation for link headers to accurately reflect the current code behavior. It corrects the example output for the `links` attribute, showing that it now returns a dictionary containing URL and relation details instead of a simple string.

Updates the PyPI publishing GitHub Action in the publish workflow from version 1.12.4 to 1.13.0. This minor version bump ensures the CI pipeline uses the latest stable release of the action for deploying packages.

This commit updates the `AuthObject` class in `requests/models.py` to use a patched version of the HTTP basic authentication handler. It ensures that the default authentication mechanism relies on the corrected handler implementation rather than the standard library version.

This commit adds a test to verify that `Session` objects correctly persist and merge query parameters across multiple requests. It ensures that default parameters are included in subsequent calls and can be overridden or removed by passing new parameters.

This commit adds the HTTP 511 status code to the status code dictionary in the requests library. It ensures that the "Network Authentication Required" response is properly recognized and mapped to its standard aliases.
This commit adds a link to the httpbin.org website in the documentation sidebar. It updates the sidebarintro.html and sidebarlogo.html templates to include this external resource for users.
This commit adds a new TODO.rst file to the project. It lists a task to fix 405 Exceptions, indicating a planned change to handle HTTP Method Not Allowed errors.
This commit updates the documentation index to correct the formatting of the Python version recommendation. It changes the emphasis on the word "highly" from bold to italics in the warning message.

This commit adds PyPy to the test environment list in the tox configuration. It defines a specific test environment for PyPy that uses the pypy-c interpreter, allowing the project's test suite to run under this alternative Python implementation.

This commit optimizes the `prepare_headers` method in the `PreparedRequest` class by instantiating the `CaseInsensitiveDict` directly from the header items. This avoids creating an intermediate dictionary, making the header preparation process faster.

This commit updates the documentation to include the necessary import statement in the introductory code examples. It ensures users can copy and run the demo snippets without errors by adding the missing import line to the README and docs index.

This commit simplifies the `_parse_content_type_header` function in `requests/utils.py` by replacing explicit slice objects with direct string slicing syntax. The change removes unnecessary variable assignments while preserving the exact same behavior for parsing content type parameters.
This commit adds Rubén Abad to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS file. It updates the project's credit list to acknowledge his patches and suggestions.
Adds a JavaScript snippet to the documentation layout to integrate Gauges analytics tracking. This enables the collection of visitor statistics for the site.

This commit ensures that cookies from the response are correctly extracted and stored in the Response object. It introduces a new utility function, dict_from_cookiejar, in requests/utils.py to convert cookie data into a dictionary. The Request class now uses this function to populate the cookies attribute during response construction.
This commit removes outdated Python 3.1 and 3.2 version classifiers from the project's setup configuration. It also adds the tox.ini file to the gitignore list to prevent it from being tracked.

This documentation update clarifies that the `requests.Session` class is not a context manager. It corrects the API example in `docs/api.rst` to show standard instantiation and usage, removing the incorrect `with` statement.

This commit updates the API documentation to clarify that the streaming logic was inverted in version 1.0. It notes that the old `prefetch` parameter is now `stream`, and that `stream` is required for raw response reading.

This commit updates the library to import abstract base classes from the collections.abc module instead of the deprecated collections module. This ensures compatibility with Python 3.10 and later, where these classes were removed from the original location. The change affects core classes like RequestsCookieJar and CaseInsensitiveDict.

This commit changes the order of operations in the `Request.prepare` method within the `requests` module. It ensures that authentication is prepared before the request body, which may affect how credentials are applied to the final request.
This commit updates the .gitignore file to exclude the MANIFEST file from version control. This prevents the build artifact from being accidentally committed to the repository.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 0.11.3. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the package's initialization file to reflect the new release.
The requests library now attempts to import its async module during initialization. If the async module is unavailable, the import failure is silently ignored to prevent startup errors.

This commit fixes a typo in the quickstart documentation where "HTTP" was incorrectly used instead of "HTML" when describing content encoding. The change updates the user guide to accurately reflect that HTML and XML formats specify their encoding.

The `Response.json` method in `requests/models.py` now returns `None` instead of raising an exception when the response body contains invalid JSON. This change ensures that parsing failures are handled gracefully, allowing users to check for `None` to detect malformed data.

This commit fixes a test in the TestTimeout class within test_requests.py that was incorrectly passing without verifying the expected exception types. It ensures the test properly asserts that a connection timeout raises both a ConnectionError and a Timeout exception.

This commit introduces a new requests namespace, updating documentation and core modules like requests/auth.py and requests/sessions.py. It refines URL handling and authentication logic, ensuring digest auth resets correctly on redirects and that user agents transfer properly.

This commit updates the project documentation by removing a special Unicode symbol from the introductory text in the index file. It corrects the display of the library description to use standard characters, ensuring the text renders correctly for all users.
This commit updates the project history for version 0.10.2, noting significant improvements to URL quoting and the addition of new allowed cookie key values.

This commit adds explanatory comments to the `Request._build_url` method in `requests/models.py`. It clarifies the steps for handling international domain names, encoding paths, and processing query parameters. No functional behavior is changed.

This commit fixes a typo in the `Request` class within `requests/models.py` that caused a crash when building a response. The `_build_response` method now correctly closes the underlying connection object instead of referencing a non-existent attribute.
This commit updates the project's changelog to document a bug fix in the `Response.history` attribute. It clarifies that a previous issue affecting the response history has been resolved.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar template to replace the previous sponsorship credit for Linode with a new credit for the Government of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. It also removes the embedded social media follow buttons for the project maintainer from the sidebar.

This commit fixes the `Response.iter_content` method in `requests/models.py` to correctly handle the first chunk of a response by respecting the specified chunk size. It also ensures the underlying file descriptor is properly closed at the end of the iteration to prevent resource leaks.

This commit allows subclasses of string and bytes types to be used as HTTP header parts, preventing validation errors for custom types. It updates the header validation logic in the requests.utils module to correctly handle these subclasses.

This commit updates the documentation in `docs/index.rst` to remove a redundant link to the Requests 3 project page. It simplifies the maintenance-mode notice for Requests 2.x by keeping the text but deleting the extra hyperlink.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar templates to reposition the newsletter subscription section. It moves the "Get Updates" block within the sidebar intro and logo files to adjust the layout.

The CI configuration now installs the project package itself before installing the remaining dependencies. This ensures the local code is available during the test run, preventing potential import errors or version mismatches.

This commit refactors the `Response` class in `requests/models.py` to delegate encoding detection to a utility function. It removes internal logic for parsing content types and encoding from the response object, simplifying the class structure.
This commit updates the Makefile to suppress F821 errors during flake8 checks. It prevents the linter from flagging undefined names, which may occur in dynamic code contexts.

This commit updates the documentation's custom stylesheet to target a specific search dropdown element within the sidebar. It replaces a broad selector with a precise path to ensure the styling applies only to the intended interface component.

Adds a new `iter_json` method to the `Response` class in `requests/models.py`. This allows users to efficiently parse and yield JSON objects from a stream of newline-delimited data, filtering out empty lines.

The `curl_from_request` function in `requests/utils.py` now supports file uploads by generating the appropriate curl command arguments. This change allows users to convert requests containing file data into executable curl commands, replacing the previous placeholder for this feature.

This commit updates the project's build and CI configuration by renaming the Travis CI script target to `travis` and adding a new `PYFLAKES_WHITELIST` variable to the Makefile. It also refines the `.gitignore` file to exclude coverage reports and pyflakes violation logs from version control.

The `should_bypass_proxies` function in `requests/utils.py` now correctly returns `True` for URLs without a hostname, such as those using the `file` scheme. This prevents errors when checking proxy settings for local file paths.

This commit adds a trailing newline to the end of the `_get_autoauth` function in `requests/core.py`. It ensures the file ends with a proper line break, which is a standard convention for text files. No functional behavior is changed.

The Session class in the requests module now defaults the verify parameter to True, ensuring SSL certificate verification is enabled by default for security. This change also bumps the library version to 0.9.0.

This commit updates the dependency marker in setup.py to use sys_platform instead of platform_system. This change improves compatibility for users installing the package on Windows with Python versions older than 3.3, preventing potential installation failures.

This commit fixes a bug where unpickled Session objects contained an extra, obsolete attribute not present in the original instance. By removing the 'prefetch' entry from the Session class's __attrs__ list, the unpickled session now matches the original exactly.

This commit changes the authentication mechanism in the requests library to use callable objects instead of tuples. Users can now pass any callable as the auth argument, which modifies the request before dispatch. The main changes involve the AuthBase class and related authentication handlers in requests/auth.py.

This commit removes legacy code and compatibility shims for Python 2.6 from the requests library. It simplifies the logging setup in `requests/__init__.py` by removing the custom `NullHandler` fallback and updates string formatting in `requests/adapters.py` and other modules to use modern syntax.

This commit restructures the configuration system by renaming the config module to `_config` and updating imports across the API, models, and sessions modules. It modifies the `request` function and `Session` class to use a new `get_config` helper and a dictionary-style `get` method for accessing settings like timeouts and proxies.
This commit updates the project's README documentation. It replaces a blank line with a non-breaking space paragraph to adjust the page layout.

This commit updates the project's README to fix the logo image source. It changes the URL to point to the correct file location within the repository, ensuring the logo displays properly for users viewing the documentation.

This commit updates the project's README to correct the placement of the Python version support statement and the satisfaction guarantee. It moves the support details to a more logical position within the documentation and adjusts the wording of the guarantee.

This commit corrects a documentation error in the advanced user guide where a streaming example incorrectly used a POST request. It changes the method to GET to prevent a 405 error when accessing the httpbin stream endpoint.

This commit updates the Ruff pre-commit hook from version 0.16.0 to 0.16.1 in the .pre-commit-config.yaml file. It ensures the project uses the latest patch release of the Ruff linter for code quality checks.

This commit fixes a crash in the requests library's status_codes module that occurred when running Python with the optimization flag enabled. The _init function now correctly handles cases where the module docstring is missing, preventing a type error during initialization.

This commit pins the pipenv version to 3.1.9 in the Makefile to prevent installation of newer, potentially unstable releases. It ensures the project's initialization process uses a known working version of the dependency manager.

This commit standardizes how the requests library handles data structures, ensuring that both dictionaries and lists of key-value pairs are accepted for parameters like headers and cookies. It updates the Session class and utility functions to use a new from_key_val_list helper, improving consistency across the library.
This commit updates the .gitignore file to exclude the requests.egg-info/ directory from version control. This prevents build artifacts from being accidentally committed to the repository.
This commit removes a horizontal rule from the project's README file. It cleans up the documentation layout without altering any functional code or behavior.

This commit updates the version to 2.6.0 and documents a security fix in the `requests` library. It resolves a cookie handling vulnerability on redirects that could expose users to session fixation attacks.

This commit replaces the placeholder documentation index with a comprehensive introduction to the Requests library. It highlights the library's simplicity and ease of use compared to standard Python modules, providing a basic example of making an HTTP request.

This commit adds a one-second timeout to the `test_connection_error_invalid_port` test in `test_requests.py`. This change accelerates the test failure when connecting to an invalid port, preventing the test suite from hanging indefinitely.

This commit upgrades the bundled charade library to version 1.0.3, improving character encoding detection accuracy. It adds a check in the detect function to ensure input is a bytes object, preventing errors when unicode strings are passed.

This commit updates the community documentation to list the python-rexster project. It adds a reference to the Rexter client, which provides a simple interface for graph databases, to the "Modules" section of the out-there guide.

This commit removes a misleading comment from the `_parse_content_type_header` function in `requests/utils.py`. The comment incorrectly claimed that using a dictionary literal was faster than initializing an empty dictionary, which is not true. This change clarifies the code without altering its behavior.
This commit finalizes the release notes for version 0.6.3 by setting the release date to October 13, 2011. It updates the HISTORY.rst file to reflect the official release status.

This commit adds a test to ensure that the requests library does not raise a TypeError when a header value is set to None. It verifies that the library handles this edge case gracefully without crashing.

This commit clarifies the documentation for the `Session` class in `requests/sessions.py`. It corrects the description of the `cert` attribute to explicitly state that it is used for SSL client certificates, rather than just generic SSL certificates.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Request` class where URL paths were incorrectly double-escaped. It ensures that special characters in the path are properly encoded only once, preventing malformed request URLs.

This commit updates pre-commit hook versions and applies minor code style fixes across the requests library. It removes unnecessary parentheses in tuple unpacking within modules like models and adapters, and cleans up blank lines in auth and adapters.

This commit removes a stale package reference from the project's setup configuration. It fixes an installation error caused by trying to include a module that no longer exists in the source code. The change updates the `setup.py` file to reflect the current project structure.

Previously, sending both query parameters and a request body in a POST or PUT request would raise an error. This change allows the `post` and `put` functions in `requests/api.py` to accept both simultaneously, passing them separately to the `Request` class for proper handling.

This commit updates the cookie handling logic in the `requests` package to reference RFC 2965 instead of the outdated RFC 2068. It renames the internal variable tracking forbidden characters to reflect the new standard, ensuring the module aligns with current cookie specifications.
The README now links the TravisCI status badge to the live status page for the master branch. This change updates the image URL in the README.rst file to reflect the correct branch.
The close-issues workflow no longer passes a custom token to its jobs. This removes the reliance on the MY_TOKEN secret for authentication.

This commit standardizes the spelling of "behavior" to "behaviour" across the project's documentation. It updates the API, community support, and advanced user guides to ensure consistent British English usage.

This commit upgrades the bundled urllib3 library to version 1.9.x within the requests package. It updates core modules like connection handling, pooling, and utilities to reflect the new version's features and changes.

This commit clarifies the documentation for the timeout parameter in the requests library. It explicitly states that the timeout value is measured in seconds for the request function and the Session class.

This commit adds unit tests for the requests.structures module, specifically covering the CaseInsensitiveDict and LookupDict classes. It verifies behaviors such as case-insensitive key access, item retrieval, and representation formatting.

This commit simplifies the test initialization module by removing legacy import logic for the urllib3 package. It now directly imports urllib3 and its exceptions, eliminating the previous conditional checks for bundled versus standalone versions.

This commit adds support for proxy authentication by introducing a new HTTPProxyAuth class in requests/auth.py. It allows users to pass credentials for proxies, which are then attached to requests via the Proxy-Authorization header. The Request class in requests/models.py is updated to parse proxy URLs and apply this authentication automatically.
This commit fixes a punctuation error in the advanced user documentation. It replaces a period with a comma in the sentence describing automatic keep-alive behavior within a session.
This commit updates the project's dependency list to include flake8 for code linting. It also fixes a missing newline at the end of the requirements file.
This commit updates the copyright year in the requests package from 2013 to 2014. It modifies the copyright metadata strings within the `requests/__init__.py` module to reflect the current year.

This commit adds the regular expressions module to the imports in the requests models file. It prepares the codebase for future functionality that requires pattern matching within the request or response handling logic.

This release fixes a security vulnerability in the requests library where a malicious URL could cause the wrong hostname's credentials to be retrieved from a netrc file. It also includes various documentation improvements. The version number in the module is updated to 2.32.4.

This refactoring removes duplicate code in the requests authentication module by introducing a shared helper function. It ensures that both HTTPBasicAuth and HTTPProxyAuth use the same logic to generate Basic Auth headers, improving maintainability without changing user-facing behavior.

This commit updates the requests library to improve PEP8 compliance by replacing `== None` comparisons with `is not None` and fixing spacing in tuple definitions. It affects core modules such as `requests/auth.py`, `requests/cookies.py`, and `requests/compat.py`, as well as several test files.

This commit updates the documentation index to include Heroku and Transifex in the list of testimonials. It adds these two companies to the existing mention of PayPal, expanding the section that highlights user endorsements.
This commit updates the project documentation to recognize Niteo as a new sponsor. It adds a section to the sponsors page detailing their contribution to the 2018 Requests 3.0 fundraiser.

This documentation update corrects an example in the advanced user guide for the `merge_environment_settings` function. It replaces an incorrect `None` argument with an empty dictionary to accurately reflect the expected usage for environment settings.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to fix inconsistent spacing in code examples. It standardizes the formatting of dictionary arguments in HTTP request examples within the `docs/user/quickstart.rst` file.

This commit updates the project's changelog to document version 2.14.0. It highlights new support for the `no_proxy` key in proxy settings and improved error handling for invalid certificate paths. Additionally, it notes bug fixes for non-ASCII redirect headers.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to remove a reference to GitHub. It replaces the example of fetching GitHub's public timeline with a generic test using httpbin. The change clarifies the initial request example in the user guide.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Request` class where relative URLs with query strings were incorrectly encoded during redirection. By encoding only the path component, the `Request._build_response` method now preserves query parameters, preventing broken redirects.

This commit updates the `test_uppercase_scheme_redirect` test in `test_requests.py` to verify that the final response URL matches the expected redirect target. It ensures the test correctly validates the URL returned by the request, improving the reliability of the test suite.

This commit moves the safe mode exception handling from the top-level API request function to the Session class. This ensures that safe mode correctly catches errors when using Session objects, not just direct API calls. The change primarily affects the Session class and the safe_mode module.

This commit updates the project history to document the removal of the legacy AuthManager and related classes. It notes the replacement of urllib2-based authentication with a new tuple-based system that uses handler callbacks.
This commit updates the advanced user documentation to clarify how proxy environment variables are configured. It also adds a note specifying that proxy URLs must include the scheme.
Adds a basic test suite for the requests module. The new RequestsTestCase class includes a placeholder test that verifies a simple assertion.

This documentation update clarifies that the `async.map` function returns a new list rather than modifying the original input. It addresses user confusion by explicitly assigning the result to a variable in the example within the advanced user guide.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` is refactored to use explicit keyword arguments instead of a generic dictionary. This change makes the function signature clearer and allows for better type checking and documentation.

This commit disables the `test_invalid_content` and `test_safe_mode` tests within the `RequestsTestSuite` class in `tests/test_requests.py`. These tests were removed to prevent flaky failures caused by unreliable DNS resolution or network connectivity issues during test execution.

This commit adds a test to the RequestsTestCase in test_requests.py to verify that sending a multipart POST request with unicode data and a file attachment works correctly. It ensures the request returns a successful status code when handling non-ASCII characters in the form data.

This commit adds support for HTTPS client certificates by exposing `key_file` and `cert_file` parameters in the `requests` library. Users can now pass these files to the `request` function or `Session` to authenticate with servers requiring client-side SSL certificates.

This commit fixes a regular expression in the `parse_header_links` function within `requests/utils.py`. It corrects the pattern used to split header values, ensuring that links separated by commas and spaces are parsed correctly.

This commit adds the HTTP 421 Misdirected Request status code to the requests library. It updates the status_codes module to include this new code, allowing users to reference it in their applications.
This commit updates the project's README documentation file. It adds a single blank line to the file, likely to improve formatting or spacing. No functional code or user-facing behavior is changed.
This commit updates the documentation to include a hyperlink to the author's Twitter profile. It modifies the text in the main documentation file to make the author's name clickable for users.

This commit updates the project's contributor list by adding Honza Javorek to the "Patches and Suggestions" section. It acknowledges a new contributor without altering any functional code or behavior.

This commit updates the documentation index to expand the displayed table of contents depth from one level to three. It also adds a new entry for the community extensions section, making these additional resources visible to users browsing the docs.

This update bumps the urllib3 version to 1.13.1 within the requests package. It fixes a bug in the VerifiedHTTPSConnection class where IPv6 hostnames were not properly validated because square brackets were not stripped before checking the certificate.

This commit updates the usage example in the requests package's main module to use Python 3 syntax. It changes the print statement in the documentation to include parentheses, ensuring the example is valid for modern Python versions.
This commit adds a MANIFEST.in file to the documentation package. It ensures that the history, readme, and license files are included when building the distribution.

This commit removes the documentation page for community extensions from the project's docs. It deletes the file that previously listed curated third-party tools and libraries built on top of the Requests library.

This commit updates the project's contributor list by adding Chris Adams to the "Patches and Suggestions" section. It ensures the AUTHORS file accurately reflects all individuals who have contributed to the codebase.
This commit adds a build status badge to the project's README file. It displays the current CI status for the develop branch, allowing users to quickly verify the project's health.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to remove the invalid charset parameter from JSON content-type headers. It corrects the example response headers to accurately reflect that JSON types do not include a charset specification.

This commit updates the test suite in test_requests.py to use py.test style assertions and context managers instead of unittest methods. It modernizes the codebase without changing the underlying behavior of the cookie parsing functions.

This commit fixes broken tests in the RequestsTestSuite within test_requests.py. It removes outdated headers and commented-out code, then re-enables assertions to verify that POST requests to the postbin service return a successful status code.

This commit improves the documentation for the `Response.text` property in the `requests` module. It clarifies that a `LookupError` occurs when an encoding is not found, often due to a misspelling, before the code attempts a blind encoding.
This commit fixes a broken hyperlink in the project documentation. It corrects the syntax in the index file so the link to the external code example renders properly for users.
The CI workflow now tests against the stable Python 3.13 release instead of a development version. It enables prerelease package installation to ensure compatibility with the latest dependencies.

This commit updates the build process to use the "release" branch of the urllib3 dependency instead of the "python3" branch. It ensures the project builds against the stable release version of the library.

This commit ensures that proxy URLs include an explicit scheme, preventing errors when the scheme is missing. It replaces the automatic scheme prepending logic in the HTTPAdapter with a validation check that raises an exception if the scheme is absent.

This commit fixes an issue where accessing the text property of a response with an empty body would fail. It ensures that the Response.text method in the requests module correctly returns an empty string when the response content is missing.

This commit corrects the indentation of a comment in the installation documentation to ensure it renders properly. The change fixes a formatting error in the `docs/user/install.rst` file, improving the visual presentation for users reading the setup instructions.

This commit adds the urllib3 library to the requests package, providing thread-safe connection pooling and reuse for HTTP requests. It introduces the HTTPConnectionPool class to manage persistent connections and handle retries, improving performance for users making multiple requests to the same host.

This commit fixes a bug in the HTTPDigestAuth class where concurrent requests would fail authentication due to a shared counter. By changing the num_401_calls attribute to a threading.local instance, each thread now maintains its own independent count of 401 responses. This ensures that simultaneous authentication requests do not interfere with one another.

This commit updates the project documentation to list new features, including gevent support, session cookie persistence, and various authentication methods. It also modifies the sessions module to support these capabilities.

This commit updates the project's README to fix a broken badge link. It corrects the URL for the "Say Thanks" badge by properly encoding the space character, ensuring the image displays correctly for users viewing the documentation.

This commit updates the project's README to replace Markdown badge syntax with raw HTML image tags. The change affects the display of download, version, and contributor statistics in the project documentation.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to clarify how to handle chunked encoded responses. It advises using the `iter_content` method on the `Response` object, specifically recommending a chunk size of `None` when the request is streamed.

This commit updates the documentation in docs/dev/todo.rst to reflect the current Python version support. It removes Python 3.1 and 3.2 from the list and adds Python 3.4 and 3.5, ensuring users see accurate compatibility information.

This commit updates the project's setup configuration to explicitly declare support for Python 3. It adds the appropriate classifier to the package metadata, ensuring the project is correctly identified as compatible with the Python 3 language version.

This commit adds a helper function named `dict_to_sequence` to the `requests/sessions.py` module. It standardizes input by converting dictionary-like objects into a sequence of key-value pairs, ensuring consistent handling for internal dictionary updates.

This commit changes the type annotation for the `headers` attribute in the `Request` class from a mutable mapping to a standard mapping. It also updates the `HeadersType` alias in the types module to reflect this change, ensuring the API correctly represents headers as read-only data.

This commit performs a minor cleanup in the `requests` library's `models` module. It removes an unnecessary blank line within the `Request` class definition, improving code readability without altering functionality.

This commit removes the Hellobar advertisement script from the documentation layout. Users will no longer see the promotional banner at the top of the documentation pages. The change modifies the `layout.html` template file.

This commit updates the package description in setup.py to "Python HTTP for Humans." It changes the metadata displayed for the project, replacing the previous tagline with a simpler, more user-friendly phrase.

This commit updates the project documentation to reflect that the library now officially supports Python 3.7. It clarifies the supported version range for users checking compatibility. The change is made in the README file.

This commit removes a redundant comment from the `prepare_body` method in the `PreparedRequest` class within `requests/models.py`. The comment was already present earlier in the file, so its removal cleans up the code without changing any functionality.

This commit corrects the docstring for the `_map_api_methods` method within the `Session` class in `requests/sessions.py`. It fixes minor grammatical errors and punctuation to improve the clarity of the documentation. No functional code changes were made.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the `requests/async.py` module that prevented the code from running on Python 2.5. It updates the `_patched` function to correctly pass the `return_response` argument by modifying a copy of the keyword arguments instead of using invalid syntax.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Session.request` method where the logic for checking the `verify` parameter was incorrect. It ensures that SSL verification is properly enabled when `verify` is set to `True` or left as `None`, preventing unexpected behavior during environment variable inspection.
This commit initializes the basic structure of the requests package. It creates the core module and sets up the package initialization file to import from it.
This commit removes a testimonial from Steve Pike in the project documentation. It shortens the overall length of the testimonials section on the main index page.

This commit adjusts whitespace in the `requests/hooks.py` module. It adds a blank line after the imports and removes a trailing blank line within the `dispatch_hook` function. No functional behavior is changed.

This commit fixes an issue where the `block` parameter was ignored for non-blocking connections in the `Request` class. It also ensures `Response.content` correctly handles empty data by falling back to `raw.data`.

This commit allows users to specify a 'no_proxy' entry within the proxies dictionary argument, enabling direct control over which hosts bypass proxy settings. It updates the Session class and utility functions to pass this value through the proxy resolution logic.

This commit removes the exception handling in the Response.text property that previously suppressed Unicode decoding errors. Users will now see errors when the response content cannot be decoded, rather than receiving an empty string.

This commit fixes a crash in the `requests` library that occurred when passing `None` as a file value in the `files` parameter. It updates the `_encode_files` method in `requests/models.py` to skip `None` values, making the behavior consistent with how `None` is handled in query parameters and JSON bodies.

This commit adds regression tests to the RequestsTestSuite in tests/test_requests.py. It verifies that the prefetch setting persists correctly across HTTP redirects and can be overridden when sending requests. These tests ensure the library handles response content iteration and configuration changes as expected.
This commit updates the README.md file to fix the alignment of the project logo. It adds indentation to the image tag, ensuring the logo displays correctly centered within the documentation.
This commit updates the project's README documentation. It adds a prominent message encouraging users to financially support the maintainer via a Cash App link.

This commit corrects a documentation typo in the `requests/defaults.py` module. It fixes the formatting of the `store_cookies` parameter description to ensure it renders correctly in the generated documentation.
This release updates the Requests library to version 0.8.2. It allows cookies to contain square brackets and underscores, fixing a previous restriction on these characters.

This commit reorders the sidebar logo template to move the Requests Stickers link to a different position within the documentation sidebar. The change affects the `docs/_templates/sidebarlogo.html` file, altering the visual layout of the documentation site.

This commit updates the `Request` and `Response` classes in `requests/models.py` to store HTTP headers using a `CaseInsensitiveDict`. This ensures that header lookups are case-insensitive, preventing errors when accessing headers with varying capitalization.

This commit refines the authorization stripping logic in the `SessionRedirectMixin` class within `requests/sessions.py`. It now requires standard HTTP or HTTPS ports to be used for the exception that allows credentials to persist during an HTTP to HTTPS upgrade on the same host.

The Request class now encodes the hostname portion of URLs using the IDNA standard. This allows requests to correctly handle internationalized domain names, such as those containing non-ASCII characters, by converting them to their ASCII-compatible form.

This commit removes the unused import of `auth_manager` from the `requests/core.py` module. It cleans up the internal code structure without altering any user-facing behavior or fixing a specific bug.
Updates the CI test matrix to replace the pre-release Python 3.10 with the stable version. It also adds a new test job for PyPy 3.7 on Ubuntu.

This commit adds support for building and publishing Python wheel packages. It introduces a new publish target in the Makefile to handle both source and wheel distributions, and configures the package as universal in setup.cfg.

This commit fixes a resource leak in the HTTPDigestAuth class by ensuring the connection is properly closed after handling a 401 response. It replaces the direct call to the raw stream's release method with the standard close method, preventing potential connection exhaustion.

This commit updates the `Session.get` method in the `requests` library to explicitly accept a `params` argument, aligning its signature with the standard `requests.get` function. This change ensures that query string parameters are passed correctly to the underlying request, preventing potential issues with parameter handling.

This commit removes the `close` method from the `Response` class and stops assigning `read` and `close` attributes to the response object during construction. It also introduces a typo in the `content` property, changing the file object reference from `self.fo` to `self.fo.read()`.

This commit fixes a bug in the HTTPDigestAuth class where expired nonces caused immediate 401 errors instead of automatically renegotiating. Users no longer need to manually reinitialize authentication after long periods of inactivity. The change also simplifies attribute assignment by removing unnecessary setattr calls.

This commit fixes an issue where CJK characters in file upload parameters caused errors. It updates the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to use `builtin_str` for encoding fields, ensuring proper handling of non-ASCII text. A new test verifies that POST requests with CJK parameters work correctly.

This commit removes the redirect cache from the Session class in the requests library. It eliminates the storage of permanent redirect URLs to prevent potential memory issues and simplify session state management.

This commit updates the project's documentation index to improve readability and searchability. It refines the description of Python's built-in urllib2 module and adjusts the introductory text for the Requests library.

This commit adds detailed docstrings to several helper functions in the requests/utils.py module, including dict_from_cookiejar and cookiejar_from_dict. It clarifies the expected input parameters for these utility functions to improve documentation quality.

The `dispatch_hook` function in `requests/hooks.py` now prints the full traceback when an exception occurs during hook execution, rather than issuing a brief warning. This change provides developers with more detailed diagnostic information to identify the root cause of errors.

This commit updates the sponsor documentation to clarify that Heroku supports Kenneth Reitz's open source work during work hours. The change modifies the text in the sponsors file to provide more specific context about the nature of the sponsorship.

The `Request` class in `requests/core.py` now correctly handles HEAD requests by sending the appropriate method and avoiding the reading of response content. This fixes a bug where HEAD requests were not processed properly, ensuring users receive accurate responses for these requests.

This commit updates the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to use a proxy pool manager instead of a single connection pool. It changes how proxy connections are established in the `send` method, allowing for better management of multiple proxy connections.

This commit prevents pytest from altering the project's warning filters, ensuring that warning behavior remains consistent during test runs. It introduces a new pytest.ini configuration file to disable the warnings plugin and updates MANIFEST.in to include this file in the distribution.

This commit adds a test to verify that the requests library correctly records the full chain of redirects in the response history. It ensures that after following three redirects, the history length is exactly three for both HTTP and HTTPS requests.

Updates the CodeQL security analysis workflow to use version 3.26.0 of the github/codeql-action. This minor version bump ensures the repository's automated security scanning uses the latest available action features and fixes.

This commit corrects a typo in the authentication documentation where the import statement incorrectly referenced "request" instead of "requests." It ensures the example code in the user guide is accurate and functional.

This commit updates the contributor list in the AUTHORS.rst file to reflect a GitHub username change. It replaces the old handle for Danilo Bargen with the new one, ensuring the project's credits remain accurate.

This commit updates the README documentation to reflect the correct attribute for accessing response text, changing references from `content` to `text`. It also removes the entire "Usage" section, which previously demonstrated basic authentication examples.

This commit ensures that low-level socket errors are converted into a standard ConnectionError within the Request.send method. This change allows users to catch connection failures using a consistent exception type instead of handling raw socket errors.

This commit updates the dependency constraints in the setup.py file to allow newer versions of the idna library. It raises the maximum permitted version from 2.8 to 2.9, enabling users to install the latest compatible release without manual intervention.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar templates to display a new sponsorship message crediting Linode and other organizations. It replaces the previous "Support Requests 3.0" call-to-action with this updated attribution in the sidebar introduction and logo sections.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the release process documentation. It fixes the word "dependences" to "dependencies" in the description of hotfix policies.
This commit fixes a typo in the module docstring of `requests/api.py`. It corrects the spelling of "impliments" to "implements" for accurate documentation.

This commit removes redundant feature descriptions from the project's README and documentation index. It cleans up the introductory text in the README and docs modules, replacing the removed content with a new testimonials section in the documentation.

This release updates the Requests library to version 2.29.0, improving standardization by deferring chunked request handling to urllib3. It also relaxes header component requirements to support bytes and str subclasses.

This commit updates the project history file to finalize the release notes for version 0.5.1. It documents new features including header access without fetching the body, list-based parameters, and forced basic authentication as the default.

This commit fixes incorrect cookie expiration times by using UTC-based calculations instead of local time. The `morsel_to_cookie` function in `requests/cookies.py` now uses `calendar.timegm` to ensure cookies expire at the correct moment regardless of the server's timezone.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to use modern dictionary literals instead of the dict() constructor for clarity. It also corrects an example showing how to add a hook to a session, changing it from assignment to appending to the list.

The `RequestsCookieJar` class in `requests/cookies.py` now supports updating its contents directly from another `CookieJar` instance. Previously, this operation was not explicitly handled, potentially causing errors or unexpected behavior when merging cookie stores. This change allows users to seamlessly combine cookies from different sources.

This commit updates the project's README to include a centered image linking to Kenneth Reitz's website. It adds visual branding to the documentation without altering any code behavior or functionality.
This commit adds Antti Kaihola to the project's list of contributors. It updates the AUTHORS.rst file to include his name and GitHub handle under the "Patches and Suggestions" section.
This commit removes the PyPI download count badge from the project's README. It cleans up the documentation by deleting the image reference and its associated link.
This commit fixes a missing newline at the end of the tox.ini configuration file. It ensures the test environment setup is correctly formatted for the tox runner.

This commit updates the project's release notes to reflect recent changes. It documents that `RequestException` now inherits from `IOError` instead of `RuntimeError`, and notes improvements to `no_proxy` parsing and data value handling.

This commit refactors the `requests` library's `models` module to improve code organization and readability. It updates the `Response` class to use a new utility for decoding response content and adjusts the `Request` class's authentication handling logic.

This commit fixes an issue where the request body was not sent when a server responded with a 307 or 308 status code during a POST or PUT request. The change updates the `resolve_redirects` method in the `SessionRedirectMixin` class to correctly handle these specific redirect statuses.
This commit updates the project history log to document version 0.7.4. It records a fix for session hooks, resolving issues related to their functionality.

This release fixes a bug in the status_codes module where the init function failed when attempting to append to a None docstring. The version number is updated to 2.19.1 to reflect this specific bugfix.

This commit updates the project history to document a change in SSL verification behavior. It clarifies that client certificates are now ignored when verification is disabled, affecting how the client handles secure connections.

This commit updates the contributing documentation to improve readability by separating the "be cordial" rule from the statement welcoming contributions. The change is limited to the docs/dev/contributing.rst file.

The `super_len` function in `requests/utils.py` now handles cases where the total length is unknown. It prevents errors by treating a missing length as zero and only updating the current position when a valid length exists.

The `get_netrc_auth` function in `requests/utils.py` now uses a `raise_errors` parameter instead of `ignore_errors`. This change inverts the default behavior so that netrc parsing errors are silently ignored unless the user explicitly requests them to be raised.

This commit removes Python 3.0 from the list of supported programming languages in the project's setup configuration. It clarifies that the software no longer claims compatibility with that specific Python version.
This commit restricts the flake8 linting process to only check the `requests` directory instead of the entire project. It prevents unnecessary linting errors from unrelated files in the repository.

This commit adds tests to verify that the requests library correctly maps the HTTP 425 status code to its various textual aliases, such as "TOO_EARLY" and "UNORDERED". The new test case is located in the TestPreparingURLs class within the test suite.
This commit updates the project's test dependencies to require a specific minimum version of the pytest framework. It modifies the requirements file to ensure compatibility with newer test features.
This commit adds a unit test to the RequestsTestCase in test_requests.py. It verifies that the requests session correctly removes a cookie when the server sends an expiration date in the past.

This commit updates the API documentation in the README to explicitly specify the data types for the HTTP response fields. It clarifies that the status code is an integer, headers are a dictionary, and content is bytes, improving clarity for users reading the response structure.

This commit introduces the `requests.adapters` module, establishing the `BaseAdapter` and `HTTPAdapter` classes to manage transport connections. It provides the foundational structure for handling HTTP requests via urllib3, defining default pool sizes and retry behaviors.

This commit introduces a new configuration option, `timeout_fallback`, to control whether the library uses the global socket timeout as a fallback. The `Request` class now checks this setting before applying the global timeout, allowing users to disable this behavior.

This commit updates the test suite in tests/test_requests.py to handle Python 3 text and bytes differences. It modifies the test_post_fields_with_multiple_values_and_files_as_tuples method to ensure correct data types are used for form fields and files.

This commit fixes a crash in the `Response` class of the `requests` library that occurred when accessing link headers if they were missing. It changes the behavior to safely return `None` instead of raising a `KeyError` when the `link` header is not present in the response.

This release updates the version to 2.32.2 and documents a deprecation in the Requests library. It renames the internal `_get_connection` method to the public `get_connection_with_tls_context` to help custom HTTPAdapters migrate safely after recent security changes.
This commit removes a trailing blank line from the project's history file. It is a minor formatting cleanup that does not change any functional behavior or user-visible features.

This commit modifies the `Response` class in `requests/models.py` to support lazy loading of response data. It allows users to access response headers without immediately downloading the entire body, improving performance for large files.

This commit updates the GitHub issue template to clarify that the diagnostic command is only available in Requests version 2.16.4 and later. It instructs users on older versions to provide basic system information instead.

This commit updates the copyright year from 2014 to 2015 across the project. It modifies the LICENSE file, the documentation configuration in docs/conf.py, and the package metadata in requests/__init__.py to reflect the new year.

This commit changes how the Request class formats cookie headers by using a semicolon and space as the separator instead of a carriage return and newline. This adjustment improves compatibility with web servers that do not properly handle the previous line-break format.

This commit refactors the `remove_cookie_by_name` function in `requests/cookies.py` to simplify the logic for filtering cookies. It replaces nested conditional checks with early exits, making the code easier to read without changing the behavior of removing cookies by name, domain, or path.
