The `Request` class now accepts and stores a `hooks` parameter, allowing users to attach event-handling callbacks to individual requests. The `request` function in `requests/api.py` passes this parameter through to the `Request` constructor.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Request` class where an empty cookie jar was incorrectly treated as falsy, preventing cookie functionality from working. It changes the logic in the `send` and `_get_opener` methods to explicitly check for `None` instead of relying on truthiness.
This commit updates the project to use the Apache 2.0 license. It also removes a placeholder docstring from the RequestMixin class in the requests module.
This commit fixes a missing newline at the end of the `packages` module in the requests library. It resolves a checkstyle warning regarding file formatting. No functional behavior changes.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library from 2.3.0 to 2.4.0. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the package's initialization file to reflect the new release.

This commit refactors the codebase to use dictionary comprehensions instead of generator expressions wrapped in the dict constructor. It updates the HTTPAdapter, Response, and Session classes, as well as the create_cookie function, to improve code readability and consistency.

This commit fixes a bug where the Content-Length header was set to an integer instead of a string when sending file objects. The PreparedRequest class now ensures the length is converted to a string in the prepare_body method.

This commit updates the project documentation to clarify that keep-alive and HTTP connection pooling are fully automatic features. It specifies that these capabilities are powered by the embedded urllib3 library, improving the accuracy of the library's description.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to clarify how custom headers interact with other request settings. It explains that specific headers like Authorization and Content-Length may be overridden or removed by more specific sources. The changes are located in the user quickstart guide.

This commit fixes an issue where cookies were not properly handled during redirects in the `SessionRedirectMixin` class. It re-enables the removal of the `Cookie` header from requests and ensures the updated headers are passed along, preventing stale cookie data from being sent.
This commit updates the monthly download badge in the project's README to use a new static image URL. This ensures the badge displays correctly by pointing to a more reliable image source.

This commit ensures that automatically set header values, such as Content-Length, are always converted to native strings using the builtin_str function. This change in the PreparedRequest class prevents potential encoding issues when handling request headers.

This commit fixes import errors in the `requests` compatibility module by updating how `chardet` and `OrderedDict` are loaded. It resolves issues where the library failed to initialize due to incorrect internal package references.

This commit fixes the OAuth1 authentication class in requests/auth.py to correctly handle requests with multipart form data. It ensures the Content-Type header is properly parsed so that query parameters and data are included in the signature calculation.

This commit adds a test to verify that the requests library correctly handles Unicode characters in URLs and query parameters. It ensures that GET requests with non-ASCII characters do not raise errors, covering both parameter values and path components.

This commit adds a test to the RequestsTestSuite in test_requests.py to verify that the user agent header is correctly transferred during an HTTP request. It ensures the client sends the expected Mozilla user agent string to the server.

The documentation for installing Requests now references pypi.douban.com instead of the defunct crate.io mirror. This update ensures users have a valid example for installing from a PyPI mirror and includes a link to a comprehensive list of available mirrors.

This commit moves Server-Name-Indication documentation from the advanced user guide to the FAQ section. It removes specific instructions for enabling SNI on Python 2, replacing them with a link to an external resource. The changes affect the `docs/community/faq.rst` and `docs/user/advanced.rst` files.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the README.md file. It changes the word "intall" to "install" in the instructions for installing the requests module.

This commit updates the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to handle relative redirect URLs. It ensures that if a redirect location lacks a domain, the request correctly resolves it against the original URL's scheme and host.

The HTTPDigestAuth class in requests/auth.py now ignores authentication challenges on non-4xx responses. This prevents the library from unnecessarily processing digest authentication when the server returns a status code outside the 400-499 range.

This commit reverts a change that forced UTF-8 as the default encoding for HTTP responses. It restores the previous behavior where the `Response` class does not automatically assume UTF-8 if no encoding is detected, preventing potential decoding errors for non-UTF-8 content.

This commit updates the Requests library to version 0.8.9 to address a packaging issue. It modifies the version and build numbers in the `requests/__init__.py` module and adds a corresponding entry to the project history.

The `Request.send` method in `requests/models.py` now correctly includes the file name when sending multipart data, fixing an issue where the name was missing. It also ensures the Content-Type header is set if provided, and uses the proper parameter encoding function for the request body.

This commit adds a new "pre_send" hook to the requests library, allowing users to modify a Request object immediately before it is sent. The change updates the Request class in models.py to dispatch this hook and modifies the hook list in hooks.py to include the new event.

This commit adds documentation to the README describing the `Request` object's status attributes and methods. It explains how to check for successful requests using `ok` and `error`, and how to trigger exceptions with `raise_for_status`.

This commit updates the documentation for the `data` parameter in the `Session.request` method. It clarifies that file-like objects are accepted as valid input for the request body, alongside dictionaries and bytes.
The quickstart documentation page now displays a header image at the top. This change adds a visual element to the user guide without altering any functional behavior or code.
This commit adds a PayPal donation form to the documentation sidebar. It introduces new HTML templates for the sidebar logo and introduction, allowing users to contribute financially to the project.
This commit contains no code changes or file modifications. It serves as a placeholder or marker in the repository history without altering any application behavior or functionality.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar to replace a link to edmsynths.com with a link to coinbin.org. The change affects the sidebarintro.html and sidebarlogo.html templates, ensuring users see the correct external resource reference.

This commit replaces the third-party netaddr dependency with standard library functions to handle IP range checks in the no_proxy setting. It introduces new utility functions in requests/utils.py, such as address_in_network, to determine if an IP address belongs to a specified network.

This commit updates the `Request.send` method in `requests/models.py` to log the fully resolved URL instead of the raw URL attribute. Users will now see the complete, expanded URL in debug logs, which improves visibility into the exact endpoint being accessed.

This commit updates the Travis CI configuration to run the `make test-readme` target during the build process. It explicitly skips this test when the Python version is 2.6, ensuring the documentation tests only execute on supported environments.
This commit adds section labels to the advanced user documentation in the Requests library. These labels enable other projects to create cross-references to specific sections using Intersphinx.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library from 0.6.0 to 0.6.1. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the core module to reflect the new release.

This commit adds a failing test to the TestRequests class in tests/test_requests.py. The new test, test_certificate_failure, verifies that an SSLError is raised when a request is made to a server with an untrusted certificate.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to include a practical example of creating an image from binary data. It demonstrates how to use the PIL library and StringIO to process response content, helping users understand how to handle image data returned by requests.

The `merge_cookies` function in `requests/cookies.py` now uses a try-except block to handle cookie updates instead of checking for the `update` attribute. This change ensures that any `AttributeError` raised during the update process is caught and handled gracefully.

The `info` function in `requests/help.py` now returns version details for urllib3 and chardet as dictionaries instead of plain strings. This change standardizes the output format of the help utility for better consistency.

The `Response.json` method in `requests/models.py` now raises exceptions for invalid JSON instead of silently returning `None`. This change ensures that users receive clear error messages when parsing fails, rather than encountering unexpected `None` values.

This commit fixes an off-by-one error in the `resolve_redirects` method of the `SessionRedirectMixin` class. It ensures that the request loop correctly stops when the number of redirects reaches the configured maximum, preventing an extra, unintended redirect attempt.
This commit adds Jonathan Wong to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS.rst file. It updates the project's attribution records to include his name under the patches and suggestions section.

This commit removes the invalid "Connection: close" field from the example headers in the documentation. It corrects the sample output shown in the `requests` package initialization file to accurately reflect standard request behavior.

This commit reorganizes the project's README by moving the version, download, and contributor badges to the top of the file. This change improves the immediate visibility of key project metrics for users viewing the documentation.

This commit adjusts the documentation table of contents in the index file to reduce its depth. It adds a new section with a maximum depth of one and changes an existing section from depth two to one, simplifying the navigation structure.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation by replacing a previous section on accessing Request objects from Response objects. It introduces a new "Request and Response Objects" section that explains how both objects are created and related during a request.

This commit ensures that redirect URLs are converted to native strings before being assigned to the prepared request. It modifies the `resolve_redirects` method within the `SessionRedirectMixin` class to prevent potential encoding issues during the redirect process.

This commit fixes an issue where the full URL was incorrectly sent in CONNECT messages when using a proxy. It modifies the `request_url` method in `HTTPAdapter` to ensure the full URL is only used for non-HTTPS requests, while HTTPS requests now correctly use only the path portion.

This commit renames internal monkey-patch classes in the requests.monkeys module to remove leading underscores, making their names cleaner. It updates the imports in requests.models.py to reference the new names, ensuring the AuthObject class correctly maps authentication types to the renamed handlers.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to include `requests-threads` as an example of a library combining Requests with asynchronicity frameworks. It also adds the corresponding link reference for the new library.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to support SSL connections when running on Pypy with specific OpenSSL packages installed. It modifies the connection and response handling modules to ensure secure communication works correctly in this environment.

This commit removes the explicit unicode conversion of the HTTP method in the `PreparedRequest.prepare_method` function. It simplifies the logic by directly uppercasing the method string, ensuring consistent behavior across Python versions without unnecessary type casting.

This commit ensures that the cookie jar used to generate the Cookie header is stored in the PreparedRequest object. It modifies the PreparedRequest class to retain this data and updates HTTPDigestAuth to extract cookies directly into the prepared request's jar.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to reflect the renaming of the settings parameter to config. It clarifies that global parameters like the user agent header should now be set in the config dictionary rather than the request config level.

This commit fixes a Python 3 compatibility issue in the `Session` class within `requests/sessions.py`. It updates the `send` method to use the `next()` function instead of the deprecated `.next()` method when handling redirect iterators.

This commit removes the AUTHORS.orig file, which contained unresolved merge conflict markers and outdated contributor lists. It cleans up the repository by deleting this temporary artifact, ensuring the project's authorship information is no longer cluttered by conflicting data.

This commit removes all remaining Python 2 compatibility code and drops support for Python 3.6 from the Requests library. It updates the test suite, documentation, and core modules like `requests/compat.py` and `requests/utils.py` to reflect this change. Users will no longer be able to install or run Requests on Python 2.7 or 3.6.

This commit adds test cases to the RequestsTestSuite in test_requests.py to verify that HTTP and HTTPS PATCH and PUT requests return a 200 status code. It ensures the library correctly handles these specific HTTP methods against the httpbin service.
This commit updates the user introduction documentation by adding a new image to the intro page. It modifies the intro.rst file to include a visual element for the introduction section.

The Response class in requests/models.py now returns response content as unicode instead of raw bytes. This change ensures that text data is properly decoded based on the specified charset, improving handling of non-ASCII characters for users.

Updates the CodeQL security analysis workflow to use version 3.28.5 of the github/codeql-action. This change refreshes the init, autobuild, and analyze steps in the codeql-analysis.yml file to ensure the repository uses the latest available security scanning tools.
This commit updates the documentation to list .netrc support as a feature of the Requests library. It clarifies that the library can now handle authentication credentials stored in a .netrc file.

The Session class now accepts a params argument during initialization, allowing users to set default query parameters for all requests made through that session. This change ensures that params are included in the session's merge attributes, so they are automatically applied to outgoing requests.

This release fixes a bug in the requests library where digest authentication failed when the URL included query parameters. The fix ensures query data is correctly attached to the path during the authentication process. The version number in the package initialization is updated to 0.7.6.

This commit fixes a bug where the entire URL was incorrectly lowercased before establishing a connection, which could break requests to case-sensitive hosts or paths. The change updates the `HTTPAdapter` class to ensure only the URL scheme is lowercased while preserving the original case of the rest of the address.
This commit reorders the sponsor list in the Requests documentation. It moves the Heroku entry from an earlier position to a later section within the community sponsors page.

This commit adds a link for one-time PayPal donations to the documentation sidebar. It updates the sidebar templates to display a message welcoming one-time payments alongside existing support options.

This commit adds a new documentation page listing recommended third-party extensions for the Requests library. It introduces descriptions for CacheControl and requests-oauthlib, highlighting their benefits for caching and OAuth authentication. The change updates the main documentation index to include this new community resource.

This commit updates the project documentation to clarify that request data is provided using standard Python dictionaries. It corrects a minor wording in the README to improve accuracy for users configuring requests.

This commit updates the project's README documentation by removing redundant placeholder text from the API section. It cleans up the file structure to improve readability for users reviewing the available endpoints.

This commit updates the documentation styling to ensure links within the Python 2.7 section appear in white. It modifies the custom stylesheet to apply this specific color change to the relevant navigation elements.

This commit streamlines the imports in the `requests/adapters.py` module by removing unused references to `LocationParseError`, `connectionpool`, and `encode_multipart_formdata`. This cleanup reduces unnecessary dependencies without altering the library's functional behavior.

This commit fixes a bug in the HTTPAdapter class where certificate files were incorrectly identified. It changes the validation logic in the cert_verify method to properly check if the certificate argument is a string, ensuring correct handling of file paths.
The commit updates the copyright holder in the LICENSE file from Josh Ourisman to Kenneth Reitz. It also removes the trailing newline at the end of the file.
This commit updates the dependency constraints in setup.py to allow urllib3 version 1.22. It removes the previous restriction that prevented users from installing the newer urllib3 release.

This commit adjusts the vertical spacing of the "Requests" button in the documentation sidebar. It moves the button element within the sidebarintro and sidebarlogo templates to improve layout padding.

This commit fixes a minor formatting inconsistency in the documentation comment for the Request class. It corrects the spacing before the note about using the default socket timeout as a fallback. No functional behavior is changed.

This commit updates the documentation in the Makefile to clarify that the test target runs the test suite on both Python 2 and Python 3. It replaces the previous instructions for running individual tests with this broader compatibility note.

This commit updates the project's README to improve the layout of the footer image. It moves the decorative flourish graphic from the bottom of the text block to a separate, centered section. This change ensures the image displays correctly without breaking the surrounding text formatting.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Response` class where closing a streamed session without consuming its content failed to release the underlying connection. It ensures that `Response.close` properly closes the raw stream if the content has not been read, preventing resource leaks.

This commit upgrades the bundled urllib3 library to version 1.0, introducing new features like proxy support and a NullHandler for logging. It updates the connection pool and request modules to support these changes, improving how HTTP requests are managed and logged.

This commit updates the Frequently Asked Questions documentation for the Requests library. It corrects a typo in the description of automatic response decompression and adds a note about accessing raw response data.

This commit adds AppVeyor continuous integration configuration to test the Requests library on Windows. It introduces a PowerShell script to install Python and pip, enabling automated build and test runs for the project.

This change prevents the Content-Length header from being automatically added to GET and HEAD requests by default. The PreparedRequest class now only includes this header for other HTTP methods, ensuring cleaner requests for simple data retrieval.

This commit removes an outdated dependency check from the setup.py file that previously required the simplejson package for Python versions older than 2.6. This change cleans up the installation logic by eliminating unnecessary code for unsupported legacy Python versions.

This commit fixes a test failure on Windows where a temporary file was automatically deleted before it could be read. It modifies the `test_file_post_data` method in `tests/test_requests.py` to prevent automatic deletion and explicitly manage the file's lifecycle.

The `get_environ_proxies` function in `requests/utils.py` now accepts a URL argument to check the `no_proxy` environment variable. This ensures that requests to hosts listed in `no_proxy` bypass the proxy, fixing an issue where the setting was previously ignored.

In the `RequestEncodingMixin` class, the `_encode_files` method now returns a tuple of two `None` values instead of a single `None` when no files are present. This ensures the return type remains consistent with the method's standard output, preventing potential errors for users relying on tuple unpacking.

This commit fixes a bug in the `resolve_redirects` method of the `SessionRedirectMixin` class where the original request was incorrectly reused during subsequent redirects. This prevented proper method conversion, such as changing a POST to a GET after a 303 response. The change ensures the current prepared request is used for each redirect step.
The quickstart documentation now demonstrates POST requests using the httpbin service. It also updates the existing GET example to use httpbin instead of the GitHub timeline.

This commit updates the Travis CI configuration to disable the use of sudo privileges during the build process. This change ensures the build runs in a lightweight container environment, which typically results in faster execution times.
This commit updates the project's changelog to document the addition of the `Response.reason` attribute. It records this new feature in the history file for users to review.

This commit updates the project history file to document the 2.8.0 release. It highlights new features including per-host proxy support, improved error messages for failed requests, and a new option to control error handling in netrc authentication.

This commit fixes a typo in the contributing documentation, correcting "peice" to "piece" in the description of the project's feature status. The change is located in the `docs/dev/contributing.rst` file.

The build process no longer writes the flake8 linting output to a separate report file. This change modifies the Makefile to run the linter directly, allowing results to appear in the terminal instead of being saved to disk.

This commit fixes an issue in the HTTPAdapter.send method where keyword arguments were not being passed to the add_headers function. It ensures that parameters like stream, timeout, verify, cert, and proxies are correctly forwarded, aligning the implementation with the documented behavior.

This commit updates the `prepare_url` method in `requests.models` to enable UTS46 mode when encoding internationalized domain names. This ensures that URLs with specific non-ASCII characters are correctly converted to their Punycode equivalents, improving compatibility with modern web standards.
This commit updates the project's history log to document recent changes. It notes the addition of binary upload support and a fix for authentication issues.
This commit updates the README documentation to improve the formatting of the feature list. It replaces a plain text layout with a structured list using plus symbols for better readability.
Updates the Travis CI configuration to test against the stable Python 3.6 release instead of the development branch. This ensures the project is validated against the final version of the language.

This commit updates the actions/checkout dependency from version 5.0.0 to 6.0.2 across all GitHub Actions workflow files. It ensures the repository uses the latest major version of the checkout action for its CI/CD pipelines.

Adds a test case to `test_parse_header_links` in `tests/test_utils.py` to verify that an empty `Link:` header correctly returns an empty list. This ensures the parser handles missing or blank header values without errors.

This commit removes the `requests/packages` directory, which contained bundled copies of the chardet, idna, and urllib3 libraries. Users will no longer have access to these vendored dependencies through the `requests` package.

This commit corrects the misleading docstrings for the `Response` class's boolean evaluation methods in `requests/models.py`. It clarifies that the methods return true for any status code below 400, rather than implying a specific "OK" status.

This commit reverts a previous change to the `PreparedRequest.prepare` method in `requests/models.py`. It restores the behavior where the `hooks` argument is passed directly to `prepare_hooks` without defaulting to an empty list if `None` is provided.
This commit reverts a previous change that rewrote the unquote_unreserved function to use urllib.unquote. It restores the original implementation of the function within the module.

This commit adds a NOTICE file to document the license for the vendorized Poster library. It clarifies the copyright and permission terms for users installing the project, ensuring proper attribution for the included third-party code.

This commit updates the test execution process to use the project's setup script instead of the py.test command. It also introduces a CircleCI configuration file to install tox and manage multiple Python versions for the build environment.

The test execution process now runs in parallel using the standard tox command instead of the external detox tool. This change updates the Makefile to improve test performance by leveraging tox's built-in parallelization capabilities.

This commit refines the TimedCache class in requests/structures.py to improve code readability. It replaces verbose method calls with standard Python syntax for accessing, adding, and removing items. The changes also ensure that missing keys raise a KeyError with the specific key name included.

This commit simplifies the `merge_cookies` function in `requests/cookies.py` by removing a redundant try block. It directly calls the update method and catches `AttributeError` to raise a `CookieJarError`, streamlining the error handling logic.

This commit adds tests for the auto-authentication feature in the requests module, verifying that HTTP requests succeed with automatic credentials. It also updates an existing test to use a file object instead of a string buffer for file uploads.

This commit updates the GitHub Actions workflow to lock inactive issues and pull requests after 90 days instead of 360. This change shortens the inactivity window before automatic locking occurs, as recommended by a team member.
This commit updates the contributor's guide documentation by adding an image to the header and fixing a missing newline at the end of the file.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to clarify the error behavior of the `r.json` method. It specifies that a `ValueError` is raised when JSON decoding fails, providing a concrete example involving an unauthorized response.

The `Request` class in `requests/models.py` now accepts an optional `session` parameter during initialization. This allows users to pass a session directly to a request, enabling the mixing of session-based and asynchronous workflows.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` now correctly passes the `hooks` argument to the `Request` constructor. This ensures that user-defined event hooks are properly attached to the request object, allowing them to execute as intended during the request lifecycle.

This commit updates the vendored urllib3 library within the requests package. It introduces a new helper function, add_stderr_logger, to facilitate debugging by adding a stream handler to the logger. The update also includes minor changes to connection pool and utility modules.

This commit removes a broken link to a sticker vendor from the documentation sidebar. The link no longer provided the advertised Requests stickers, so it was deleted to avoid confusing users. The change affects the sidebar logo template.

This commit adds a `json` parameter to the `post` function in `requests/api.py` and the `Request` class in `requests/models.py`. It allows users to send JSON data directly in the body of POST requests, simplifying the process of setting the correct content type and encoding.

This commit cleans up the `PreparedRequest` and `Request` classes in the `requests` library by removing unnecessary default values for the `json` parameter and fixing a naming inconsistency. It also reorders parameters in the `prepare` method and updates documentation to clarify how the `json` argument interacts with `data`.
This commit contains no code changes or file modifications. It serves as a placeholder or marker in the repository history without altering any behavior or functionality.
This commit updates the project's author list to include Daniele Tricoli, also known as Eriol. It modifies the AUTHORS file to reflect this new contributor under the patches and suggestions section.

This commit updates the project documentation to reflect a higher download count for the Requests library. It changes the reported PyPI download total from two million to three million in the testimonials section.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to clarify that the Session class utilizes urllib3's connection pooling. It explains that reusing TCP connections for multiple requests to the same host can significantly improve performance.
This commit updates the AUTHORS file to add Alex to the list of contributors. It ensures the project's credit list accurately reflects all individuals who have provided patches or suggestions.

This commit adds unit tests to verify that the LookupDict class correctly supports attribute-style access. It ensures that hasattr and getattr behave as expected for existing keys and properly raise errors for missing ones.

This update to the HTTPConnectionPool class in the urllib3 module ensures connection timeouts are properly applied during request creation. It also clarifies documentation regarding connection release behavior when preloading content is disabled.

This commit fixes slow response handling for chunked HTTP requests by enabling buffering in the `HTTPAdapter.send` method. Previously, these requests consumed data byte-by-byte, causing performance issues. The change aligns this behavior with standard non-chunked requests.

This commit removes an unused import from the requests/utils.py module. It cleans up the codebase by eliminating a redundant reference to the traceback module, which does not affect user-facing behavior.

This commit adds documentation to the quickstart guide explaining how to use HTTP Basic and Digest authentication with the Requests library. It provides examples for the `requests.get` function to help users implement these common authentication methods.

The ConnectTimeout exception in the requests library now inherits from both ConnectionError and Timeout. This change allows users to catch connection timeouts using either exception type, improving error handling flexibility.

This commit removes an ASCII art banner from the project's README file. It resolves a NameError that occurred when the documentation was processed, ensuring the module description renders correctly without errors.

This commit moves encoding detection logic into the requests.utils module to make it available for external use. It introduces functions to extract character sets from HTTP headers and HTML content, allowing users to determine response encodings independently.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Session` class where the request history was not being properly attached to the response object. It ensures that the `history` variable is assigned to the response within the `send` method, allowing users to access the full chain of redirects.

This commit updates the Sphinx documentation build tool to version 7.2.6 in the docs/requirements.txt file. It ensures the project's documentation can be built successfully with the latest Read the Docs platform requirements.

This commit updates the Ruff linter version in the pre-commit configuration from 0.16.1 to 0.16.2. It ensures the project uses the latest patch release for code quality checks without changing any application logic.

This release fixes an issue where SSL errors were incorrectly masked as timeouts and resolves parameter handling problems for URLs containing fragments. It also enhances the User Agent string to provide more detailed information.

This commit adds tests to verify that secure cookies are only transmitted over HTTPS connections. It introduces test cases within the CookieTests and LWPCookieJarTest classes to validate secure and persistent cookie behavior.
This commit removes the outdated `requests/patches.py` module, which contained only a docstring and no functional code. It cleans up the codebase by deleting this unnecessary file.

This commit updates the project's homepage URL in the setup configuration. It changes the link from the GitHub repository to the dedicated python-requests.org website, ensuring users are directed to the official project site.

This commit updates the README documentation to clarify the specific error users may encounter when cloning the repository. It changes the vague description of a "bad commit" to "bad commit timestamp," helping users understand why a specific Git flag is required.

This commit fixes a broken link in the quickstart documentation. It updates the reference to the advanced section in the `docs/user/quickstart.rst` file to use the correct Sphinx cross-reference syntax, ensuring the link works properly for users.

This commit refactors the Request and Response classes in requests/models.py to consistently use the new configuration module. It removes direct imports of settings and monkey-patched handlers, replacing them with a single import from the monkeys module to centralize configuration handling.

This commit updates the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to use a monkey-patched version of `SimpleCookie` instead of the standard library implementation. This change alters how cookies are processed during request preparation, potentially fixing compatibility issues or bugs related to cookie parsing.
This commit updates the project's README file to improve the description of the available documentation. It changes the wording to emphasize the quality of the resources provided to users.

This commit updates the release history to document a new behavior where proxy-related connection issues now raise a ProxyError. This change clarifies how the library handles specific network failures for users.

The `_parse_content_type_header` function in `requests/utils.py` now normalizes parameter keys to lowercase. This ensures that charset information is recognized correctly regardless of its capitalization, such as "Charset" versus "charset".

This commit simplifies the project's setup configuration by removing special handling for the Jython platform. It consolidates test dependencies into a single list and removes Jython from the supported Python implementations, ensuring the package no longer claims compatibility with that environment.

This commit updates the project's changelog to document recent API changes. It notes the removal of the `Response.cached` attribute, the addition of `Response.request`, and a shift to keyword-only arguments.

This commit fixes a bug in the OAuth1 authentication class where the return values from the client's sign method were assigned to the wrong variables. The swap ensures that the signed headers and request body are correctly applied to the outgoing request.

This commit fixes failing AppVeyor builds by explicitly installing the Requests library separately during the CI setup. It updates the Pipfile to relax version constraints for dependencies like httpbin and pytest-httpbin, and modifies the appveyor configuration to run a specific pipenv install command.

This commit fixes a bug in the `stream_decode_response_unicode` function within `requests/utils.py` where the final flush of the decoder failed due to an incorrect input type. It ensures the function correctly handles the end of the stream by passing a byte string instead of a text string to the decoder.
This commit adds a link to the edmsynths.com website in the documentation sidebar. It updates the sidebarintro.html and sidebarlogo.html templates to include this new navigation item.

This commit updates the release history to document a fix for handling objects that raise exceptions during size determination. It notes that such objects are now sent using chunked transfer encoding instead of causing a failure.

This commit updates the contributing documentation to clarify the project's stance on docstrings. It replaces a previous prohibition with specific syntax examples for writing docstrings in the Requests codebase.

This commit fixes a typo in the project's documentation by correcting "PST Requests" to "POST Requests" in the API section. It also adjusts the indentation of the surrounding HTTP method list items in the README file for consistency.

This commit updates the `setup.py` file to explicitly list all subpackages of the `requests` library, including `chardet`, `idna`, and `urllib3`. This ensures that all necessary modules are correctly included when the package is installed or distributed.

This commit updates the project's release history to document version 2.4.2. It lists new features like JSON upload support and bytestring URL handling, alongside bug fixes for authentication and iteration errors.

This commit corrects the documentation for the response object in the quickstart guide. It removes an incorrect example showing the status as a combined string, ensuring users understand the proper structure of the status and reason fields.

This commit corrects a documentation example in the main index file to use the `text` attribute instead of `content` when displaying a response body. It ensures the documentation accurately reflects the correct method for accessing response data.
This commit updates the documentation title in the API reference file. It changes the heading from "API" to "Developer Interface" to better reflect the content's purpose for users.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar template to display the correct sponsor name. It changes the text from "the Government of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg" to "CERT Gouvernemental - GOVCERT.LU" in the sidebarlogo.html file.

This commit refactors the `rebuild_proxies` method in `requests/sessions.py` to improve code readability. It replaces a try-except block with a direct dictionary lookup and restructures the logic for setting proxy authentication headers.
This commit refactors the Request class in requests/core.py to improve code clarity. It replaces direct class identity checks with isinstance calls when encoding dictionary keys and values to UTF-8.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the advanced user documentation. It changes "version-controled" to "version-controlled" in the security warning within the `docs/user/advanced.rst` file.

This commit reverts the optimization that cached a default SSLContext in the HTTPAdapter class. It removes the preloaded context creation to restore previous behavior, likely addressing issues with SSL configuration or performance regressions.

The OAuth1 Client class now uses a module-level logger instead of calling the logging module directly. This change standardizes debug output for signature generation, ensuring log messages are properly attributed to the specific module.

This commit fixes a bug in the HTTPAdapter class where certificate verification incorrectly used the adapter's instance attribute instead of the request-specific verify parameter. Users relying on per-request verification settings will now see the correct behavior.
This commit updates the documentation to fix a broken link to the Certifi project. It replaces the outdated URL with the current Read the Docs address in the advanced user guide.

Updates the CodeQL security analysis workflow to use version 3.29.0 of the github/codeql-action. This minor version bump ensures the repository's automated security scanning uses the latest available action features and fixes.
This commit adds playful emoticon aliases to the HTTP status code mappings in the requests library. Users can now access status codes 301, 404, and 500 using these new symbolic names.

This commit adds a deprecation warning to the `get_connection` method within the `HTTPAdapter` class. Users who subclass `HTTPAdapter` and override this method will now see a warning indicating that they should migrate to `get_connection_with_tls_context` for future compatibility.

This commit reverts a previous change that attempted to make safe mode compatible with request timeouts. It restores the original behavior in the `requests.models` module, where safe mode would not properly handle timeout exceptions, and removes the associated test case.

This commit ensures that the `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE` environment variable is restored to its original state after the package installation process completes. It prevents the setup script from permanently altering the user's Python environment, which could otherwise suppress the creation of bytecode files in subsequent sessions.

This commit adds a unit test to the RequestsTestCase in test_requests.py to verify that POST requests with mixed data types, including JSON strings and file uploads, do not trigger encoding errors. It ensures the library correctly handles these scenarios by confirming a successful response status.

This commit modifies the `Request.send` method in `requests/models.py` to prevent automatic content decoding by urllib3. It changes the `decode_content` parameter to `False`, ensuring raw response data is handled explicitly by the Requests library rather than relying on urllib3's internal decoding behavior.

This commit updates the project history to document a bug fix in the Content-Type header parsing logic. The change makes the parsing process case-insensitive, ensuring that variations in character encoding specifications are handled correctly.

This commit adds Python 3.3 to the continuous integration test matrix and removes a blank line from the test suite. It ensures the project is verified against the older Python version and cleans up the test file formatting.
This commit updates the documentation to reflect that the library is now powered by httplib and urllib3 instead of urllib2. It also corrects a minor formatting error in the NIH attribution line.

This commit updates the documentation index to improve link formatting and accuracy. It adds a version prefix to the release link and corrects the reference to the urllib2 module to point to the proper library documentation.
This commit updates the project's README documentation. It replaces the ASCII art banner with a cleaner, more standard text header. No functional code or behavior is changed.

This commit modifies the `Request.send` method in `requests/models.py` to execute the authentication callable before encoding the request body. This ensures that authentication headers are correctly applied to the final request payload, preventing potential issues where authentication data might be missing or incorrectly formatted during transmission.

This commit refactors the Session class in requests/sessions.py by renaming its base class to SessionRedirectMixin and simplifying the constructor to remove explicit parameter definitions. It also updates the import to use default_hooks instead of the removed HOOKS constant.

The `ok` property in the `Response` class now catches `HTTPError` instead of the broader `RequestException`. This prevents unrelated request errors from being incorrectly treated as HTTP status failures, ensuring the property accurately reflects the response status.

This commit updates the project's README to fix a broken image link. It changes the file extension of the flourish image from PNG to JPG, ensuring the logo displays correctly for users viewing the documentation.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to clarify that connect and read timeouts are not based on wall clock time. It explains that the actual elapsed time for a request may exceed the specified timeout values.

This commit updates the development dependency on pytest-httpbin from version 2.0.0 to 2.1.0rc1. The change is applied to both the requirements-dev.txt file and the test requirements list in setup.py.

This commit removes the automatic closing of ad-hoc sessions in the `request` function within `requests/api.py`. It also introduces a new `OldRequest` class in `requests/models.py` and adds a `send` method to `PreparedRequest`.

This commit updates the documentation in docs/index.rst to correct the Python version support statement. It changes the text to use en-dashes and an ampersand for a more concise presentation of the supported versions.

This commit fixes a bug where the read timeout was ignored when streaming responses, causing requests to hang indefinitely. The `HTTPAdapter.send` method now consistently applies the read timeout to all requests. A new test verifies that streaming requests correctly raise a timeout exception.

This commit updates a comment in the `PreparedRequest` class within `requests/models.py` to clarify that URL-based authentication is extracted before other methods. It does not change any functional behavior or fix a bug, but improves the documentation of the `prepare_auth` method.

This commit updates the `stream_decode_response_unicode` function in `requests/utils.py` to handle `None` encodings by falling back to the response's apparent encoding. It ensures that streaming responses are decoded consistently with the standard `text()` method, preventing silent failures or incorrect output when the encoding is not explicitly set.
Adds a new image file for the Korean language extension. This provides the visual asset required for the Korean locale.
Bumps the package version to 0.2.3 in the requests/core.py module. This update increments the version string and build number to reflect the new release.

This commit updates the test suite for the requests library to use the correct import path for the Session class. It also renames a test method to accurately reflect that it tests HTTP rather than HTTPS authentication.

This commit adds documentation to the `requests` package stub, explaining that vendored dependencies are independent libraries. It clarifies that changes to these libraries must be made in their respective upstream repositories rather than within `requests`.

Adds basic tests for internationalized domain names in the requests library. The new TestPreparingURLs class verifies that URLs with non-ASCII characters are correctly converted to Punycode and percent-encoded.
This documentation update corrects the example HTTP status code from 200 to 204 in the index file. It also adds a new line demonstrating how to access the response content attribute.

This commit updates the project's setup configuration to explicitly declare a dependency on the oauthlib package. It ensures that the required version range is installed alongside the application, preventing potential compatibility issues.

This commit simplifies error handling in the HTTPAdapter.send method by combining separate exception blocks for protocol and socket errors into a single clause. It ensures both error types are consistently converted into a ConnectionError, streamlining the code without changing user-facing behavior.
This documentation update changes the contact information for reporting Red Hat vulnerabilities. It replaces the individual contact with the Python Maintenance Team in the community guidelines.

This commit introduces the `requests.async` module, which provides an asynchronous interface to the Requests library using gevent. It allows users to send multiple requests concurrently via a `map` function, returning `Request` instances instead of immediate responses.
This commit updates the documentation index to align with the project's README. It replaces outdated download and license badges with a current PyPI version badge in the docs/index.rst file.

This commit clarifies that accessing the raw socket response via the Response object requires setting prefetch to false during the initial request. It updates the quickstart documentation and adds a comment to the Response class to highlight this dependency.
This commit removes a Bitcoin donation address from the documentation sidebar. It updates the `sidebarintro.html` template to eliminate the specific wallet link, cleaning up the user interface.

This commit updates the Requests library to use the chardet package instead of the deprecated charade library for character encoding detection. It corrects the import in the compatibility module and updates documentation references in the Response class and package README.

The `get_environ_proxies` function in `requests/utils.py` now uses `urllib` to detect proxy settings. This change allows the library to recognize proxies configured in the operating system, such as macOS System Configuration or the Windows registry, rather than relying solely on environment variables.

This commit adds tests to the TestTimeout class in tests/test_requests.py to verify that passing Timeout objects with None values for connect and read parameters works correctly. It ensures that setting these timeouts to None does not prevent requests from succeeding, covering scenarios where users might want to allow indefinite blocking.
Adds a GitHub Actions workflow to run CodeQL security analysis on the repository. This enables automated static code analysis for vulnerabilities on pushes and pull requests to the master branch.

This commit adds a new configuration option to the requests library's defaults module. When enabled, it ensures that URIs are automatically percent-encoded, preventing issues with special characters in URLs.
The build system now runs the test suite with parallel execution and process isolation. This change modifies the Makefile to speed up testing by distributing work across eight workers.

This commit configures Dependabot to group all GitHub Actions and pre-commit updates into single pull requests. This reduces the number of individual PRs users must review by bundling related dependency updates together.

This commit updates the `iter_lines` method in the `Response` class to ensure compatibility with Python 3. It changes the default value of the `decode_unicode` parameter to `True` and fixes a line-splitting check to correctly handle byte comparisons.

This commit fixes a missing import in the `requests/auth.py` module that caused an error when using OAuth authentication on Python 2. The `extract_params` function is now correctly imported within the Python 2 conditional block, resolving the issue.

This commit updates the project documentation by finalizing the release date for version 0.6.0 and correcting typographical errors in the history and readme files. It standardizes the capitalization of feature descriptions and fixes inconsistent apostrophe usage in the project description.

This commit introduces a new module, `requests/status_codes.py`, that provides a lookup dictionary for HTTP status codes. It allows users to easily map numeric status codes to their corresponding descriptive names, such as "ok" or "created," using the `LookupDict` structure.

This commit reverts an unintended modification in the test suite for the requests module. It restores the correct import statement in tests/test_requests.py, ensuring the test environment loads the expected compatibility utilities.

This commit removes the `requests.defaults` module, which previously defined global configuration constants like default headers and redirect limits. The `PreparedRequest` class in `requests.models` is updated to no longer rely on these removed defaults.

This commit disables the automatic authentication logic within the `Request` class in `requests/models.py`. By commenting out the code that processes authentication objects and retrieves credentials, the library no longer automatically applies stored authentication to requests.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 2.0.0. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the package's initialization file to reflect the new release.

This commit improves the documentation for the `address_in_network`, `dotted_netmask`, and `is_ipv4_network` functions in `requests/utils.py`. It adds clear docstrings with examples to explain how these utilities handle IP address validation and network mask conversion.

This release fixes a bug where OAuth authentication failed when used with POST requests. It also includes general bugfixes for the requests library. The version number in the package initialization module was updated to 0.13.9.

This documentation update clarifies the rationale for maintaining Python 2.7 support in the Requests library. It removes the previous justification that linked the support timeline to pip's release schedule, instead focusing solely on the project's commitment to its user base.

This commit fixes the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` by correctly initializing the `auth` attribute and updating the response building logic to use the `cookies` attribute instead of `cookiejar`. It also removes an unused import from `requests/api.py` and comments out a raw stream close operation.

This commit fixes a rendering issue in the advanced user documentation where a note about connection timeouts was incorrectly indented. The change ensures the text displays properly within the `docs/user/advanced.rst` file.

This commit updates the project documentation and history files to reflect current statistics and formatting. It increases the reported weekly download count in the README and adjusts the version header in the history log.

This commit updates the changelog for version 2.4.0, documenting new features and improvements. It highlights the automatic sending of keep-alive headers, support for separate connect and read timeouts, and a refactored method for merging environment settings.

This commit renames the optional dependency group from "betterssl" to "security" in the requests package setup. Users installing the package with the security extra will now use the updated name to enable SSL verification features.

This commit updates the test suite to ensure compatibility with Python 3. It modifies the `test_response_is_iterable` method within the `RequestsTestCase` class to use the modern `next()` function instead of the removed iterator method.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` now accepts a `return_response` parameter to control whether the response object is returned. This change updates the internal async wrapper in `requests/async.py` to pass the new flag, ensuring consistent behavior across synchronous and asynchronous calls.

This commit updates the project's history file to finalize the 1.0.0 release date and detail major architectural changes. It documents the removal of configuration options, authentication helpers, and most hooks, while introducing swappable connection adapters and a new character encoding dependency.

This commit integrates the oauthlib library into the requests package, adding support for OAuth 1.0a and OAuth 2.0 authentication. It introduces new modules for handling request signing, token management, and parameter encoding, allowing users to securely authenticate API requests.

This commit fixes a bug where urllib3's SSLError was leaking through instead of being converted to requests' SSLError. It updates the Response class in requests/models.py to properly wrap these exceptions during content iteration.
This commit hides the revision system inline element in the Flask documentation theme by setting its display property to none. The change is made in the flasky.css_t stylesheet file.

The `iter_lines` method in the `Response` class now reads data in larger chunks instead of single bytes. This change fixes universal line ending handling but removes the ability to specify custom line separators.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the installation documentation. It changes the word "Requsts" to "Requests" in the user guide, ensuring the project name is spelled correctly for readers.

This commit updates the indentation in the RequestsTestSuite test file to use spaces instead of tabs. It affects the test cases for HTTP 302 redirects, ensuring consistent formatting without changing the actual test logic or behavior.

This commit prevents crashes when a response specifies an unknown or invalid encoding. It updates the `get_unicode_from_response` and `stream_decode_response_unicode` functions in `requests/utils.py` to catch lookup errors and return raw content instead of failing.

This commit applies PEP 8 formatting standards to the HTTPAdapter class in the requests module. It adjusts the line wrapping of the HTTPResponse.from_httplib call within the send method to improve code readability without altering functionality.

This commit removes the strict mode configuration option from the Request class in requests/models.py. It ensures that POST requests are always converted to GET requests upon receiving a 301, 302, or 303 redirect, matching standard browser behavior.
Updates the CodeQL security analysis workflow to use version 4.32.0 of the github/codeql-action. This change refreshes the automated code scanning process in the repository's CI pipeline.
This commit updates the GitHub handle for Kenneth Reitz in the AUTHORS.rst file to reflect his renamed account. It ensures the project's contributor list links to the correct, current profile.

This commit adds a new entry to the community documentation, linking to a blog post titled "Python for the Web." It highlights a resource that teaches users how to interact with the web using the Requests library.

The `parse_header_links` function in `requests/utils.py` now safely handles empty or whitespace-only header values by returning an empty list instead of failing. This prevents errors when parsing link headers that contain no data.

This commit updates the .gitignore file to exclude specific test scripts from version control. It prevents the files t.py and t2.py from being tracked by git, keeping the repository clean of temporary test artifacts.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to clarify how SOCKS5 proxies handle domain resolution. It explains that the standard socks5 scheme resolves domains on the client side, while the socks5h scheme is required to resolve them through the proxy server.

This commit fixes a TypeError in the `morsel_to_cookie` function within the `requests` module. The error occurred because the function passed unsupported keyword arguments to the `create_cookie` method. The fix removes these invalid parameters to ensure cookies are created correctly.

This commit updates the release history to clarify a behavior change in version 1.2.1. It notes that 301 and 302 redirects now change the HTTP verb to GET for all request types, not just POST, to improve browser compatibility.
This commit adds the nose testing framework to the project's requirements file. It ensures the necessary dependency is installed for running tests, addressing a missing package issue.
Adds a new image file named flower-of-life.jpg to the ext directory. This commit introduces a static asset to the project without modifying any existing code or functionality.
This commit adds a comment to the setup.py file that links to a resource for learning more about the setup process. It does not change any functional behavior or fix a bug.

This commit removes an unnecessary list conversion when iterating over HTTP status codes in the requests library. It optimizes the initialization of the status code lookup dictionary by iterating directly over the dictionary items instead of creating a redundant list copy.

The Request class in requests/models.py no longer restricts the HTTP method to a predefined list of standard verbs. This change allows users to assign any custom method string to a request, removing the previous validation that would raise an error for non-standard methods.

This documentation update clarifies that installation commands should be executed in a terminal rather than a Python REPL. It modifies the user installation guide to prevent new users from mistakenly running these commands in an interactive session.

The `get_netrc_auth` function in `requests.utils` now uses the URL's hostname directly for netrc lookups instead of parsing the network location. This change simplifies the code and ensures the correct host is used for authentication credential retrieval.

This commit fixes the RequestsCookieJar class in requests/cookies.py to correctly handle duplicate cookies and implement missing dictionary-like methods. It ensures that accessing cookies by name returns a single item rather than a list, and that keys and values methods function properly.

This commit updates the CI configuration to correctly generate and upload code coverage reports to Codecov. It modifies the Makefile to output XML coverage data and adds the codecov package to the project's dependencies.

This release fixes a packaging issue where test certificates were missing from the source distribution on PyPI. The update includes the necessary files in the manifest and bumps the version to 2.32.1.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar templates to replace outdated Gittip links with the new Gratipay domain. It also adjusts the width of the donation widget iframe to improve the layout appearance.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar template to include a new link to the Open DSM-5M website. The change modifies the sidebarlogo.html file to add this external resource to the navigation menu.

Adds a test to verify that asynchronous requests correctly handle cookies when using a requests.Session. It ensures that cookies set on the session persist across requests, while cookies from non-session requests do not leak into the session state.

This commit fixes a bug where the base_headers dictionary was shared by reference across all Session instances, causing unintended state changes. It now uses a deep copy in the Session class initialization to ensure each session has independent header configuration.

This commit fixes an issue where cookies from intermediate responses were not saved when using HTTP Digest authentication. It updates the `Session.send` method in `requests/sessions.py` to extract cookies from all responses in the request history. The test suite is also updated to use the correct authentication class.

This commit removes the initialization of the `content` attribute to `None` within the `Response` class constructor. This change likely addresses a documentation or type-hinting issue where the attribute was explicitly set before being populated, ensuring the `Response` object behaves as expected when accessed.
This commit adds a prefetch option to the Session class in the requests library. Users can now enable prefetching during session initialization or on individual requests to improve performance.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to reflect the correct attribute for accessing response content. It changes the example from using the deprecated content attribute to the standard text attribute, ensuring users see the proper method for retrieving response data.

This commit fixes a crash in the `Session.request` method that occurred when the session's cookie jar was not a standard `RequestsCookieJar`. It replaces the previous copy and update logic with a shallow copy and explicit cookie setting to ensure compatibility with various cookie container types.

This commit updates the CI test execution in the Makefile to use the `--search-test` flag and increase the parallel process count to 30. It also passes the Python interpreter path via the `--core-target` variable to the test runner.

Updates the CodeQL security analysis workflow to use version 3.27.0 of the github/codeql-action. This minor version bump ensures the automated code scanning process runs with the latest available features and fixes.

This commit updates the documentation's top bar template to replace a Python 2 retirement countdown with a link to the Requests 3.0 project. It also disables the JavaScript code that previously calculated the remaining time for Python 2 support.

This commit fixes broken tests in the TestRequests class by updating file references from requirements.txt to Pipfile. It ensures that tests for POSTBIN file uploads and conflicting parameters correctly read the new dependency file format.

The `send` function in `requests/async.py` previously ignored the `pool` argument and simply delegated to the request object's send method. This change makes `send` actually utilize the provided connection pool, fixing a broken or incomplete implementation.

This commit simplifies the URL validation logic in the `Request` class within `requests/models.py`. It removes the separate `_checks` method and moves the URL existence check directly into the `send` method, streamlining the request preparation process.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` now imports the `config` module instead of `settings`. It retrieves the default timeout from `config.settings.timeout` to ensure the application uses the new configuration structure.

The default User-Agent header now includes the Python implementation name and version number. This change modifies the `requests/defaults.py` module to detect whether the environment is CPython or PyPy and append the appropriate version details.

This commit corrects a copy-paste error in the docstring for the GuessJSONUTFTests class in tests/test_utils.py. It replaces an incorrect description referencing HTTPS functionality with the accurate description for JSON UTF encoding guessing tests.
This commit fixes a typo in the quickstart documentation by correcting the phrasing of a sentence about OAuth. It removes redundant text and improves the flow of the explanation in the user guide.

This commit refactors the `merge_setting` function in `requests/sessions.py` to improve clarity and fix bugs related to case sensitivity. It ensures that header removal and parameter merging behave correctly by using case-insensitive logic where appropriate.

This refactoring extracts the logic for handling authentication headers during redirects into a new method called `rebuild_auth` within the `SessionRedirectMixin` class. It simplifies the `resolve_redirects` method by delegating the process of stripping credentials for new hosts and applying netrc authentication to this dedicated helper.

This commit adds tests for the `rewind_body` utility and the `_body_position` attribute within the `requests` module. It verifies that request bodies can be correctly reset to their initial state after being read, including handling edge cases where the underlying file object lacks seek or tell capabilities.
This commit removes the project's main documentation file, README.rst. Users will no longer see the library's description, badges, or usage instructions in the repository root.

This commit refactors the URL preparation logic in the `PreparedRequest` class within `requests/models.py`. It consolidates the URL reconstruction and re-quoting steps into a single operation, removing outdated comments and redundant code.

This release updates the requests library to version 0.10.2, addressing a "Too many open files" error and improving URL handling for bare domains. It also optimizes unicode error replacement by removing a redundant processing pass.

This commit adds a string representation method to the CaseInsensitiveDict class in the requests library. It ensures that logging headers displays a standard dictionary format instead of revealing internal implementation details, making debug output cleaner and more readable.

This documentation update clarifies that the lack of Server-Name-Indication support is a limitation of Python 2.6 and 2.7, rather than a bug in the Requests library. It modifies the FAQ to help users correctly identify the root cause of SSL connection issues.

This commit fixes a bug in the `MockRequest` class within `requests/cookies.py` where passing a `Response` object directly to `urlparse` caused errors. It now correctly extracts the network location by parsing the response's URL string instead.

This commit removes the dependency on the certifi package, which is being end-of-lifed. The `where` function in `requests/certs.py` now exclusively returns the path to Requests' own vendored CA bundle, eliminating the previous logic that checked for an installed certifi module.

This commit prevents a crash in the `extract_cookies_to_jar` function within the `requests` library. It adds a check to skip cookie extraction if the response object lacks a valid original response, avoiding errors when processing responses that do not contain underlying connection data.
This commit adds Chris Dary to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS.rst file. It updates the project's credit list to acknowledge his patches and suggestions.
This commit corrects a typo in the README.md file where the documentation URL was missing a forward slash. It ensures the link to the Python Requests documentation is properly formatted for users.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to clarify that response bodies are now downloaded immediately by default. It explains how to use the `prefetch` parameter to defer downloading until the content is accessed.

This commit fixes installation and test crashes that occurred when the multiprocessing module was unavailable or could not determine the CPU count. It modifies the PyTest class in setup.py to catch these errors and default to a single worker process instead.

This release updates the requests library to version 2.19.0, relaxing version pins for idna and urllib3 to support newer releases. It also removes Python 2.6 support references and updates compatibility checks in the main module.

This commit updates the documentation for the requests module to explain how to pass a CookieJar object to send cookies with HTTP requests. It clarifies the behavior of the get, post, put, head, and delete functions by adding the cookies parameter to their usage examples.

This commit introduces the project's changelog file, HISTORY.rst, to document version history. It records the initial release version 0.2.0 and a prior 0.0.1 entry, providing users with a clear timeline of project milestones.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Session` class where the `patch` method was missing the `self` parameter. This error would cause an exception when users attempted to send HTTP PATCH requests through a session.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the project's changelog. It fixes the typo in the description of improved redirect behavior within the HISTORY.rst file.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 1.2.2. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the package's initialization file to reflect the new release.
Updates the GitHub Actions workflow files to use version 5.6.0 of the actions/setup-python action. This minor version bump ensures the CI environment uses the latest stable release for Python setup.

This commit adds several utility functions to the requests.utils module, including parse_list_header, parse_dict_header, randombytes, and unquote_header_value. These functions, adapted from the Werkzeug library, provide robust parsing for HTTP headers and secure random byte generation.

The `super_len` function in `requests/utils.py` no longer uses the return value of `seek` to determine the total length of file-like objects. This change prevents incorrect length calculations for objects like `StringIO` where `seek` might return `None` or an unexpected value.

This commit enables Python 3.7 testing in the project's continuous integration configuration. It updates the Travis CI setup to include the 3.7 development version in the test matrix, allowing the build system to verify compatibility with this new Python release.

This update ensures compatibility with Python 3.3 by addressing changes in the standard library's cookie handling. It modifies the MockRequest class in requests/cookies.py to correctly map the unverifiable attribute to the existing is_unverifiable method, preventing potential errors during cookie policy verification.

This commit updates the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to automatically use the operating system's CA certificate bundle for SSL verification when no specific certificate path is provided. It introduces a new utility function, `get_ca_bundle_path`, in `requests/utils.py` to locate the system bundle, improving default security behavior for users.

The `map` function in `requests/async.py` now accepts generators and other iterators, not just lists. This change allows users to pass any iterable of requests without manually converting it to a list first.

This commit upgrades the bundled urllib3 library to version 1.19 within the requests package. It updates core modules like connection, connectionpool, and response to incorporate the new library's features and bug fixes.

This commit updates the project's changelog to clarify recent feature descriptions. It corrects the wording for URL parameterization and file upload capabilities, and refines the description of the new HTTP authentication system.

This commit adds the chardet library as a project dependency and fixes a missing newline at the end of the requirements file. It ensures the character encoding detection package is installed correctly for the application.

This commit introduces a new dummy socket server for unit testing, allowing developers to simulate network interactions without external dependencies. The Server class manages the server lifecycle and handles incoming connections, while a basic test verifies its functionality.

Adds a new `safe_mode` configuration option to the `requests` library's default settings. This change introduces a flag in `requests/defaults.py` that users can enable to modify the library's behavior, likely for enhanced security or stability.

This commit updates the project's release history to document version 2.5.0. It details new features like retry support and response line splitting, alongside bug fixes for URL parsing and authentication. The changes also note behavioral updates, including deprecation warnings and stricter HTTP version restrictions.

This commit refactors the `rebuild_proxies` method in the `Session` class to preserve the `Proxy-Authorization` header during request redirects. Previously, this header was incorrectly stripped, potentially breaking authenticated proxy connections. The change ensures that proxy credentials remain intact when the session resolves new proxy settings.

This commit adds a new SSLError exception class to the requests library. It allows users to specifically catch SSL-related connection failures, which were previously grouped under the general ConnectionError.
Moves the module-level docstring into the `Server` class in `dummyserver/server.py`. This ensures the documentation is correctly associated with the class rather than the entire module.

This commit updates the Pipfile.lock to pin specific versions of dependencies like packaging and pyparsing. It also corrects the package index URL to the standard PyPI endpoint and updates the file's integrity hash.

This commit corrects the documentation for the `requests.async` module. It updates the module title and description to accurately reflect that it implements the main Requests system after monkey-patching urllib2 with eventlet or gevent.
This commit adds a changelog directive to the project's history file. It establishes the structure for recording future release notes. The change affects the HISTORY.rst module.

This commit fixes a bug in the OAuth1 class where authentication headers were lost during HTTP redirects. The change ensures the OAuth1.__call__ method correctly returns the response object, preventing the authentication state from falling off.

This commit makes the default values for the `stream` and `verify` parameters explicit in the `Session.request` method and the top-level `request` function. It also updates the documentation in `api.py` to accurately reflect these defaults, improving clarity for users.

This commit improves concurrent performance in the `requests` library by preloading the default SSL context at module import time. It modifies the `HTTPAdapter` to reuse this cached context instead of reloading root certificates for every request, reducing overhead during high-concurrency operations.
This commit updates the project history to document a new feature. It allows users to send file uploads and POST data simultaneously in a single request.
This commit updates the release date for version 0.8.0 in the HISTORY.rst file. It also adds a changelog entry noting that file uploads now send real names.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 0.13.5. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the package's initialization file to reflect the new release.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to explain how to send multiple values for a single form key using a list. It clarifies that passing a dictionary with list values allows users to submit multivalued form-encoded data.

Updates the CodeQL security analysis workflow to use version 2.21.3 of the github/codeql-action. This major version upgrade replaces the previous 1.1.39 release in the codeql-analysis.yml file, ensuring the project uses the latest supported security scanning tools.

This commit fixes an issue where requests with proxy URLs lacking a valid host would fail unexpectedly. It adds validation in the HTTPAdapter.get_connection method to raise a new InvalidProxyURL exception if the proxy host is missing.

This commit reverts unintended changes to the default parameter values for the `Session.request` method in the `requests` library. It restores the `stream` and `verify` arguments to their original defaults of `False` and `True`, respectively, while preserving the desired docstring updates.
