This commit updates the NOTICE file to replace the deprecated Charade library with Chardet. It also adds the Mozilla Public License 2.0 attribution for the cacert.pem file, which is now sourced directly from Mozilla.

This commit updates the project title and introductory text in the documentation index. It changes the main heading to "Requests: HTTP for Humans" and adjusts the description to emphasize usability for human beings.
This commit updates the project history to announce version 0.6.5, which introduces a new offline test suite. This change allows developers to run tests quickly without requiring network access.

This commit moves the project attribution credit from the top of the README to the bottom. It updates the documentation file to reposition the acknowledgment for Kenneth Reitz and the Python Software Foundation.

This commit adds PyPy3 to the Travis CI test suite to ensure the project runs correctly on that interpreter. It also fixes a resource leak in the `Server` class within `tests/testserver/server.py` by explicitly closing the socket after handling requests.

This commit updates the project documentation to include The Washington Post in the list of testimonials. It adds a link to the organization's website alongside existing entries like Twitter, Inc.

This commit updates the project history to document version 0.10.0. It notes that the default encoding for text responses is now ISO-8859-1 and introduces a new multiple-hooks system, including the `Response.register_hook` method.

This commit fixes a crash in the `Session.request` method of the `requests` library that occurred when running in safe mode. It prevents an error when the response object has no cookies by checking if the cookies attribute is not None before attempting to process them.

This commit removes an outdated import example from the project's documentation index. It updates the user-facing documentation to reflect current usage patterns. The change affects the docs/index.rst file.

This commit consolidates separate gzip and deflate streaming functions into a single `stream_decompress` utility in `requests/utils.py`. It also removes redundant gzip decoding from `Response.content` in `requests/models.py`, as the underlying library already handles this process.

This documentation update adds a hyperlink to the Mozilla trust store in the advanced user guide. It clarifies the source of the root CAs bundled with the Requests library by linking directly to the Mozilla certificate data file.

This commit consolidates multiple examples of sending form data with repeated keys into a single section within the quickstart documentation. It removes redundant code snippets from the user guide to improve clarity and reduce repetition.

This commit adds Jon Parise to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS.rst file. It updates the project's attribution records to reflect new contributions.

This commit fixes an issue where cookies set during a redirect were not properly applied to subsequent requests. It updates the `resolve_redirects` method in the `SessionRedirectMixin` class to ensure the `Set-Cookie` header is correctly transferred to the prepared request.

This commit fixes a bug in the HTTPAdapter class where unpickling an adapter failed to correctly restore the pool blocking configuration. This commit adds an `origin_req_host` property to the `MockRequest` class in `requests/cookies.py`. It ensures the mock object correctly exposes the origin request host, likely resolving compatibility issues with cookie handling logic that expects this attribute.

This commit fixes a crash in the HTTPDigestAuth class when processing authentication responses containing string data. It ensures that string inputs are properly encoded to bytes before being passed to the MD5 and SHA1 hashing functions.

This commit updates documentation and code references to reflect the project's move from the "requests/requests" GitHub path to the new "psf/requests" organization. It ensures that links in the README, history, and user guides point to the correct repository location.

This commit updates the documentation for the `proxy_headers` method within the `HTTPAdapter` class in the `requests` library. It removes an outdated parameter description from the docstring to improve accuracy.
This release updates the requests library to version 0.14.1, adding compatibility with Python 3.3. It also simplifies the default accept-encoding header and includes general bug fixes.

This commit fixes an issue where query parameters were incorrectly passed to direct requests during the redirect resolution process. The change modifies the `resolve_redirects` method within the `SessionRedirectMixin` class to stop supplying these parameters.

This commit adds a new contributor's guide to the documentation, providing guidelines and advice for those interested in contributing to the requests project. It also updates the main documentation index to include a link to this new guide.

This commit updates the package configuration to include the `oreos` module in the list of distributed packages. It ensures that the `oreos` component is properly recognized and installed alongside other dependencies like `urllib3`.

This commit optimizes the HTTPDigestAuth class in requests/auth.py by compiling the regular expression used to parse authentication headers. It improves performance in the handle_401 method by reusing the compiled pattern instead of recompiling it on every request.

This commit updates the project's README documentation. It modifies the closing statement to replace "You can trust this code" with "You may certianly put your trust in this code," introducing a typo in the process.

This commit updates the sponsors documentation page by adding a decorative emoji sequence to the end of the file. It also corrects the file's line ending to include a proper newline character.
This commit adds Dj Gilcrease to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS file. It updates project attribution to recognize the individual's patches and suggestions.
This commit updates the changelog to document a fix in the Requests library. It clarifies that SSL problems now correctly raise an SSLError instead of a ConnectionError when using urllib3 v1.22.

This commit updates the Makefile to simplify the dependency installation process. It removes specific version constraints for pipenv, allowing the latest available version to be installed during the init step.

This commit adds a requirements file for the documentation build process to ensure Read the Docs uses a stable version of Sphinx. It pins the Sphinx dependency to version 4.2.0 to prevent unexpected breakages during documentation generation.

This commit adds failing tests to verify that the test server correctly handles UTF-8 Byte Order Marks in text and JSON responses. It also includes a test for the JSON UTF-8 guessing utility to ensure BOMs are properly detected.

This commit updates the project's changelog file to prepare for the next release. It adds a new development section with placeholders for upcoming improvements and bug fixes.

This commit fixes broken RST markup in the community vulnerabilities documentation. It corrects the syntax for PGP key fingerprints so that the associated Keybase links render properly for users.

This commit regenerates the test certificates for the expired, mutual TLS, and valid server scenarios. It updates the associated keys and certificate files within the tests/certs directory to ensure compatibility with OpenSSL 3.4.0.

The `iter_content` method in the `Response` class now catches low-level socket errors and re-raises them as `ConnectionError` exceptions. This change ensures that network interruptions during content streaming are handled consistently with other connection failures.

The BaseAdapter class in requests/adapters.py now correctly defines the mandatory parameters for its send method, aligning with the required adapter interface. This update also includes improved documentation for the send and close methods to clarify their expected behavior and arguments.

This commit ensures that proxy connections in the HTTPAdapter class respect the configured connection pool settings. Previously, proxies ignored the pool size limits, which could lead to resource exhaustion. Now, the get_connection method correctly applies the pool connection count, maximum size, and blocking behavior to proxy requests.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to a newer version. It modifies the RecentlyUsedContainer class to use a reentrant lock instead of a standard lock, preventing potential deadlocks during nested operations.

This commit corrects the documentation for the `raise_for_status` method in the `Response` class. It clarifies that the method creates a new `HTTPError` exception on each call rather than raising a previously stored one.

This commit adds tests to the UtilsTestCase class in test_requests.py to verify that the get_environ_proxies function correctly handles domain names and IP addresses within the no_proxy environment variable. It ensures that specific hostnames and IP ranges are properly excluded from proxy settings.

The RequestsCookieJar class in requests/cookies.py now raises a CookieConflictError when accessing a cookie name that matches multiple entries. This prevents ambiguous lookups by forcing users to specify domain and path arguments for clarity.
This commit updates the project version to 0.8.3 and corrects the release date in the history log. It also adds Idan Gazit to the list of contributors in the authors file.

This commit updates the "security" extra in setup.py to replace outdated dependencies with modern alternatives. It swaps pyOpenSSL, ndg-httpsclient, and pyasn1 for newer versions of pyOpenSSL, cryptography, and idna.

This commit optimizes the `Session.request` method in the `requests` library by removing a redundant `Request.copy` operation. It ensures the request object is copied only once before being updated and prepared, improving performance without changing user-facing behavior.

This commit updates the project's README to include a direct link to the "Contributor Friendly" issue tag. It also adds a note encouraging new contributors to reach out for help if they feel uncertain about submitting a pull request.
This commit updates the project's README documentation. It adds a blank line to the text, likely to adjust the visual spacing of the content.

This release adds support for multipart file uploads in POST and PUT requests via a new file attribute. It also introduces a Request.url attribute to handle context and redirects. The changes are implemented in the requests.core module.

This commit adds standard package metadata attributes to the requests module, including a description, project URL, and author email. These additions improve the library's integration with package managers and documentation tools by providing essential project information.

This commit fixes a grammatical error in the project documentation by changing "Requests allow" to "Requests allows." The change ensures the main module name is used with the correct singular verb form in the index file.

This commit resolves merge conflicts and applies Python 3 compatibility fixes to the requests library. It updates the Request class to properly percent-encode URLs during redirects and adjusts the Response class for Python 3 string handling. This commit updates the documentation to include Runscope in the list of organizations that use the Requests library. It modifies the testimonials section in the main documentation file to reflect this new user.

This commit removes the explicit charset parameter from the JSON content type in the PreparedRequest class. It also ensures the request body is encoded to bytes only if it is not already, preventing redundant encoding operations.

This commit updates the project's dependency configuration in setup.py to handle Python 3 compatibility. It conditionally includes the chardet2 package for Python 3 environments while retaining chardet for Python 2, and removes support for Python 2.5.

This commit improves compatibility with the POSTER header in the `Request` class within `requests/core.py`. It changes the `send` method to merge custom headers with existing ones instead of replacing them, preventing the loss of default headers.

This commit fixes a documentation typo in the `Response` class within `requests/models.py`. It corrects the capitalization of the word "If" in the docstring for the `text` property, ensuring the description of encoding behavior is grammatically correct.

This commit corrects a typo in the test suite for the requests extension. It ensures the test for cookies on redirects checks the correct response variable, preventing false failures in the test suite.

This commit adds a new `deps` target to the Makefile that fetches the urllib3 library from GitHub and installs it into the requests package directory. It ensures the correct version of urllib3 is available for the project's dependencies.

This commit fixes a Unicode decode error in Python 2 when handling redirects to non-ASCII locations. The `resolve_redirects` method in `SessionRedirectMixin` now properly converts the URL scheme to a native string before constructing the final URL.

This commit fixes a typo in the `Response` class where the raw connection attribute was incorrectly named `fo` instead of `raw`. It also updates the `raise_for_status` method and adjusts connection handling in `Request` to properly manage socket blocking and cleanup.

This commit releases version 2.18.4 of the requests library. It updates the version number in the `__version__.py` file and finalizes the release notes in `HISTORY.rst`. The release includes a bug fix that adds header names to error messages for invalid headers.

This commit introduces a new hook registration system for the Request class in the requests module. It replaces direct assignment of hook dictionaries with a structured approach that initializes empty lists for each event type and uses a new register_hook method to add callbacks. This change ensures hooks are properly managed and appended to the correct event lists.
This commit pins the Sphinx dependency to version 1.5.5 or lower to ensure compatibility with Python 2.6. It updates the project's dependency configuration files to enforce this version constraint.

This commit adds a new "out there" section to the documentation, listing external modules, articles, and integrations related to the project. It updates the main documentation index to include this new community resource page.

The CI configuration now runs the full test suite instead of only a subset of tests. This change updates the Makefile and Travis CI setup to execute all non-external tests, ensuring broader coverage during continuous integration.

This commit cleans up the version module by removing the encoding declaration and replacing literal emoji characters with their Unicode escape sequences. It also updates the setup script to explicitly specify UTF-8 encoding when reading the version file.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the string representation of the CaseInsensitiveDict class. Previously, calling the string method on this object would raise an error due to a missing closing parenthesis. The fix ensures the dictionary displays correctly when printed.

This commit updates the changelog to document that `Response.content` now returns only bytes, while a new `Response.text` property returns only unicode. It also notes the removal of the `decode_unicode` function and the addition of a `Response.register_hook` method for pipeline hooks.

This commit updates the README documentation to clarify how to enable automatic HTTP authentication. It replaces incomplete text with a clear explanation and example for the `add_autoauth` function, which registers authentication objects for specific base URLs.

The `merge_hooks` function in `requests/sessions.py` now delegates to `merge_setting` instead of using custom logic. This change ensures that hook merging behavior remains consistent with other settings, fixing a failing test that expected this unified approach.

This commit updates the documentation template to clarify that Requests 3.0 is currently in development. It modifies the promotional banner text in the hacks.html file to accurately reflect the project's status.

This commit updates the documentation for the `Response.json` method in the `requests` library. It clarifies that a `ValueError` is raised when the response body does not contain valid JSON, helping users understand potential error conditions.

This commit updates the project history to clarify that the new `requests.async` module enables asynchronous requests using gevent. It refines the release notes for version 0.6.3 to better describe the functionality of the added module.

This commit fixes a typo in the documentation for the `request` function in `requests/api.py`. It corrects a missing backtick in the parameter description, ensuring the HTTP method list is properly formatted for users reading the API reference.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the advanced user documentation for the `requests` library. It clarifies the description of the `Response` class methods, specifically how to access the undecoded body via `Response.raw`.

This commit fixes an import error that occurred when using the library on AppEngine. It moves the `netrc` import inside the `get_netrc_auth` function in `requests/utils.py` to prevent module-level failures in restricted environments.

This commit fixes a bug in the `should_bypass_proxies` function within the `requests` library where domain boundaries were not correctly handled when checking the `no_proxy` environment variable. It ensures that hostnames are properly stripped of leading dots before comparison, preventing incorrect proxy bypass decisions for specific domains.

This commit fixes test failures on Python 2.6 and 2.7 by redefining `unichr` and `chr` at the module level in `tests/test_utils.py`. It resolves issues where the `__builtins__` dictionary did not follow standard CPython conventions, ensuring the `GuessJSONUTFTests` class runs correctly across different Python versions.
This commit corrects the indentation of the changelog entries in HISTORY.rst. It ensures the list items under the release notes are properly aligned for consistent formatting.

This commit introduces the Invoke task runner to manage project workflows. It adds a build task in invokefile.py and defines test and dependency management tasks in tasks.py. The requirements file is updated to include the invoke library.

This commit introduces a new HTTPError exception class to distinguish HTTP status code errors from general request failures. It updates the Response.raise_for_status method to raise this specific error instead of the generic RequestException, allowing users to catch HTTP errors separately.

The test suite for the requests library no longer inherits from unittest.TestCase, changing the base class for test cases to a plain object. This affects the RequestsTestCase and TestRequests classes in test_requests.py.

The `get_netrc_auth` function in `requests/utils.py` now allows callers to receive parse or permission errors when reading a netrc file. A new `ignore_errors` argument controls this behavior, defaulting to `True` to preserve the previous silent failure mode.

Updates the CodeQL security analysis workflow to use version 3.24.0 of the github/codeql-action. This minor version bump ensures the automated code scanning process runs with the latest available features and fixes.

This commit reverts a previous update to the documentation, removing the native.js script and associated HTML templates. It restores the original state of the docs index and static assets, undoing the changes made to the sidebar and logo templates.

The `default_headers` function in `requests/utils.py` no longer includes "compress" in the default `Accept-Encoding` header. This change prevents the library from requesting content compressed with the less efficient compress algorithm, limiting requests to gzip and deflate.
This commit updates several image assets in the extension directory, including the flourish, license, and requests logo files. It also adds a new screenshot file to the project.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 2.10.0. It also corrects the copyright year in the package metadata to 2016.

This commit updates the API documentation to replace deprecated GitHub timeline URLs with the current events endpoint. It ensures the examples in the API changes section reflect the correct, functional request targets for users.

This commit fixes a crash in the `PreparedRequest.prepare_body` method when handling certain file-like objects that raise an `UnsupportedOperation` error. It ensures the request preparation process handles this specific exception gracefully instead of failing.

Updates the actions/setup-python dependency from version 5.4.0 to 5.5.0 in the lint and test workflows. This minor version bump ensures the CI environment uses the latest stable release of the Python setup action.

This commit removes the custom DocSearch integration from the documentation sidebar. It deletes the associated styles, input field, and script from the sidebar templates, simplifying the user interface.

This commit removes the editable install flag from the project's requirements file. It ensures the local package is installed as a standard dependency rather than a development link, preventing potential build or deployment issues.

This commit reverts previous pyflakes fixes in the test suite to restore the original code style. It affects the `tests/test_requests.py` module, specifically the `RequestsTestSuite` and `TestBaseMixin` classes. The change ensures the test code aligns with the project's preferred formatting conventions.

This commit adds documentation to the advanced user guide explaining how to access and modify the Request object. It clarifies the structure of request and response data, which is useful for developers building custom authentication or handling requests across different methods.

This commit fixes a bug in the `HTTPAdapter` class that prevented users from providing custom SSL contexts via transport adapters. It restores the ability to override specific connection pool key parameters, ensuring custom SSL configurations are correctly applied.

This commit fixes a bug in the HTTPDigestAuth class where a missing algorithm field in the server challenge caused an error. It now correctly defaults to MD5 when the algorithm is not specified, ensuring digest authentication works as expected.

This commit fixes the `Response.text` property in `requests/models.py` to correctly handle decoding errors by using the `replace` error handler. It also removes a redundant fallback block that attempted to decode the content again, simplifying the logic.

This commit fixes an issue in the `Request` class where the response body was not being properly saved. It ensures the content is stored correctly by adjusting the preload setting and explicitly assigning the response content.

This commit updates the CodeQL security analysis workflow to use version 4.36.0 of the github/codeql-action. The change modifies the codeql-analysis.yml file to ensure the automated security scanning process runs with the latest minor release.

This commit pins the more-itertools dependency to versions below 6.0.0 in the Pipfile to maintain Python 2.7 compatibility for the test suite. It resolves a failure caused by the library dropping support for Python 2.7 in its latest release.

This commit adds a new configuration option, `allow_unicode`, to control how the `Response` class handles character encoding. It replaces a previous warning-based approach with a direct check of this setting in the `Response.__getattr__` method, allowing users to explicitly enable or disable unicode handling.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to use Sphinx cross-referencing syntax for exception classes. It ensures that references to ConnectionError, HTTPError, and Timeout link directly to their full definitions in the requests.exceptions module.

This commit corrects spelling errors and typos across the documentation and source code of the Requests library. It updates text in modules such as `requests.models` and `requests.sessions` to improve clarity and professionalism.

This commit corrects inaccurate HTTP status codes listed in the API documentation. It updates the status code lookup table in the `docs/api.rst` file to reflect the correct values for specific endpoints.

This commit removes the test for the deprecated `requests.settings` context manager from the `RequestsTestSuite`. It reflects the removal of the `settings` feature, which previously allowed users to temporarily override request timeouts.

This commit updates the docstring for the `Session` class in `requests/sessions.py`. It clarifies that the `cert` keyword argument accepts either a string path to a certificate file or a tuple containing the certificate and key.

This commit renames the `cookiejar` parameter to `cookies` in the `request` function and its convenience wrappers like `get` and `post`. It also simplifies null checks for the cookie jar within the `Request` class to use truthiness evaluation.

This commit adds a documentation note explaining that the connection timeout applies to each individual IP address attempt. On servers with multiple addresses, the total wait time can be a multiple of the specified timeout. The change updates the advanced user guide to clarify this behavior.

This commit updates the `PreparedRequest` class in `requests/models.py` to correctly handle bytestring URLs on Python 3. It fixes an issue where byte strings were not properly decoded, ensuring the URL is converted to a standard string format for processing.
This commit adds Chase Sterling to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS.rst file. It updates the project's attribution records to acknowledge the individual's patches and suggestions.
This commit adds the initial README file for the Requests library. It provides a brief description of the project as a simple HTTP module and includes a decorative ASCII art logo.

This release fixes an error that occurred when calling iter_content on a response that had already been fully downloaded. The version is updated to 0.14.0 in the requests module, and the project documentation URL is corrected.

This commit updates the vulnerability disclosure process for the requests library. It replaces direct email and PGP key instructions with a link to open a draft Security Advisory on GitHub. The documentation file now points to the new SECURITY.md file.

This commit updates the contribution instructions in the README to help new contributors find relevant documentation. It adds links to the Contributor's Guide and development philosophy before the step for checking open issues.

The `get_auth_from_url` function in `requests/utils.py` now correctly decodes percent-encoded characters in usernames and passwords extracted from URIs. This fixes a bug where special characters in credentials were not properly unquoted, potentially causing authentication failures.

This commit enables connection pooling by passing the pool configuration through the request and response objects. It updates the `Request` and `Response` classes in `requests/models.py` to carry this configuration, while `Session` in `requests/sessions.py` now correctly passes the pool to the underlying connection.

This commit adds new test cases to the RequestsTestSuite in test_requests.py. It verifies that GET requests correctly handle query parameters and mixed URL parameters, ensuring the library returns the expected status codes.

This commit updates the community FAQ documentation to remove cPython 2.5 from the list of supported versions. It clarifies the current compatibility scope for users checking the project's requirements.

This commit reverts a change in the `Response.iter_lines` method within `requests/models.py` that replaced a standard `while True` loop with `while 1`. It restores the conventional loop syntax to improve code readability and maintainability without altering the underlying behavior.

This commit renames the `yield_responses` parameter to `yield_requests` in the `Session` class to better reflect its behavior. It corrects the logic in `resolve_redirects` and `send` to ensure redirects are handled properly when this flag is set.

This commit ensures that custom hooks are correctly applied when using prepared requests. It adds a new method to the PreparedRequest class that normalizes hook data structures, and updates the Request class to invoke this preparation step. The `head` function in `requests/api.py` now defaults to disallowing redirects. This prevents the library from automatically following redirect responses when a user issues a HEAD request, ensuring the behavior matches standard HTTP expectations.
This commit reverts an accidental change in the test setup for the RequestsTestSuite. It restores the sleep duration in the setUp method to 0.01 seconds, ensuring tests run quickly as intended.

This commit removes the hard dependency on the certifi package from the project's setup configuration. It adds documentation explaining that Requests now optionally uses certifi for CA certificates if installed, allowing users to update trusted certificates without changing code.

This commit updates the project's README to clarify that documentation is available. It changes the final section heading to explicitly mention reading the manual, improving discoverability for users seeking help.

This commit changes the default value of the `decode_unicode` parameter in the `Response.iter_lines` method from `None` to `False`. This adjustment makes the default behavior more explicit and aligns the code with clearer documentation standards.

This commit removes an outdated check for Python 2.6 in the Travis CI configuration, allowing the readme test to run on all supported Python versions. It also eliminates duplicate job definitions that previously repeated the same test and CI steps.

This commit fixes a bug in the `PreparedRequest` class where URL parameters were incorrectly handled during URL preparation. It ensures that the `params` component from the parsed URL is properly ignored to prevent conflicts with the `params` argument passed to `Session.request`.

Updates the actions/checkout dependency from version 4.0.0 to 4.1.0 in the repository's GitHub Actions workflows. This change applies to the codeql-analysis, lint, and run-tests workflow files to ensure the latest minor version is used for checking out code.
This commit updates the copyright string in the documentation configuration file. It removes the HTML link to Kenneth Reitz's website, replacing it with plain text to simplify the copyright notice.
This commit updates the contributing documentation to include "pass" statements in the docstring syntax examples. It clarifies the expected code structure for contributors writing docstrings.
The CI test workflow now runs on Ubuntu 22.04 instead of Ubuntu 18.04. This updates the Linux environment used for automated testing to a newer, supported version.

This commit updates the test environment configuration for the screw project to version 2.4. It removes Python 2.4 from the list of supported test environments, meaning the project no longer validates compatibility with that older Python version.

This commit performs a minor code cleanup in the `Request` class within `requests/models.py`. It adjusts the formatting of the `maxsize` parameter in the `send` method to improve consistency. No functional behavior changes are introduced.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to clarify the library's design philosophy, emphasizing a focus on simple use cases over full HTTP specification support. It also refines the feature list to highlight the ease of handling cookies and authentication with single parameters.

This commit resolves a merge conflict in the `requests/utils.py` module by updating the `unquote_unreserved` function. It replaces the previous decoding logic with a new implementation that uses a public `UNRESERVED_SET` constant to validate and decode percent-encoded characters.

This commit reorganizes the documentation by moving authentication instructions from the quickstart guide into a dedicated user guide file. It updates the main index to link to this new section, improving the structure of the Requests library documentation.
Updates the visual icon for the Flourish extension. This change replaces the existing image file with a new version, altering the appearance of the extension's icon in the user interface.
This commit adds an AUTHORS file to the project to list the development lead and contributors. It documents the individuals responsible for writing and maintaining the Requests library.

Adds a test to verify that request-specific cookies override session cookies without modifying the session state. This ensures the `requests` library correctly handles cookie precedence during HTTP requests.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 0.8.8. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the package's initialization file to reflect the new release.

This commit corrects a spelling error in the advanced user documentation. It fixes the misspelled term "Sesssion" to "Session" within the advanced.rst file, ensuring accurate references to the Session class.

This commit corrects a spelling error in the docstring of the Session class within the requests module. It changes the word "persistience" to "persistence" to accurately describe the class's ability to maintain cookies across requests.

The `get_netrc_auth` function in `requests/utils.py` now stops searching for a netrc file immediately upon finding one, rather than continuing to iterate through all possible locations. This cleanup also simplifies the return logic by explicitly returning `None` when no file is found.

This commit modifies the `prepare_url` method in `requests/models.py` to relax IDNA encoding requirements for hostnames. It now allows hostnames that fail strict IDNA checks to proceed if they contain only ASCII characters and do not start with a wildcard, preventing unnecessary connection errors for valid but non-standard hostnames.
This commit removes a duplicate entry for Den Shabalin from the project's contributor list. It ensures the AUTHORS file accurately reflects unique contributors without redundant names.

Adds support for Carbon Ads in the documentation sidebar by introducing new CSS styles and updating the sidebar templates. This change allows the project to display sponsored content within the documentation interface.

This release fixes a bug in the requests library where GET and HEAD requests incorrectly followed redirects even when the user explicitly disabled this behavior. The update ensures that the follow_redirect=False parameter is respected for these request types.

This commit restructures the "Redirection and History" section in the quickstart documentation. It clarifies that Requests handles redirection by default and provides a clearer explanation of the Response.history property, including its contents and ordering.

This commit updates the cookie test suite to replace advanced assertion methods with basic boolean checks, ensuring compatibility with Python 2.6. It modifies the CookieTests and LWPCookieJarTest classes to remove assertions that are unavailable in older Python versions.

This commit reverts a previous change to the `Response.ok` method in the `requests` library. It restores the behavior where the method returns `True` for any status code below 400, rather than raising exceptions for error statuses.

This commit fixes a bug in the `RequestsCookieJar` class where cookie values containing escaped double quotes were incorrectly stripped of their surrounding quotes. This documentation update clarifies how to access decoded text from HTTP responses by replacing references to binary content with the text property. This commit updates the test suite for request handling to use a standard assertion instead of a method call. It modifies the `test_safe_mode` function within the `RequestsTestSuite` class to verify that the response content is empty.

This commit updates the test suite for the requests module to use standard Python assertions instead of unittest-style methods. It specifically modifies the test for unconsumed session responses to verify connection closure using the new syntax.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` now accepts all optional parameters via keyword arguments instead of a long explicit list. This simplifies the function signature and reduces code duplication while maintaining the same behavior for users making HTTP requests.

This commit fixes a packaging error in the setup.py module by adding a missing import for the os library. This resolves potential installation failures that could occur when the build script attempted to use operating system functions without the required dependency.

This commit fixes a bug in the test suite where header validation checks were not actually asserting equality, allowing failures to go unnoticed. It updates the `test_header_validation` method in `tests/test_requests.py` to properly verify that request headers match the expected values.

This commit updates the version constraints for pytest, pytest-httpbin, and pytest-xdist in the Pipfile to resolve testing infrastructure issues. By pinning these dependencies to specific compatible ranges, it ensures the test suite runs reliably without unexpected failures from newer library versions.

This commit adds support for streaming response content to the `Response` class in `requests/models.py`. This commit adds missing blank lines to the RequestsTestSuite class in test_requests.py. It improves code readability and formatting consistency without altering any functional behavior or test logic.
This commit corrects inconsistent indentation in the package list within setup.py. It replaces a tab character with spaces to ensure uniform formatting for the charade package entry.

This commit updates the project's README to remove a trailing period from the sentence describing the number of dependent repositories. It also removes an empty line that previously followed this statement.

This commit fixes a test failure related to calculating elapsed time for requests. It updates the `Session` class in `requests/sessions.py` to properly pass the `allow_redirects` parameter to the `send` method, ensuring accurate timing data is recorded.

This commit cleans up the project's README by removing trailing whitespace from several lines. It improves the documentation's formatting consistency without altering the visible text or changing any application behavior.

This commit removes the requirements.txt file, which previously listed development dependencies like pytest and Sphinx. This change likely reflects a shift to a different dependency management strategy or the removal of unused development tools.

This commit improves the handling of Unicode characters in URL paths within the `Request` class. It ensures that non-ASCII path segments are properly encoded as UTF-8 before being processed, preventing errors when making requests to URLs containing international characters.

This commit updates the project's FAQ documentation to clarify that Python 2.7 support will continue until pip drops it. It also strongly recommends that users migrate to Python 3.5 or later due to the end of security updates for Python 2.7.

This commit prevents the `PreparedRequest` class from processing URLs with non-standard schemes like `data:`. This commit adds documentation for the `requests.Request` class to the API reference. It ensures the class and its inherited members are properly listed in the generated documentation.

This commit renames the private `_get_connection` method to `get_connection_with_tls_context` within the `HTTPAdapter` class. It updates the method's documentation to clarify that it is intended for subclassing and exposes the TLS context handling logic more explicitly.

This commit removes duplicate and redundant logic from the `get` and `head` functions in `requests/api.py` and the `Request` class in `requests/models.py`. This commit adds a default maximum redirect limit of 30 to the configuration settings. It ensures that the requests library automatically caps the number of redirects a session will follow, preventing potential infinite loops.

This commit updates the Request class in requests/models.py to use the get_environ_proxies utility for setting proxy configurations. It replaces manual environment variable checks with a centralized function, ensuring consistent handling of HTTP and HTTPS proxy settings.

This commit removes the Azure Pipelines configuration files for Linux and Windows, effectively disabling automated continuous integration builds. It reverts a previous change that had introduced these pipeline templates, returning the project to its prior state without this specific CI setup.

This commit adds the chardet2 module to the requests package, providing a comprehensive suite of tools for automatic character encoding detection. It includes various probers and distribution analysis classes to identify specific character sets like Big5, EUC, and GB2312.

This commit simplifies the donation section in the documentation sidebar by removing the "Donate" heading and introductory text. It leaves only the "Buy Requests Pro" button in the sidebarintro and sidebarlogo templates.
This commit adds the wheel package to the development requirements. It ensures the necessary tooling is available for building Python distribution packages during development.
This commit adds takluyver to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS.rst file. It updates the project's credit list to acknowledge the individual's patches and suggestions.

This commit corrects the heading hierarchy in the advanced user documentation. It updates the section title for specific SSL versions to use the proper subheading style, ensuring the document structure is consistent.

This commit fixes a broken hyperlink in the project documentation. It corrects the formatting of the link to the Requests 3.0 support page in the main index file. Users will now see a properly formatted link instead of broken text.

This commit prevents infinite redirect loops in the `Session.send` method of the `requests` library. It stops the client from endlessly cycling between URLs when a server responds with circular 301 redirects, ensuring the request terminates instead of hanging.

This commit updates the project's dependency requirements to allow urllib3 version 1.23. It modifies the setup.py file to relax the upper version limit, enabling users to install the newer library version without conflicts.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the advanced user documentation for the requests library. It corrects the formatting of a code block in the `docs/user/advanced.rst` file to ensure proper rendering of the SSL certificate workaround instructions.
This commit updates the project's README documentation. It swaps the position of the license image and the decorative emoji line to adjust the visual layout of the page.

This commit restores the missing documentation for the `Session.request` method in the `requests` library. It ensures that users can see the method's description and parameter details when viewing the API reference.

This commit updates the documentation index to correct the formatting of the Python version recommendation. It adjusts the emphasis on "Python 3" and "highly" to improve readability in the user-facing warning message.

This commit adds a test to verify that copying a RequestsCookieJar correctly preserves a custom cookie policy. It ensures that the copied jar retains the specific policy class assigned to the original, preventing potential data loss during duplication.

The `proxy_bypass_registry` function in `requests/utils.py` now normalizes the `ProxyEnable` registry value to an integer, preventing type mismatches on Windows. This ensures proxy bypass logic works correctly regardless of whether the registry stores the value as a string or a number.

This commit updates the setup.py file to correctly handle the removal of the bundled oauthlib package. It fixes a version check to use is_py3 instead of is_py2, ensuring the package list is properly configured for Python 3 environments.

This commit updates the bundled charade library within the requests package to improve character encoding detection. It modifies the detect function and various prober classes to enhance the accuracy of identifying text encodings.

This commit updates the URL preparation tests to normalize percent-encoded bytes before comparing results. It ensures that equivalent encodings with different letter cases are treated as identical, preventing false failures in the TestPreparingURLs module.
The CI workflow no longer runs tests on older macOS runners for Python 3.8 and 3.9. This removes the previous workaround that pinned those versions to the macos-13 image, simplifying the test matrix.

This commit updates the installation documentation to fix a broken link. It corrects the URL for the section comparing pip to easy_install, ensuring users can access the correct guidance on why easy_install is discouraged.
This commit updates the build number for the requests package. It increments the internal build identifier in the `__init__.py` module to reflect a new release version.

This commit fixes a bug in the requests package where the chardet library was incorrectly mapped to a single module instead of its full namespace. The change in the packages module ensures that every chardet submodule is properly aliased under requests.packages.chardet, preserving the correct package structure.

This commit adds new issue templates for bug reports, feature requests, and help requests to the GitHub repository. It standardizes the information users must provide when submitting issues, such as reproduction steps and system details.

This change prevents the OAuth1 authentication class from overwriting an existing Content-Type header when the request body is form-encoded. Previously, the header was always set, which could conflict with user-specified types. Now, it only applies the default if no content type is already present.

This commit updates the docstring for the HTTPAdapter class in the requests library. It clarifies how to achieve granular control over request retry conditions by suggesting the use of urllib3's Retry class.

This commit removes the static list of translated documentation links from the sidebar template. Users will no longer see direct links to French, German, Japanese, or Chinese versions of the documentation in the sidebar.

This commit fixes a broken link in the project's README. The AUTHORS link previously pointed to a non-existent develop branch, causing a 404 error for users. It now correctly references the master branch.

This commit replaces the single connection reuse mechanism with a connection pool system to improve performance. It updates the `request` function, `Request` class, and `Session` class to accept and manage a pool manager instead of a single connection.

This commit updates the installation guide to point to the correct Pipenv website. It fixes a broken link in the documentation that previously directed users to an outdated URL. The change is located in the user installation documentation file.

This commit adds Python 3.8 to the Appveyor continuous integration configuration. It ensures the project's test suite runs against the new Python version, verifying compatibility for users upgrading to 3.8.

This commit fixes an issue in the `Session.send` method where requests created by a different library instance were incorrectly rejected. It changes the validation logic to check for unprepared `Request` objects instead of verifying the `PreparedRequest` type, ensuring valid requests are sent while still providing a clear error for invalid inputs.

This commit updates the release notes for version 2.6.1 to reflect the removal of the VendorAlias import machinery. It clarifies that the previous fix for unvendored dependencies in PyInstaller executables is no longer applicable.
This commit updates the project's history log to document the addition of the OPTION method. It records this new feature in the release notes for user awareness.
This commit releases version 2.22.0 of the requests library. It updates the version number in the package metadata and refreshes the dependency lock file to reflect the new release.

This commit updates the release history documentation to properly format the shell command for installing the SOCKS proxy dependency. It ensures the installation instruction is displayed as code in the rendered README, improving readability for users.

This commit updates the project's changelog to document version 0.4.0. It highlights new features including a response history list for tracking redirects, case-insensitive header dictionaries, and support for Unicode URLs.

The Makefile now ensures that bundled dependencies like urllib3 and chardet are checked out at their latest tagged release rather than the default branch. This change guarantees that the build process uses stable, versioned code for these packages.

This commit modifies the setup.py script to prevent the PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE environment variable from being set during the package build process. Instead of preserving the variable's original value, the script now explicitly removes it from the environment, ensuring a consistent build state.

This commit updates the requests-logo.ai file by converting font layers to curves. This change ensures the logo renders consistently across different systems without relying on specific font installations.
This commit enables the pip cache in the Travis CI configuration to speed up build times by reusing installed Python packages. The change modifies the .travis.yml file to add the cache directive.

This commit updates the idna library to version 2.2.0 by refactoring the uts46data module. It replaces a single large data tuple with multiple lazy-loading functions to improve memory efficiency during import.

The `Request` class in `requests/core.py` now supports basic GET requests by initializing parameters and data attributes. The `send` method executes the request using `urllib` and stores the response, preventing duplicate sends unless explicitly overridden.

This commit extends the `RequestEncodingMixin` in `requests/models.py` to support custom headers for individual files in multipart POST requests. Users can now pass a four-tuple in the `files` argument, where the final element is a dictionary of extra headers to include for that specific file.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar templates to change the wording of the donation prompt. It replaces references to purchasing a copy with a request for financial support and renames the button to "Requests Pro."

This commit removes the `test_vendor_aliases` test and updates `test_urllib3_retries` in `tests/test_requests.py` to import `Retry` directly from `urllib3` instead of the deprecated `requests.packages` namespace. These changes clean up the test suite by eliminating outdated checks for removed vendor aliases.

This commit simplifies the tox configuration by removing the explicit installation of the socks extra. Since Tox installs the package by default and PySocks is already listed in test requirements, this redundant step is no longer necessary.

This commit removes a redundant comment from the documentation configuration file. It cleans up the codebase by eliminating a duplicate line in the HTML static path settings. No functional behavior is changed.

The `super_len` function in `requests/utils.py` now calculates the length of file-like objects by seeking to the end instead of calling `getvalue`. This change improves compatibility with objects like `BytesIO` that lack a `getvalue` method while preserving the original read position.
This commit updates the project's release history file to prepare for a new version. It adds a new development section with placeholders for upcoming improvements and bug fixes.
This commit updates the project's README documentation. It likely clarifies usage instructions or project details for users. No specific code logic or functional behavior is altered.

This commit modifies the `HTTPAdapter` class in `requests/adapters.py` to correctly handle certificate verification for HTTPS requests. It ensures that a default CA bundle path is used when verification is enabled but no specific certificate location is provided, fixing potential issues with SSL verification behavior.

This commit removes hook dispatch logic from the top-level request loop in the Session class and the async send function. It moves these operations to ensure hooks are executed at the correct stages of the request lifecycle, preventing potential issues with hook execution order.

This commit removes the outdated build status badge from the project's README. The change simplifies the documentation by eliminating a reference to a CI service that is no longer relevant or useful to users.

This commit adds a test to verify that `Session.get_adapter()` performs case-insensitive prefix matching when selecting an HTTP adapter. It ensures that URLs with mixed-case schemes or hosts correctly resolve to the mounted adapter, confirming the expected behavior of the `requests` library.
This commit adds PayPal to the list of testimonials in the project documentation. It also updates the local virtual environment configuration file to point to a specific path.
Adds a decorative image to the authentication documentation page. This change updates the user-facing guide by including a visual element at the top of the authentication section.
This commit removes a duplicate contributor entry from the project's author list. It cleans up the AUTHORS.rst file by deleting a redundant line for a specific contributor.

This commit updates the documentation for the project's community section. It changes the heading in the sponsors file from "Corporate Sponsors" to "Community Sponsors" to better reflect the nature of the contributors.

This commit adds a new `coverage` target to the Makefile, allowing developers to run tests with code coverage reporting. It also updates the project requirements to include the `pytest-cov` dependency and credits a new contributor.

This documentation update adds a new section noting that Requests is built into the Python for iOS runtime. It also replaces outdated OAuth library references with a mention of HTTPie in the community modules list.

This commit fixes a typo in the advanced user documentation that prevented a cross-reference link to the Session API from rendering correctly. The change updates the reference syntax in the advanced.rst file to ensure users can navigate to the session documentation.

This commit updates the `prepare_url` method in the `PreparedRequest` class to handle missing network locations more strictly. It now raises an `InvalidURL` error if a URL lacks a network location, rather than silently proceeding with an incomplete address.
This commit updates the README documentation to include a new content attribute in the example configuration. It clarifies the available options for users setting up the project.

This commit updates the import of SimpleCookie in requests/utils.py to source it from the compatibility module instead of the standard library. This ensures consistent cookie handling across different Python versions.

This commit fixes a typo in the status code title validation logic within the requests module. It corrects a misspelled method call and simplifies the condition to properly check for backslash and forward slash prefixes.

This commit adds a test to the RequestsTestSuite that verifies the data received by the httpbin service. It ensures that when a file is posted, the server correctly parses and returns the file content as expected.
This commit updates the copyright year in the requests package's initialization file from 2015 to 2016. It is a metadata change that does not affect the library's functionality or user behavior.

This commit adds a test to verify that using a Unicode string for the HTTP method in a Request object works correctly. It ensures the prepared request method is converted to a standard string and that the request completes successfully.

This commit updates the project's history file to explicitly mark the removal of the `decode_unicode` function and the change to bytes-only `Response.content` as backwards incompatible. It also corrects the punctuation for the entry regarding the default ISO-8859-1 encoding for text subtypes.

The `Session.send` method in `requests/sessions.py` now raises a `ValueError` if a user attempts to send an unprepared `Request` object. This prevents accidental errors by ensuring only `PreparedRequest` instances are processed, improving the library's robustness against common usage mistakes.

This commit removes a redundant instruction line from the GitHub issue template. It simplifies the user-facing guidance for reporting issues by deleting the text that told users to run a specific command.
This commit fixes a broken hyperlink in the advanced user documentation. It updates the URL for the essay on Python HTTP adapters to point to the correct, working location.

This commit updates all project URLs to use the secure HTTPS protocol instead of HTTP. It affects documentation, configuration files, and core modules like `requests/sessions.py` and `requests/utils.py` to ensure links are secure.

This commit updates the project's README to clarify that the library automatically handles form-encoding for PUT and POST requests. It also highlights the new capability to send JSON data directly, removing the need for manual encoding.

This commit disables the automatic monkey patching for eventlet and gevent in the requests core module. It prevents the library from altering global socket behavior, which could cause unexpected side effects in applications that manage their own concurrency.

This commit updates the `requests/core.py` module to import the `session` object from the `sessions` package. This change makes the session functionality available at the root package level, allowing users to access it directly without navigating through submodules.

This commit fixes a bug in the `resolve_redirects` method of the `SessionRedirectMixin` class where 303 See Other responses were not correctly identified. The issue was caused by using the `is` operator instead of `==` for status code comparison, which prevented proper redirect handling for POST requests.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to include an alphabetized list of request attributes and their descriptions. It clarifies the available options for configuring requests, such as redirect behavior, authentication, and SSL certificates, within the docs/user/advanced.rst file.
Updates the CodeQL security analysis workflow to use version 3.23.0 of the github/codeql-action. This minor version bump refreshes the static analysis tools used in the CI pipeline.

This commit removes the unit test for the max_retries parameter from the RequestsTestCase in test_requests.py. It reverts a previous change that added a test to verify that retry settings are correctly passed to the underlying HTTP connection pool.

This release updates the requests library to version 0.13.7, introducing support for key-value lists and improving Digest Authentication. It also fixes proxy exclusion issues, clarifies UnicodeError exceptions, and automatically casts URLs to strings.

Adds a test to verify that relative redirects are correctly tracked in the response history. This ensures the requests library accurately records the number of intermediate steps when following relative URLs.

This commit updates the Pipfile to use a functional PyPI endpoint, resolving installation failures caused by an invalid source URL. It also simplifies the Makefile by removing specific version exclusions from the pipenv installation command.

This commit modifies the `PreparedRequest` class in `requests/models.py` to skip URL validation for non-HTTP schemes. It prevents errors when using custom protocols like `data:` or `file:` by bypassing standard URL preparation logic.

This commit fixes a bug in the `get_netrc_auth` function within `requests/utils.py` where the function would crash if no network credentials were found for a given URL. It now safely returns `None` when the netrc lookup yields no result, preventing an error during authentication.

This commit updates the Requests library to support Python 3 by replacing deprecated imports and ensuring proper byte encoding for authentication headers. It modifies the HTTPBasicAuth class and related utilities to handle string-to-byte conversions correctly, preventing errors when generating basic auth credentials.

This commit adds installation instructions for gevent to the user documentation, clarifying the need for the libevent dependency on various operating systems. It also updates the advanced guide to link to these new installation steps.
This commit updates the project's README documentation. It adds a small HTML spacer element to adjust the page layout. No functional code or user-facing behavior is changed.

This commit simplifies the logic in the `Response.text` property within `requests/models.py`. It moves the empty content check outside the exception handling block, ensuring that empty responses return an empty string without attempting to decode content.

This commit updates the sidebar documentation template to change the Certifi project description from "Recommended CA Bundle" to "Best CA Bundle." It also replaces a horizontal rule with an empty paragraph tag to adjust the layout spacing.

This commit reverts a previous fix that attempted to preserve read errors when accessing the response content multiple times. It restores the original behavior in the `Response` class where errors are raised immediately during content iteration rather than being stored for later retrieval.

This commit fixes a crash in the `Response.text` property of the `requests` library that occurred when the response encoding was `None`. It now catches the resulting `TypeError` and attempts to decode the content without specifying an encoding, preventing the application from failing.

This commit updates the README to correct the URL for the pipenv tool. It changes the link from the old domain to the new official site, ensuring users are directed to the correct resource for installing the requests module.

This commit updates the Ruff linter version in the pre-commit configuration from 0.15.20 to 0.15.21. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the Ruff pre-commit hook for code quality checks.

This commit updates the Requests documentation to list Linode as a patron sponsor. It replaces the placeholder text indicating no current sponsors with a description of Linode's cloud hosting services.
This commit updates the FAQ documentation to confirm that keep-alive support is now available. It changes the response in the community FAQ from a pending status to a definitive affirmative.

Adds a new SVG logo file for the requests project. This version converts all text fonts to curves, ensuring the logo renders consistently across different systems without requiring specific font installations.

This commit updates the project's contributor list by adding Daniel Hengeveld to the "Patches and Suggestions" section. It ensures the AUTHORS file accurately reflects all individuals who have contributed to the codebase.

This commit updates the test suite for the requests module to ensure header order is correctly preserved. It fixes a test failure by converting the header items to a list before comparison, preventing issues with iterator consumption.

This commit fixes an invalid escape sequence warning in the module docstring of `requests/status_codes.py`. It changes the docstring to a raw string to prevent Python from interpreting backslashes as escape characters.
This commit updates the project documentation by repositioning the download count badge higher on the page. It also removes the code coverage badge from the main index file.

This commit enables the maximum redirect limit in the SessionMixin.resolve_redirects method. It fixes a bug where the application would ignore the configured limit and potentially loop indefinitely, now correctly raising a TooManyRedirects exception when the limit is exceeded.

This commit adds Megan Emurayama to the project's author list. It also modifies the Request class in requests/core.py to set a default socket timeout and adjust how request data is encoded and stored.

This commit clarifies the documentation for the `json` parameter in the quickstart guide. It explains that users can pass a dictionary directly for automatic encoding, rather than manually encoding the data themselves.

The Session class no longer exposes the timeout attribute in its list of configurable properties. This change removes an extraneous setting that users can no longer modify directly on the session object.

This commit fixes an issue in the HTTPAdapter where custom SSL contexts passed via pool manager arguments were ignored when verify was set to true. It ensures the default SSL context is only used if no custom context is already configured in the pool manager.

This commit updates the project's README documentation to correct grammatical errors and standardize terminology. It changes the subject from "Requests" to "Requests allows" and updates "api" to "API" for consistency.

This commit fixes test failures on platforms like Alpha and RISC-V Linux where the test server could not accept connections. It changes the `Server` class in `tests/testserver/server.py` to use a non-zero backlog value for the `listen` call, ensuring the socket can properly handle incoming connections.

This commit updates the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to align redirect behavior with standard browser practices. It changes the HTTP method to GET for 303 responses and for 301 or 302 responses when the original request was a POST and strict mode is disabled.

This commit updates the version number to 2.13.0 in the requests module and adds release notes to the history file. It documents that the idna library is now loaded only when necessary to save memory, and notes updates to bundled urllib3 and idna versions.

This commit removes the sidebar introduction template, eliminating the Twitter follow button, mailing list link, and list of other projects from the documentation sidebar. The change affects the `sidebarintro.html` file.
This commit updates the release date for version 2.3.0 in the project history. It also corrects a typo in the changelog description regarding how dictionaries are displayed as strings.

Fixes a documentation typo in the advanced user guide that incorrectly referenced the Request object's content property. The text now correctly points to the Response object's content property for manual encoding adjustments.

This commit updates the documentation to clarify that requests do not time out by default unless a timeout value is explicitly set. It modifies the advanced and quickstart guides to ensure users understand this behavior. The change also adds new contributors to the project's author list.

This commit enables the `Request` class in `requests/core.py` to include form data alongside file uploads. Previously, sending data with files was not supported, but now the data is merged into the file payload during the `send` method.

This release reverts the SSLContext caching feature introduced in version 2.32.0, which caused various issues across different use cases. The change updates the version number in the `requests` module to 2.32.5 and documents the removal in the project history.

This commit moves the `store_cookies` setting from a separate argument into the main configuration dictionary for the `requests` library. Users can now control cookie persistence by setting the `store_cookies` key in the `config` dict passed to `Session` or `request` methods, rather than using a dedicated parameter.

This commit adds a test to verify that requests correctly set cookies when the Host header is provided as a bytestring. It ensures the session handles this input type without failing during domain lookup. The change is located in the TestRequests class within the test suite.

The `check_compatibility` function in the `requests` module now limits the urllib3 version string to three components. This prevents compatibility checks from failing when urllib3 reports a version with more than three numeric parts.
This commit updates the documentation to reflect that the library now supports Python 3.4. It modifies the supported version range in the main index file to include the new release.

This commit removes trailing whitespace from several files within the documentation directory. It cleans up formatting in the manifest, theme configuration, and user guide files to improve code hygiene.

This release updates the Requests library to version 1.0.1, primarily addressing a proxy configuration issue within the HTTPAdapter module. Users relying on proxy settings will now experience corrected behavior for HTTP requests.

This commit updates the actions/checkout dependency from version 4.2.0 to 5.0.0 across multiple GitHub workflow files. It ensures the repository uses the latest major version of the checkout action for its CI/CD pipelines.

This commit updates the `requests` library to support chardet version 7. It raises the upper version limit in the dependency configuration and the `check_compatibility` function, preventing compatibility errors when using the newer chardet release.

This commit reverts a previous change that attempted to fix a TypeError in the HTTPConnectionPool class. It restores the original timeout handling logic in the _raise_timeout method, removing the specific error message checks that were added to handle Python 2.7 compatibility issues.

This commit fixes an issue where the JSON parameter was not passed to the body preparation logic, potentially causing incorrect content types. It updates the `PreparedRequest` class to handle JSON data properly and corrects a test assertion to check the request headers.
The CodeQL security analysis workflow now targets the main branch instead of the master branch. This ensures automated code scanning runs on the correct default branch for the repository.

This commit updates the style guide documentation to improve the presentation of docstring examples. It adjusts the formatting of the sample text in the contributing guide to ensure it displays correctly.

This commit updates the project's release history to document security fixes. It notes that the library no longer exposes sensitive authorization headers when a request is redirected, addressing two specific vulnerabilities.

This release adds support for merging dictionary arguments in the Session class within the requests core module. It also finalizes the version number and updates the project history to document the new offline test suite and session functionality.

This commit ensures that the response URL is decoded into a unicode string rather than remaining a byte string. It modifies the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to apply UTF-8 decoding when building the response object.

This commit adds support for URL encoding with plus signs by importing quote_plus and unquote_plus in the compatibility layer. It updates the imports in requests/compat.py and re-exports them in requests/utils.py to make these functions available to the rest of the library.

This commit updates the HTTP 425 status code definition in the `requests` library's `status_codes` module. It adds the "too_early" alias to the existing names, ensuring the status code is correctly identified by all its standard variations.

This commit adds a test to verify that requests sessions correctly handle redirects when danger mode is enabled. It ensures the session does not crash or fail unexpectedly during a multi-step redirect sequence. The test is added to the RequestsTestSuite in the test_requests module.
This commit updates the project's author list by adding Matt Kohl to the contributors section. It includes his name and a link to his GitHub profile in the AUTHORS.rst file.

This commit corrects a typo in the project's README file, changing "Rquests" to "Requests" in the introductory description. It ensures the library name is spelled correctly for users reading the documentation.

This commit reverts a previous change that converted the font layer in the requests-logo.ai file to curves. It restores the original vector graphics structure and metadata dates, ensuring the logo file matches its prior state.
This commit removes the documentation for the asynchronous API module, indicating that async support has been dropped. It also adds documentation for the `PreparedRequest` class to the API reference.
This commit updates the project's README documentation by adding an image link to the Flourish logo. It does not alter any code logic or user-facing behavior.

This commit adjusts the mobile documentation theme to improve layout responsiveness. It changes the width of the main document container from a fixed percentage to auto, allowing it to adapt better to smaller screens.

This commit updates the changelog for version 2.9.1, documenting fixes for a regression that prevented sending binary strings as request bodies in Python 3. It also notes corrections to cookie expiration date calculations that failed in specific locales.

This commit fixes an issue in the `request` function within `requests/core.py` where passing both `data` and `params` arguments caused the `params` to be ignored. The `Settings` class in `requests/config.py` now supports a `verbose` attribute. This change enables users to configure verbose output behavior through the settings object.
This commit reverts the version number in the requests package from 0.10.3 back to 0.10.2. It updates the `__version__` attribute in the `requests/__init__.py` module to reflect this change.

This commit updates the project history to document new features and breaking changes. It highlights automatic unicode decoding, a new decode_unicode setting, and the removal of read and close methods. It also introduces a new r.fo interface for advanced response usage.

This commit updates the Travis CI badge and link in the README to use the correct, non-secure URL. It fixes a broken link that previously redirected to an invalid address and removes the unnecessary "secure" prefix from the image source.

This commit refactors the Session class in requests/sessions.py by extracting environment variable handling into a new merge_environment_settings method. It separates the logic for applying proxy and certificate settings from the main request method, improving code organization.

This commit updates the TravisCI configuration to align with the platform's required infrastructure migration. It removes the deprecated `sudo` directive from the `.travis.yml` file, ensuring the build environment remains compatible with the new Linux infrastructure.

This commit removes proxy information from PreparedRequests, as proxy settings are now handled exclusively by the session. The change updates the imports in the requests/models.py module to include urldefrag, reflecting the removal of proxy-related logic from the request preparation process.

This commit updates the test suite to run correctly on Python 3 by fixing import paths and handling byte strings. It modifies the test server and related test cases to ensure socket operations use bytes instead of text, resolving compatibility issues.

This commit updates the project history to document the introduction of a new unicode decoding system. It notes that this feature relies on the overridable `Response.encoding` attribute to handle text decoding.

This commit fixes an issue where the Request class in requests/models.py did not correctly identify HTTP redirect status codes. It introduces a constant for valid redirect statuses and updates the response building logic to set the redirect flag appropriately.

This commit adds a test to verify that the test server's context manager properly closes the server upon exit. It ensures that attempting to connect to the server after the context block ends raises a socket error, confirming the port is no longer active.

This commit refactors the `get_auth_from_url` function in `requests/utils.py` to improve code readability and consistency. It consolidates the logic for extracting authentication credentials from a URL, ensuring a single return path for the resulting tuple.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Response.raise_for_status` method within the `requests` library. Previously, the method would always raise an `HTTPError` even when no error message was present. Now, it only raises the exception if an error message is actually defined.

This commit corrects a typo in the quickstart documentation where the cookie jar example incorrectly used the "site" parameter instead of "domain." It ensures the documentation accurately reflects the correct API usage for setting cookies.

This commit removes the `decode_gzip` and `unicode_from_html` functions from the `requests/utils.py` module. These utilities were considered unnecessary or incorrect, so their removal cleans up the codebase without altering the library's core request handling behavior.

This commit changes the SSL certificate bundle selection logic in the `requests` library to prioritize the `certifi` package over the operating system's default bundle. This commit adds ASCII art to the top of the core module and removes trailing whitespace from the exceptions module. It does not change any functional behavior or fix bugs, serving only as a cosmetic update to the codebase.

This commit reverts a previous update to the certificate bundle in the requests library. It restores the original cacert.pem file, ensuring that the library uses the previously trusted set of root certificates for secure connections.

This commit adds a label to the SOCKS heading in the advanced user documentation. It enables other documentation pages to link to this section using intersphinx references instead of requiring full URLs.

This commit separates the preparation of requests from the sending process in the requests library. It adds a copy method to the Request class and an update_request method to the Session class to merge session settings into a request object.
