This commit updates the advanced user documentation to explicitly include the "http://" scheme in proxy URL examples. It clarifies that users must provide a scheme for proxy configurations to avoid potential connection issues, while maintaining backward compatibility for existing code.

This commit adds documentation to the advanced usage guide explaining Server Name Indication (SNI) and its role in SSL virtual hosting. It details how the Requests library enables SNI support on Python 2 by requiring specific third-party packages, such as pyOpenSSL and ndg-httpsclient.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to version 1.20.0, bringing in the latest bug fixes and features for HTTP connection handling. It also corrects the Makefile to ensure the library is pulled from the release branch, preventing version mismatches during the build process.

This commit adds a backport of the OrderedDict class to the urllib3 package, ensuring dictionary insertion order is preserved on older Python versions. It provides a complete implementation of the OrderedDict interface, including methods for iteration, updating, and view operations.

This commit updates the HTTPAdapter.send method to use the new urllib3 Timeout class for managing connection and read limits. It distinguishes between streaming and non-streaming requests, applying read timeouts only when the response is not streamed.

The `send` function in `requests/async.py` now correctly utilizes the provided connection pool to manage concurrency, rather than ignoring it. The `map` function was updated to spawn individual request jobs directly, ensuring that asynchronous requests are properly executed and returned.

This commit updates the project's test dependency from py.test to pytest and removes the use of pip mirrors in the CI configuration. It also clarifies the docstring for the Request.prepare method to specify that it constructs a request for transmission.
This commit adds Justin Murphy to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS file. It updates the project's credit list to acknowledge his patches and suggestions.

This commit updates the Travis CI configuration to install development dependencies, ensuring testing tools are available during the build. It also adds a requirements.txt file to explicitly pin the versions of all project dependencies.
This commit updates the project's README documentation. It modifies the HTML structure by adding an extra empty paragraph tag to adjust the page layout.

This commit updates the GitHub issue template to provide a clearer structure for reporting URI-related problems. It adds a dedicated section for system information and a code block for pasting command output, replacing the previous free-form text.

This commit removes unnecessary executable permissions from documentation and test files, including `AUTHORS.rst` and `requests/sessions.py`. It also strips the shebang line from `tests/test_requests.py` to ensure these files are treated as standard data rather than scripts.

This commit ensures the requirements.txt file is included when building the package distribution. It fixes an issue where the dependency list was missing from the source archive, potentially causing installation problems for users. The change modifies the MANIFEST.in configuration file.

This commit fixes a bug in the `requests` library where closing a response did not return the underlying connection to the pool. This prevented users with blocking connection pools from reusing connections efficiently. The fix modifies the `Response.close` method to ensure the connection is properly released after being closed.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Response.iter_content` method where a broad exception handler masked errors unrelated to missing stream attributes. It replaces the catch-all logic with a specific check for the `stream` attribute, ensuring that only the intended urllib3 case is handled.
This commit fixes a minor typo in the project's README documentation. It removes a redundant comma from the installation success message to improve readability.
This commit updates the Pipfile.lock to align with current dependency constraints. It removes outdated host environment markers and updates package hashes to ensure consistent installation behavior.
This commit corrects malformed documentation links in the authentication and quickstart guides. It updates references to the AuthBase and Request classes to ensure they resolve correctly for users.
Adds a test to the RequestsTestSuite that verifies the behavior of cached responses. It checks that content is correctly retrieved when making requests with both prefetching disabled and enabled.
This commit updates the project's contributor list by adding Rolando Espinoza La fuente to the authors file. It ensures the new contributor is properly credited in the documentation.

This commit updates the changelog for version 2.11.0, documenting new support for the ALL_PROXY environment variable and stricter header validation to prevent smuggling. It also lists bug fixes for JSON decoding errors, NO_PROXY handling, and OpenSSL issues.

This commit cleans up linting warnings in the test suite and build configuration to improve the development experience. It adjusts the Makefile to run tests with verbose output and refactors the test_requests.py module to resolve pyflakes issues.

This commit updates tests in the test_requests.py module to correctly verify that response content is not consumed during prefetch operations. It replaces reliance on a previous crash behavior with explicit assertions that the content remains unconsumed, ensuring the tests accurately cover the intended API behavior.
This release updates the authentication system to use simpler callable objects and adds a new session parameter to API methods. It also improves logging by displaying the full URL during requests.

Adds a `reason` property to the `Response` class in the `requests` module. This allows users to access the HTTP reason phrase associated with a response, such as "OK" or "Not Found," directly from the response object.

This commit updates the documentation for the `request` function in the `requests` module. It explicitly lists the valid HTTP methods, such as GET and POST, that users can pass as the method argument.
This commit updates the Python setup action in the test workflow from version 2.3.4 to 4.7.0. It ensures the CI environment uses a more recent and supported version of the setup tool.

This commit adds the HTTPAdapter class to the API documentation, making its methods and parameters visible to users. It also expands the class docstring in requests/adapters.py to explain its role in handling HTTP requests and its configuration options.

This commit updates the Request class in requests/models.py to use symbolic status code constants instead of hardcoded numeric values for redirect handling. It also replaces a fixed redirect limit with a configurable setting, allowing users to adjust the maximum number of redirects permitted.

This commit updates the documentation's custom stylesheet to ensure select elements always span the full width of their container. It adds a CSS override to the `custom.css` file to prevent other styles from restricting the width.

This commit updates the documentation to replace broken links pointing to the old kenreitz.org domain with valid URLs on kennethreitz.org. It corrects references in the copyright notice, contributing guidelines, and advanced user guide to ensure users can access the intended external resources.

This commit adds the required .readthedocs.yaml configuration file to resolve documentation build failures caused by a missing default config. It specifies the build environment, Python version, and Sphinx settings for the project.
This commit updates the project's README to include a badge displaying the supported Python versions. The badge links directly to the package's PyPI page for easy access.

This commit updates comments in the `SessionRedirectMixin` class within `requests/sessions.py` to follow standard spacing and sentence case conventions. It improves code readability by ensuring consistent formatting for inline documentation.

This commit adds a new optional dependency group named "betterssl" to the project's setup configuration. It allows users to install additional SSL-related libraries, including pyOpenSSL, ndg-httpsclient, and pyasn1, by specifying this extra during installation.

This commit removes the unnecessary setter for the `content` property in the `Response` class within `requests/models.py`. It eliminates a workaround for Python 2.5 compatibility, simplifying the code without changing user-facing behavior.

This commit corrects the documentation for the proxies parameter in the HTTPAdapter class and the select_proxy function. It clarifies that the dictionary can map schemes or combinations of schemes and hosts to proxy URLs, improving accuracy for users configuring proxy settings.

Adds GSSAPI/Kerberos authentication support to the requests library via the new HTTPKerberosAuth class in requests/auth.py. This enables users to authenticate with Kerberos-protected servers, though the implementation currently has known issues with handling redirects and 403 responses.

This commit ensures that the `sent` attribute of a `Request` object is set to `True` after the request is successfully sent. This change allows users to reliably check the `sent` flag to determine if a request has been dispatched.
This commit removes the module docstring and encoding declaration from the `requests/patches.py` file. It cleans up the file header without altering any functional behavior or user-facing features.

This commit reorganizes the Requests documentation by moving the netrc authentication section under the Basic Auth heading. It clarifies that netrc credentials are used to send requests with HTTP Basic Auth when no explicit authentication method is provided.

This commit restores Python 3.2 compatibility in the test suite by replacing removed Unicode literal syntax with a helper function. The `u` function in `test_requests.py` ensures tests run correctly across Python 2 and 3 versions.

This commit updates the CaseInsensitiveDict class in requests/structures.py to use the OrderedDict from the compatibility module instead of the standard library version. This ensures consistent behavior across different Python versions, particularly regarding header order preservation.

This commit updates the project's README documentation to correct a typo in a URL example and clarify the API usage. It specifies that the `status_code` attribute is accessed via the `response` object rather than directly on the main object.

This commit fixes an error that occurred when loading the default certificate bundle from a zip archive. It introduces a new utility function, `extract_zipped_paths`, to handle this extraction process. The `HTTPAdapter` class is updated to use this new functionality during certificate verification.

This commit adds documentation to the `Response` class in `requests/models.py`. It clarifies that when `decode_unicode` is enabled, the response content is decoded using the best available encoding. This helps users understand how text content is processed.

This commit renames internal helper functions within the HTTPDigestAuth class in requests/auth.py to explicitly indicate the hashing algorithm used. It replaces the generic name h with md5_utf8 and sha_utf8, and updates the variable H to hash_utf8 for improved code clarity.
This commit corrects a grammatical error in the quickstart documentation. It clarifies that the Requests library performs automatic location redirection for all HTTP verbs except HEAD.

This commit moves exception classes from the models module to a new dedicated exceptions module. It updates the core module to import these exceptions from their new location, ensuring consistent error handling across the library.

This commit updates the BaseSSLError class in the urllib3 connection pool module to inherit from Exception instead of the deprecated BaseException. This change ensures the custom SSL error class follows standard Python exception hierarchy conventions.

This commit moves the request timing logic from the HTTPAdapter to the Session class. It ensures that the elapsed time recorded in the response object is calculated within the Session.send method, aligning with a specific design request.

This commit updates the documentation for the Request class in the requests module. It corrects the description of the querystring data parameter to accurately state that it accepts a dictionary, rather than a dictionary or byte.

This commit updates the documentation for the `head` function in the `requests` module. It clarifies that the `allow_redirects` parameter defaults to `False` for HEAD requests, which differs from the standard behavior of other request methods.

This commit simplifies the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` by replacing complex reference tricks with direct object assignments when linking requests and responses. It also corrects the `do_block` flag in the `send` method to prevent unintended blocking behavior during streaming.

This commit fixes a serialization error in the `requests` library's `Session` class when caching session objects. It addresses the issue where the thread-safe `RecentlyUsedContainers` object could not be pickled directly. The fix converts the redirect cache to a dictionary during serialization and restores it upon deserialization.
This commit adds a new contributor to the project's author list. It updates the AUTHORS.rst file to include Park Ilsu under the "Patches and Suggestions" section.

This commit updates the project documentation to reflect that Python 3.7 is now officially supported. It modifies the README, FAQ, and development todo files to include Python 3.7 in the list of compatible versions.

This commit updates the project documentation to reflect that the library has surpassed one million downloads from PyPI. The change modifies the download count statistic in the testimonials section of the main index file.

This commit renames the imported Timeout class to TimeoutSauce within the HTTPAdapter.send method. This change prevents a naming conflict with the standard library's Timeout class, ensuring the correct timeout behavior is applied during requests.

This commit updates the HTTPDigestAuth class in requests/auth.py to use single quotes for string formatting. It standardizes the quote style for the A1 and A2 variables within the handle_401 method. No functional behavior changes are introduced.

This commit updates the `requests` module to replace local success flags with direct attributes on the `Response` object. It ensures that `Request.send` correctly sets the `ok` and `error` properties, allowing users to check response status more consistently.

This commit modifies the HTTPAdapter class in the requests module to cache proxy connection managers. It prevents the creation of a new proxy manager for each request by reusing existing instances stored in a dictionary, improving efficiency for repeated proxy connections.

This commit adds import stubs to the requests packages module, allowing users to access urllib3 directly through the requests namespace. It creates a series of files that re-export the standard urllib3 library components, ensuring compatibility for code relying on this specific import path.
This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library within the requests package. It modifies core modules such as connectionpool and poolmanager to refresh the underlying HTTP client functionality.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 0.10.4. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the package's initialization file to reflect the new release.
This commit updates the project's changelog to document the addition of Eventlet and Gevent monkeypatch support. It also clarifies the status of cookie support in the history file.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 2.9.2. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the package's initialization file to reflect the new release.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar templates to make the "Support Requests Development (3.0)" heading a clickable link. It directs users to an external page for supporting the project's development. The changes affect the sidebarintro and sidebarlogo HTML templates.

This commit updates the README documentation to reflect the new string representation of response data. It clarifies that accessing response attributes now returns quoted strings, matching the updated behavior of the library's data types.

This commit updates documentation files to consistently capitalize the project name as "Requests" instead of "requests." It corrects minor wording in the README, API reference, and developer guides to improve clarity and branding consistency.

This commit fixes an issue where proxy authentication headers were not generated if the password was empty. The `proxy_headers` method in the `HTTPAdapter` class now includes the header whenever a username is provided, regardless of the password.

This release fixes several URL handling issues in the requests library. It allows technically invalid but common hostnames to pass through if IDNA encoding fails, and prevents errors for URLs with leading whitespace or missing schemes.

The `Session.request` method in `requests/sessions.py` now accepts a `return_response` parameter. When set to false, it returns the prepared request object instead of the final response, allowing users to inspect or modify the request before sending.

This commit updates the documentation for the requests library. It increases the table of contents depth in the main index and clarifies section titles in the installation guide to explicitly mention "Requests" and "Source Code."

The `get_auth_from_url` function in `requests/utils.py` now correctly decodes percent-encoded characters in the username and password fields. This fixes an issue where special characters in credentials were not properly unquoted when extracting authentication from a URL.

This commit relocates the test server module into the tests directory, making it part of the test suite structure. The Server class and its associated helper functions are now accessible under the new tests.testserver path.

This commit adds proxy support to the HTTPAdapter by introducing a get_connection method that selects the appropriate connection pool based on the URL scheme. It also updates the send method signature to accept proxy configuration, allowing users to route requests through specified proxies.

This commit updates the `request` function in `requests/api.py` to retrieve the session from the `kwargs` dictionary instead of a separate `session` variable. This change likely fixes an issue where a user-provided session was not being correctly passed to the underlying request logic.

This commit fixes a crash in the `PreparedRequest.prepare_url` method when handling Unicode URLs on Python 2. Previously, the code attempted to decode Unicode strings, causing an error that was not properly handled. It now restricts decoding operations to byte objects only.

This commit removes the `prefetch` argument from the `Session.request` method in the `requests` library. Users will no longer be able to pass this parameter when making requests, as it has been stripped from the function signature.

This commit updates the version number in the requests module to 2.6.2 and adds release notes to the history file. It documents a bug fix that resolves an issue where compressed data sent as chunked data was not properly decompressed.

This commit standardizes the docstrings for several exception and warning classes in the requests.exceptions module by ensuring they end with a period. It also removes redundant pass statements from the RequestsWarning and FileModeWarning class definitions.

This commit prevents Python from generating bytecode files during the package publishing process. It modifies the setup.py script to set an environment variable that disables bytecode writing when the publish command is invoked.

Updates the GitHub Actions workflow in the publish.yml file to use version 7.0.0 of the actions/download-artifact action. This change ensures the CI pipeline uses the latest major version for downloading build artifacts.

This commit introduces the `Session` class in the `requests` module to manage and persist settings like cookies, authentication, and proxies across multiple requests. It allows users to maintain state between calls, improving the handling of persistent connections and data.

This commit corrects documentation examples in the advanced user guide that referenced the httpbin service without the .org domain. It ensures the URLs in the code snippets are valid, preventing users from copying broken links.

This commit fixes a bug in the `PreparedRequest.prepare_url` method where URLs without a network location were incorrectly processed. It ensures that both the scheme and network location are present before proceeding, preventing errors when handling incomplete URLs.
This commit fixes a malformed HTML tag in the project's README file. It corrects the closing paragraph tag to ensure the documentation renders properly in web browsers.

This commit fixes an error that occurred when using proxies after an HTTPAdapter instance was deserialized. It ensures the HTTPAdapter class properly initializes its proxy manager and configuration dictionaries during the state restoration process.

The `Request` class in `requests/models.py` now defaults the `redirect` parameter to `False` instead of `True`. This change ensures that redirect chains are not followed by default, requiring users to explicitly enable this behavior.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar templates to remove a specific author's name from the newsletter subscription text. The change affects the `sidebarintro.html` and `sidebarlogo.html` files, making the update message more generic for users.

This commit updates the MANIFEST.in file to include HISTORY.md instead of HISTORY.rst in the package distribution. This ensures the correct changelog file is bundled when the project is packaged for release.

This commit fixes a bug in the `unquote_unreserved` function within `requests/utils.py` where invalid percent-encoded sequences were incorrectly processed. It now ensures that only alphanumeric characters are treated as valid unreserved characters, preventing potential errors or security issues during URL decoding.

This commit fixes ResourceWarnings in the test suite by ensuring file handles are properly closed after use. It updates several test methods in the TestRequests class to use context managers for file operations, preventing unclosed file resource leaks.

This commit refactors the `_parse_content_type_header` function in `requests/utils.py` to simplify parameter parsing by removing a list comprehension and using a dedicated string for stripping characters. It also adds a test case to verify the function correctly handles double quotes in content type headers.

This commit adds a unit test to the RequestsAPIUnitTests class in tests/unit/test_requests_api.py. It verifies that the requests.get function correctly passes keyword arguments to the underlying request method.

This commit modernizes the build system for the requests library by adopting PEP 517 standards. It introduces a new pyproject.toml file to define project metadata and dependencies, replacing the legacy setup.py and setup.cfg configuration.

This commit fixes a TypeError in the Response class that occurred when calling the json method on a response with no content. It prevents the error by checking if the content exists before attempting to determine its length.

This commit adds a missing anchor label to the documentation introduction page. It ensures that links referencing the ISC License section resolve correctly for users navigating the docs. The change modifies the `docs/user/intro.rst` file.

This commit updates the test suite for the requests module to verify that error messages for invalid headers include the specific header name. It modifies the TestRequests class to assert that the exception text contains the relevant header identifiers when validation fails.

This commit updates the documentation for the `requests` library to clarify that `Session.headers` must be set to an `OrderedDict` to preserve header order. It corrects a reference in the advanced user guide to ensure users understand the specific data type required for this feature.

This commit clarifies the documentation for the advanced user guide regarding proxy configuration. It explains that the socks5 scheme performs DNS resolution on the client, while socks5h resolves domains on the proxy server, aligning with curl's behavior.

This commit fixes a Python 3 compatibility error in the `Request` class within `requests/models.py`. It replaces a removed standard library function with a lambda expression to correctly process the `no_proxy` setting, preventing crashes when sending requests.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 0.6.3. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the core module to reflect the new release.

This commit updates the wording in the documentation sidebar templates to encourage financial support rather than purchasing a copy. It also renames the donation button to "Requests Pro" in the sidebar introduction and logo files.

This commit updates the project's README to display the license image directly instead of showing raw text. It modifies the documentation file to improve the visual presentation of the license information for users.

This commit adds a Zizmor workflow to audit GitHub Actions configurations and applies recommended security fixes. It restricts workflow permissions to the job level and disables credential persistence in checkout steps across multiple CI files.

The `curl_from_request` function in `requests/utils.py` now supports basic authentication by including user credentials in the generated command. This change allows users to convert requests with authentication into valid curl commands, replacing previous placeholder comments.

This commit refactors the `prepare_hooks` method in the `PreparedRequest` class to simplify hook registration. It replaces manual list initialization and extension logic with calls to the existing `register_hook` method, reducing code complexity.

This commit updates the test suite to work with pytest 8 by replacing the deprecated `pytest.warns(None)` call with `pytest.warns()` in the `TestRequests` class. It also relaxes the development dependency constraint to allow pytest versions up to 8.

This commit removes the global `defaults` dictionary from `requests/defaults.py` and its associated imports. It also uncomments the `send` method in `BaseAdapter` to properly raise a `NotImplementedError`. These changes streamline the library's configuration handling by eliminating redundant default settings.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library from 0.2.5 to 0.3.0. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the core module to reflect the new release.

This commit updates the documentation templates to improve the site's appearance. It adds a hyperlink to the "About Requests" heading in the sidebar and includes a "Fork me on GitHub" ribbon in the top-right corner of the layout.

This commit removes the HACKING documentation file and strips out the singleton pattern implementation from the Settings class in requests/config.py. It also updates the tox configuration to reflect these repository changes.
This commit corrects a typo in the project's history documentation. It updates the import example to reference the correct `urllib3` module instead of the non-existent `urllib` package.
This commit updates the project's README file by adding a blank line to the documentation. It makes no functional changes to the codebase or user-facing behavior.

This commit fixes Python 2 compatibility issues in the chardet library by converting byte characters to integers before processing. It updates the CodingStateMachine, Latin1Prober, and SingleByteCharSetProber classes to handle string encoding correctly.

This commit adds a test to verify that the requests library correctly parses link headers from HTTP responses. The new test method, test_links, checks that the 'next' relation is properly extracted from a GitHub API response.

The `from_key_val_list` function in `requests/utils.py` now raises a clearer error message when it encounters data that is not a two-item tuple. This change improves the diagnostic information provided to users when invalid input is passed to the function.
This commit updates the documentation index to include Work for Pie in the list of notable users. It adds a link to the Work for Pie website alongside the existing Readability reference.

This commit adds a promotional message to the documentation sidebar, encouraging companies to purchase a copy of the Requests library. The change updates the sidebar template files to include a link to a Gumroad store.

This commit fixes a bug in the Request class where parameter values that were iterable but not lists failed to be UTF-8 encoded. The _encode_params method now correctly handles these types, ensuring proper data encoding for multivalued inputs.

This commit updates the test suite to run in parallel using the pytest-xdist plugin. It modifies the Makefile to invoke pytest with distributed execution and adds the new dependency to both the requirements and setup files.

This commit fixes Windows build failures on Appveyor where the system could not replace the running executable. It updates the installation step in the appveyor.yml configuration to run pip through the Python interpreter instead of directly.

This commit adds trailing whitespace to several lines within the RequestsTestSuite class in test_requests.py. It does not alter any functional behavior or fix a bug, serving only as a minor formatting adjustment to the test file.

The Makefile now redirects the output of the flake8 linting command to a file named flake8_report.txt. This change ensures that linting results are saved to disk for later review instead of only appearing in the terminal.

The `Response.raise_for_status` method in `requests/models.py` now falls back to ISO-8859-1 encoding when decoding the HTTP reason phrase fails as UTF-8. This prevents crashes when servers return non-UTF-8 status messages, ensuring the error is raised correctly instead of failing during decoding.
This commit removes an unused import from the requests.adapters module. It cleans up the code by eliminating the unnecessary reference to urldefrag, which does not affect user-facing behavior.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to version 1.14, bringing in various internal improvements and bug fixes. It modifies core modules like connectionpool and poolmanager to ensure compatibility with the new version.
This commit updates the project documentation to change the phrasing of the daily download count and adds a celebratory message. The change is located in the main documentation index file.

This commit adds support for custom redirect handling and .history tracking to the requests library. It modifies the Request class to accept a redirect parameter and integrates a new HTTPRedirectHandler into the response building process.

This commit fixes a documentation indentation error in the `Session.get` method within the `requests` library. It corrects the formatting of the `params` argument description to ensure the continuation line aligns properly with the preceding text.

This commit adds a documentation example to the Advanced Usage guide demonstrating how to implement automatic retries for failed connections. It clarifies that while the library does not retry by default, users can enable this behavior using the HTTPAdapter class and urllib3's Retry utility.

This commit fixes an issue where cookie values wrapped in double quotes were not properly unquoted, causing incorrect data to be stored. The `RequestsCookieJar` class now strips surrounding quotes in its `set_cookie` method to ensure clean values.

This commit fixes a crash in the `morsel_to_cookie` function within `requests/cookies.py` that occurred when processing cookies with a string-based `max-age` attribute. By explicitly converting the value to a float, the function now correctly calculates the expiration time instead of raising a type error.
This commit updates the project's contributor list by adding Juan Riaza to the section for patches and suggestions. It acknowledges a new contributor without altering any functional code or behavior.

This commit adds the missing documentation entry for the Timeout exception in the API reference. It ensures that references to this exception in the quickstart guide are properly hyperlinked to the new documentation page.

This commit fixes a minor formatting inconsistency in the `parse_header_links` function within `requests/utils.py`. It adds a missing space after a comma in a regular expression split call, ensuring the code adheres to standard style guidelines without altering functionality.

This commit optimizes the version extraction process in the setup.py module by replacing a line-by-line loop with a single search operation. This change makes the package installation process faster and more efficient.

This commit removes an unused variable assignment from the `Request` class in `requests/models.py`. It cleans up the `send` method by deleting a line that set a local variable to false, which had no effect on the library's behavior.

In the `Response` class within `requests/core.py`, the initial value of the `error` attribute is changed from `False` to `None`. This ensures that the absence of an error is represented by `None` rather than a boolean, preventing potential logic errors when checking for error states.

This commit fixes a bug in the `requests` library where the status code 200 alias was incorrectly defined as a raw string. It corrects the backslash escaping in `status_codes.py` to ensure the alias is interpreted as a literal string rather than a regex pattern.

This commit prevents gevent from patching the standard library if eventlet is already active, avoiding potential conflicts between the two libraries. The change modifies the import logic in `requests/core.py` to check for the presence of eventlet before attempting to apply gevent monkey patches.
This commit adds Den Shabalin to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS file. It updates the project's credit list to acknowledge his contributions.
This commit corrects a non-standard em dash character in the AUTHORS.rst file to a standard hyphen. It ensures the contributor list displays consistently across different text editors and terminals.
This commit removes the dedicated coverage job from the Windows pipeline in the Azure Pipelines template. It also corrects a trailing whitespace character in the display name of the main test job.

Adds a test to the RequestsTestCase class in test_requests.py that verifies a ConnectionError is raised when attempting to connect to an invalid port. This ensures the library correctly handles connection failures for unreachable network endpoints.

This commit updates the documentation for the default configuration parameters in the requests.defaults module. It clarifies the descriptions for settings like base_headers, timeout, and max_redirects, while removing outdated entries such as accept_gzip and proxies.

This commit adds a `send` method to `PreparedRequest` and a `next` property to `Response` to simplify request handling and redirect navigation. It also updates the `Session` class to support yielding responses during the redirect resolution process.

This commit updates the project history file to document version 2.5.1. It lists bug fixes for HTTP error handling, location parsing, and file-like object filenames, alongside a behavioral change to the raise_for_status function.

This commit replaces bare assert statements with unittest's self.assert* methods in the test_requests and test_requests_ext modules. This change ensures that test failures provide descriptive error messages instead of generic assertion errors, improving the clarity of debugging output for developers.
This commit updates the project's README to improve the placement of the download badge. It moves the badge from the top of the file to a position below the main title.

This commit removes the HelloBar script from the documentation layout. It eliminates the external banner that previously appeared on the site, ensuring no third-party tracking or advertising code is loaded.

This commit fixes a documentation build failure by correcting how the requests library version is imported. It updates the import statement in the docs/conf.py configuration file to use the proper module path.
This commit updates the httpbin dependency in the requirements file from version 0.0.4 to 0.0.6. It ensures the project uses the newer release of the HTTP testing server library.

This commit splits the connection error test in the RequestsTestCase class into two separate tests for invalid domains and invalid ports. It also updates the test URL for the invalid domain case to ensure the test reliably triggers a connection error.

The `check_header_validity` function in `requests/utils.py` now includes the specific header name in the error message when an invalid type is detected. This change helps users identify exactly which header caused the `InvalidHeader` exception, improving debugging clarity.

This commit updates the API documentation to reflect the correct module names for enabling debug logging in Python 3. It clarifies that `http.client` is the modern equivalent of the legacy `httplib` module, ensuring users can correctly configure the `HTTPConnection` debug level.

This commit fixes a bug in the `get_encoding_from_headers` function within `requests/utils.py` where the content-type delimiter was incorrectly set to a semicolon with a trailing space. The change ensures the delimiter is strictly a semicolon, allowing the function to correctly parse character encoding information from HTTP response headers.
This commit updates the project history to document that Session objects are now picklable. It also notes that invalid schema URLs now raise a ValueError.

This commit updates the test suite for the requests module to use direct attribute assignment instead of the setattr function. It modifies the test_iter_content_handles_socket_error method within the RequestsTestCase class to improve code clarity.
This commit updates the project history log to document the addition of redirection authentication handling. It records the new feature in the release notes without modifying any source code.
This commit restores Python 3.3 to the project's continuous integration test matrix. It ensures that the codebase is verified for compatibility with this older Python version during automated builds.

The Makefile's init target now generates a requirements.txt file and installs dependencies directly via pip instead of relying solely on Pipenv. The coverage target is updated to run pytest directly rather than through the Pipenv wrapper.

This commit updates the project's sponsor documentation to reflect a rebranding. It changes the label for the Microsoft Cloud Developer Advocates to Azure Cloud Developer Advocates in the sponsors file.

The `iter_content` method in the `Response` class now validates that the `chunk_size` argument is an integer. If a non-integer value is provided, it raises a `TypeError` instead of failing later or behaving unexpectedly.

This commit fixes URI re-encoding issues in Python 3 by correcting the `requote_path` utility to handle string paths instead of bytes. It ensures `Request.full_url` properly requotes the path and prevents `Request.path_url` from double-quoting already-encoded segments.
This commit updates the project documentation to clarify the installation section title. It changes the heading from "Python Module Installation" to "Requests Module Installation" in the README file.
This commit adds Robin Linderborg to the project's list of contributors. It updates the AUTHORS.rst file to include the new name under the "Patches and Suggestions" section.

This commit renames the `encode_urls` configuration option to `encode_uri` in the `requests` library. The change updates the default settings and the `Request` class to use the new key, ensuring consistent behavior for URL encoding.

This commit updates the test suite in test_requests.py to use a local helper function instead of hardcoded external URLs. This change allows the tests to run in an offline environment without requiring internet access to httpbin.org.
This commit adds the `ssl_match_hostname` package to the project's dependencies in `setup.py`. It ensures the SSL hostname matching library is explicitly installed alongside the application.

This commit fixes the encoding of multipart/form-data requests when fields share the same name. It updates the Request class to accept a list of 2-tuples for the files argument, ensuring repeated data fields are handled correctly.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to use the `io` module instead of the deprecated `StringIO` module. This ensures the provided code example remains compatible with Python 3.x, where the old import path is no longer available.

This commit ensures that HTTP connections are properly closed during redirections to prevent resource leaks. It modifies the `_build_response` method in the `Request` class within `requests/models.py` to explicitly close the previous response object before proceeding.

This commit removes the automatic import of the async module from the main requests package. It prevents potential runtime errors during initialization by stopping the library from attempting to load async functionality by default.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to strongly recommend using the timeout parameter for all production requests. It warns that omitting this setting can cause programs to hang indefinitely, making the guidance more prominent for users.

This commit modernizes import statements in the requests API and core modules by switching to relative imports. It also replaces wildcard imports with explicit function and exception names to improve code clarity and maintainability.

The `prepare_hooks` method in the `PreparedRequest` class now safely handles cases where the hooks argument is `None`. This prevents a crash when preparing requests without defined hooks, ensuring the test for unicode URL preparation passes.

This commit updates the version number to 2.6.1 and adds release notes to the history file. It documents bug fixes for import issues in PyInstaller executables, simplifies the PreparedRequest API, and improves redirect handling and Unicode error management.

This commit updates the Makefile to configure the flake8 linter to ignore unused import statements. This prevents the build from failing due to F401 errors, allowing developers to keep imports that are not directly used in the code.

This commit modifies the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to prevent automatic content decoding when building responses. It ensures that raw data is preserved by explicitly disabling the `decode_content` option during the request send process.

This commit fixes a crash in the `RequestsCookieJar.set_cookie` method when processing cookies with non-string values. It adds a type check to ensure the cookie value supports string operations before attempting to strip quotes, preventing errors during cookie parsing.
This commit removes the pytest-mock dependency from the project's requirements file. It simplifies the test environment by eliminating an unused or redundant testing utility.

This commit updates the project's README to refine the description of the library's capabilities. It changes the wording to state that the tool is ready for building robust HTTP-speaking applications for the needs of today.

This commit adds Ryan Kelly to the project's author list and updates the changelog for version 0.8.2. It also corrects the documentation build configuration to properly reference the renamed author file.

This commit updates the `curl_from_request` function in `requests/utils.py` by renaming variables and adjusting string formatting. The changes are primarily cosmetic, with no functional impact on the generated curl commands.

This release fixes a bug where responses with a zero content-length failed to process correctly. It also adds a new asynchronous mapping function and prevents the library from crashing when network credentials are missing.

This update modifies the `HTTPConnectionPool` class in the `urllib3` module to improve connection management. It replaces the direct internal method call with `response.release_conn()`, which properly tracks the release state of the connection.

This commit ensures that user-specified request options, such as timeouts or certificate settings, are correctly passed to hooks when resending authenticated requests. It updates the `HTTPDigestAuth` class and `dispatch_hook` function to forward keyword arguments, preventing the loss of these configurations during authentication retries.

This commit restructures the safe mode feature to catch exceptions at the API level rather than within the models. It introduces a new decorator in safe_mode.py that wraps the request function to return a blank response when errors occur. This change simplifies error handling in models.py and cookies.py by removing previous conditional checks.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library from 0.5.1 to 0.6.0. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the core module to reflect the new release.
Adds a new documentation page listing corporate sponsors for the Requests library. This update clarifies the project's funding sources and highlights its widespread usage in critical infrastructure.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to improve HTTPS connection handling through proxies. It modifies the VerifiedHTTPSConnection class to correctly establish tunnels and adds proxy-related parameters to the HTTPConnectionPool and PoolManager classes.

This commit updates the CodeQL analysis workflow to run exclusively on the master branch, removing the proposed/3.0.0 branch. It also simplifies the configuration by replacing the matrix strategy with a direct Python language specification.

This commit updates the copyright link in the documentation configuration to point to a new, valid URL. It resolves a broken link issue in the generated documentation footer. The change is made within the `docs/conf.py` file.

This commit finalizes the release date for version 1.2.0 in the project history. It documents a significant change in the requests module where hooks now receive all user-specified request arguments, enabling them to make secondary requests with identical parameters.

The `dict_from_string` function in `requests/utils.py` now catches and ignores exceptions raised during cookie parsing. This prevents the library from crashing when it encounters malformed or untrusted cookie data, ensuring that invalid cookies are simply skipped rather than causing a failure.

This commit fixes the `ok` property and `__nonzero__` method in `requests.models` to correctly reflect HTTP error statuses. Previously, these attributes did not account for server errors, leading to incorrect boolean evaluations. Now, they use `raise_for_status` to ensure accurate status reporting.
This commit updates the project's README file. It removes specific text from the documentation, likely to correct a typo or clarify instructions for users.
The test runner now uses nosetests with color output instead of plain Python execution. The project dependencies are updated to include rudolf and reorder existing packages.

This commit fixes broken documentation styling and sidebar content. It adds a CSS rule to ensure select elements span the full width and updates the sidebar templates to display a new development section header.

This commit updates the documentation for the Request class in requests/models.py. It removes the outdated list of specific HTTP methods from the method attribute description, simplifying the text to just "HTTP Method to use."

This commit adds support for the HTTP 451 status code, "Unavailable For Legal Reasons," to the requests library. It updates the status_codes module to recognize this new code, allowing users to handle responses indicating legal restrictions.

This commit introduces a pluggable connection adapter system to the `Session` class in `requests/sessions.py`. It allows users to mount custom adapters for specific URL prefixes, replacing the previous hardcoded use of a single `HTTPAdapter` for all requests.

The hooks module is restructured into a package, and the dispatch_hooks function no longer requires a key argument. The request function now uses setup_hooks to initialize default hooks, including new response hooks for unicode encoding and decompression.

This commit introduces a new hooks system to the requests library, allowing users to customize request arguments before they are sent. The main `request` function in `requests/api.py` now accepts a `hooks` parameter and uses the new `dispatch_hook` function from `requests/hooks.py` to process these modifications.

This commit removes the `set_http_proxy` helper method from the `Session` class in the `requests` library. It reverts a previous change that added a user-friendly way to configure HTTP and HTTPS proxies, restoring the original proxy configuration behavior.

This commit refactors a single test in the TestRequests class into two distinct tests to improve clarity. It separates the verification of case-insensitive prefix matching from the specific mixed-case scenario, ensuring each behavior is tested independently.

This commit removes unused and commented-out attributes from the Request and PreparedRequest classes in requests/models.py. It cleans up the codebase by deleting dead code related to timeout, prefetch, verify, and cert settings.

This commit updates the `Request.send` method in `requests/models.py` to handle prefetching. When the prefetch option is enabled, it now marks the response content as consumed, preventing unnecessary data re-reading.

This commit updates the Requests documentation by adding a new quickstart guide and refining installation references. It also corrects the supported Python version description in the introduction to clarify that support for Python 3.x is planned.

This commit fixes inconsistent indentation in the docstrings of the `requests/core.py` module. It standardizes the spacing for class and method descriptions, such as those for `Request` and `_Request`, to ensure proper formatting.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to a newer version, modifying connection handling and utility functions. It renames standard library imports to avoid naming conflicts and introduces a port mapping dictionary for HTTP schemes.

This commit removes the automatic eventlet and gevent monkey-patching from the requests core module, requiring users to explicitly handle asynchronous behavior. It also eliminates the unnecessary AuthObject class and refactors the Request class to use a unified request method for all HTTP verbs.

This commit corrects a spelling error in the docstring of the test_fragment_update_on_redirect function within tests/test_lowlevel.py. It changes "encounterd" to "encountered" to improve documentation clarity without altering any code behavior.

This commit applies PEP 8 style fixes to the Request and Response classes in requests/models.py. It corrects indentation and adds missing spaces after commas in function definitions and calls, improving code readability without changing behavior.
This commit updates the project's metadata in setup.py to declare compatibility with Python 3.4. It adds the specific classifier for this version to the package configuration.

This commit optimizes the `Response` class in `requests/models.py` by caching the decoded text content. It prevents redundant decoding operations when the `Response.text` property is accessed multiple times, improving performance for repeated reads.

This commit updates the `httpbin` helper function in `test_requests.py` to use `urlparse.urljoin` instead of simple string concatenation. This ensures that the constructed URLs are properly formatted, preventing potential path resolution errors when appending suffixes to the base URL.

This commit ensures that expired cookies are properly removed from the session's cookie jar during requests. It modifies the `Session` class in `requests/sessions.py` to use `extract_cookies_to_jar` instead of manually updating a temporary cookie jar, preventing stale cookies from persisting.

The `http_basic` function in `requests/auth.py` now explicitly converts username and password arguments to strings before encoding. This ensures consistent behavior when non-string types are provided. The code also updates the base64 import to use the standard `base64` function.

This commit introduces a new function, `merge_session_cookies`, in the `requests/cookies.py` module to safely combine request-specific cookies with the session's existing cookie jar. It ensures that cookies provided in a request do not overwrite or modify cookies already stored in the session, preserving the session's state during requests.
This commit updates the project roadmap in the README file. It replaces vague placeholder tasks with specific goals for creating Sphinx documentation and writing exhaustive unit tests.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the project's contribution guidelines. It updates the documentation to accurately state that the library is in a perpetual feature freeze.

This commit updates the installation documentation to replace a broken link with a working StackOverflow answer. It clarifies why users should prefer pip over easy_install by providing a valid external reference.

This commit removes the `invoke` dependency from the project's requirements and updates the development documentation. It simplifies the test execution instructions by replacing the `invoke test` command with a direct call to `py.test`.

This commit updates the project's documentation links to point to the new requests.readthedocs.io domain. It modifies references in the README, contributing guide, and history files to ensure users access the correct documentation site.

This commit introduces `MissingSchema` and `InvalidSchema` exceptions to the `requests` library, allowing users to catch specific URL validation errors separately from general value errors. It updates the `Request` class to raise these new exceptions instead of generic `ValueError` objects when a URL lacks a valid schema.
This commit updates the maintainer contact information in the project documentation. It adds Nate Prewitt to the list of primary maintainers in the support and contributing guides.
This commit updates the .gitignore file to exclude the docs/_build directory from version control. This prevents generated documentation build artifacts from being tracked by git.

It changes the behavior to use a local variable within the `unicode_content` method, ensuring that encoding attempts are tracked only for the current response.

This commit fixes the `Response.iter_content` method in `requests.models` to correctly apply Unicode decoding even when the response content has already been fully consumed. Previously, the `decode_unicode` parameter was ignored in this specific scenario, potentially returning incorrect data types to the user.
This commit adds Jonas Obrist to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS.rst file. It acknowledges his patches and suggestions to the project.

This commit moves the code of conduct, contributing guidelines, and security policy files into the .github directory. It also updates the security policy to use standard Markdown formatting instead of reStructuredText.

This commit adds a failing test to the RequestsTestSuite in tests/test_requests.py. It verifies that requesting a URL with an invalid scheme raises a URLRequired exception instead of a generic ValueError.

This commit clarifies the documentation for the `iter_content` and `iter_lines` methods in the `Response` class. It explains that when `decode_unicode` is enabled but no encoding is detected, raw bytes are returned unless the user manually sets the response encoding.

This commit prevents the `merge_setting` function in `requests/sessions.py` from including headers with `None` values in the final request. It ensures that if a session header is set to `None`, it is not sent to the server, fixing an issue where such headers could cause unexpected behavior.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to a newer version, changing the default behavior so that security warnings are always displayed rather than only once. It also refines connection handling in the HTTPConnectionPool and HTTPSConnectionPool classes, including updates to proxy preparation and timeout management.

The `default_headers` function in `requests/utils.py` now includes a `Connection: keep-alive` header in the default request headers. This change enables persistent HTTP connections by default, allowing clients to reuse connections for multiple requests to the same server.

This commit updates the `Request._encode_params` method in `requests/models.py` to correctly handle list values within dictionaries. It enables the `doseq` option during URL encoding, ensuring that list items are properly serialized as repeated parameters instead of being ignored or malformed.

This commit fixes a build failure by adding the missing PySocks dependency to the project's requirements. It updates both the pinned and unpinned requirements files to include the necessary package version.
This commit adds a new development section to the project's release history file. It introduces a placeholder for upcoming bug fixes, preparing the documentation for the next release cycle.

This commit adds initial installation documentation for the Tablib package. It introduces instructions for installing dependencies using pip and easy_install, and begins a section on alternative installation sources.

This commit adds test cases to the `test_invalid_url` method in `test_requests.py`. It verifies that `PreparedRequest` correctly raises an `InvalidSchema` error for URLs missing a scheme, such as `localhost:3128`.

This commit introduces the MultiDict and TypeConversionDict classes to the requests structures module. It provides a dictionary implementation that supports multiple values for a single key and allows type conversion during value retrieval.

This commit corrects a broken link to the AI Policy in the project's contribution guidelines. It updates the path in the CONTRIBUTING.md file to point to the correct location within the repository, ensuring users can successfully access the policy document.

This commit ensures that the response URL is properly decoded from UTF-8 bytes to a string in the `Request` class. It fixes an issue where the URL might remain encoded, affecting how users view the final request destination.
This commit updates the GitHub profile link for Kenneth Reitz in the AUTHORS.rst file. It corrects the outdated username to reflect the author's current account handle.

This commit updates the contributor's guide documentation to improve the clarity and flow of the introductory text. It refines the opening message to contributors, making the welcome more direct and concise.

This commit updates the package manifest to include the entire tests directory in source distributions instead of a single test file. This ensures that all test modules are available when users install the package from a tarball.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the project's history documentation. It updates the changelog entry for the proxy resolution fix to properly spell "entries" instead of "entires."

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to improve HTTP response handling and boundary generation. It modifies HTTPConnectionPool to use buffered responses when available and replaces the legacy boundary selection logic in filepost with a UUID-based approach.

This commit updates the development todo documentation by removing entries for tasks that have already been completed. It cleans up the list to reflect the current project status, specifically deleting items related to OAuth support, Poster removal, and context manager flexibility.

This commit modifies the `Response` class in `requests/models.py` to handle responses with a status code of zero. It prevents the `content` property from attempting to read the body for such responses, instead setting it to `None` to avoid potential errors.

This commit fixes a crash in the `morsel_to_cookie` function within `requests/cookies.py` that occurred when a cookie's max-age value contained non-numeric characters. It now safely ignores invalid max-age values instead of raising an error, ensuring the request process continues smoothly.
This commit updates the project's contributor list by adding Erik Wickstrom to the "Patches and Suggestions" section. It modifies the AUTHORS.rst file to reflect this new contribution.

The sponsorship link in the GitHub funding configuration was updated to point to the new Python Software Foundation sponsorship page. This ensures users are directed to the correct URL for the relaunched program.
This commit updates the quickstart documentation to reflect accurate cookie handling behavior. It replaces a specific external URL and cookie example with generic placeholders in the user guide.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 2.16.2. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the `__version__.py` file to reflect the new release.
This commit updates the project history to announce version 0.11.3, which introduces experimental OAuth2 support. Users will now have access to this new authentication feature in the updated release.

This commit updates the project's README to clarify that the Requests library powers many daily tools. It replaces a brief joke with a statement highlighting the library's widespread, often invisible usage.

This commit updates the documentation index to rename the "Developer Guide" section to "Contributor Guide." The change clarifies the intended audience for that part of the manual.
This commit removes a redundant comment and an empty line from the quickstart documentation. It cleans up the example demonstrating how to access cookies from a response in the user guide.

This commit adds a test case to the RequestsTestCase class in test_requests.py. It verifies that the Request.copy() method creates a distinct object with identical attributes, ensuring the copy functionality works as expected.

This commit adds a Proxy-Auth header to HTTP requests when the proxy URL includes credentials. It modifies the HTTPAdapter class in requests/adapters.py to extract authentication details and apply them during the send process.
This commit updates the project history file to announce version 0.6.3. It highlights the introduction of a new asynchronous requests feature as the primary change for this release.

This commit updates the Ruff linter version in the pre-commit configuration from 0.15.16 to 0.15.17. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the Ruff pre-commit hook for code quality checks.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to version 1.21.1 within the requests package. It refreshes core modules like connection handling, response decoding, and SSL utilities to incorporate the latest upstream fixes and improvements.

This commit fixes a bug in the `super_len` function within `requests/utils.py` where calculating the length of Python 2 StringIO objects failed. It now correctly handles cases where the length is initially reported as None by using the file position or defaulting to zero.

This commit adds new entries to the community FAQ documentation, covering how Requests handles encoded data, custom user agents, and proxy support. It also corrects a missing newline at the end of the file.

This commit updates the project's README to clarify that the tool handles HTTP redirects. It adds a sentence to the introductory text stating that the application will follow redirects, improving user expectations regarding its network capabilities.

This commit adds a `time_taken` attribute to the `Response` class to record the duration of each HTTP request in seconds. The `HTTPAdapter` now measures this time during the send process, allowing users to easily check how long a request took to complete.

This commit adds deprecation warnings to the `get_encodings_from_content` and `get_unicode_from_response` functions in `requests.utils`. Users will now see a warning when calling these functions, informing them that they will be removed in version 3.0.0.

This commit updates the project history log to document improvements in HTTP error handling. It clarifies that the software now manages HTTP errors more effectively, though specific behavioral changes are not detailed in this entry.

This commit updates the project's README to refine the introductory text regarding Python HTTP libraries. It clarifies the author's frustration with existing modules by adjusting the phrasing and emphasis in the overview section.

This commit reorganizes and expands the project documentation by moving the FAQ to a new community section and adding a dedicated support page. It updates the main index and quickstart guides to reflect these structural changes, improving user navigation.

This commit updates the project history to document an improvement in error reporting. It notes that error messages for invalid headers now include the specific header name, making debugging easier for users.

This commit adds test cases to the TestPreparingURLs class in tests/test_requests.py to verify the handling of IDNA-encoded and IPv6 URLs. It also updates tests/test_utils.py to include a check for Unicode ASCII conversion.
Bumps the package version from 0.2.2 to 0.2.3 in the setup.py file. This update reflects a new release of the software without changing any functional code or behavior.

In the `Session` class, the `request` method now stores the response history as a tuple instead of a list. This change ensures the history is immutable, preventing accidental modifications to the request chain after a response is received.

This commit applies PEP 8 style fixes to the test suite in test_requests.py. It refactors the setUp method in RequestsTestSuite to assign the connection object to a temporary variable before storing it, improving code readability.

This commit updates the AppVeyor CI configuration to run the code coverage upload command within the Pipenv virtual environment. This ensures the correct dependencies are available when submitting coverage data to Codecov.

This commit adds support for the `prefetch` option in `Session` and `Request` objects, allowing response content to be fetched immediately upon request. It ensures this setting is preserved when sessions are pickled and unpickled, preventing data loss during serialization.

This commit updates the Quickstart documentation to fix a flaky example where comparing full response text could fail due to non-deterministic metadata from the httpbin service. This commit removes trailing whitespace from curl command strings in the test suite. It updates the test_requests.py file to ensure consistent formatting in the test cases.

This commit clarifies the documentation for the `timeout` parameter in the `Session.request` method. It explicitly states that the value is measured in seconds, preventing user confusion about the time unit.

This commit updates the developer documentation to warn downstream packagers that they must redistribute the `cacerts.pem` file. This ensures that SSL functionality works correctly in repackaged versions of the Requests library.

This commit removes a humorous warning about the dangers of using the Python standard library for HTTP from the project's README. It cleans up the documentation by deleting the satirical text that previously appeared at the end of the file.

This commit updates the project's README to include a sidebar image linking to the official documentation. It improves the user experience by providing a direct visual link to the Requests library's documentation site.

This commit fixes a bug in the test server's `consume_socket_content` function where the loop could terminate prematurely if no data was available immediately after the initial check. It moves the socket readiness check inside the loop to ensure all available data is read before stopping.

This commit moves the test for handling uppercase URL schemes during redirects from the TestCaseInsensitiveDict class to the RequestsTestCase class. It corrects a previous merge error that placed the test in the wrong location, ensuring it runs within the appropriate test suite.

This commit corrects the intersphinx configuration in the documentation build file to point to the official Python standard library documentation. This commit fixes a compatibility issue where the `callable` function was unavailable in Python 3.1. It replaces these calls with `isinstance` checks against `collections.Callable` within the `Request` class and its test suite.

This commit restores the `__attrs__` list to the `Session` class in `requests/sessions.py`. It ensures that the `__getstate__` method correctly serializes session attributes by removing a conditional check that previously allowed the method to return an empty dictionary.

This commit restructures the project by moving the main package into a new src directory. It updates the Makefile and pyproject.toml to reference the new location, ensuring build tools and linters target the correct path.

This commit updates documentation files to replace insecure HTTP links with secure HTTPS equivalents. It ensures that references to external resources, such as the Sphinx documentation site, use the modern secure protocol. The changes affect the documentation build scripts and community guides.

This commit updates the project's history file to add missing periods to the end of several changelog entries. It standardizes the punctuation for recent release notes, including items regarding session parameters and header expansion.

This commit updates the Ruff linter version in the pre-commit configuration from 0.15.15 to 0.15.16. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the Ruff pre-commit hook for code quality checks.

This commit removes an unused import from the requests module. It cleans up the codebase by eliminating a redundant reference that did not affect functionality.

This commit updates the documentation to list Readability as a user of the Requests library. It adds Readability to the existing list of organizations that use the library internally, improving the accuracy of the project's testimonials.

This commit removes the `packages` import from the `requests` module. It also deletes a blank line following the `core` import. These changes clean up the package initialization file without altering core functionality.

This commit updates the project's README documentation. It adds a missing separator line to a table, ensuring the table renders correctly for users viewing the project overview.

This commit updates the project's history log to reflect the release of version 0.2.0. It reorganizes the version entries and renames the initial release notes to "Birth!" to mark the project's official launch.

This commit clarifies the origin of specific characters allowed in cookies by extracting them into a dedicated constant. It updates the legal character set in the `requests/packages/oreos/monkeys.py` module to reference this new variable, improving code readability without changing functionality.

This commit adds a new test job to the CI workflow to run tests on the Python 3.11 development branch. It marks this specific test run as experimental, allowing the project to verify compatibility with the upcoming Python version without blocking standard releases.

This commit adds an explicit import of the `encodings.idna` module to `requests/models.py`. This commit refactors the `requests` library by moving the `request` and `get` functions from the `api` module to the `Session` class. It updates the `api` module to delegate these calls to a default session instance, ensuring consistent behavior for users calling top-level functions.

This commit fixes a bug in the `requests.packages` module where the `chardet` alias was incorrectly pointing to the original module object instead of the renamed one.
