This commit adds a test to verify that `Session.get_adapter()` correctly selects the most specific URL prefix when multiple adapters are mounted. It ensures that requests to a URL matching a longer, more specific prefix use the corresponding adapter rather than a broader one.

This commit fixes a bug in the OAuth1 authentication class where URL parameters were incorrectly duplicated during the request flow. It resolves the issue by clearing the request's parameter dictionary after the initial URL construction. The change also removes a stray tab character from the HTTPDigestAuth class.
This commit adds a new release entry for version 2.15.1 to the project's history file. It documents a minor update with a brief, informal note acknowledging that errors occur.
This commit bumps the Requests library version to 0.7.2. It updates the version number in the package initialization module and adds a changelog entry noting a fix for the PATCH method.

This commit adds the FreeBSD certificate bundle path to the list of possible CA bundle locations in the `requests` utility module. It ensures that the library can correctly locate and use the system certificate store on FreeBSD systems.

This release fixes a chunked encoding error and adds support for configuring proxies via environment variables. The update introduces a new trust_env setting in the defaults module to enable reading configuration from the surrounding environment.

This commit removes unnecessary leading slashes from httpbin endpoint paths in the test suite. It updates the `httpbin` helper and related test methods in `tests/test_requests.py` to use clean path suffixes, ensuring consistent URL construction for HTTP requests.

This commit adds an `allow_redirects` parameter to the `request` function and `Request` class in the `requests` library. It enables users to explicitly control whether redirects are followed for POST, PUT, and DELETE requests, improving handling of 301 and 303 status codes.

This update improves compatibility with older Python 2.6 versions by safely checking for the `_tunnel_host` attribute in the `VerifiedHTTPSConnection` class. It also refines host comparison logic in `HTTPConnectionPool` to ensure correct behavior when default ports are used.

This commit fixes a bug where HTTP basic authentication failed when credentials contained non-ASCII characters. It updates the test suite to properly decode byte strings before sending them to the httpbin server, ensuring unicode usernames and passwords are handled correctly.
This commit adds Peter Manser to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS file. It updates the project's credit list to acknowledge his contributions.

The setup.py script now supports a "test" command that runs the test suite and exits, replacing the previous publish function. It also updates the package description to "Awesome Python HTTP Library that's actually usable."

This commit updates the project documentation to explicitly credit urllib3 as a core dependency alongside httplib. It modifies the introductory text in the README and main documentation index to reflect this technical detail.

This commit prevents the requests library from crashing at import time if the Python interpreter lacks the ssl module. It modifies the adapters module to wrap the default SSL context creation in a try-except block, setting the context to None if the import fails.

Adds a new test to the RequestsTestSuite that verifies POST requests with file uploads and custom headers. This ensures the library correctly handles sending files alongside specific header data to a remote server.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the `get_netrc_auth` function within `requests/utils.py` that caused a crash when running under Python 3. It updates the exception handling to use the correct tuple syntax, ensuring the function properly handles network credential parsing errors.

The `dict_from_string` function in `requests/packages/oreos/core.py` now returns a standard dictionary instead of a `MultiDict`. This change simplifies the cookie parsing logic by using standard dictionary updates rather than specialized multi-value storage.

This commit improves how the `Request` class handles exceptions in safe mode, ensuring that error attributes are correctly propagated to the response object. It modifies the `send` and `_build_response` methods in `requests/models.py` to provide more consistent behavior when requests fail.
This commit fixes broken HTML formatting in the project's README file. It adds missing closing tags to ensure the text displays correctly in rendered documentation.
This commit updates the project's README file to remove decorative emojis from the main title and adds a new image to the documentation.
This commit adds the httpbin package to the project's requirements file. It ensures the necessary dependency is installed for the application to function correctly.
Updates the project documentation to reflect current usage statistics. It replaces the outdated monthly download count with a new figure highlighting over 400,000 daily downloads.
This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to version 1.19.1. It fixes a Python 3 compatibility issue in the App Engine module by replacing a deprecated import with a six.moves equivalent.

This commit updates the Travis CI configuration to fix a shell syntax error in the test script. It changes the command execution format to ensure the README tests run correctly on supported Python versions.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Session` class where the response object was not correctly updated after the response hook was executed. It ensures that the modified response returned by the hook is properly assigned, preventing the session from holding onto the original, unmodified response.

This commit fixes a bug in the VerifiedHTTPSConnection class where the constructor failed to pass arguments to the parent class. Previously, initializing the connection would raise an error because the base class required specific parameters. Now, the constructor correctly forwards all keyword arguments to the HTTPSConnection parent.
This commit removes the project banner image and the tagline from the README. It simplifies the project's front page by deleting these decorative elements.
This commit updates the donation form in the documentation sidebar templates. It changes the hosted button ID and adjusts the available donation tiers and labels.

This commit fixes a UnicodeDecodeError that occurred when processing URLs containing non-ASCII characters. It ensures the URL is decoded to UTF-8 before being joined in the Request class's _build_response method.

This commit updates the documentation index to include the National Institutes of Health in the list of U.S. Federal Institutions. It clarifies the project's affiliation by adding NIH to the existing list of recognized institutions.

This commit adds failing tests to the RequestsTestSuite in tests/test_requests.py to verify that invalid percent-encodings in URLs are handled correctly. It ensures that the path_url property preserves malformed sequences like %TEST or %%TEST%% without raising errors or altering the string.

This commit updates the smoke test in the GuessJSONUTFTests class to handle UTF-16 surrogate pairs and UTF-8 decoding errors. It ensures the test correctly validates that the encoding guesser remains stable when processing random data that may contain invalid sequences.

This commit updates the test suite to support urllib3 2.0 by upgrading pytest-httpbin and adding the trustme library. It replaces the reliance on a legacy certificate with a new fixture that generates a certificate lacking a subjectAltName, ensuring the HTTPS warning tests remain valid.

The `header_expand` function in `requests/utils.py` now accepts both dictionaries and tuples of header data. This change allows the function to process header information provided in tuple format, expanding it into the expected structure for further use.
This commit removes a redundant legacy super() call from the Response class in the requests module. It cleans up the initialization process without changing any user-facing behavior or functionality.

This commit cleans up the test_requests.py module by removing unused imports and variables. It also applies PEP-8 formatting fixes to improve code style consistency. No functional behavior changes are introduced.

This commit removes the redundant `get` method from the `Session` class in `requests/sessions.py`. The deleted code was an unnecessary wrapper that duplicated functionality already handled by the base class, simplifying the session implementation.

This commit updates the changelog to document that network timeouts and connection errors are now treated as explicit exceptions. It clarifies that these URLErrors are raised when calling the `raise_for_status` method on a request object.

This documentation update adds the `all_proxy` environment variable to the list of supported proxy settings in the advanced user guide. It clarifies that users can configure Requests using this variable, providing a specific example for setting up a SOCKS proxy.

This commit fixes an issue where the request body and Content-Length header were incorrectly retained during HTTP redirects. It modifies the `resolve_redirects` method in `requests/sessions.py` to strip these elements from the new request, ensuring data is not resent.

This commit fixes an issue in the `get_auth_from_url` function within `requests/utils.py` where URL-encoded credentials were not properly decoded. It now unquotes the URL before extracting authentication details, ensuring that percent-encoded characters in usernames or passwords are handled correctly.

This commit fixes a crash in the `get_environ_proxies` function within `requests/utils.py` that occurred on early Python 2.6 versions on OS X. It wraps the `proxy_bypass` call in a try-except block to safely handle specific errors, preventing the library from failing when determining proxy settings.
Adds a `read` method to the `Request` class in `requests/core.py`. This method returns the request's content, providing a standard interface for reading request data.

The installation documentation for the Requests library now points to the correct personal PyPI mirror URL. This update ensures users can successfully install the package from the alternative source if the main repository is unavailable.

This commit adds missing documentation to the `request` function in the `requests.api` module. It clarifies the function's purpose and details its parameters, improving the user experience for developers reading the API reference.

This commit updates the project documentation in docs/index.rst to simplify the description of the library. It replaces a humorous, informal tagline with a more direct statement about the ease of sending HTTP requests.

This commit removes the unused `extract_zipped_paths` call from the `HTTPAdapter` class in the `requests` library. It simplifies certificate verification by directly using the default CA bundle path instead of attempting to extract zipped paths.

This commit updates the CI configuration to use the project's Makefile for installation instead of directly invoking pipenv. It also modifies the Makefile to run tests within the pipenv environment, ensuring consistent dependency management during test execution.
This commit updates the project's README to improve the formatting of the feature support section. It replaces a plain text header with a centered HTML heading for better visual presentation.

This commit ensures that cookies are always persisted in the `Session` class, fixing a bug where they were previously only saved during redirects. The cookie persistence logic was moved from the `SessionRedirectMixin` to the main `Session.request` method to apply to all requests.

This commit updates the error message in the `check_header_validity` function within `requests/utils.py`. It adds a space after the colon in the header name format to improve readability when an invalid header value is detected.

The `send` function in `requests/async.py` previously ignored the pool argument and simply delegated to the request object. This change makes `send` actually utilize the provided connection pool, fixing a broken or incomplete implementation.

The `raise_for_status` method in the `Response` class now includes the request URL in HTTP error messages. This change helps users identify which specific request failed when encountering unexpected client or server errors.

This commit adds validation for HTTP header names and values to prevent malformed data. It introduces the `check_header_validity` function in `requests/utils.py` to ensure headers do not contain leading spaces or return characters.

This commit adds a test to verify that the requests library correctly handles chunked uploads when sending data from a generator. It ensures the Transfer-Encoding header is set to chunked and the request completes successfully. The new test function is named test_chunked_upload.

This commit adds a test case to the RequestsTestCase class in test_requests.py. It verifies that a cookie jar created from a dictionary is correctly sent with a request. This ensures the cookie parameter works as expected for users managing sessions.

This commit removes the `URLRequired` exception from the API documentation because it is dead code and never actually raised. It clarifies that invalid URLs instead trigger `MissingSchema`, `InvalidSchema`, or `InvalidURL`, preventing user confusion about the library's error handling behavior.

This commit fixes a rendering issue in the documentation index where an image was incorrectly indented, causing it to appear as a nested element rather than a top-level figure. The change corrects the formatting in the `docs/index.rst` file to ensure the image displays properly on the main page.
The Makefile's publish target now includes a step to register the package with the Python Package Index. This ensures the project is properly registered before proceeding with the upload process.
This commit updates the AUTHORS.rst file to add Ben Bass to the list of contributors. It also fixes a missing newline at the end of the file.
The project's README now displays the logo as an SVG file instead of a PNG. This change improves image quality and scalability for users viewing the documentation.

This commit documents a limitation in the `PreparedRequest.prepare_cookies` method where the Cookie header is not regenerated if it already exists. It explains that this behavior, caused by cookielib, means the function only works once per request object unless the header is manually removed.

This commit removes a documentation note in the development TODO file that advised downstream repackagers to redistribute the cacerts.pem file for correct SSL functionality. The change updates the project's documentation to reflect that this specific requirement is no longer necessary.

This commit adds documentation to the `requests` module, specifically for the `add_autoauth` function. It explains how to register an authentication object to a URL domain for automatic activation. The changes clarify the behavior of auto-authentication for users configuring HTTP requests.

This commit introduces a new `merge_cookies` function in the `requests/cookies.py` module to safely combine session cookies with request parameters. It updates the `Session.request` method in `requests/sessions.py` to use this function, ensuring cookies are merged correctly without overwriting existing session data.

This commit fixes a test failure in the `RequestsTestSuite` by correcting the expected exception type for the `raise_for_status` method. It updates the test to assert that `urllib2.HTTPError` is raised instead of `requests.HTTPError`, ensuring the test suite runs correctly.
This commit updates the project's changelog to include the release date for version 0.7.1. It modifies the HISTORY.rst file to display the specific date alongside the version number.

This release fixes a dependency compatibility issue in the requests library by adjusting version markers to support older setuptools releases. The update bumps the package version to 2.14.2 in the main module.

This commit updates the project's release history file to document changes for version 2.1.0. It lists improvements to HTTP redirect handling, streaming uploads, and header parsing, along with various bug fixes and internal updates.

Adds Azure Pipelines configuration to run automated tests on Linux and Windows. This introduces new template files and a main pipeline definition to support continuous integration across multiple Python versions.

This commit fixes a missing space in the documentation sidebar template. It ensures the text "More" is properly separated from the link to Kenneth Reitz's website, improving readability for users viewing the project documentation.

This commit adds unit tests to the RequestsTestSuite in test_requests.py to verify the behavior of the curl_from_request utility. It ensures that the function correctly generates curl command strings for various HTTP methods, including GET, HEAD, and PATCH, as well as requests with custom headers and parameters.

This commit introduces a new utility function, `add_dict_to_cookiejar`, in the `requests/utils.py` module. It allows users to populate a cookie jar directly from a key-value dictionary, providing a more flexible way to manage cookies than the previous method.

This commit updates the `status_codes` module in the `requests` library to include HTTP status code names defined in RFC 9110. It adds new aliases for codes 102, 413, 414, and 422, reflecting the standard's updated terminology for these responses.

The Makefile now runs the test suite in parallel to speed up the coverage report generation. This change adds concurrency flags to the pytest command, allowing tests to execute simultaneously across multiple processes.

Adds initial cookie support to the requests library by allowing users to pass a cookie jar to the request function. The Request class now processes cookies during sending and extracts them from responses, enabling persistent session management.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` now falls back to global proxy settings when no explicit proxies are provided. This allows users to configure default proxy behavior globally via the new `proxies` attribute in `requests/config.py`.

This commit removes the entire legacy test suite, including modules like test_requests.py and the dummy server infrastructure. It also updates the Makefile and CI configuration to reflect the removal of these outdated tests.

This commit refactors the test suite in test_requests.py to use pytest fixtures for generating httpbin URLs. It replaces static environment variables with dynamic helper functions, httpbin and httpsbin_url, that construct valid test endpoints on demand.

This commit fixes an issue where response cookies were not properly extracted into the session's cookie jar. It updates the `HTTPAdapter.build_response` method to call the cookie extraction function and initializes the `Response` object's cookies with an empty cookie jar instead of `None`.

This commit refactors the URL construction logic in the `HTTPAdapter.request_url` method to improve readability and performance. It introduces boolean flags to explicitly track whether the request is using a SOCKS proxy or a standard HTTP proxy, simplifying the conditional branching for URL generation.

This commit updates the `SessionRedirectMixin` in `requests/sessions.py` to remove `Content-Type` and `Transfer-Encoding` headers, in addition to `Content-Length`, when following redirects. This prevents sending stale or invalid headers that could cause errors during the redirected request.

This commit fixes an issue where Unicode characters in Basic HTTP authentication credentials caused errors. It updates the `_basic_auth_str` function in `requests/auth.py` to properly decode byte strings before processing.

This commit updates the project documentation by removing a promotional link to a programming quiz from the main index page. It retains the notice that Requests 2.x is in maintenance mode, focusing solely on security fixes.

This commit adds a Bitcoin donation address to the project's documentation sidebar. It updates the sidebar introduction and logo templates to display the wallet link, allowing users to easily find the donation information.

This commit updates a broken documentation link in the community FAQ. It corrects the URL for the custom headers guide to point to the latest version of the Requests documentation instead of the master branch.

This commit fixes a minor formatting inconsistency in the `patch` function within `requests/api.py`. It removes an extra space before the `data` keyword argument in the internal request call, ensuring the code adheres to standard style guidelines.

This commit corrects the GitHub handle for Ian Cordasco in the project's author list. It updates the reference in the AUTHORS.rst file to point to the correct username, ensuring accurate attribution for core contributors.

This commit improves static typing for third-party imports in the requests library by adding missing typecheck dependencies to the project configuration. It removes unnecessary type ignore comments from modules like `__init__.py` and `compat.py`, ensuring cleaner type checking for imports such as chardet and cryptography.

This commit corrects type annotations for headers in the requests library to accurately reflect that they are mutable. It updates the HeadersType alias and the headers attribute in the Request and Session classes to use MutableMapping instead of read-only Mapping types.
This commit updates the AUTHORS.rst file to add Ed Summers to the list of contributors. It also corrects the file formatting by ensuring a proper newline at the end of the document.

This commit removes a trailing blank line from the main entry point in requests/help.py to satisfy flake8 linting rules. It ensures the module passes style checks without altering any functional behavior.

This commit reorders the Gittip donation widget within the documentation sidebar templates. It moves the widget to appear earlier in the sidebarintro.html and sidebarlogo.html files, adjusting its visual position for users.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation for the Transport Adapter. It corrects minor formatting inconsistencies in the text describing how to access the PreparedRequest object from a Response.

This commit adds a new CONTRIBUTING.md file to the repository. It provides guidelines for contributors, directing users to the official documentation and clarifying that the issue tracker is for bugs and features, not general questions.

This commit adds a test to the RequestsTestSuite in tests/test_requests.py. It verifies that the library accepts custom objects with string representations as valid URLs, supporting use cases like the furl library.

This commit introduces the MultiDict and TypeConversionDict classes to the requests.structures module. It provides a dictionary-like structure that supports multiple values for a single key and allows type conversion when retrieving items.

This commit introduces an automated release process that triggers a GitHub Actions workflow when version tags are pushed. It replaces manual uploads by using trusted publishing to securely distribute artifacts to PyPI, including upload attestations. The changes are implemented in the publish workflow file and the Makefile.
This commit updates the project's README documentation. It replaces a static feature list table with a CSS style block, likely to improve the visual presentation of the feature grid.
This commit updates the community support documentation to improve readability by breaking text into smaller paragraphs. It also corrects a typo and adds a list of CVE identifiers to the guide.
This commit updates the AUTHORS file to add James Rowe and Daniel Schauenberg to the list of contributors. It also fixes a missing newline at the end of the file.
Adds a Travis CI configuration to run the test suite on Python 2.6, 2.7, and 3.2. It sets the environment variable for the HTTP bin URL and executes the lazy make target.

This commit updates the project's README to fix a broken "Say Thanks" badge link. The change corrects the URL in the documentation file, ensuring the badge displays properly for users viewing the project page.

Adds a test to the RequestsTestSuite in test_requests.py that verifies session objects correctly persist cookies across multiple requests. This ensures that cookies set during a session are automatically sent in subsequent calls without manual reconfiguration.

This commit updates the setup script to use single quotes for file paths, improving consistency with the project's style. It modifies the file opening logic in setup.py to ensure the version file is read correctly.

This commit updates the documentation file for project authors by adding an image reference. It modifies the authors.rst file to include a link to a photo, enhancing the visual presentation of the contributor list.

This commit fixes a compatibility issue in the `stream_decompress` function within `requests/utils.py`. It ensures the decompression buffer is initialized with a proper bytes object, preventing potential errors when handling compressed data streams.

This commit adds a new section to the developer documentation outlining the process for contributing to the project. It details steps for checking issues, forking the repository, writing tests, and submitting pull requests. The changes are located in the `docs/dev/todo.rst` file.

This commit simplifies the HTTPDigestAuth class in requests/auth.py by removing a redundant attribute lookup. It directly accesses the value of the 401 call counter in the handle_401 method, improving code clarity without changing behavior.

This commit modifies the setup.py file to restrict the inclusion of the oreos package to Python 2 environments only. It ensures that the package list is dynamically adjusted based on the Python version, preventing unnecessary dependencies from being installed on Python 3.

This commit updates the lock-threads GitHub Action from version 4.0.1 to 5.0.0 in the lock-issues workflow. The change ensures the repository uses the latest major version of the dependency for locking inactive issues and pull requests.

This commit fixes a crash in the HTTPAdapter.send method that occurred when sending chunked uploads. It corrects the variable used to retrieve the response, ensuring the connection object is properly referenced. A new test verifies that generator-based data can be safely posted.

This update ensures compatibility with Python 3.3 by addressing changes in the standard library's cookie handling. It modifies the MockRequest class in requests/cookies.py to correctly map the unverifiable attribute to the existing is_unverifiable method, preventing potential errors during cookie policy verification.

This commit removes an outdated warning in the community documentation stating that the Debian package for Requests was stuck on an old version. The note is deleted because the package is now up to date. The change affects the `docs/community/out-there.rst` file.
This commit adds Tom Moertel to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS.rst file. It updates the project's credit list to acknowledge his patches and suggestions.
This commit updates the `requests` package to import `urllib3` instead of `poster`. It changes the underlying HTTP library used by the module, affecting how requests are handled internally.

The `post` and `put` functions in `requests/core.py` now accept a `multipart_files` parameter. This allows users to upload files using multipart encoding by passing a dictionary of filenames and file-like objects.

This commit updates the Pipfile to use the new syntax for package names and local editable installs. It renames the local project entry to a hash-based identifier and adjusts package names to lowercase, ensuring compatibility with the updated pip-tools format.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the `requests/auth.py` module that prevented the library from loading. It replaces a broken conditional import block with a try-except structure to safely handle missing dependencies.

The PyTest command in setup.py now dynamically determines the number of parallel test workers based on the available CPU cores instead of using a fixed value of eight. This adjustment allows the test suite to better utilize the resources of the Travis CI environment.

The RequestsCookieJar class in requests/cookies.py now consistently returns lists from its keys, values, and items methods, matching the Python 2 dictionary API. This change removes conditional logic that previously returned iterators on Python 3, ensuring predictable behavior for users accessing cookie data.

This commit updates the `SessionRedirectMixin` in `requests/sessions.py` to include the final request and response objects when raising a `TooManyRedirects` exception. This allows users to inspect the specific HTTP interaction that triggered the redirect limit error.
This commit adds Jeremy Selie to the project's list of contributors. It updates the AUTHORS file to recognize his patches and suggestions alongside existing contributors.
This commit updates the version number of the charade package from 1.0.0 to 1.0.1. It also removes trailing whitespace from several lines in the module's initialization file.

This commit adds descriptive comments to the default configuration values in the `requests/defaults.py` module. It clarifies the purpose of settings such as timeout, redirect limits, and connection pool sizes for users and developers.

This commit enables pickling of `Session` and `HTTPAdapter` objects by implementing custom serialization methods. It ensures that connection pool settings are correctly restored after unpickling, allowing users to serialize and deserialize request sessions without errors.

This commit updates the `_encode_files` method in `requests/models.py` to handle file data more consistently with parameter encoding. It ensures that non-iterable values are treated as single items and that string fields and values are explicitly encoded to UTF-8 bytes.

This commit fixes an issue where running tests via the Makefile would incorrectly include test files from a local virtual environment, causing errors. It updates the Makefile to explicitly target the main test file, ensuring only the project's tests are executed.

This commit fixes a bug in the HTTPDigestAuth class where the digest authentication header was not recognized if the "Digest" prefix used different capitalization. The handle_401 method now uses a case-insensitive regular expression to strip the prefix, ensuring the challenge is parsed correctly.

This commit fixes a bug where the `resolve_redirects` method in `requests/sessions.py` incorrectly raised an `InvalidSchema` exception for URLs with uppercase schemes. It now normalizes the scheme to lowercase before processing, allowing redirects to resolve successfully regardless of the original capitalization.
This commit initializes the project by adding a README file. It establishes the repository's initial documentation structure.

This commit updates the community support documentation to include PGP key fingerprints for project maintainers. It adds the fingerprint for sigmavirus24 and a placeholder for lukasa to the support guide.

This commit updates the documentation for the `_Request` class in `requests/core.py`. It adds a docstring explaining that the class is a hidden wrapper around `urllib2.Request` that allows for manual setting of HTTP methods.

This commit fixes an issue where HTTP response encodings were not being set correctly, potentially causing text decoding errors. It updates the `build_response` method in the `HTTPAdapter` class to apply the encoding derived from response headers.

This commit initializes the project's documentation infrastructure by adding the necessary Sphinx configuration and build scripts. It introduces the core files required to generate the project's documentation, including the main index and build automation.

This commit fixes a potential double-release error in the HTTPConnectionPool class. It ensures that the connection is not passed to the response object if the pool is already scheduled to release it in a finally block.

This commit makes the `Request` class in `requests/core.py` more robust by using safe attribute access when building HTTP responses. It prevents potential crashes if the underlying response object lacks expected properties like `code`, `headers`, or `url`.

This commit fixes an issue where request hooks were lost during redirects. It updates the `resolve_redirects` method in `requests/sessions.py` to explicitly pass hooks to the new request. A clarifying comment is also added to `requests/models.py` regarding hook ordering.

This commit adds a promotional sidebar section to the documentation templates. It informs users that the Hitchhiker's Guide to Python is available as a physical book and includes a link to purchase it.
This commit merges changes into the requests library, specifically updating the async module. It removes outdated metadata variables and reformats the public API list in requests/async.py.
This commit adds a new TooManyRedirects exception to the requests library. It modifies the Request class to raise this error when a request exceeds thirty redirects, preventing infinite loops.
This commit adds a Flattr donation button and support request section to the documentation sidebar. It also updates the sidebar link text to reference the Read the Docs version of the site.

This commit updates the documentation template to clarify the nature of the sponsored content. It changes the label in the `hacks.html` file from "Sponsored by" to "Sponsored Ad by" for better transparency.

The `resolve_redirects` method in `requests/sessions.py` now creates a copy of the incoming request before processing redirects. This change ensures that the original request object remains unmodified, preventing potential side effects when the session handles multiple redirect steps.

This commit fixes a bug where uploading a zero-length file incorrectly forced chunked transfer encoding, causing failures on services like S3. The change modifies the `prepare_body` method in `requests/models.py` to only use chunked uploads when the file length is genuinely unknown.

This commit refactors the Requests library to use a centralized compatibility module for Python 2 and 3 differences. It updates imports in `auth.py`, `models.py`, and `utils.py` to rely on `compat` for functions like `urlparse` and `StringIO`. This ensures consistent behavior across Python versions for request handling and response processing.

This commit cleans up the imports in the requests models module by removing unused compatibility aliases and adding a new utility import. It also removes unnecessary blank lines from the Request and Response classes to improve code readability.
This commit removes the project's Travis CI configuration file, ending automated testing on that platform. Users will no longer see build status updates from Travis for this repository.

This commit removes trailing whitespace from documentation files and the Travis CI configuration. It cleans up the project to prevent unnecessary changes in future diffs, ensuring that unrelated edits do not introduce spurious whitespace modifications.

This commit adds a new `strict_mode` configuration option to the `requests` library's defaults module. When enabled, it instructs the library to strictly adhere to RFC standards, such as handling POST redirects correctly.

This commit updates the idna package within the requests library to use relative imports instead of absolute imports. This change ensures the module correctly references its internal components, preventing potential import errors when the package is used as a standalone module.

This commit updates the project's README to display the full-size logo instead of the smaller version. The change affects the main documentation file, ensuring the visual branding is more prominent for users viewing the repository.

This commit fixes import errors in the requests package by switching to absolute imports. It updates the main module initialization to correctly reference internal submodules, ensuring the library loads without failing.

This commit updates the community documentation to clarify that Kenneth Reitz is the author who tweets about Requests releases. It also removes the section describing the project's mailing list subscription process.
This commit updates the AUTHORS file to include Andrey Petrov in a new Urllib3 subsection. It restores contributor credit that was previously present in a backup version of the file.
This commit removes a redundant self-referencing link from the documentation sidebar. It updates the sidebarintro.html template to clean up the navigation menu.

The test suite in test_requests.py now respects an HTTPBIN_URL environment variable to specify the target server, defaulting to the local port if unset. This allows users to run tests against a remote HTTPBin instance, such as on Windows, without requiring a local server.

This commit updates the urllib3 collections module to import the MutableMapping class from a new internal package instead of the standard library. This change ensures the codebase uses the updated collection definitions, likely to support specific behavior or compatibility requirements within the library.

This commit updates the documentation for the PreparedRequest class in the advanced user guide. It clarifies how to use Session.prepare_request() to ensure session-level state, such as cookies, is correctly applied to the request.

This commit adds a `url` attribute to the `Response` object in the `requests` module, allowing users to detect redirects by checking the final URL after a request. It also corrects the `Request` class to strictly compare the HTTP method against uppercase 'GET' instead of using a case-insensitive check.

This documentation update clarifies that SNI support is available in Python 2.7.9 and later, correcting the previous statement that it was exclusive to Python 3. The change updates the FAQ to reflect that native SNI support was backported to Python 2.7.9 as part of PEP 466.

This commit adds test coverage for HTTP keep-alive behavior in both direct and proxy connection scenarios. It introduces a dummy server module to track connection counts, allowing verification that requests reuse connections as expected.

This commit removes unused imports from the test suite to clean up the codebase. It specifically deletes the `merge_cookies` import from `tests/test_requests.py` and the `cookiejar_from_dict` import from `tests/test_utils.py`.

The Request class in requests/models.py now accepts a hooks parameter to support response hooking. It also fixes a crash when redirect responses lack cookies and corrects the keep-alive configuration key to use an underscore.

This commit fixes a documentation example in the advanced user guide that was missing the expected output from a hook. It adds the missing URL to the example in the `docs/user/advanced.rst` file to ensure the documentation accurately reflects the behavior.

This commit updates the project's README to replace the word "secured" with "protected" when describing the Python Software Foundation's role. It also removes a decorative image and adjusts whitespace formatting within the documentation file.

The HTTPDigestAuth class now stores all authentication state in thread-local storage to prevent data corruption when used across multiple threads. This change ensures that nonce counts and challenge data are isolated per thread, improving the reliability of concurrent HTTP requests.

The `guess_filename` function in `requests/utils.py` now correctly handles file objects with non-string name attributes, preventing crashes when sending such files. This fixes an issue where passing certain file-like objects, such as those from CherryPy, would cause the request to fail.

This commit makes the cookie jar in PreparedRequest a private implementation detail by renaming the public cookies attribute to _cookies. It updates HTTPDigestAuth and SessionRedirectMixin to use the new internal name, preventing users from directly accessing or modifying the cookie jar.
This commit updates the package manifest to include the test_requests.py file in the distribution. This ensures the test module is properly packaged when the project is built or installed.
This commit removes a stray "Note" label from the quickstart documentation. It cleans up the user guide by deleting an unnecessary text artifact that did not contain any actual content.

This documentation update fixes a shell command in the advanced user guide that would fail in Zsh due to unquoted brackets. The change adds quotes around the package name in the pip install instruction to prevent wildcard interpretation.

This commit standardizes the documentation for the `json` parameter in the `post`, `put`, and `patch` functions within `requests/api.py`. It clarifies that the parameter accepts a JSON-serializable Python object, ensuring consistency across the API's docstrings.

This commit adds a test to verify that HTTP HEAD responses with empty bodies are handled correctly. It ensures that accessing the content and text attributes of such responses does not cause errors. The change is located in the RequestsTestSuite within the test module.

This commit removes the explicit `__all__` list from the `requests/async.py` module. It changes how the module's public API is defined, likely relying on the wildcard import from `core` to determine available names instead of a hardcoded list.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to demonstrate how to send string data as file uploads using the requests library. It clarifies the behavior for users who need to transmit text content as a file attachment in a POST request.

This commit updates the documentation for the `requests` library to clarify that SSL certificate verification is enabled by default. It corrects a misleading example that suggested users must explicitly set `verify=True` to enable this security feature. Additionally, the documentation now uses a different example domain to ensure the error message remains accurate.
This commit corrects spelling errors in the project documentation. It fixes typos in the sidebar introduction template and the advanced user guide, ensuring accurate text for readers.
This commit adds a public HOOKS tuple to the requests/hooks.py module, listing the available hook points. It allows users to programmatically discover which hooks are supported by the library.

This commit adds a failing test to the RequestsTestCase in test_requests.py. It verifies that cookies are correctly sent when a request is redirected, ensuring the session maintains state across HTTP redirects.

This commit fixes an issue in the HTTPAdapter.send method where an incorrect timeout value was passed to the connection pool. It now uses a dedicated default pool timeout instead of the request timeout, preventing unexpected connection delays.

This commit removes the Requests stickers advertisement from the documentation sidebar. It replaces that link with a new, styled section for native sponsor ads, allowing for dynamic branding and links.

The Request class in requests/core.py now calls a new _checks method before sending a request. Additionally, the send method wraps the URL opening logic in a try-except block to raise a RequestException if the connection fails.

This commit improves the documentation build process by adding a check for the Sphinx executable in the Makefile. It provides a clear error message if Sphinx is not installed or not in the system path, preventing confusing build failures.

This commit updates the `requests.packages` module to correctly map `chardet` and `charset_normalizer` imports. It ensures these dependencies are properly aliased within the `requests` namespace, preventing import errors when the library is used.
This commit updates the project's history documentation to correct a formatting error in a code example. It adds a new, improved import statement example to the release notes.

This commit restores test files that were accidentally lost during a previous merge. It re-adds the unit and integration test suites for the requests library, ensuring that API and integration tests are available again.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to improve SSL error handling and clarify timeout documentation. It introduces a BaseSSLError exception class in connectionpool.py and refines the HTTPConnectionPool and HTTPResponse modules for better consistency.

This commit fixes an issue where authentication credentials were incorrectly stripped during redirects involving default ports. It updates the `should_strip_auth` method in `SessionRedirectMixin` to recognize when both the old and new URLs use their scheme's default port, preventing unnecessary credential removal.

Updates the lock-threads GitHub Action from version 3.0.0 to 4.0.1 in the lock-issues workflow. This major version bump ensures the repository uses the latest stable release for automatically locking inactive issues and pull requests.

This commit adds Python 3.12 support to the project's metadata and testing configuration. It updates the setup file to include the 3.12 classifier and modifies the tox configuration to run tests on Python 3.12.

This commit fixes an issue where accessing the content of an empty HTTP response would result in a `None` value instead of an empty byte string. The `Response` class in `requests/models.py` now correctly returns an empty byte sequence for zero-length responses.

The `morsel_to_cookie` function in `requests/cookies.py` now correctly adjusts cookie expiration times by subtracting the local timezone offset. This fixes a bug where cookies were treated as expired or valid at the wrong times due to incorrect timestamp conversion.

This commit removes outdated installation instructions for the gevent library from the user documentation. It cleans up the install guide by deleting the section that previously explained how to set up gevent for concurrent requests.
This commit removes an unused import from the requests/auth.py module. It cleans up the code by eliminating a redundant reference to the bytes type, which does not affect user-facing behavior.

This commit fixes an issue where authentication credentials were not properly applied during redirects. It ensures the `Request` class correctly assigns the provided authentication arguments in the `send` method.

This commit adds a docstring to the `test_get_auth_from_url` method within the `UtilsTestCase` class in `test_requests.py`. The comment clarifies that the test verifies the correct extraction of username and password from well-encoded URIs according to RFC 3986.

This commit updates the documentation for the `request` function in `requests/api.py` to clarify the `allow_redirects` parameter. It corrects the description to accurately reflect that redirection is enabled or disabled for all HTTP methods, not just POST, PUT, and DELETE.

This commit updates the project history to note the removal of a redundant generator for chunked transfer encoding. It also records a fix where the Response.ok method no longer raises a Timeout Exception when safe_mode is enabled.

This commit restricts GitHub Actions workflows to the minimum necessary token permissions, enhancing security by preventing excessive access. It updates the codeql-analysis, lint, and run-tests workflow files to explicitly define read and write scopes for specific actions.

This commit resolves Python 3.6 deprecation warnings caused by invalid escape sequences in docstrings. It updates the `get`, `post`, and other request methods in `requests/api.py`, as well as the `Session` class in `requests/sessions.py`, to use raw strings.
This commit cleans up code examples in the advanced user documentation. It simplifies the formatting of the Request constructor call to improve readability.
This commit updates the community sponsors documentation to include a note that Slack is currently hiring. It adds a link to their careers page for interested users.
This commit adds a new contributor, "Dull Bananas," to the project's author list. It updates the AUTHORS.rst file to credit this individual for their patches and suggestions.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 2.12.1. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the package's initialization file to reflect the new release.

This commit adds support for Python 3.14t (free-threading) to the project's continuous integration tests. It updates the test workflow to include the new version and adds a corresponding classifier to the project metadata.
Updates the CodeQL security analysis workflow to use version 4.33.0 of the github/codeql-action. This minor version bump refreshes the automated code scanning process in the repository's CI pipeline.

This commit simplifies error handling in the `Response.text` property of the `requests` library. It consolidates the exception handling for unicode decoding by catching both `LookupError` and `TypeError` in a single block, removing the need for a separate fallback encoding step.

This commit updates the project's README file by removing a blank line and deleting the download and version badge images. These changes clean up the documentation layout without affecting the library's code or functionality.
This commit removes trailing whitespace from the `curl_from_request` function in `requests/utils.py`. It cleans up the source code formatting without altering the function's behavior or logic.
This commit adds a new "lazy" target to the Makefile. It allows developers to run the test suite for the requests module using nosetests with color output.
Updates the flake8 linter configuration in the pre-commit setup. It switches the repository source from GitLab to GitHub and upgrades the tool version from 4.0.1 to 6.0.0.

This commit fixes a typo in the docstring for the `cookiejar_from_dict` function within the `requests/utils.py` module. It corrects the spelling of "dictionary" to ensure accurate documentation for users.

This commit fixes a crash in the `Request` class when handling URLs that are already strings, preventing unnecessary decoding errors. It also updates the `Response` class to use a more efficient method for joining content bytes and corrects the test file path in the Makefile.

This commit updates the RequestsTestCase in test_requests.py to use native string keys for HTTP headers instead of ASCII-encoded bytes. It removes the need for explicit encoding when accessing header values like 'accept' and 'Accept' in the test suite.

This commit updates the HTTP status code names in the requests library to align with RFC 7238 terminology. It renames the 308 status from "resume" to "permanent_redirect" and the 307 status from "temporary_moved" to "temporary_redirect" within the status codes module and session redirect logic.

This commit updates the project documentation and internal comments to reflect the removal of Python 3.3 support. It clarifies that the library now officially supports Python 3.4 through 3.6, ensuring users are aware of the current compatibility range.
This commit updates the linting workflow to use the latest Python setup action and adds a ten-minute timeout to prevent stalled jobs. It also bumps the pre-commit configuration to a newer version.
Adds a new test module, test_iteration.py, containing the IterationTestCase class. It includes a basic assertion test and a test that prepares and sends a GET request using the requests library.

The `settings` context manager in the `requests` module is refactored to accept arbitrary keyword arguments instead of a single timeout value. This change generalizes the mechanism for temporarily modifying and restoring module-level configuration variables.

This commit fixes test failures in the Requests library by replacing the deprecated `assertAlmostEquals` method with `assertEquals` in the test suite. It also removes extraneous blank lines from the session and structures modules to clean up the codebase.

This commit updates the test suite for the requests module to verify that specific URL preparation scenarios correctly return a 425 status code. It adds assertions to the TestPreparingURLs class to ensure the expected behavior is maintained.

This commit optimizes the `RequestEncodingMixin._encode_files` method in `requests/models.py` by preventing unnecessary data duplication. It directly passes string or byte inputs to the request field instead of wrapping them in memory streams, resulting in a 30-40% performance improvement.

This commit disables zip-safe installation for the package by setting the `zip_safe` flag to `False` in `setup.py`. This ensures the package is extracted to disk rather than run directly from a zip archive, preventing potential import errors or file access issues.

This commit adds a test to the RequestsTestSuite in test_requests.py to verify that session-level headers are correctly merged with request-specific headers. It ensures that when a new User-Agent header is passed to a request, it overrides the persistent session header as expected.

This commit updates the Travis CI configuration to explicitly install the nose testing framework. It resolves a build failure where the test runner was missing, ensuring the test suite can execute properly during continuous integration.
This commit updates the project's contributor list by adding a new name to the "Patches and Suggestions" section. It modifies the AUTHORS.rst file to recognize Om Prakash Kumar as a contributor.

The project's README now displays a smaller logo image instead of the previous sidebar graphic. This change updates the documentation's visual appearance by referencing a new, compact logo file added to the static assets.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to a newer version. It adds a stream method to the HTTPResponse class for efficient data reading and introduces an is_fp_closed utility function to check file pointer status.

This commit fixes a relative import error in the `requests/sessions.py` module to ensure compatibility with Python 3. It resolves a failure that would occur when initializing a session by correcting the import path for the `HTTPAdapter` class.

This commit updates the Twitter Streaming API documentation to use OAuth 1.0a authentication instead of the deprecated XAuth method. It corrects the example in the advanced user guide to reflect the new API requirements and endpoint version.

This commit refactors the argument handling logic within the Session class in requests/sessions.py. It replaces the previous method of merging instance attributes with keyword arguments by introducing a dedicated collector for session-specific parameters. This change streamlines how request arguments are prepared before being passed to the underlying request methods.

This commit fixes the package installation process by removing the bundled chardet and idna dependencies from the setup configuration. Users will no longer see these specific subpackages listed during installation, resolving potential conflicts with external dependency management. The change modifies the package list in the setup.py file.
This commit fixes a documentation formatting error in the quickstart guide. It corrects the rendering of the `chunk_size` parameter name in the user documentation.
This release updates the requests library to version 0.14.1, adding compatibility with Python 3.3. It also simplifies the default accept-encoding header and includes general bug fixes.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library from 0.3.0 to 0.3.1. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the core module to reflect the new release.

This commit reorders the Gittip donation widget within the documentation sidebar templates. It moves the widget to appear earlier in the sidebarintro.html and sidebarlogo.html files, adjusting its visual position for users viewing the site.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to explain how the requests library handles repeated response headers. It clarifies that multiple values for the same header are combined into a single comma-separated string, in accordance with RFC 7230.
This commit corrects a typo in the docstring for the `Request.send` method within the `requests` module. It changes the word "of" to "if" to accurately describe the return value behavior.

This commit adds a `support_http0.9` flag to the `requests` library, allowing users to disable support for legacy HTTP 0.9 responses. By default, the flag remains true to preserve existing behavior, but setting it to false enables strict validation of the status line. This change affects the `Session` class and the `request` function.

This commit allows the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to accept raw byte strings as file values in multipart uploads. Previously, passing a string instead of a file object would cause an error, but now the library automatically wraps it in a `StringIO` object. A new test verifies that posting string data as files works correctly.
This commit updates the project's contributor list by adding Ed Morley to the "Patches and Suggestions" section. It modifies the AUTHORS.rst file to acknowledge this new contributor.

Adds a `prepare` method to the `Request` class in `requests/models.py`. This method returns a deep copy of the request object, allowing users to create independent copies of request configurations without modifying the original.

The project removes the requirements.txt file, eliminating the pinned list of dependencies for tools like Sphinx and pytest. This change simplifies the repository structure by deleting a file that is no longer needed for the build or test process.

This commit updates the vulnerability reporting documentation to reflect a change in the primary contact person and their PGP key. It also adds a new entry for a security fix released in version 2.20.0.

This commit corrects a typo in the documentation for the `HTTPAdapter` class in the `requests` library. It fixes the parameter name in the docstring for the `send` method, changing "vert" to "cert" to accurately describe the SSL certificate argument.

This commit adds unit tests for the `requests.hooks` module to verify the behavior of the `dispatch_hook` function and the `default_hooks` factory. It ensures that hook lists correctly process data and that the default configuration returns an empty response list.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to clarify the benefits of using `async.map` over sequential `Request.send` calls. It explicitly notes that `async.map` guarantees the execution of the `response` hook, improving understanding of asynchronous request handling.

This commit fixes an issue where passing byte strings as query parameters resulted in incorrect URL encoding. The `_encode_params` method in the `RequestEncodingMixin` class now converts byte data to a native string before processing. A new test verifies that byte parameters are correctly encoded in the final request URL.

Replaces the previous list-based authentication handling with a dedicated AuthManager class in requests/core.py. This update adds support for all authentication types supported by Python, improving how credentials are stored and applied during requests.

This commit updates the .gitignore file to exclude compiled Python bytecode files from version control. It also corrects a missing newline at the end of the file, ensuring proper formatting for the existing pylint.txt entry.
This commit fixes a spelling error in the Requests documentation. It corrects the word "Priminent" to "Prominent" in the sponsor benefits list within the community sponsors page.

Adds a test to the RequestsTestSuite that verifies HTTP Basic authentication works when credentials are passed as a tuple. This ensures the requests library correctly handles tuple-formatted auth parameters for GET requests.

This commit updates the available hook points in the requests library, replacing the "args" hook with "pre_prepare" and "post_prepare" in the HOOKS tuple within requests/hooks.py. It also comments out several unused imports in requests/models.py.

This commit updates the contributing documentation to use a more emphatic and direct tone when discouraging certain codebase changes. It modifies the text in the contributing guide to clearly state that specific actions are not permitted.

This commit fixes documentation references by ensuring `ConnectTimeout` and `ReadTimeout` are accessible at the top level of the `requests` package. It updates the imports in `requests/__init__.py` to include these exception classes, resolving discrepancies in the API documentation.

This commit fixes an issue in the `PreparedRequest` class where the `prepare_content_length` method incorrectly overwrote an explicitly set `Content-Length` header for non-GET or HEAD requests. It now only calculates the length if the header is not already present, preserving user-defined values.
The setup.py module now reads the project description from Markdown files instead of reStructuredText. This updates the package metadata to reflect the new documentation format.

The `Request.copy` method in `requests/models.py` now creates shallow copies of mutable fields like headers and parameters. This prevents modifications to a copied request from unintentionally altering the original request's data.
This commit corrects the paragraph formatting of the Urllib3/MIT license text within the NOTICE file. It ensures the legal disclaimer and permission clauses are properly structured for readability.

This commit updates the legal character set for cookie names in the `requests/packages/oreos/monkeys.py` module. It adds the at-sign to the list of permitted characters, allowing cookies with names containing this symbol to be processed correctly.

This commit fixes an issue where unpickling a Response object would cause an AttributeError if the raw attribute was accessed. It ensures the raw attribute is explicitly set to None during the unpickling process in the Response class.

This commit moves the `test_chunked_upload` test from `tests/test_requests.py` to `tests/test_lowlevel.py`. It reorganizes the test suite to better categorize low-level functionality, ensuring the test for sending generator data with chunked encoding resides in the appropriate module.

This commit updates the documentation to remove the claim that the Library of Congress uses the Requests library. It corrects the testimonial section in the project's index file to reflect that only Twitter is listed as an internal user.

This commit fixes a bug in the `SessionRedirectMixin` where redirect history entries could incorrectly reference themselves. It ensures that each response in the history only contains the preceding responses, preventing circular references. A new test verifies that the history structure is correct for multi-step redirects.

This commit corrects the installation command for the Requests library in the community documentation. It updates the `out-there.rst` file to specify the correct package name, ensuring users can successfully install the dependency via apt-get.

This commit removes a network-dependent test from the RequestsTestCase in test_requests.py. It eliminates a check that made a live HTTP request, aligning the test suite with a new approach that relies on the request.prepare method to avoid external network calls.

The `morsel_to_cookie` function in `requests/cookies.py` now directly parses the Expires header string without first checking if it is a string type. This simplifies the logic for converting cookie expiration dates, relying on the standard format defined by the RFC.

This commit updates the Travis CI configuration to remove the conditional execution of the readme test for Python versions other than 2.6. The change simplifies the build script by eliminating the version check, ensuring the readme test runs consistently across all supported Python environments.

The `prepend_scheme_if_needed` function in `requests/utils.py` now uses `urllib3`'s `parse_url` instead of the standard library's `urlparse` to handle URL components. This change addresses a parsing defect where `urlparse` incorrectly identified the network location in certain URLs, ensuring more reliable scheme prepending.

This commit updates the AUTHORS.rst file to include Twitter profile links for two contributors. It adds social media handles for Alexander Karpinsky and Michael Becker to their respective entries in the credits list.
This commit updates the README to document a workaround for cloning the repository. It instructs users to use a specific Git flag to ignore malformed commit timestamps, preventing clone failures.
This commit adds Mikko Ohtamaa to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS file. It updates the project's credit list to acknowledge his contributions.
This release adds SOCKS proxy support to the requests library, allowing users to route traffic through SOCKS proxies. It also updates the bundled urllib3 dependency to version 1.15.1.

This commit adds a docstring to the Session class in the requests module. It also includes minor formatting adjustments with blank lines. These changes improve code documentation and readability without altering functionality.

This commit corrects a typo in the documentation string within the requests.exceptions module. It ensures the text accurately references the correct module name, improving the clarity of the library's error handling documentation.

This commit updates the Pipfile.lock to use the correct PyPI package index URL and refreshes the file's hash. It ensures the dependency lock file is valid and consistent with the project's configuration.

This commit implements basic handling configuration and auto-authentication in the `requests` module. It adds the `head` method to the `Request` class and initializes the `auth` attribute. This commit contains no code changes or file modifications. It serves as a placeholder or marker in the repository history without altering any behavior or functionality.

This commit cleans up documentation for request defaults in the requests library. It removes outdated entries for timeout and unicode decoding from the defaults module and fixes a typo in the max_redirects description.

This commit adds a new script to automate the project's continuous integration testing process. It runs the test suite with coverage reporting and executes static code analysis, saving the results to a file for review.

This commit removes the deprecated tox configuration file, which previously defined test environments for Python 2.5, 2.6, and 2.7. Users will no longer see these legacy Python versions listed when running tox commands.

This commit adds a documentation section to the project's README file. It provides users with a direct link to the official online documentation at python-requests.org, improving discoverability of the project's guides and reference materials.

This commit updates the project documentation to consolidate the list of companies using the library into a single sentence. It also corrects the reported download count from PyPI, increasing the figure from 100,000 to nearly 1,000,000.

This commit resolves a circular dependency by moving the `to_native_string` function from `requests/utils.py` to `requests/_internal_utils.py`. It updates `requests/cookies.py` to import the function from its new location, ensuring the module loads correctly without import errors.

This commit adds cookie support to the core HTTP request functions in the requests module. Users can now pass a cookie jar to get, post, put, delete, and head requests to maintain session state across calls.

This commit ensures the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` always includes a `Content-Length` header. It sets the value to zero for empty requests or the byte length of the body for non-empty ones, preventing missing headers during transmission.

This commit fixes a bug in the `_parse_content_type_header` function within `src/requests/utils.py` where malformed Content-Type headers caused incorrect parsing. It corrects the handling of parameter values to ensure they are properly extracted and stripped of surrounding characters.

This commit fixes a bug in the `PreparedRequest` class where the error message for invalid URLs could fail to display correctly. It ensures the URL is properly converted to a native string before formatting, improving the clarity of the error message shown to users.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Request` class where file fields were incorrectly appended to the wrong list during encoding. It ensures that file data is properly added to `new_fields` instead of `fields`, resolving issues with posting multiple values and files.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation for the requests library. It removes outdated examples of using a non-existent helper method and environment variables for proxy configuration. The text now clarifies that Python-level settings take precedence over environment variables.

This change updates the Response class in requests/models.py to correctly handle HTTP responses with multiple encoding values. Previously, the code only recognized gzip compression if it was the sole value, but now it detects gzip even when listed alongside other encodings.

The OAuth1 authentication handler now signs requests even when they lack a body, ensuring consistent signature generation for all HTTP methods. This change modifies the OAuth1 class in the requests.auth module to remove the previous condition that skipped signing for empty payloads.
This commit adds gunicorn to the project's dependency list. It ensures the web server is installed when setting up the environment.
This commit updates the AUTHORS.rst file to add Alexander Karpinsky to the list of contributors. It acknowledges his patches and suggestions to the project.
This commit adds a test to the RequestsTestCase class in test_requests.py. It verifies that sending a multipart POST request with unicode data and a file attachment returns a successful status code.
This commit updates the release notes to document recent changes. It highlights the addition of MD5-sess to Digest Auth and a fix for cookies not persisting when set via the functional API.
This commit removes the pyflakes static analysis step from the CI build process. It modifies the Makefile to stop generating a violations report, leaving only the test suite execution.

This commit updates the project documentation to reflect a higher download count for the Requests library. It changes the reported PyPI download total from one million to 1.5 million in the testimonials section.

This commit reverts a minor documentation typo in the CaseInsensitiveDict class within the requests library. It corrects the spacing in the docstring for the .lower() method reference, ensuring the text reads correctly without altering any functional behavior.

This commit updates the documentation for the `apparent_encoding` property in the `Response` class within `requests/models.py`. It adds a credit to Ian for the Charade library, which provides the encoding detection functionality.
This commit corrects a misspelling of the author's name in the documentation. It updates the "Articles & Talks" section in the community guide to properly credit Daniel Greenfeld.

This commit allows the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to accept file-like objects as body data. Users can now pass an open file stream directly to the `data` parameter, which the library will handle appropriately during encoding and sending.

This commit corrects a spelling error in the project's release history file. It fixes the typo "credentions" to "credentials" in the description of a previous bug fix related to authentication.
