This commit updates the project's changelog to reflect recent changes. It notes the expansion of experimental OAuth support, a speed fix for non-iterated content chunks, and the relocation of the pre_request hook for better usability.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to reflect a more detailed error message for request timeouts. It clarifies that the `requests.exceptions.Timeout` exception now includes specific connection and timeout values in its output.

The `patch` function in `requests/api.py` previously ignored the `data` argument, always sending an empty body. This fix ensures the provided data is correctly passed to the underlying request, allowing users to include payloads in PATCH requests.

This commit standardizes HTTP method names to lowercase strings within the requests library. It updates the get, head, and options functions in requests/api.py and the corresponding methods in the Session class in requests/sessions.py to ensure consistent behavior.

This commit fixes a logic error in the `HTTPAdapter` class within the `requests` library. It corrects the `cert_verify` method to properly handle certificate objects that are not strings, ensuring valid configurations are accepted instead of being rejected.
This commit adds a fundraising status line to the documentation sidebar templates. It displays a target amount and the current funds raised to users viewing the project's documentation pages.

This commit adds documentation to the quickstart guide explaining how to pass query parameters in GET requests using the `params` argument. It includes a practical example demonstrating how to encode a dictionary into the URL query string.

This commit updates the documentation homepage to replace a direct donation link with a referral link to a programming quiz. It encourages users to take the quiz, noting that a donation will be made to the project if they secure a job through the platform.

This commit reverts a previous merge that modified the documentation sidebar templates. It restores the original link URLs for the Quickstart, Advanced Usage, and other sections in the sidebarintro.html and sidebarlogo.html files.

This commit restructures the documentation by splitting the user guide into separate pages for installation, quickstart, and advanced usage. It updates the main index to link to these new sections and moves the API reference to the developer internals section.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Response.iter_lines` method where the final line of a response was truncated if it did not end with a newline. It ensures the trailing remainder is correctly yielded, preventing data loss for users processing incomplete final lines.

This commit introduces a new `FileModeWarning` to alert users when files are opened in text mode, which can cause length calculation errors. It updates the `requests` module to emit this warning by default, improving visibility into potential data handling issues.

This commit refactors the redirect handling logic in the `SessionRedirectMixin` class by extracting method modification rules into a new `rebuild_method` function. It adds tests to verify that HTTP redirects correctly change POST requests to GET while preserving HEAD requests, preparing the codebase for future strict mode support.

This commit updates the HTTPAdapter class in the requests library to explicitly pass the strict parameter to urllib3. It ensures that the underlying connection pool manager enforces strict HTTP protocol compliance during initialization.

The `Request` class in `requests/models.py` now accepts a `cookies` parameter instead of `cookiejar`. This change updates the internal attribute and handler logic to use the new name, aligning the API with standard cookie handling terminology.

This commit removes the custom randombytes utility from requests/utils.py and replaces its usage in the HTTPDigestAuth class with the standard os.urandom function. This change simplifies the codebase by relying on the built-in operating system API for generating secure random bytes.

This commit normalizes the casing of several development dependencies in the Pipfile, such as Sphinx and PySocks, to match standard package naming conventions. It also updates the corresponding lock file to reflect these changes and adjust related dependency versions.

This commit moves the pre_request hook execution earlier in the Request.send method to allow users to modify the request before it is fully prepared. This change enables overriding HTTP request behavior, such as handling cache matches, without wasting CPU time on unnecessary calculations.

This commit removes the deprecated `strict` parameter from the `init_poolmanager` method in the `HTTPAdapter` class. It cleans up the internal configuration for connection pools, ensuring compatibility with newer versions of the underlying HTTP library.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar to display "Stay Informed" instead of "Get Updates." The change affects the sidebarintro.html and sidebarlogo.html templates, altering the heading text visible to users browsing the site.

This commit updates the `Request` class in `requests/core.py` so that its `read` method delegates to the associated `Response` object instead of returning content directly. It also adds a new `read` method to the `Response` class to support this delegation.

The Session class in the requests module now includes a string representation method, allowing users to see a readable identifier when printing the object. This change also renames the module file from session.py to sessions.py.

This commit corrects the project title in the documentation sidebar templates to include the article "The." It also updates the sidebar introduction to explicitly state that proceeds are donated to the DjangoGirls organization.

This update clarifies that read timeout errors are no longer retried when a Session is configured with a positive max_retries value. The change is documented in the project's release history to inform users of this specific behavioral adjustment.

This commit fixes a documentation error in the advanced user guide where the `stream` parameter was incorrectly described as `False` for streaming responses. It corrects the instruction to set `stream` to `True` when using `iter_lines()`.

This commit adds a missing assertion to the `test_uppercase_scheme_redirect` test in `test_requests.py`. It verifies that the HTTP response status code is 200, ensuring the test correctly validates the behavior of the `TestCaseInsensitiveDict` class.

Adds a new utility function, `parse_header_links`, to the `requests.utils` module. This function parses HTTP Link header values into a dictionary of URLs and their associated parameters, enabling users to programmatically extract pagination or related resource links from response headers.

This commit corrects the documentation in the README to use the standard `requests` library name instead of the incorrect `request` in example code snippets. It ensures users see the proper module name when copying usage examples for HTTP methods like get, head, and put.

This commit updates the documentation comments in the `requests.api` module to use standard HTTP terminology. It replaces informal phrases like "GET parameters" and "POST data" with precise references to the query string and request body for functions such as `get` and `post`.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to highlight Requests' built-in OAuth support. It replaces the previous reference to the external requests-oauth library with examples demonstrating the native OAuth1 authentication class.

This commit removes the ability to use Cookie objects directly as keys when accessing or setting items in the RequestsCookieJar. Users can no longer pass a cookie instance to the __getitem__ or __setitem__ methods, requiring them to use string names instead.

This commit updates the project documentation to replace the Travis CI status badge with a new badge for the requests-trunk build. The change affects the README file, altering the visual indicator users see for the project's build status.
This commit updates the project's README documentation file. It adds a small HTML spacer element to adjust the page layout. No functional code or user-facing behavior is changed.

This commit removes unused Python version and platform detection flags from the requests.compat module. It cleans up the codebase by deleting obsolete variables that are no longer referenced, without changing any user-facing behavior.

This commit removes a warning log message from the `Response.json` method in `requests/models.py`. It also corrects a comment to reference the `chardet` library instead of `charade` when describing the fallback encoding behavior.

This commit updates the `RequestEncodingMixin` class in `requests/models.py` to use the standard `str` function instead of the internal `compat.builtin_str` helper. This change simplifies the code for encoding file fields within the `_encode_files` method without altering the underlying behavior.

This commit updates the Ruff linter version in the pre-commit configuration from 0.15.18 to 0.15.20. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the Ruff pre-commit hook for code quality checks.
This commit corrects a typo in the docstring of the `address_in_network` function within `requests/utils.py`. It changes the phrase "on IP" to "an IP" to improve the clarity of the documentation.

This commit corrects a typo in the README.md file by changing the invalid HTML attribute "alignment" to "align" for the download badge. This ensures the badge displays correctly centered in the project documentation.

This commit updates the vulnerability disclosure documentation by adding an image to the page. The change affects the `docs/community/vulnerabilities.rst` file, enhancing the visual presentation of the community guidelines.

This commit fixes a CI failure caused by an invalid file opening mode in the setup script. It corrects the `open` call in `setup.py` to properly specify the UTF-8 encoding when reading the version file.

This commit updates the project's changelog to document recent improvements. It notes the removal of the cgi module to speed up loading, the addition of SHA-256 and SHA-512 digest authentication support, and the normalization of adapter prefixes for URL comparison.

This commit fixes a bug in the HTTPAdapter where the URL scheme check incorrectly used a string prefix match. It now uses proper URL parsing to accurately identify the scheme, ensuring proxies are only bypassed for HTTPS requests.

This commit fixes file uploads failing when using HTTP digest authentication by encoding multipart data during request creation. The change modifies the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to process file data immediately, ensuring the content length is correctly calculated before authentication headers are generated.

This commit updates the dependency markers in setup.py to replace range-based Python version checks with explicit version equality checks. It ensures the win_inet_pton package is only installed for Python 2.6 and 2.7 on Windows, avoiding potential compatibility issues with other versions.
This commit adds Joseph McCullough to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS file. It also fixes a missing newline at the end of the file.

This commit improves the documentation for the `Session` class in the `requests` library. It clarifies the purpose and default type of the `cookies` attribute, helping users understand how outstanding cookies are managed within a session.

This commit updates the project documentation to reflect a new download milestone. It changes the reported PyPI download count for the Requests library from eight million to twelve million in the testimonials section.
This commit updates the test suite to use simplejson as a fallback when omnijson is unavailable. It ensures the request tests run successfully in environments lacking the omnijson dependency.

This commit adds documentation for the `close` method within the `Response` class in the `requests` module. It clarifies that the method releases the underlying connection back to the pool and notes that it typically does not need to be called explicitly by users.

This commit fixes a crash in the `Session.send` method of the `requests` library that occurred when handling redirects. It prevents an unhandled `StopIteration` exception from being raised when the redirect resolution chain is exhausted.

This commit improves the visual spacing around code blocks in the documentation. It updates the `hacks.html` template to add specific padding to highlighted preformatted text, resulting in better readability for users viewing the docs.

This commit fixes broken documentation links in the `HTTPAdapter`, `request`, and `Session` classes. It replaces direct links to HTML files with Sphinx cross-references to ensure the "timeouts" section is correctly accessible in the generated documentation.

This commit adds a failing test to the RequestsTestSuite in test_requests.py. It verifies that the requests library correctly handles Unicode characters in HTTP headers, specifically targeting a bug in Python 2.x environments.

This commit updates the top-level docstring in the `requests` package to provide a clearer description and practical usage examples. It replaces the minimal header with detailed instructions for making GET and POST requests, improving the initial user experience.
This commit updates the Ruff linter version in the pre-commit configuration from v0.15.9 to v0.15.11. It ensures the project uses the latest available release for code quality checks.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to clarify how to modify request bodies and headers after preparation. It also corrects a formatting error in the file upload section to ensure code examples display correctly.

This commit fixes a bug in the `SessionMixin.resolve_redirects` method within `requests/sessions.py` where the response object was not being yielded correctly. It ensures that the final response is properly returned to the user when handling HTTP redirects.

This commit updates the documentation to reflect that Requests now officially supports Python 3.5 and later, rather than the previous range of 3.4 through 3.8. It clarifies the supported versions in the README and FAQ to prevent user confusion about compatibility.

This commit fixes a compatibility issue in the test suite for Python 2.6, where the `assertNotIn` method was unavailable. It updates the `test_no_content_length` method in `RequestsTestCase` to use a standard boolean assertion instead, ensuring the tests run correctly on older Python versions.

This commit fixes an issue where sending non-string data alongside files caused errors in Python 3. The `_encode_files` method in `requests/models.py` now avoids converting byte strings to text, ensuring multipart requests work correctly with mixed data types.
This commit removes the html5lib dependency from the project's requirements file. It likely addresses installation issues or conflicts caused by this specific package version.

This commit removes an outdated reference to a deleted test file from the package manifest. It ensures the distribution build process no longer attempts to include a non-existent file, preventing potential packaging errors. The change affects the MANIFEST.in configuration file.

The `super_len` function in `requests/utils.py` now handles failed seek operations gracefully. Previously, a file-like object that could not be seeked would raise an error, but it now returns a length of zero instead.

This commit adds a test to the RequestsTestSuite in test_requests.py that verifies HTTP basic authentication works correctly. It ensures that when credentials are registered for a domain, subsequent requests to that domain successfully authenticate and return a valid response.

The `Request` class in `requests/core.py` now accepts configuration arguments directly during initialization, allowing users to set properties like URL and headers without manual assignment. This change also updates the module's helper functions to support these new constructor parameters.

This commit restores the original ordering of data and parameters in the `Request` class within `requests/models.py`. It ensures that form fields are processed before file uploads, correcting the sequence in which request body components are encoded.

This commit updates the project's FAQ documentation to list Python 3.4 as a supported version. It clarifies the compatibility status for users checking the official requirements. No code changes were required for this update.

This commit adds a new JavaScript module to the documentation site that handles the loading and display of native advertisements. It introduces functions to initialize ad zones, manage configuration options, and render ad content within the page.

This commit updates the project to support version 2.6 of the idna library. It modifies the dependency constraints in setup.py to allow the newer version, resolving compatibility issues for users who have upgraded their environment.
The `Response` class now returns its `url` attribute as a Unicode string instead of a byte string. This change ensures consistent text handling for response URLs across the library.

This commit corrects the formatting of an RFC quotation in the quickstart documentation. It removes unnecessary blockquote markers from the text, ensuring the citation displays correctly in the rendered user guide.

This commit updates the documentation for the RequestsCookieJar class and related cookie utilities. It adds the class to the API reference and refines the docstrings in the cookies module to improve clarity.

This commit adds a test case to the TestGuessJSONUTF class in tests/test_utils.py to verify that UTF-8 files with a byte order mark are correctly identified as UTF-8. It also updates .gitignore to exclude virtual environment and build directories.

This commit updates the .gitignore file to exclude Jenkins build artifacts from version control. It adds coverage.xml, nosetests.xml, and pylint.txt to the ignored files, preventing these generated reports from being accidentally committed.

This commit updates the project's metadata in setup.py to declare support for Python 3.13. It adds the appropriate trove classifier, ensuring the package is correctly identified as compatible with this new Python version in package indexes.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to use single-quoted strings in code examples for consistency. It also corrects a request example to use the POST method and adds steps for manually setting the request body and removing the Content-Type header.
This commit removes the version pin for the pipenv package in the Makefile. It allows the build process to install the latest available version of pipenv instead of a specific older release.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library to 1.0.2. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the package's initialization file to reflect the new release.

This commit updates the documentation to list the specific Python versions and platforms officially supported by the library. It moves the interpreter details from the introduction to the FAQ and clarifies that Python 3 support is imminent.

This commit adds documentation to the advanced user guide explaining that Requests uses blocking IO by default. It clarifies that accessing response content blocks until the download completes, even when using streaming features, and directs users to external projects for non-blocking alternatives.

This commit updates the project's author list by correcting the section title from "Keepers of the Four Crystals" to "Keepers of the Crystals." The change is made in the AUTHORS.rst file to reflect the accurate group name.

This update allows HTTPConnectionPool to accept a per-request timeout parameter, overriding the pool's default setting for individual requests. It modifies the _make_request method to handle this new argument, ensuring more granular control over connection timeouts.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to a newer version, improving compatibility with Python 2 by using six utilities for dictionary iteration. It refines the RecentlyUsedContainer class and adjusts connection handling in the HTTPConnectionPool module.

This commit updates the `test_mixed_case_scheme_acceptable` test in `test_requests.py` to remove HTTPS scheme variations from the test data. It ensures the test only validates mixed-case handling for HTTP URLs, simplifying the test scope.

This commit adds unit tests for the `should_bypass_proxies` function in the `requests.utils` module. It verifies that the function correctly identifies local network addresses and hostnames that should bypass proxy settings.
This commit makes minor wording adjustments to the quickstart documentation. It clarifies phrasing in the sections describing cookie access and invalid HTTP response handling.

This commit updates the AUTHORS.rst file to add Chris Van Horne to the list of contributors. It ensures the project's credit list accurately reflects all individuals who have provided patches or suggestions.

The Request class in requests/core.py now raises a URLRequired exception if the URL is missing, preventing silent failures. It also removes a redundant try block around parameter encoding, simplifying the send method's error handling.

The `text` property in the `Response` class now checks if an encoding is defined before attempting to decode the response content. This prevents errors that occurred when trying to decode data without a specified encoding.

This commit removes the safe mode feature from the requests library, eliminating the `safe_mode` setting and the `catch_exceptions_if_in_safe_mode` decorator. It deletes the `safe_mode` module and updates the `Session` class to stop handling exceptions based on this removed configuration.
This commit updates the urllib3 dependency constraint in setup.cfg to allow versions up to 3.0. It resolves compatibility issues for users installing the package with newer urllib3 releases.

This commit ensures that HTTP header keys are converted to native strings instead of being encoded as ASCII bytes. It modifies the `PreparedRequest` class in `requests/models.py` to use the `to_native_string` utility, preventing potential encoding errors when handling headers.
This commit updates the project's contributor list by adding Adam Tauber to the section for patches and suggestions. It acknowledges his contributions to the codebase.

This commit updates the documentation examples in the advanced user guide to use the correct domain for the HTTPS demo. It replaces outdated references to the old domain with the new one in the `requests` library documentation.
This commit updates the project history to document the addition of async pool size throttling. It records the new feature in the changelog without modifying any code.

This commit removes the outdated dependency management targets from the Makefile. It eliminates the logic that previously cloned and vendored urllib3, chardet, and idna directly into the project, simplifying the build process.

The `super_len` function in `requests/utils.py` now handles file-like objects that raise an `IOError` when calling `tell`. This prevents the utility from crashing when determining the length of streams that do not support seeking or reporting their position.

This commit adds unit tests for the `super_len` utility function in `tests/test_utils.py`. It verifies that the function correctly calculates the length of objects by checking for `__len__`, `tell`, and `fileno` methods, ensuring accurate size reporting for various file-like objects.

This commit updates the `test_invalid_content` method in `test_requests.py` to prevent test failures caused by unreliable DNS providers that may resolve non-existent domains. It adds a warning comment and disables redirects for the request to ensure the test behaves consistently across different network environments.

This commit updates the `iter_lines` method in the `Response` class within `requests/models.py` to use the integer `1` instead of the boolean `True` for the loop condition. This change ensures the infinite loop behaves consistently across different Python versions without altering the user-facing functionality.
This commit updates the installation documentation for the Requests library. It removes references to the deprecated easy_install method and simplifies the instructions to focus solely on using pip.
This commit updates the advanced user documentation to correctly format the name of the c_rehash utility. It ensures the tool name is displayed with proper code styling in the manual.

The `iter_lines` method in the `Response` class now accepts an optional `newline` parameter. This allows users to specify a custom line delimiter for splitting response data, rather than relying solely on the default line break behavior.

This commit updates the release history for version 2.1.0, documenting fixes for connection leaks during chunked uploads. It clarifies that connections are now properly cleaned up on errors and returned to the pool on success.

This commit moves the definition of the `builtin_str` alias from the `requests.models` module to the `requests.compat` module. It ensures the correct string type is consistently imported across Python versions, resolving potential compatibility issues.

This release improves HTTP client behavior by fixing infinite digest authentication redirects and handling invalid URL encodings. It also enhances file uploads by supporting multi-part data on redirects and prevents errors when reading empty response content.

This commit improves the display of code blocks on mobile devices by allowing them to extend beyond the standard right margin. The change is implemented in the `hacks.html` template file, ensuring text does not wrap awkwardly on smaller screens.

This commit updates the `SessionRedirectMixin` in `requests/sessions.py` to preserve URL fragments during redirects, ensuring the fragment from the previous URL is appended if the new location lacks one. This behavior aligns with RFC 7231 and prevents loss of anchor information when navigating between pages.
This commit updates the release history to document version 2.16.1. It notes the restoration of the requests.packages namespace for compatibility and a bugfix for urllib3 version parsing.

This commit refactors the OAuth1 class in requests/auth.py to simplify the content-type validation logic by using a constant and intermediate variables. It also removes trailing whitespace from the HTTPDigestAuth class to improve code readability.
This commit updates an outdated Sphinx documentation link in the contributing guide. It ensures the reference points to the current, secure documentation site rather than the old, unencrypted URL.

This commit updates the project history file to document the v0.2.4 release. It highlights new support for Python 2.5 and PyPy-c v1.4, along with improvements to the Request object constructor and the addition of auto-authentication tests.

This commit adds unit tests to the TestRequests class in tests/test_requests.py to verify Content-Length header calculation. It specifically checks that the header correctly counts bytes rather than characters when the request data is a string containing multi-byte UTF-8 characters.

This commit updates the contribution guidelines in the documentation to clarify that maintainers may reject contributions that do not align with the project's current goals or needs. It refines the wording in the "Contribution Suitability" section to provide clearer context for potential rejections.

This commit updates the authentication module to import OAuth utilities directly from the oauthlib package instead of using an obsolete internal wrapper. This change ensures the library relies on the standard external dependency for OAuth functionality.

This commit standardizes the indentation of docstrings and method signatures in the requests/core.py module. It replaces inconsistent tab-based spacing with uniform four-space indentation for classes like _Request and Request. No functional behavior or user-facing logic is altered.
This commit adds James Clarke to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS.rst file. It updates the project's attribution records to include a new name under the patches and suggestions section.

This commit updates the MANIFEST.in file to include Pipfile and Pipfile.lock in the source distribution. This ensures that dependency management files are packaged correctly for users installing from source.
This commit fixes a linting error in the requests exceptions module by adding a missing blank line. It ensures the RetryError class definition complies with flake8 formatting rules.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 library to version 1.15.1 within the requests package. It refreshes core modules like connection pooling, SSL handling, and response processing to incorporate the latest upstream improvements and bug fixes.

The code of conduct documentation now references the Python Community Code of Conduct instead of the previous external essay. This update replaces the old "be cordial" URL with the official Python guidelines in the project's contributing guide and conduct file.

The `info` function in `requests/help.py` previously crashed on Python 2.6 because the `ssl` module lacked the `OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER` attribute. This fix safely checks for the attribute's existence, preventing the error and displaying an empty string for the SSL version when it is unavailable.

This commit removes Python 3.5 from the supported versions and disables the `requests[security]` extra, which previously installed PyOpenSSL. Users will no longer see Python 3.5 in the test matrix or documentation, and the security extra will no longer provide additional dependencies.

This commit updates the `cookiejar_from_dict` function in `requests/utils.py` to accept a `CookieJar` instance directly, returning it unchanged if provided. It also removes the `domain` parameter and replaces the deprecated `Cookie` module with `cookielib` for better compatibility.
This commit updates the project documentation to improve the clarity and tone of the introductory text. It refines the description of the standard library's limitations in the docs/index.rst file.

This commit updates the requests package to expose the Session class directly in the top-level namespace. Users can now import Session alongside the existing session function without accessing the internal sessions module.

This commit updates the release process documentation to correct version number examples and remove trailing whitespace. It also adds clarifying text explaining that major releases are rare and occur only when breaking changes are introduced.

This commit relaxes the character validation in the Oreos module to accept colons and braces in cookie keys. It prevents the library from raising errors when processing non-standard cookies sent by other services.

This commit adds support for the eventlet library to the requests module. It modifies the urllib2 import in requests/core.py to attempt loading the eventlet green version first, falling back to the standard library if eventlet is not installed.

This commit removes custom scrollbar styling from the Flasky documentation theme. Users will now see their browser's default scrollbars instead of the previously defined thin, rounded appearance. The change affects the static CSS file used for the documentation site.

This commit refactors the `resolve_redirects` method in `requests/sessions.py` to improve code readability and structure. It consolidates cookie extraction into a single line and adds a conditional check to strip authentication headers only when they are present during redirects.

This commit adds a test to verify that accessing a cookie with duplicate names raises an error unless a specific domain is provided. It ensures the cookie jar correctly handles domain-specific lookups to prevent conflicts. The changes are located in the TestRequests class within the test suite.
This commit adds support for sending multipart file uploads in the requests library. It modifies the Request class to handle file data during POST requests, allowing users to upload files directly.

In the testserver module, the Server class now sets its stop event immediately after closing the socket. This ensures the server signals its shutdown state right away, preventing potential race conditions during the termination process.

This commit bumps the Requests library version to 2.34.0.dev1 and updates the changelog. It documents a bug fix where Response.history no longer references itself, preventing infinite loops during traversal.

In the `RequestEncodingMixin` class, the `_encode_files` method now correctly identifies string data using `basestring` instead of just `str`. This ensures proper handling of both byte strings and Unicode strings when encoding request files.

This commit updates the documentation for the `Response.json` method in the `requests` library. It clarifies that the specific exception raised for invalid JSON depends on the Python version and whether the `simplejson` package is installed.

This commit rewrites the CaseInsensitiveDict class in requests/structures.py to function as a proper case-insensitive mapping. It ensures that Session headers correctly handle key lookups regardless of case while preserving the original key casing for iteration.

This commit updates the automated message posted when closing issues that contain questions. It clarifies that the project cannot answer questions on the issue tracker and directs users to Stack Overflow with a direct link. The change modifies the GitHub Actions workflow for closing issues.

The `Response.content` property in `requests/models.py` now returns `None` instead of raising an error when the underlying stream is invalid. This prevents crashes when accessing content from failed requests, such as those with unresolvable domains.
This commit updates the project's contributor list by adding a new name to the authors file. It ensures that piotrjurkiewicz is credited for their patches and suggestions.

This commit cleans up the test suite in test_requests.py by removing a leftover print statement and an outdated TODO comment. It also adds a blank line to improve formatting within the RequestsTestSuite class.

This commit adds an explanatory comment to the `resolve_redirects` method within the `SessionRedirectMixin` class in `requests/sessions.py`. It clarifies why the original prepared request is used to extract cookies from the response, ensuring the cookie jar is updated correctly during redirects.

This commit ensures that the Content-Length header is always included for HTTP PATCH requests. Previously, this header was only added for POST and PUT methods, which could cause issues with servers expecting a body length. The change modifies the prepare_content_length method in the PreparedRequest class.

This commit fixes a typo in the quickstart documentation for the requests library. It corrects the spelling of "response" in the description of the timeout parameter, ensuring the text accurately describes that the timeout applies only to the connection process, not the body download.

This commit fixes an issue where URLs containing quoted slashes were incorrectly handled during request processing. It introduces a new `requote_path` function in `requests/utils.py` to properly manage URL path quoting. The `Request` class in `requests/models.py` now uses this function to ensure correct URL construction.

This commit fixes a bug in the `HTTPAdapter` class where connection errors were incorrectly treated as timeouts. It ensures that `NewConnectionError` exceptions are no longer raised as `ConnectTimeout`, improving error handling accuracy. This change is a temporary compatibility fix scheduled for removal in a future version.

This change modifies the `Session.request` method in `requests/sessions.py` to only fall back to the session's default verification setting when the `verify` parameter is explicitly `None`. Previously, any falsy value passed to `verify` would trigger the fallback, potentially overriding intentional settings.
This commit updates the AUTHORS.rst file to add Jason Emerick to the list of contributors. It also fixes a missing newline at the end of the file.
This commit cleans up comments in the requests/config.py module. It removes outdated timeout documentation and adds a brief note about default attributes within the Settings class.

This commit enables automatic decompression of deflate-encoded responses when using the Response.iter_content method. It also refactors Response.iter_lines to rely on iter_content, ensuring consistent handling of compressed data streams.

This commit corrects an incorrect GitHub profile link in the project's author list. It updates the reference for Robin Linderborg to point to the correct username, ensuring the link resolves properly for users.

This commit updates the project's README to correct the description of the Requests library's popularity. It changes the claim from being one of the most downloaded packages of all time to being the most downloaded Python package today.

This commit fixes a test failure in the `RequestsTestSuite` where a unicode literal caused issues on Python 2. It introduces a temporary workaround to ensure the `test_POSTBIN_GET_POST_FILES_STRINGS` test passes correctly across different Python versions.

This commit updates the contributing documentation to correct the PEP 8 reference link. It changes the URL from the Python.org PEP page to the dedicated pep8.org site. The change affects the `docs/dev/contributing.rst` file.

This commit fixes a typo in the MANIFEST.in file that prevented the requests/cacert.pem file from being included in the distribution package. Users building the package would previously have been missing this certificate file.
This commit fixes a minor typographical inconsistency in the documentation sidebar templates. It adds a missing period to the fundraising amount text in the sidebarintro and sidebarlogo HTML files.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to improve the formatting of proxy configuration examples. It consolidates multi-line dictionary definitions into single lines for better readability in the `advanced.rst` file.
Adds a new CI job to the GitHub Actions workflow that runs the test suite against urllib3 1.26.x. This ensures the project remains compatible with the older urllib3 major version.

This commit resolves CI and build failures by migrating the project's linting and formatting tools from Black, isort, and pyupgrade to Ruff. It also drops support for Python 3.10 on PyPy, removing that version from the test matrix.

This commit adds detailed parameter documentation to the `Request` class in `requests/models.py`. It clarifies the expected inputs for the `__init__` method, such as headers, data, and authentication, improving the clarity of the API for users.

This commit fixes a bug in the `PreparedRequest` class where the error message for invalid URLs could fail to display correctly. It ensures the URL is properly encoded before being included in the suggestion, preventing potential encoding errors when the message is generated.

The `Response.content` property in `requests.models` now returns `None` when the underlying raw data is missing, rather than raising an error or returning an empty string. This ensures that empty responses correctly report no content, fixing a potential inconsistency in how missing data is handled.

This commit fixes a bug in the `header_expand` function where Unicode header strings were incorrectly processed as iterables instead of being returned as-is. It updates the type check to use `basestring` from `requests/compat.py`, ensuring compatibility across Python versions.
This commit updates the project's changelog to document the release of version 2.14.1. It notes a bugfix that adjusts dependency markers to improve compatibility with older versions of pip.
This commit adds docstrings to test methods in test_requests.py to clarify their purpose. It also updates a test case to verify that header updates are handled case-insensitively.

This commit updates the documentation template to use a new site identifier for the embedded content. It changes the data attribute value in the hacks.html file to ensure the correct tracking or configuration is applied.

This commit centralizes the JSON library import logic by moving the fallback from simplejson to the standard json module into the requests/compat.py file. It removes the duplicate import block from requests/models.py, which now imports json directly from the compatibility module.

This commit updates the API documentation for the `request` function, `Request` class, and `Response` class. It adds a usage example to the `request` function and clarifies the descriptions for the `Request` and `Response` classes.

This commit adds a test to verify that session-level cookies are correctly persisted and returned by the server. It ensures the `requests` library properly handles cookie state within a session object.

This commit improves the Makefile's readme validation target by using explicit command-line flags for the Python setup check. It adds clear success and failure messages to help users quickly identify if the README or HISTORY files contain invalid markup.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the `put` function within `requests/core.py` that prevented the module from loading on Python 2.5 and PyPy. The change removes an invalid byte string prefix from the default argument, ensuring the function definition is compatible with older Python versions.
This commit adds Kamil Madac to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS.rst file. It updates the project's attribution records to recognize his contributions.

This commit reorganizes the test suite by moving the original request tests into a new integration test directory. The change affects the test_requests.py module, establishing a clearer separation between different test categories.

This commit updates the main documentation index to use a more reliable example URL for the requests library. It replaces the previous GitHub API demonstration with a request to httpbin.org, showing a successful response and JSON output.

This commit updates the project's README documentation to improve formatting and clarity. It removes bold styling from the library name and adds a warning label to the cautionary text regarding other HTTP libraries.
This commit corrects a broken hyperlink in the AUTHORS.rst file. It fixes the GitHub profile link for the contributor "Dull Bananas" by adding the missing closing parenthesis to the URL.
This release adds Python 3 support to the requests library while dropping support for Python 2.5. The version number in the requests module is updated to 0.10.1 to reflect these changes.

This commit updates the project's sponsor documentation to highlight Slack's significant contribution to the 2018 fundraising campaign. It clarifies that Slack was the first organization to donate, noting that their gift immediately surpassed the total fundraising goal.

This commit refactors the HTTPAdapter class in the requests library by extracting proxy manager creation logic into a new method called proxy_manager_for. This change allows subclasses to customize how proxy managers are instantiated without modifying the main connection retrieval process.

This commit updates the documentation in the advanced user guide to use Python 3 compatible syntax. It changes a print statement example to include parentheses, ensuring the code snippet is valid for modern Python versions.

The `request` function in `requests/api.py` now accepts a `config` parameter. This allows users to pass configuration options directly to the request, which are then forwarded to the underlying session.
This commit updates the version number of the requests library from 0.3.3 to 0.3.4. It modifies the version and build identifiers in the core module to reflect the new release.

This commit corrects a documentation error in the installation guide. It changes the text in the `docs/user/install.rst` file to refer to the Requests library instead of Tablib, ensuring the documentation accurately describes the correct software package.

This commit adds a GitHub banner to the documentation site, allowing users to easily navigate to the project's source code repository. It updates the Sphinx theme configuration in `docs/conf.py` to specify the GitHub user and repository name.

This commit fixes the error message formatting for JSON decoding failures in the requests library. It modifies the JSONDecodeError class to initialize its parent classes in a specific order, ensuring the detailed JSON error message is preserved instead of being overwritten by generic IOError arguments.
This commit reverts a previous change to the documentation theme's stylesheet. It restores the commented-out state of the body and list styling rules in the small_flask.css file.

This commit fixes an issue in the `Request` class where posting data containing floats or lists would fail. It ensures these values are properly converted to strings before encoding, allowing mixed data and file uploads to work correctly.
This release adds support for honoring netrc files, allowing users to store credentials for automatic authentication. The change is documented in the project's history file.

This commit corrects the documentation in the README to accurately reference the Response object instead of the Request object for attributes like status code and headers. It ensures users understand that these properties belong to the response returned by the library.

This commit updates the user documentation to remove references to the underlying CookieJar object. It clarifies that the Session class handles cookie persistence automatically, removing the need for users to access the jar directly.

This commit fixes a spelling error in the project documentation. It corrects the word "maintinence" to "maintenance" in the index file to ensure accurate communication about the project's support status.

This commit removes the pyflakes linting targets and related configuration variables from the Makefile. It simplifies the build process by eliminating the code that checks for Python syntax errors and unused imports.

This commit removes an unnecessary call to the redirect resolution logic within the Session.send method when redirects are not being followed. It ensures that the request history is correctly set to an empty list in this scenario, avoiding redundant processing.

This commit fixes the documentation build process by moving the command to generate the HTML site into the correct target. It ensures the `site` target properly builds the docs, resolving a previous issue where the build command was misplaced.

This commit cleans up code style in the test suite and test server. It removes unnecessary blank lines in the TestContentEncodingDetection class and refactors the consume_socket_content function in the test server to define the chunk size as a local variable instead of a default argument.

This commit improves the documentation by adding cross-links to the urllib3 project and correcting minor grammatical errors. It enables the intersphinx extension in the Sphinx configuration to support these external references.

The `_basic_auth_str` function in `requests/auth.py` now emits deprecation warnings when non-string usernames or passwords are provided. This prepares users for the removal of this behavior in version 3.0.

This commit fixes the `Response.text` property in `requests/models.py` to return a standard string instead of a Unicode literal. This ensures compatibility with Python 3, where the `u` prefix is no longer valid syntax.

This commit adds Python 3.6 to the AppVeyor continuous integration configuration. It enables automated testing for the new Python version by defining the necessary environment variables and specifying the corresponding tox environment.

This commit modifies the `PreparedRequest` class in `requests/models.py` to lazily load the `idna` library. It ensures the dependency is imported only when encoding a host, preventing startup delays and allowing the library to function even if the vendored package is unavailable.

This commit fixes a bug in the HTTPDigestAuth class where the request URI was incorrectly set to an empty string during HTTP redirections. By ensuring the path defaults to a forward slash, the digest authentication header now complies with RFC 2616 requirements.

This commit removes the outdated PyPI mirror installation instructions from the user documentation. It eliminates the section in the install guide that suggested using third-party mirrors when the main package index was unavailable.

This commit fixes the `PreparedRequest.prepare_content_length` method in `requests/models.py` to correctly calculate the Content-Length header for file-like objects. It ensures the length reflects only the remaining data to be sent and restores the file pointer to its original position instead of the start.

This release removes external dependencies and adds a new `Response.reason` attribute. It also fixes an issue where client certificates were ignored when verification was disabled and adds support for signing OAuth 1.0 query parameters.

This commit updates the contributing documentation to include a positive example of code formatting immediately following a negative example. It clarifies the preferred style for function calls with multiple arguments in the Requests codebase.

This commit updates the API documentation to clarify that logging is configured using the `requests.packages.urllib3` logger rather than the top-level `requests` logger. It corrects the example in the `docs/api.rst` file to reflect the proper logging namespace.

This commit partially reverts a previous change in the `PreparedRequest` class within `requests/models.py`. It restores the use of a dedicated `complexjson` import for serializing JSON bodies, ensuring compatibility with specific JSON handling requirements.

This release updates the requests library to version 0.12.0, introducing a new cookie interface backed by a CookieJar with a dictionary-like API. It also adds a pre_send hook, implements lazy encoding for data and parameters, and improves certificate handling by loading system bundles when certify is unavailable.

This commit adds a unit test to verify that the `select_proxy` function in the `requests.utils` module correctly chooses proxies based on specific hostnames. It ensures that requests to a particular host use its dedicated proxy, while other hosts fall back to the default or no proxy.

This commit fixes an issue where HEAD requests with redirects could hang or fail to complete. It modifies the `Response.iter_content` method in `requests/models.py` to stop processing when no content is received. A new test verifies that HEAD requests with redirects now return successfully.

This commit adds documentation to the API reference explaining how to migrate from version 1.0 to 2.0. It details specific API changes, such as `RequestException` now inheriting from `IOError` and invalid URL escapes raising a `RequestException` subclass instead of a `ValueError`.
This commit removes the license image and adds a new PSF logo image to the extension directory. It updates the visual assets used by the project without altering any code logic or functionality.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the project's README file. It changes the word "gaurenteed" to "guaranteed" in the installation section to ensure accurate documentation.

This commit cleans up the `Settings` class in `requests/config.py` by adding blank lines for readability. It also converts the inline comment for the `timeout_fallback` attribute into a standard docstring.
This commit updates the Ruff linter version in the pre-commit configuration from 0.15.14 to 0.15.15. It ensures the project uses the latest patch release for code quality checks during development.

This commit fixes a Python 3 compatibility issue in the test suite by updating the string buffer import logic. It ensures the tests use the standard `io` module for Python 3, while retaining the legacy `cStringIO` fallback for Python 2.

This commit adds a `trusted_domains` list to the `Session` class, allowing users to specify hosts where authentication headers should not be stripped during redirects. It modifies the `should_strip_auth` method in `SessionRedirectMixin` to check this list before removing credentials, preventing unnecessary re-authentication for trusted sites.

This commit fixes a test failure in the `RequestsTestCase` class within `test_requests.py` that occurred when running on Python 3. It updates the `test_custom_content_type` method to correctly compare byte strings, ensuring the test passes by matching the expected content type format.

This commit corrects minor spelling and grammar errors in the project's documentation and source code. It updates the HISTORY.md and advanced user guide files, and fixes a typo in the super_len function within requests/utils.py.
This commit updates the project's contributor list by adding Marty Alchin to the section for patches and suggestions. It modifies the AUTHORS.rst file to reflect this new credit.

This commit updates the contributing documentation to replace placeholder text with more descriptive examples for docstrings. It modifies the sample code in the contributing guide to better illustrate the expected syntax and style for function documentation.

This commit fixes a crash in the `Request` class where building a response from a raw object without headers raised a "None is not iterable" error. It changes the default value for missing headers from `None` to an empty dictionary in the `_build_response` method.

This commit prevents the Session class from consulting the redirect cache when the allow_redirects parameter is set to False. Previously, this could cause incorrect URL resolution or unexpected behavior for requests that explicitly disabled automatic redirects. The change ensures the redirect cache is only accessed when redirects are permitted.

The `requests` library now accepts a single `cert` argument instead of separate `key_file` and `cert_file` parameters. This allows users to pass either a path to a PEM file or a tuple containing the certificate and key paths. The change affects the `request` function, `Request` class, and `Session` class.
This release fixes a long-standing issue where network connections could hang indefinitely. The update bumps the version to 0.13.6 in the requests module and documents the fix in the project history.

This commit fixes a regression where binary request bodies were incorrectly converted to strings, causing data corruption. It modifies the `PreparedRequest` class in `requests/models.py` to preserve byte data during URL preparation. A new test verifies that binary PUT requests maintain their byte format.

This commit adds a build status badge to the project's README file. It displays the current state of the Azure Pipelines CI build, providing users with immediate visibility into the project's build health.
This commit updates the project's release history to document a minor dependency change. It notes that `win_inet_pton` is now a conditional requirement for the socks extra on Windows with Python 2.7.

This commit removes outdated references to the pyflakes linter from the codebase. It cleans up the .gitignore file and eliminates unnecessary variable assignments in requests/cookies.py and requests/utils.py that were previously used to suppress linter warnings.

This commit clarifies the documentation for the requests library, specifying that the `auth` parameter takes precedence over `.netrc` files, which in turn override raw HTTP headers. It updates the authentication and quickstart guides to accurately reflect this hierarchy of credential sources.

This commit updates the compatibility module to prefer the faster cchardet library for character encoding detection when it is installed. If cchardet is unavailable, the code falls back to the standard chardet package, ensuring continued functionality across different environments.

This commit updates the project's README to replace informal marketing language with a more professional description of the library's capabilities. It clarifies that the Requests module simplifies sending HTTP/1.1 requests by handling query strings and data encoding automatically.

This commit fixes a bug in the `requote_path` function within `requests/utils.py` where reserved URI characters were incorrectly encoded, altering the URI's semantics. It introduces a new helper, `unquote_unreserved`, to selectively decode only unreserved characters before re-encoding illegal ones. This ensures URIs are normalized without corrupting reserved characters.

This commit fixes a Python 3 compatibility error in the `header_expand` function within `requests/utils.py`. It updates the type check to use `str` instead of the removed `unicode` type, preventing crashes when processing string headers.
This commit updates the author documentation by replacing an outdated image link with a new one. The change affects the `docs/dev/authors.rst` file, ensuring the displayed photo is current.
This commit updates the documentation string in the requests package's main module. It changes the example header from "Basic POST usage" to "... or POST" to align with the master branch.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the setup.py file that would have prevented the package from installing correctly. It adds a missing comma to the list of included packages, ensuring the chardet module is properly registered.

This commit reverts a previous change that automatically stripped UTF-8 Byte Order Marks from response text. It restores the original behavior in the `Response` class within `requests/models.py`, ensuring that BOM characters are preserved in the output rather than being removed.

This commit corrects a typo in the test suite for the requests module. It updates the `test_unconsumed_session_response_closes_connection` method to use the proper assertion methods, ensuring the test correctly verifies that the response content is not consumed and the connection is closed.

The HTTPAdapter.request_url method in the requests library no longer strips leading slashes from request paths. This change preserves the original path structure, ensuring that URLs starting with multiple slashes are passed through unchanged rather than being normalized to a single slash.

This commit fixes the test suite in tests/test_requests.py to use the __file__ variable instead of a hardcoded filename when opening the test file. This ensures the tests work correctly regardless of the current working directory. It also standardizes the spacing in a dictionary definition.

This commit adds a "Request Object Attributes" section header to the advanced user documentation. It organizes the existing content in the `docs/user/advanced.rst` file by clearly labeling the relevant section.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to reflect the new cookie API. It changes the example from printing the entire cookie dictionary to accessing a specific cookie value directly, ensuring users see the correct usage pattern.

This commit updates the copyright year in the documentation configuration from 2015 to 2016. It modifies the `conf.py` file to ensure the generated documentation displays the correct current year for the Requests project.
This commit removes a trailing whitespace character from the Request class definition in requests/core.py. It is a minor cleanup that does not alter any functional behavior or user-visible output.

This commit replaces the dynamic `supported_schemes` function with a static `SCHEMAS` list in `requests.defaults`. It updates the `Request` class in `requests.models` to validate URL schemes against this new list, simplifying the scheme validation logic.

This commit corrects a misleading example in the quickstart documentation for the requests library. It clarifies that the key in the files dictionary should be the field name, such as 'file', rather than the actual filename, to align with the library's behavior.

This commit updates the documentation to reflect that the `json` attribute is now a method rather than a property. It corrects examples in the index and quickstart guides to show calling `r.json()` and clarifies that decoding failures now raise an exception instead of returning `None`.

This commit modifies the `iter_content` method in the `Response` class to prevent users from calling iteration methods multiple times on a single streamed request. It now raises a `RuntimeError` if the response content has already been consumed, ensuring that repeated attempts to read the stream fail explicitly rather than silently.

This commit restores the visibility of the sidebar navigation on mobile webpages. It removes a CSS rule that previously hid the sidebar element, ensuring users can access navigation links on smaller screens.

This commit removes an unnecessary IDE configuration file that defined a project dictionary. The change cleans up the repository by deleting a file that is not required for the application's functionality or build process.

This commit updates the project history to document version 0.3.2, which introduces automatic decompression of GZip encoded content and support for tuple-based HTTP authentication. It also corrects a minor formatting error in the previous release notes.

This commit updates the documentation introduction to use an include directive for the license text instead of hardcoding it. This change ensures the copyright years remain synchronized with the source code, preventing outdated information in the user guide.

This update documents a fix in the development history where passing None as a file pointer to the files parameter no longer raises an exception. The change clarifies that this specific input is now handled gracefully without error.

This commit refactors the `requests` library's compatibility layer to properly import `SimpleCookie` and URL utilities for both Python 2 and 3. It also cleans up redundant imports in `requests/models.py`, ensuring the `Request` class uses the correct underlying modules.

Adds a `json` property to the `Response` class in `requests/models.py` that parses and returns the JSON content of a request. If the content is not valid JSON, it returns `None` instead of raising an error.

This commit rearranges the timeout type checks within the `send` method of the `HTTPAdapter` class in `requests/adapters.py`. It swaps the order of the conditional branches to check for tuples before `TimeoutSauce` objects, with no change to the resulting behavior.
This commit contains no code changes or file modifications. It serves as a placeholder in the repository history without altering any application behavior or fixing specific issues.

This commit updates the project's changelog to clarify that automatic unicode decoding now relies on HTTP headers. It also documents the new interface for advanced response usage and the automatic expansion of parameterized headers.

This commit removes outdated documentation references to the `safe_mode` and `danger_mode` options from the quickstart guide. Users will no longer see instructions for these configuration settings in the user documentation.

The Makefile now runs the test suite using pytest instead of tox, changing how developers execute tests locally. It also removes the flake8 linting rule, eliminating the dedicated command for code style checks.

The HTTPDigestAuth class now correctly quotes the qop value in the Authorization header, ensuring compliance with HTTP digest authentication standards. This change fixes a potential issue where servers might reject requests due to improperly formatted headers.
This commit updates the version number in the requests core module from 0.6.2 to 0.7.0. It marks the start of the 0.7.0 development cycle without changing any functional behavior.

This commit adds a missing parameter description to the documentation for the `Session.request` method in the `requests` library. It clarifies how the `hooks` argument should be formatted, improving the clarity of the API reference for users.

This commit introduces a new cookie management module for the requests library, enabling users to store, retrieve, and send cookies across HTTP sessions. It defines the CookieJar class to handle cookie storage and extraction, along with MockRequest and MockResponse classes to bridge requests objects with the standard library's cookie handling.
This commit adds the `docs/_build` directory to the `.gitignore` file. It prevents generated documentation build artifacts from being tracked by version control, keeping the repository clean.
This commit updates the documentation for the community updates page. It renames the "Software Updates" section to "Release and Version History" and removes two blank lines from the file.
This commit updates the project's contributor list by adding Frank Kumro Jr to the "Patches and Suggestions" section. It also corrects a missing newline at the end of the file.

This commit updates the development documentation to announce a feature freeze for the Requests library. It clarifies that new feature requests are no longer accepted, focusing contributions on bug fixes and testing.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to use the variable name `r` instead of `_r` in code examples. This change ensures consistency with standard naming conventions used elsewhere in the library's documentation.

This commit fixes a bug in the `Request` class where a `Cookie` header was incorrectly set to the string "None" when no cookies were present. It ensures the header is only added if a valid cookie string exists, preventing malformed requests. A regression test was added to verify that no `Cookie` header is sent when cookies are empty.

This commit updates the support documentation to include a link for asking questions on StackOverflow and adds instructions for reporting security vulnerabilities. It also expands the list of maintainers to contact on Twitter, ensuring users have accurate and complete channels for getting help.

This commit adds the `.idea` directory to the project's `.gitignore` file. This prevents IntelliJ IDEA configuration files from being tracked by version control, keeping the repository clean of local development environment settings.
This commit removes unused imports from the `requests.models` module. It cleans up the code by eliminating references to `urlunparse` and `urljoin` that were not being used.

This commit fixes an application error in the `get_netrc_auth` function within `requests/utils.py`. It prevents crashes by catching `AttributeError` alongside existing exceptions when processing network authentication files.
